title_ar: شرح الجزرية الجزء الأول
title_en: Commentary on al-Jazariyyah — Part One
body_ar: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين وأصلي وأسلم على من بعث رحمة للعالمين وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين، السلام عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته، أما بعد فإن الله تعالى أنزل القرآن على محمد (ص) بلسان عربي مبين، وقد جاء به جبريل عليه السلام إلى رسول الله (ص) منجما في ثلاث وعشرين سنة، ينزل بحسب الوقائع وبحسب ما يسأل عنه أهل الأرض وكان ذلك اتصالا بين أهل السماء وأهل الأرض، وارتباطا بين الخلق والخالق، جل وعلا ببيان ما يريده منهم وتشريع ما يرتضيه لهم، وقد ختم الله الرسائل إلى أهل الأرض برسالة محمد (ص)، وختم الكتب المنزلة إلى أهل الأرض بالقرآن، وجعله مصدقا لما بين يديه من الحق ومهيمنا على كل الكتب وناسخا لها، فلا يقبل الله من أحد بعد نزول القرآن دينا إلا هذا الإسلام الذي تضمنه هذا القرآن، وقد أنزل على هيآت متنوعة، فمنها أن يأتي الملك على هيئة رجل فيكلم رسول الله (ص) فيعي عنه ما يقول،
body_en:
In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Compassionate. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. I invoke blessings and peace upon him who was sent as a mercy to the worlds, and upon his family and his Companions and whoever has taken his guidance for guidance and his sunnah for a way, until the Day of Judgement. Peace be upon you, and the mercy of God and His blessings.

To proceed: God, be He exalted, sent the Qur'an down upon Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him) in a clear Arabic tongue. Gabriel (peace be upon him) brought it to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) in instalments over twenty-three years, coming down according to events and according to what the people of the earth asked about. That was a channel of contact between the people of heaven and the people of the earth, and a bond between the creation and the Creator — mighty and exalted is He — by the setting out of what He wants from them and the legislating of what He is content with for them. God sealed the messages to the people of the earth with the message of Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him), and sealed the books sent down to the people of the earth with the Qur'an; and He made it confirming the truth that was before it, a guardian over all the books, and abrogating them. So God accepts from no one, after the descent of the Qur'an, any religion but this Islam which this Qur'an contains. It was sent down in a variety of modes: among them, that the angel would come in the form of a man and speak to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), and he would retain from him what he said,

title_ar: شرح الجزرية الجزء الثاني
title_en: Commentary on al-Jazariyyah — Part Two
body_ar: وبهذا تعلمون أن حفص الدوري مثلا توفي في القرن الثالث والخاقاني توفي في القرن الرابع، ومكي بن أبي طالب توفي في القرن الخامس، وأهل الأندلس عموما اشتهروا بإتقان هذا العلم ولذلك فإن مكيا كان مجددا فيه ثم جاء بعده أبو عمرو الداني وهو إمام علوم القرآن كلها بلا منازع، ثم بعده تلميذه أبو داود سليمان بن النجيح وهو كذلك خليفة الداني في هذا العلم، فأهل الأندلس اشتهروا بعلوم التجويد وبتفسير القرآن كذلك فمنهم ابن عطية وابن جزي والقرطبي وأبو بكر بن العربي وغيرهم من أئمة أهل التجويد كأبي حيان وابن الفرس المالكي مؤلف كتاب أحكام القرآن، فلهم مؤلفات كثيرة جدا في خدمة القرآن.
body_en: And by this you know that Hafs al-Duri, for example, died in the third century, and al-Khaqani died in the fourth century, and Makki ibn Abi Talib died in the fifth century. The people of al-Andalus in general were renowned for their mastery of this science, and for that reason Makki was a renewer in it. Then after him came Abu Amr al-Dani, who is without dispute the foremost authority in all the sciences of the Qur'an; and after him his student Abu Dawud Sulayman ibn al-Najih, who was likewise al-Dani's successor in this science. The people of al-Andalus were renowned for the sciences of the rules of Qur'anic recitation (tajwīd), and for Qur'anic exegesis (tafsīr) as well — among them Ibn Atiyyah, Ibn Juzayy, al-Qurtubi, Abu Bakr ibn al-Arabi and others — and for others among the leading authorities in tajwid, such as Abu Hayyan and Ibn al-Faras al-Maliki, the author of the book Ahkam al-Qur'an. They have a very great many works in the service of the Qur'an.

title_ar: شرح الجزرية الشريط التاسع
title_en: Commentary on al-Jazariyyah — Tape Nine
body_ar: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين وأصلي وأسلم على من بعث رحمة للعالمين وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين يقول المؤلف رحمه الله تعالى: باب معرفة الوقوف عقد هذا الباب لبيان أمر مهم من أمور التجويد وهو حكم الوقف والابتداء، والوقف في اللغة مصدر وقف تستعمل لازمة وتستعمل متعدية، فيقال وقف فلان في الصلاة أي قام، ويقال وقف فلان راحلته أو ناقته إذا حبسها، ومنه قول عنترة
body_en:
In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Compassionate. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. I invoke blessings and peace upon him who was sent as a mercy to the worlds, and upon his family and his Companions and whoever has taken his guidance for guidance and his sunnah for a way, until the Day of Judgement.

The author (may God, be He exalted, have mercy on him) says: "Chapter on the knowledge of the pauses." He set up this chapter to expound an important matter among the matters of Qur'anic recitation (tajwīd), namely the ruling on pausing and on beginning again. Pausing (waqf), in the language, is the verbal noun of waqafa, which is used both intransitively and transitively. One says "So-and-so waqafa in the prayer", meaning that he stood; and one says "So-and-so waqafa his mount or his she-camel", when he brought it to a halt. And from this is the saying of Antarah

title_ar: شرح الجزرية الشريط الثالث
title_en: Commentary on al-Jazariyyah — Tape Three
body_ar:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين وأصلي وأسلم على من بعث رحمة للعالمين وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين.

أما بعد فيقول المؤلف رحمه الله: باب مخارج الحروف الباب في اللغة فرجة في ساتر يتوصل بها من داخل إلى خارج وبالعكس حقيقةً في المباني كباب الدار وحكما في المعاني كباب مخارج الحروف، وهو في الاصطلاح اسم لطائفة من الفن تشترك في بعض الأحكام وتتميز عن غيرها، وهو يعقد لما يحتاج لبيانه من العلم، فهذا العلم الذي هو علم الأداء من مسائله التي تحتاج إلى عقد باب مخارج الحروف، والحروف قد سبق تعريفها وهي يبٍحث فيها من أربعة أوجه، الوجه الأول: المخرج (مخرج الحرف)، والوجه الثاني الصفة التي يتصف بها الحرف،
body_en:
In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Compassionate. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. I invoke blessings and peace upon him who was sent as a mercy to the worlds, and upon his family and his Companions and whoever has taken his guidance for guidance and his sunnah for a way, until the Day of Judgement.

To proceed: the author (may God have mercy on him) says: "Chapter on the points of articulation of the letters." A bāb, in the language, is a gap in a barrier by which one passes from inside to outside and the reverse — literally so in buildings, as with the door of a house, and by extension in meanings, as with the "chapter" on the points of articulation of the letters. In technical usage it is a name for a group of topics within a discipline which share certain rulings and are marked off from others; and it is set up for whatever stands in need of exposition within the science. Now this science, which is the science of Qur'anic delivery, has among its topics ones that require a chapter on the points of articulation of the letters to be set up. The letters have already been defined, and they are examined from four aspects. The first aspect: the point of articulation (the point of articulation of the letter). The second aspect: the quality by which the letter is characterised,

title_ar: شرح الجزرية الشريط الثامن
title_en: Commentary on al-Jazariyyah — Tape Eight
body_ar:
الحمد لله رب العالمين وصلى الله وسلم على نبينا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين، السلام عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته.

أما بعد فإن من الحروف ما هو مختص ببعض الأحكام، فلا بد من العناية به للعناية بتلك الأحكام التي تختص به، وهذه الحروف هي الميم والنون واللام فهذه الحروف الثلاثة تخرج عن قواعد الحروف لبعض الاختصاصات التي تختص بها، فاحتيج لبيان أحكام تختص بها، وقد عقد المؤلف رحمه الله تعالى هذا الباب لبيان أحكام الميم ولبيان حكم النون المشددة فقال:
body_en:
Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds, and may God bless our Prophet Muhammad and grant him peace, and his family and his Companions and whoever has taken his guidance for guidance and his sunnah for a way, until the Day of Judgement. Peace be upon you, and the mercy of God and His blessings.

To proceed: among the letters there are some that have rulings peculiar to them, so they must be attended to in order that those rulings peculiar to them may be attended to. These letters are the mīm, the nūn and the lām: these three letters depart from the general rules of the letters on account of certain properties peculiar to them, and so there was a need to set out rulings peculiar to them. The author (may God, be He exalted, have mercy on him) set up this chapter to set out the rulings of the mīm and to set out the ruling of the doubled nūn. He said:

title_ar: شرح الجزرية الشريط الخامس
title_en: Commentary on al-Jazariyyah — Tape Five
body_ar: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين، وأصلي وأسلم على من بعث رحمة للعالمين، وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين، السلام عليكم ورحمة الله تعالى وبركاته، أما بعد فقد سبق أن مواضع المخارج خمسة، الجوف والحلق واللسان والشفتان والخيشوم، فهذه خمسة مواضع هي محال الضغط على الهواء المنطلق من الرئة، وفي كل مكان ضغط عليه يتركب مخرج من مخارج الحروف، وقد سبق أن العلماء اختلفوا في عدد مخارج الحروف إلى أربعة أقوال: القول الأول قول الخليل بن أحمد الفراهيدي أنها سبعة عشر، وهو اختيار ابن الجزري، القول الثاني أنها تسعة وعشرين أي أن لكل حرف مخرجا
body_en:
In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Compassionate. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. I invoke blessings and peace upon him who was sent as a mercy to the worlds, and upon his family and his Companions and whoever has taken his guidance for guidance and his sunnah for a way, until the Day of Judgement. Peace be upon you, and the mercy of God, be He exalted, and His blessings.

To proceed: it has already been established that the locations of the points of articulation are five — the cavity, the throat, the tongue, the two lips and the nasal passage. These are five locations, and they are the places where pressure is applied to the air issuing from the lung; and at every place where it is pressed, one of the points of articulation of the letters is formed. It has also already been established that the scholars differed over the number of the points of articulation of the letters, into four positions. The first position is that of al-Khalil ibn Ahmad al-Farahidi, that they are seventeen, and this is what Ibn al-Jazari chose. The second position is that they are twenty-nine, that is, that every letter has a point of articulation of its own

title_ar: شرح الجزرية الشريط الرابع
title_en: Commentary on al-Jazariyyah — Tape Four
body_ar: ثم قال: باب الصفات عقد هذا الباب لصفات الحروف، والصفة في الأصل النعت وما يميز الشيء عن غيره، والصفات ثلاثة أقسام في الأصل، صفات ذاتية، وصفات عرضية، وصفات حكمية، فالصفات الذاتية هي ما خلق الله عليه الشيء كطول الإنسان وقصره وحسنه وقبحه وبياضه وسواده ونحو ذلك هذه صفة ذاتية فيه، والصفات العرضية كالصفات الاختيارية أو الفعلية كالحركة والسكون في الإنسان، والكلام والسكوت، هذا صفة عرضية أي تعرض للإنسان، والقسم الثالث الصفات الحكمية وهي: ما ناطه الشارع به من الأحكام، كالطهارة والنجاسة، كون هذا الشيء طاهرا وكونه نجسا هذا ليس من خلقته، ولا هو عارض فيه بل هو حكم رتبه الشارع عليه، وهذا عند جمهور أهل العلم خلافا للحنفية فالحنفية يرون أن الصفات الحكمية من الصفات الأصلية لا من الصفات العارضة، فيجعلون الأحكام أصولا يرون أن الشارع كاشف لما كان سابقا في أصل الخلقة، فيرون أن الأصل في الماء الطهارة فهو صفة أصلية له، وأن الأصل في البول النجاسة فهو صفة أصلية له،
body_en:
Then he said: "Chapter on the qualities." He set up this chapter for the qualities of the letters. A quality (ṣifah), in origin, is a descriptive attribute, and whatever distinguishes a thing from something else. Qualities are, in origin, of three kinds: essential qualities, accidental qualities, and juridically assigned qualities.

The essential qualities are those upon which God created the thing — such as a person's tallness or shortness, his beauty or ugliness, his whiteness or blackness, and the like; this is an essential quality in him.

The accidental qualities are such as the volitional or active qualities — like motion and rest in a person, and speech and silence; this is an accidental quality, that is, one that comes upon the person.

The third kind is the juridically assigned qualities, and they are the rulings that the Lawgiver has attached to the thing — such as ritual purity (ṭahārah) and substantive impurity (najāsah). That this thing is pure, and that it is impure, is not part of how it was created, nor is it something accidental in it; rather it is a ruling that the Lawgiver has ordered upon it. This is so in the view of the majority of the people of knowledge, as against the Hanafis: for the Hanafis hold that the juridically assigned qualities are among the original qualities and not among the accidental ones. So they make the rulings foundational, holding that the Lawgiver is disclosing what was already there in the original constitution of the thing; and thus they hold that the original state of water is purity, so that this is an original quality of it, and that the original state of urine is impurity, so that this is an original quality of it,

The position attributed to the Hanafis here is reported, not adopted. The Sheikh states the majority view first and marks the Hanafi view as against it. The attribution must stay visible in any rendering.

The terms 'essential' (dhātiyyah) and 'accidental' (ʿaraḍiyyah) qualities are used here of created things and of letters. They are not being used in their creedal (kalām) sense, of the attributes of God, and the creedal senses must not be read into this passage.

The Arabic breaks off mid-sentence while still reporting the Hanafi position, before the Sheikh returns to his own voice or to the qualities of the letters that the chapter is about. A reader could mistake the last-stated position for his own; it is not.

title_ar: شرح الجزرية الشريط السابع
title_en: Commentary on al-Jazariyyah — Tape Seven
body_ar:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين وأصلي وأسلم على من بعث رحمة للعالمين، وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين، السلام عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته،

يقول المؤلف رحمه الله: باب الراءات عقد هذا الباب لصفة عارضة وهي الترقيق الذي تتصف به الراء، فقد سبق أن التغليظ صفة لكل الحروف المستعلية وأن الترقيق صفة لكل الحروف المستفلة وأن التغليظ يعرض في ثلاثة من الحروف المستفلة وهي الراء واللام والألف، فهذه الحروف الثلاثة مستفلة ومع ذلك يعرض فيها التغليظ، وهذا التغليظ لما كان صفة عارضة لم نذكره، والمؤلف رحمه الله تعالى ذكر ما يتعلق بالراءت ثم ذكر ما يتعلق باللامات والألفات التي معها فبدأ بالراءات فقال:
body_en:
In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Compassionate. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. I invoke blessings and peace upon him who was sent as a mercy to the worlds, and upon his family and his Companions and whoever has taken his guidance for guidance and his sunnah for a way, until the Day of Judgement. Peace be upon you, and the mercy of God and His blessings.

The author (may God have mercy on him) says: "Chapter on the rāʾs." He set up this chapter for an accidental quality, namely the thinning of the sound that characterises the rāʾ. It has already been established that thickening is a quality of all the elevated letters and that thinning is a quality of all the lowered letters, and that thickening occurs accidentally in three of the lowered letters, namely the rāʾ, the lām and the alif. These three letters are lowered, and yet thickening occurs in them accidentally. Since this thickening was an accidental quality, we did not mention it [earlier]. The author (may God, be He exalted, have mercy on him) mentioned what pertains to the rāʾs, then mentioned what pertains to the lāms and the alifs that go with them; and he began with the rāʾs, saying:

title_ar: شرح الجزرية الشريط السادس
title_en: Commentary on al-Jazariyyah — Tape Six
body_ar:
عرف التجويد تعريفا قاصرا فقال:

وهو إعطاء الحروف حقها** من صفة لها ومستحقها

قال إن التجويد هو في الاصطلاح إعطاء الحروف حقها وحق الحروف هو صفاتها اللازمة صفاتها الأصلية وهي هذه الصفات الثماني عشرة فهذا حق الحروف، ومستحقها في الاصطلاح هو الصفات العارضة، الصفات العارضة التي ذكرنا بعضها ولم نحط بها، كالغنة وكالترقيق والتفخيم وغير ذلك فهذه الصفات تسمى الصفات العارضة، فهذا اصطلاح، وإلا فلا فرق في اللغة بين الحق والمستحق، لأن الحق مستحق يستحقه صاحبه، قال:

وهو إعطاء الحروف حقها** من صفة لها ومستحقها
body_en:
He defined the rules of Qur'anic recitation (tajwīd) with a definition that falls short, saying:

*And it is the giving to the letters of their due, of the quality belonging to them, and of what they merit.*

He said that tajwid, in technical usage, is the giving to the letters of their due; and the due of the letters is their necessary qualities, their original qualities, which are these eighteen qualities — this is the letters' due. And "what they merit", in technical usage, is the accidental qualities: the accidental qualities, some of which we have mentioned without covering them exhaustively, such as nasalisation, thinning, thickening and so on. These qualities are called the accidental qualities. So this is a technical usage; otherwise there is no difference in the language between "a due" and "what is merited", because a due is something merited, which the one entitled to it merits. He said:

*And it is the giving to the letters of their due, of the quality belonging to them, and of what they merit.*

flags.context: The opening clause of the record, introducing Ibn al-Jazari's definition of tajwid.
options: a definition that falls short
an incomplete definition
a non-exhaustive definition
flags.note: qāṣir here is the Sheikh's own critical judgement on the author's definition — that it does not take in everything it should. It is not a neutral description, and it must not be softened into a compliment or strengthened into a charge of error. The technical sense in logic (a definition that is not co-extensive with what it defines) may be what is meant; a reviewer should confirm which.

translator_notes: The CMS does not expose a category or section for this record on the article view, and the 2010 archive is not reachable through the site's section listings. section/category_ar/category_en are therefore left null rather than inferred.

The published page carries only the opening excerpt of this tape; the Arabic breaks off and the full text is offered on the site as a downloadable Word document. The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends. Nothing has been supplied to complete it.
This record begins mid-discussion, with no opening formula; the beginning of the tape is not in the source.

The line of verse is the base text of al-Jazariyyah, quoted twice by the Sheikh — once before his comment and once after it. It is rendered as prose in italics per house style, and the repetition has been kept.
The double asterisk ** in the Arabic is the source's hemistich divider, not an editorial mark.

'Their due' (ḥaqquhā) and 'what they merit' (mustaḥaqquhā) are the technical terms the whole passage turns on; they have been rendered consistently and the Arabic distinction is explained by the Sheikh himself.

al-Jazariyyah is the versified primer on Qur'anic recitation by Ibn al-Jazari, and 'the author' throughout this series is Ibn al-Jazari. The series title is left transliterated and untranslated. Articles 436-446 are tapes of this one series; their tape numbering in the titles does not run in the same order as the article IDs.

title_ar: مواضيع فكرية متنوعة
title_en: Various Intellectual Topics
body_ar:
من أحكام تسيير الكفالات المدرسية

هناك ما يسمى بالكفالة المدرسية من قبل دولة أجنبية ويسيرها موظف للدولة بدون مقابل، فهل باستطاعة هذا المسير أن يأكل من هذه الكفالة وأن يأخذ ما تبقى منها بعد تسييرها كما ينبغي علما بأنه إذا أعاده للجهة التي جاء منها فسيستعمله أولئك الأشخاص؟

لا، عليه أن ينفقه على الطلاب فإن استغنوا وبقيت بقية فلينفقها على فقراء المكان الذي هم فيه، ولا يحل له أن يأخذ هو شيئا منها.
body_en:
On the Rulings Governing the Administration of School Sponsorship Funds

Question: There is what is called school sponsorship, provided by a foreign state and administered by a state employee without remuneration. Is it open to this administrator to eat from this sponsorship fund, and to take what remains of it after he has administered it as he should — bearing in mind that if he returns it to the body it came from, those persons will use it themselves?

Answer: No. He must spend it on the students; and if they have no further need of it and a remainder is left over, let him spend it on the poor of the place where they are. It is not lawful for him to take anything of it for himself.

flags.context: هناك ما يسمى بالكفالة المدرسية من قبل دولة أجنبية ويسيرها موظف للدولة بدون مقابل
options: school sponsorship fund
school bursary scheme
educational sponsorship grant
flags.note: The question describes money provided by a foreign state for schoolchildren and administered locally by an unpaid official. Whether it is a per-child sponsorship, a block grant to a school, or a bursary is not stated, and the Mauritanian arrangement the questioner has in mind should be confirmed before the rendering is fixed.

flags.arabic: ولا يحل له أن يأخذ هو شيئا منها
flags.context: The closing clause of the answer.
options: it is not lawful for him to take anything of it for himself
it is forbidden (ḥarām) for him to take anything of it
he may not take anything of it
flags.note: The Sheikh says lā yaḥillu lahu, 'it is not lawful for him', rather than using the word ḥarām. The rendering keeps his wording. A reviewer should confirm whether the English should carry the explicit term 'forbidden (ḥarām)', which the Sheikh did not himself use here.

translator_notes: The CMS does not expose a category or section for this record on the article view, and the 2010 archive is not reachable through the site's section listings. section/category_ar/category_en are therefore left null rather than inferred.

The record's title is plural ('Various Intellectual Topics') and the page offers a downloadable Word document, but only one question and answer appear on the page. The one fatwa present is complete in itself — the question is stated and the Sheikh gives his ruling — and the English is complete for it. The page nonetheless appears to be a single item drawn from a larger collection, so it has been marked as an excerpt of its source document.
The Sheikh answers the question as asked and in his own voice; he reports no other school's position here and leaves nothing open.

The questioner's final clause — that the money would be used by 'those persons' if returned — is a consideration the questioner raises, not one the Sheikh endorses. He does not respond to it, and nothing has been added on his behalf.

title_ar: فضيلة الشيخ الددو يحاضر في تظاهرة حاشدة لجمعية الشبيبة
title_en: His Eminence Sheikh al-Dedew Lectures at a Packed Event Held by the Youth Association
body_ar:
ألقى فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو ليلة البارحة 8 ديسمبر 2010 محاضرة بعنوان: "الرسالة الدعوية للجمعيات الشبابية "التي نظمتها جمعية شبيبة بناء الوطن بساحة فضاء التنوع الثقافي والبيئي بانواكشوط. وكانت التظاهرة حاشدة بجموع غفيرة من جماهير الجمعية وروادها تزاحموا لاستقبال الشيخ والسلام عليه،

وقد ركز فضيلته في المحاضرة على ضرورة سلامة الفكرة وتأسيسها على الأهداف والوسائل الشرعية كبدائل إسلامية في مجال الترفيه، منتقدا من يظنون الترفيه مخالفا للإسلام، حيث قال "إن الجمعيات ينبغي أن تؤسس على أساس راشد لتساهم في خدمة الأوطان الإسلامية... وإن الجهد الجماعي الذي تقدمه الجمعيات والنوادي في البلدان الإسلامية مطلوب شرعا، لأن عمل الكافة لا ينهض إلا بعمل الكافة".

كما ركز الشيخ على أهمية دعوة الشباب الذين قال إنهم عرضة للتشدد والتطرف، كما أنهم عرضة للانحلال والتفريط في الدين.

وقد استعرض الشيخ ذلك من خلال نماذج من حياة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مع صحابته؛ حينما بات (ص) ليلة مع صحابته رضوان الله عليهم يستمع للمنشد الذي قال له النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم "رفقا بالقوارير"، يقصد قلوب النساء.

وعزز الشيخ الحديث في الموضوع باستشهادات أخرى من حياة الصحابة مع النبي (ص).

كما وجه فضيلته إلى ضرورة جمع جهود هذه الجمعيات الصغيرة في جمعية واحدة كبيرة؛ لتكون أكبر قيمة وأكثر نتاجا.

وتحدث في ذات التظاهرة الشيخ عبد الرحمن ولد فتى الذي أجاد في الحديث عن دور الشباب والأخلاق، والحث على تحمل الأمانة والتحلي بالأخلاق الحميدة.

وكانت الكلمة المؤثرة عند عضو مجلس الشيوخ عمر الفتح؛ الذي دعا الجمعيات الإسلامية إلى الاعتناء بالجماليات في خطابها اتجاه الجماهير، كل حسب ذوقه واهتماماته.
body_en:
Last night, 8 December 2010, his eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew delivered a lecture entitled "The Mission of Calling to Islam Belonging to Youth Associations", which was organised by the Shabibat Bina' al-Watan Association at the square of the Cultural and Environmental Diversity Space in Nouakchott. The event was packed with great throngs of the association's members and regular attenders, who pressed forward to receive the Sheikh and to greet him.

In the lecture his eminence concentrated on the necessity that the idea be sound and be founded on aims and means that accord with the Sharia, as Islamic alternatives in the field of recreation, criticising those who suppose recreation to be contrary to Islam. He said: "Associations ought to be founded on a rightly guided basis, so that they may contribute to the service of the Muslim homelands… And the collective effort that associations and clubs offer in Muslim countries is called for by the Sharia, because what is the work of all can only be carried through by the work of all."

The Sheikh also concentrated on the importance of calling young people to Islam, of whom he said that they are exposed to harshness and extremism, just as they are exposed to moral dissolution and to falling short in religion.

The Sheikh surveyed this through examples from the life of the Prophet (may God bless him and grant him peace) with his Companions — as when he (peace and blessings be upon him) passed a night with his Companions (may God be pleased with them) listening to the chanter, to whom the Prophet (may God bless him and grant him peace) said, "Gently with the glass vessels", meaning the hearts of the women.

The Sheikh strengthened his treatment of the subject with further citations from the life of the Companions with the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him).

His eminence also urged the necessity of gathering the efforts of these small associations into a single large association, so that it may be of greater worth and more productive.

Speaking at the same event was Sheikh Abd al-Rahman Ould Fatta, who spoke ably of the role of young people and of character, and of the call to bear the trust and to adorn oneself with praiseworthy character.

The moving address was that of the senator Umar al-Fath, who called on the Islamic associations to attend to the aesthetic dimension of their discourse towards the public, each according to his own taste and interests.

flags.context: حينما بات (ص) ليلة مع صحابته ... يستمع للمنشد الذي قال له النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم “رفقا بالقوارير”، يقصد قلوب النساء
options: Render the gloss as the source gives it: 'meaning the hearts of the women'
Render as 'meaning the women', the usual understanding
Render the source's gloss and add a note on the usual understanding
flags.note: The gloss 'the hearts of the women' is the site report's, not necessarily the Sheikh's own words. In the standard understanding of this hadith, al-qawārīr — glass vessels — are the women themselves, likened to glass for their delicacy, not their hearts specifically. The source's gloss has been rendered as given rather than corrected, per house rule 11. Note also that the report has the Prophet listening to a chanter through the night, whereas the well-known setting of the hadith is a journey, with Anjashah driving the mounts that carried the women. The report should be checked against the lecture before publication.

flags.context: وإن الجهد الجماعي الذي تقدمه الجمعيات والنوادي في البلدان الإسلامية مطلوب شرعا
options: is called for by the Sharia
is demanded in the Sharia
is obligatory (wājib) in the Sharia
flags.note: maṭlūb sharʿan states that the Sharia calls for something without saying at which of the five rulings — obligatory or recommended — it falls. The neutral rendering has been used deliberately so that no ruling is attributed to the Sheikh that he did not give. The following clause about 'the work of all' echoes the language of a communal obligation (farḍ kifāyah), but he does not use that term and it has not been supplied.

flags.arabic: جمعية شبيبة بناء الوطن / فضاء التنوع الثقافي والبيئي
flags.context: التي نظمتها جمعية شبيبة بناء الوطن بساحة فضاء التنوع الثقافي والبيئي بانواكشوط
options: Transliterate the association's name and translate the venue, as done here
Translate both: 'the Youth for Building the Nation Association' at 'the Cultural and Environmental Diversity Space'
Transliterate both
flags.note: Both are Mauritanian proper names with no established English form. The association's own English name, if it has one, should be used; the Sheikh's office can confirm.

translator_notes: The CMS does not expose a category or section for this record on the article view, and the 2010 archive is not reachable through the site's section listings. section/category_ar/category_en are therefore left null rather than inferred.

A site news item reporting a lecture, not a text by the Sheikh. The passages in quotation marks are the report's quotation of his words; the rest is the reporter's summary. The distinction is load-bearing and has been preserved — the summarised parts must not be presented as the Sheikh's own wording.
The Sheikh is reported as criticising those who hold recreation to be contrary to Islam. No ruling of his on recreation is stated in this report, and none has been supplied.
The lecture's own title, the Arabic al-risālah al-daʿawiyyah, is rendered 'the mission of calling to Islam' in keeping with the glossary rendering of daʿwah.

title_ar: أجوبة في السيرة النبوية
title_en: Answers on the Prophetic Biography
body_ar:
من سيرة عيسى عليه السلام
هل عيسى عليه السلام خاض حربا حتى احتاج إلى دعوة الأنصار في سبيل دعوته؟
أن الحرب ليس المقصود بها المواجهة بالسلاح بل الحرب تأتي بكل الوسائل المعروفة فيها
وما الحرب إلا ما علمتم وذقتمُ** وما هو عنها بالحديث المرجم
فالحرب تأتي بالكلام والدعايات وبالمؤامرات وعيسى عليه السلام تعرض لكثير من هذه المؤامرات وتعرض مرات لمحاولة القتل والصلب، وتعرض أيضا لحروب كلامية كثيرة، وكذلك الذين عاصروه من الأنبياء، فمن هؤلاء زكرياء وقد قتل في سبيل الله، وكذلك ابن خالته يحيى وقد قتل في سبيل الله، والحواريون الذين نصروا عيسى قتل كثير منهم في سبيل الله، وعيسى رفعه الله تعالى إليه وقد حاول اليهود قتله وصلبه وشبهه الله تعالى لهم فظنوا أنهم قتلوه وصلبوه، والواقع أنهم ما قتلوه وما صلبوه ولكن شبه لهم.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ترجمة ابن تيمية
من هو ابن تيمية وهل هو شيخ نجد؟
أن ابن تيمية رجل من المسلمين من أهل الشام ليس من أهل نجد، ولد بالشام في القرن السابع الهجري وعاش فيه وتعلم واشتهر من بين أقرانه بجودة قريحته وذكائه في صباه، حتى اشتهر بذلك فكان أهل الحديث إذا أتوا دمشق أتوه فكتبوا له لوحا من الحديث فيه ستة عشر حديثا فيحفظه بالنظرة الواحدة، واشتهر بذلك في صباه فأوصى أحد علماء الحديث الكبار والده أن لا يشغله بالدنيا وأن يخصصه للعلم لعل الله ينفع به أمة محمد (ص)، فقال له أبوه إني سأتولى عنك أمور الدنيا فاشتغل أنت بأمور الدين وفرده للتعلم، فدرس في دمشق وغيرها وخاض كثيرا من بلاد الله وتعلم حتى حفظ ما يقرب من مليون حديث عن رسول الله (ص)، وقرأ بالقراءات العشر، وتعلم الفقه على مذهب الحنابلة ثم تعلم فقه المذاهب الأخرى وكان من علماء هذه الأمة، غير المعصومين الذين يخطئون ويصيبون له أخطاء مثل غيره من العلماء وصوابه أكثر من خطئه، وقد قال تلميذه ابن القيم رحمه الله إن زلات العلماء أقذار والعلماء بحار والماء إذا بلغ القلتين لم يحمل الخبث.
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
الكلام على غار ثور هل أسماء بنت أبي بكر كانت تحمل الطعام إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وأبي بكر رضي الله عنه في الغار؟
نعم كانت تحمل الطعام إليهما في الغار، وقد ذكرنا أن غار ثور كان في مكان مرتفع جدا، ونحن الآن بعد مرور الزمن الطويل وعوامل النحت والتعرية وبعد حصول مشي الناس ووضعهم للحجارة وصفها في كثير من المناطق في الجبل نصعد إلى الغار لساعتين ونصف، وهي كانت تأتي في الليل وليس لها نبراس ولا ضوء وتصعد على الأقدام.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
اسم الصحابي الذي أرسل إلى مسيلمة الكذاب
ما اسم الصحابي الذي أرسل إلى مسيلمة الكذاب وما اسم والدته وهو الذي قام بتقطيعه إربا إربا؟
أنه حبيب بن زيد وأن أمه هي نَسِيبَةُ رضي الله عنها، وهو الذي أرسله رسول الله (ص) إلى مسيلمة فكان إذا سأله هل تشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وأن محمدا رسول الله يقول: نعم، فإذا قال: أتشهد أني رسول الله؟ قال: إني أصم لا أسمع.
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
خلافة أبي بكر الصديق
ما هي أنواع الخلافات التي تولاها أبو بكر الصديق؟
لا أفهم هذا السؤال إذا كان المعنى خلافته لرسول الله (ص) فإنه تولى خلافة النبي (ص) في الأمر العام الذي هو القيادة العظمى لهذه الأمة وهو إقامة الدين وسياسة الدنيا به، وكذلك القيام بإمامة الناس في الصلاة وخطابتهم في الجمعة والقضاء بينهم وقيادة جيوشهم ونحو ذلك فهذه هي وظائف رسول الله (ص).
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
تولي أبو بكر الخلافة.
متى تولى أبو بكر الصديق الخلافة؟
أنه تولاها عند موت رسول الله (ص) فقد توفي رسول الله (ص) ضحوة الإثنين ودفن ضحوة الأربعاء وقيل مساء الثلاثاء بعد أن صلى عليه المسلمون ولم يبايع المسلمون إذ ذاك أحدا فلما كان يوم الأربعاء بعد صلاة العصر اجتمع الأنصار في سقيفة بني ساعدة يذكرون خلافة رسول الله (ص) ومن عسى أن يقوم مقامه، وخرج إليهم أبو بكر الصديق وعمر الخطاب وأبو عبيدة بن الجراح من المهاجرين فكانت بيعة أبي بكر في سقيفة بني ساعدة، ثم لما كانت بكرة الخميس بايع الناس أبا بكر على المنبر فكانت البيعة العامة وهي بيعة المسجد فبايع الناس جميعا أبا بكر إلا عددا يسيرا من الصحابة تخلفوا فمنهم من مكث ستة أشهر كعلي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه فقد مكث ستة أشهر لم يبايع ولم يخرج من بيته إلا إلى الصلاة ثم يرجع، وكان في تلك الأشهر يقوم على تمريض فاطمة بنت رسول الله (ص) فلما توفاها الله طلب بيعة أبي بكر فجلس أبو بكر على المنبر فأتاه علي رضي الله عنه فبايعه أمام الناس بمحضر منهم.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
body_en:
From the life of Jesus (peace be upon him)

Question: Did Jesus (peace be upon him) wage war, such that he had need to call for helpers (anṣār) in the cause of his mission?

Answer: That war is not meant here as confrontation by arms; rather, war comes by every means known to belong to it.

*War is nothing but what you have known and tasted, and it is no matter of conjectural talk.*

War comes through speech, through propaganda and through conspiracies. Jesus (peace be upon him) was subjected to many such conspiracies, and was several times subjected to attempts at killing and crucifixion; he was also subjected to many wars of words. So too were the prophets who were his contemporaries: among them Zechariah, who was killed in the path of God, and likewise his maternal aunt's son John, who was killed in the path of God; and of the disciples who supported Jesus, many were killed in the path of God. As for Jesus, God Most High raised him to Himself: the Jews attempted to kill him and to crucify him, and God Most High made a likeness of him appear to them, so that they supposed they had killed him and crucified him, whereas in reality they neither killed him nor crucified him — but it was made to appear so to them.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

A biographical notice on Ibn Taymiyyah

Question: Who is Ibn Taymiyyah, and is he the Shaykh of Najd?

Answer: That Ibn Taymiyyah was a man among the Muslims, of the people of Syria (al-Sham), not of the people of Najd. He was born in Syria in the seventh Hijri century and lived there, and he studied and became known among his peers for the excellence of his natural gift and for his intelligence in his boyhood, until he became famous for it, so that when the hadith scholars came to Damascus they would come to him and write out for him a tablet of hadith containing sixteen hadiths, and he would memorise it at a single glance. He became known for that in his boyhood, so that one of the great hadith scholars counselled his father not to occupy him with worldly affairs but to devote him to knowledge, in the hope that God might benefit the community (ummah) of Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him) through him. His father said to him: "I shall take charge of your worldly affairs on your behalf, so occupy yourself with the affairs of religion," and he set him apart for learning. So he studied in Damascus and elsewhere, and travelled through many of God's lands, and he learned until he had memorised close to a million hadiths from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him). He recited the Qur'an according to the ten canonical readings (qirāʾāt), and learned jurisprudence according to the school of the Hanbalis, then learned the jurisprudence of the other schools. He was one of the scholars of this community — who are not infallible, who err and who are right. He had errors, as other scholars do, and what he got right was more than what he got wrong. His student Ibn al-Qayyim (may God have mercy on him) said: the slips of the scholars are filth, and the scholars are seas, and water, when it reaches the two-qullah measure (qullatayn), does not carry impurity.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Discussion of the Cave of Thawr. Did Asma' bint Abi Bakr carry food to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) and to Abu Bakr (may God be pleased with him) in the cave?

Answer: Yes, she used to carry food to them both in the cave. We have mentioned that the Cave of Thawr was in a very elevated place; and now, after the passage of long ages, and the agents of weathering and erosion, and after people have walked there and have laid and arranged stones over many stretches of the mountain, we climb up to the cave in two and a half hours — while she used to come by night, with neither lamp nor light, and would climb up on foot.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The name of the Companion who was sent to Musaylimah the Liar

Question: What is the name of the Companion who was sent to Musaylimah the Liar, and what is his mother's name — he being the one whom Musaylimah cut to pieces limb by limb?

Answer: That he is Habib ibn Zayd, and that his mother is Nasibah (may God be pleased with her). He is the one whom the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) sent to Musaylimah. Whenever Musaylimah asked him, "Do you bear witness that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God?" he would say, "Yes." And when he said, "Do you bear witness that I am the Messenger of God?" he said, "I am deaf, I do not hear."

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The caliphate of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq

Question: What are the kinds of succession (khilāfah) that Abu Bakr al-Siddiq assumed?

Answer: I do not understand this question. If what is meant is his succeeding the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), then he assumed the succession to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) in the general office, which is the supreme leadership of this community — namely, establishing the religion and governing worldly affairs by it — and likewise leading the people in prayer, addressing them at the Friday prayer, judging between them, commanding their armies and the like. These are the offices of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him).

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Abu Bakr's assumption of the caliphate.

Question: When did Abu Bakr al-Siddiq assume the caliphate?

Answer: That he assumed it at the death of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him). The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) died in the forenoon of Monday and was buried in the forenoon of Wednesday — and it is said, on the evening of Tuesday — after the Muslims had prayed over him. At that time the Muslims had not pledged allegiance to anyone. Then, when it was Wednesday, after the afternoon prayer, the Ansar gathered in the portico of the Banu Sa'idah, discussing the succession to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) and who might stand in his place. Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, Umar al-Khattab and Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah went out to them from among the Emigrants, and so the pledge of allegiance to Abu Bakr took place in the portico of the Banu Sa'idah. Then, when it was the morning of Thursday, the people pledged allegiance to Abu Bakr upon the pulpit, and this was the general pledge, which is the pledge of the mosque. All the people pledged allegiance to Abu Bakr except a small number of the Companions, who held back. Among them were some who waited six months, such as Ali ibn Abi Talib (may God be pleased with him): he waited six months and did not pledge allegiance, and did not leave his house except for the prayer and then return. During those months he was nursing Fatimah, the daughter of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him); and when God took her, he sought to pledge allegiance to Abu Bakr. So Abu Bakr sat upon the pulpit, and Ali (may God be pleased with him) came to him and pledged allegiance to him before the people, in their presence.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
