flags.context: On the destruction of the people of Salih by the Cry.
options: so it split the membranes of their hearts (reading أشغفة as a plural of shighāf/shaghāf, the pericardium)
so it split their hearts
flags.note: أشغفة is not a standard plural of شغاف. The sense intended is plainly the pericardium, and the English follows that; the unusual form is preserved in body_ar and may be a transcription of the Sheikh's spoken Mauritanian usage.

flags.arabic: إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء
flags.context: The Sheikh's reading of Q 35:28.
options: Keep both of his denials intact, as done here
Compress to the general point
flags.note: Care point rather than a doubt. The Sheikh explicitly denies two inferences from this verse — that every person of reverent fear is a scholar, and that every scholar is a person of reverent fear — and affirms only that true reverent fear arises from knowledge of God. Both denials must survive in English, since dropping either turns the passage into a claim about the merit of scholars that he is at pains not to make.

translator_notes: Qur'anic renderings here are interpretive and are not a substitute for the Arabic.
khashyah is rendered throughout as 'reverent fear', reserving 'fear' alone for khawf, which the Sheikh uses alongside it and distinguishes from it by degree.

This is a lecture in spiritual cultivation, not a legal text. The one legal term in it, mubāḥ ('permissible'), occurs in al-Ghazali's dictum about a person acting in ignorance of the law and carries its ordinary legal sense there.

title_ar: وسائل الاستقامة والثبات على الدين
title_en: The Means of Uprightness and Steadfastness in Religion
body_ar: إن الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينه ، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا ومن سيئات أعمالنا من يهده الله فلا مضل له ومن يضلل فلا هادي له ، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له وأشهد أن محمدا عبده ورسوله صلى الله عليه وعلى آله وأصحابه وسلم تسليما كثيرا (يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اتَّقُوا رَبَّكُمُ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ مِنْ نَفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ وَخَلَقَ مِنْهَا زَوْجَهَا وَبَثَّ مِنْهُمَا رِجَالًا كَثِيرًا وَنِسَاءً وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ الَّذِي تَسَاءَلُونَ بِهِ وَالْأَرْحَامَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَلَيْكُمْ رَقِيبًا) (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آَمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَقُولُوا قَوْلًا سَدِيدًا (70) يُصْلِحْ لَكُمْ أَعْمَالَكُمْ وَيَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ ذُنُوبَكُمْ وَمَنْ يُطِعِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ فَقَدْ فَازَ فَوْزًا عَظِيمًا) أما بعد، فإن خير الحديث كتاب الله وخير الهدي هدي محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وشر الأمور محدثاتها وكل بدعة ضلالة ، عباد الله إن الله سبحانه وتعالى يهدي من يشاء إلى صراطه المستقيم ، ويثبت من أراد ثباته على ذلك الصراط ، ويمتحن الناس ويبتليهم عليه ، ومن أراد الله ثباته فإنه سيثبت وقد أمر الله سبحانه وتعالى بالأخذ بالأسباب في كل الأمور ومن ذلك أسباب الهداية والاستقامة ، فمن أسباب الهداية تعلم ما أمر الله به والعمل بما جاء به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم والاقتداء بالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في الأقوال والأعمال والاعتقادات والنيات ، ومن أسباب الهداية كذلك الضراعة إلى الله سبحانه وتعالى بسؤال الهداية ومن أسباب الهداية التدبر والتذكر ، ثم بعد ذلك أسباب الثبات على دين الله وهي أعظم وأولى باشتغال المسلم بها ، فمن أعظمها أن يتذكر المسلم أنه في هذه الحياة في سنة التدافع وفي جدلية لا بد فيها من الحسم ، وهذه الجدلية هي الاستقامة على طريق الهداية إلى الموت أو الرجوع والإنقلاب على عقبيه ، فالناس قسمان إما أن يكون الإنسان من الأتقياء وإما أن يكون من الأشقياء ، فالأتقياء هم السعداء الذين يثبتهم الله بالقول الثابت في الحياة الدنيا وفي الآخرة ، وإذا عرف الإنسان هذه الجدلية وعرف انقسام الناس إلى القسمين ، وعرف أن ذلك لا يكون بنسب ولا حسب وإنما يكون بأخذ الأسباب وباختيار الملك الديان سبحانه وتعالى حرص على أن لا يكون من الأشقياء وعلى أن يكون من أهل الهداية وأن يلزم ذلك طيلة حياته ، ثم من أسباب الاستقامة و الثبات كذلك أن يعلم الإنسان طول هذا الطريق وما عليه من المشاق ، فإن كثيرا من الناس يرجعون عند أول نكبة ويتراجعون عن طريق الاستقامة والهداية ولا يصمدون عليه ولا يثبتون لأنهم يجهلون ما عليه من النكبات والعقبات وأنتم عباد الله على صراط دنيوي هو تمثيل للصراط الأخروي وتعرفون أن الصراط الأخروي عليه كلاليب كشوك السعدان ، يتفاوت الناس عليه بحسب أعمالهم ، فكذلك هذا الصراط الدنيوي المحجة البيضاء عليه كلاليب تمسك بالناس ، فمن لم يثبت عليه فإنه سينصرف على عقبيه ، وقد قال الله تعالى: (ومن الناس من يعبد الله على حرف فإن أصابه خير اطمأن به وإن أصابته فتنة انقلب على وجهه خسر الدنيا والآخرة ذلك هو الخسران المبين) كذلك من وسائل الثبات على هذا الدين عدم الاستعجال في أن ينال الإنسان الثواب في هذه الحياة ، فثواب الله سبحانه و تعالى هو ما أعده لأوليائه في دار النعيم المقيم ، إن ذلك الثواب هو تقريب الله عز وجل لأوليائه واصطفاؤه لهم ، إذا بيض الله وجوههم وآتاهم كتبهم بأيمانهم وجعلهم في الزمرة الأولى وقربهم في الفردوس الأعلى من الجنة وأظلهم بظل عرشه يوم لا ظل إلا ظله فإنه قد اختارهم لذلك فلذلك لا بد أن يحرص الإنسان على الثواب الأخروي ، وأن يعلم أن ما يعجل له في هذه الحياة إنما هو نقص من أجره ، فقد صح عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: \"ما من سرية تخرج في سبيل الله فتغنم إلا عجل لها ثلثا أجرها وما من سرية تخرج في سبيل الله فتخفق إلا نالت أجرها كاملا\" فلذلك لا بد أن نحرص عباد الله على أن تكون الآخرة جل اهتمامنا وأن نحرص على الثواب الأخروي وأن لا نحرص على تعجل شيء من ثوابنا في هذه الحياة ، ثم اعلموا رحمني الله وإياكم أن الذين يعجل لهم شيء في هذه الحياة حتى لو كانوا من خيرة أولياء الله فإنهم دائما يبقون على حذر وخوف ، ولذلك أخرج البخاري ومسلم في الصحيحين عن عبد الرحمن بن عوف رضي الله عنه أنه كان صائما فوضعت المائدة بين يديه فإذا فيها ألوانا من الطعام فبكى بكاء شديدا حتى أبكى من حوله ، فقالوا يا أبا المنذر وما يبكيك قال إنا كنا أهل جاهلية وشر فأرسل الله إلينا رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم فآمنا وصدقنا واتبعنا فمنا من مات ولم يتعجل شيئا من أجره ، منهم أخي مصعب بن عمير قتل يوم أحد وليس له إلا سيفه وبردة عليه إن نحن غطينا بها رأسه بدت رجلاه وإن نحن غطينا رجليه بدا رأسه فأمرنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن نغطي رأسه وأن نجعل على رجليه من الإذخر فمات ولم يتعجل شيئا من أجره وبقينا وراءهم ففتحت علينا الدنيا أبوابها فنحن نهدبها فخشينا أن يقال لنا يوم القيامة: (أذهبتم طيباتكم في حياتكم الدنيا واستمتعتم بها فاليوم تجزون عذاب الهون بما كنتم تستكبرون في الأرض بغير الحق وبما كنتم تفسقون) وقد صح نظير هذا عن خباب بن الأرت رضي الله عنه وقد ثبت أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم خرج من بيته لا يخرجه إلا الجوع فلقي أبا بكر وعمر فقال ما أخرجكما من بيوتكما قالا الجوع أخرجنا ، قال وأنا ما أخرجني إلا الجوع ، فذهبوا إلى أبي الهيثم بن التيهان فضيفهما فلما أخذ مديته يريد أن يذبح شاة نهاه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن ذوات الدر أي الحلوب فلما وضع بين أيديهما عذقا من التمر ولحما وماء باردا نظر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى ذلك وقال: إن هذا من النعيم الذي تسألون عنه (ثم لتسألن يومئذ عن النعيم) إن علينا عباد الله أن نحذر أن نكون من الذين تعجل لهم أجورهم في هذه الحياة فيجنونها في أمور منقطعة لا فائدة فيها ، وإن أولئك لا يساوون عند الله شيئا فقيمتهم هي ما يعجله الله لهم من أمور هذه الدنيا الفانية ، ثم اعلموا رحمني الله وإياكم أن من وسائل الاستقامة والثبات على الدين أن نتذكر أن الاستعجال كذلك في تحصيل أمور هذه الدنيا عيب وضرر فقد أخرج البخاري في الصحيح من حديث خباب بن الأرت رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان متوسدا بردة له في ظل الكعبة قال خباب فأتيته فقلت يا رسول الله ألا تستنصر لنا ألا تدعو لنا ، فقال: إنه قد كان فيمن قبلكم يؤتى بالرجل فيوضع المنشار على مفرقه فيفرق به فرقتين ثم يؤتى بأمشاط الحديد فيمشط بها ما دون عظمه من جلد ولحم لا يصده ذلك عن دينه و والذي نفس محمد بيده ليتمن الله هذا الأمر حتى يسير الراكب من صنعاء إلى حضرموت لا يخاف إلا الله والذئب على غنمه ولكنكم قوم تستعجلون\" فحذر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم تحذيرا بليغا من هذا الاستعجال وبين ضرره وخطره وبين أن المستقبل لهذا الدين لا محالة وأن الله سينصره ويعزه بعز عزيز أو بذل ذليل ، لكن من فاته ذلك الفتح فهو خير له فالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم آتاه الله كنوز كسرى وقيصر ولكنه توفاه الله قبل أن ينال شيئا من ذلك ، فتحت على أصحابه من بعده فأنفقوها في سبيل الله ، وهذا دليل على أن من فاته الفتح فهو خير له ، والذين ماتوا قبل الفتح هم الذين صدقوا ما عاهدوا الله عليه ، فالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قبل موته بثمانية أيام وقف على شهداء أحد فقال: \"إني شهيد على هؤلاء بأن صدقوا الله ما عاهدوه عليه\" وأنتم تعلمون أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم توفاه الله ولم يشبع ثلاثة أيام متواليات ويمضي ثلاثة أشهر ما يرى في بيوته نار ، وقد كان ينام على الحصير فيؤثر في جنبه بأبي هو وأمي صلى الله عليه وسلم ثم اعلموا رحمني الله وإياكم أن من وسائل الثبات على هذا الطريق الشاق أن يتذكر الإنسان قصص السالفين السابقين الذين سلكوا الطريق من قبله وما لقوه من الأذى في سبيل الله فلنتذكر إخواني ما كان الناس يسخرون به من نوح عليه السلام ، ولنتذكر تمالُؤ الأقربين على إبراهيم حين رموه في النار ولنتذكر إخراجهم له من مدينتهم ولنتذكر كذلك ما لقي لوط من قومه ولنتذكر ما لقي النبيون من بعد ذلك إلى نبينا محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم من الأذى في سبيل الله وما لقيه أصحابه من الأذى ، فإن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان ساجدا لربه عند الركن اليماني فجاء عقبة بن أبي معيط فوضع رجله على قذال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أي مؤخرة رأسه وكان عقبة ثقيلا سمينا فما زال يدعه برجله حتى أمر من أتاه بسلا ناقة ولدت فوضعه بين كتفيه وهو ساجد لربه ، وكذلك فإن نوفلا قرن أبا بكر وطلحة بن عبيد الله بنسع وضربهما على خديهما ضربا شديدا حتى أدما خديهما ، وكذلك فإن عددا من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أوذوا أذى شديدا بالإضافة إلى ما لقوا من الضغوط الأخرى ، فهذا سعد بن أبي وقاص عندما أسلم وأشهر إسلامه أضربت أمه عن الطعام ، فأقسمت أن لا تأكل وأن لا تشرب حتى يرجع عن دينه ، فلما خشي عليها الموت همس في أذنها فقال يا أماه لو كان لك مائة نفس فخرجت نفسا تلو أخرى على أن أرجع عن ديني ما رجعت عنه ، فاحيي أو فموتي... فلذلك لا بد أن نعلم أننا ممتحنون بهذا الدين وأننا محتاجون إلى الثبات عليه ، محتاجون إلى أن نعلم أن من لم يثبت على دينه لا يضر إلا نفسه ولا يضر الله ودينه شيئا وأن هذا الدين مستمر إلى أن يرث الله الأرض ومن عليها ثم اعلموا رحمني الله وإياكم كذلك أن الذي يتذكر قصص الماضين وما هم عليه فإنه سيتوقع دائما أن ينال بعض ما نالهم بحسب درجته في الإيمان والتقوى ، فأنتم تسلكون طريقا سلكه أولئك الرائدون السابقون ولستم أكرم على الله منهم فما لقوه لا بد أن تنالوا حظكم منه يقول الله تعالى: (بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم ألم أحسب الناس أن يتركوا أن يقولوا آمنا وهم لا يفتنون ولقد فتنا الذين من قبلهم فليعلمن الله الذين صدقوا وليعلمن الكاذبين) بارك الله لي ولكم في القرآن العظيم ونفعني وإياكم بما فيه من الآيات والذكر الحكيم وتاب علي وعليكم إنه هو التواب الرحيم. الحمد لله على إحسانه والشكر له على تفضله وامتنانه وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له تعظيما لشانه وأشهد أن محمدا عبده ورسوله الداعي إلى رضوانه صلى الله عليه وعلى آله وأصحابه وأزواجه وذريته وإخوانه. عباد الله إن من وسائل الثبات على دين الله أن يقرأ الإنسان قصص الأنبياء في القرآن فقد صح عن عبد الله بن المبارك رضي الله عنه أنه قال: قصص الصالحين جند من جنود الله يثبت الله بها قلوب عباده ، ومصداق ذلك من القرآن قول الله تعالى: (وكلا نقص عليك من أنباء الرسل ما نثبت به فؤادك وجاءك في هذه الحق وموعظة وذكرى للمؤمنين) فعلينا عباد الله أن نتذكر ما كانوا فيه وما أوذوا به في سبيل الله وأن نعلم أن الطريق طويل وأن أمامنا أكثر مما لقينا وأن الطريق قد بقي منه أكثر مما مضى ، فلذلك اعلموا رحمني الله وإياكم أن عليكم أن تتوقعوا المزيد من الابتلاء على دين الله سواء كان ذلك بالضراء أو بالسراء ، وأن تعلموا أنه ليس لدى أحد منكم ضمان بالثبات على دين الله إلا من ثبته الله عز وجل ، ثم اعلموا رحمني الله وإياكم كذلك أن من وسائل الثبات على دين الله لزوم الجماعة ، فإن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: \"يد الله مع الجماعة ومن شذ شذ في النار\" وقال: \"يد الله على الجماعة وإنما يأكل الذئب من الغنم القاصية\" وقال: \"من فارق الجماعة شبرا مات ميتة جاهلية\" وقال: \"من فارق الجماعة فقد خلع ربقة الإسلام من عنقه\" وقال لحذيفة: \"تلزم جماعة المسلمين وإمامهم\" وقال: \"لا يحل دم امرئ مسلم إلا بإحدى ثلاث \"الثيب الزاني والنفس بالنفس والتارك لدينه المفارق للجماعة\" وذلك أن المؤمن إذا كان مع إخوانه فإنه سيستحي من كثير من الأمور ، وسيكون وجوده بين ظهرانيهم تثبيتا له على الحق ، وسيكون كذلك عرضة للمناصحة إذا بدرت منه بادرة ، والنصيحة هي من الذكرى والذكرى تنفع المؤمنين ، والذي ينقطع عن النصيحة ولا يجد من يوجهه في حال ضعفه ولا من يساعده على شيطانه ونفسه في حال الضعف عرضة للانقلاب على عقبيه ثم اعلموا رحمني الله وإياكم كذلك أن من أسباب الثبات على هذا الدين أن يتذكر الإنسان مسؤوليته ، فنحن الآن في وقت نمسك فيه بلواء الإسلام قد تراجع الناس عنه وتركوه في أيديكم والله سبحانه وتعالى غني عنكم فأروا الله من أنفسكم خيرا واعلموا أنكم نلتم هذا التشريف العظيم بتوفيق الله واختياره لا من تلقاء أنفسكم فلذلك لا بد أن تصمدوا عليه وتصبروا ثم اعلموا رحمني الله وإياكم كذلك أن من وسائل الثبات و الاستقامة على هذا الطريق أن يتذكر الإنسان من وراءه من الذين ينظرون إلى تصرفاته فإن استقام استقاموا وإن اعوج اعوجوا ، إنهم يعلقون عليكم الآمال وإنهم ينظرون إلى صبركم على الطريق فأنتم أساتذتهم والمقتدى بكم على طريق الاستقامة ، فإذا صبرتم صبر الناس من ورائكم وقد قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: لقد حزنت على فراق العباس بن عبد المطلب فما ثبتني إلا أعرابي قال: اصبر نكن بك صابرين فإنما صبر الرعية عند صبر الراس خير من العباس أجرك بعده والله خير منك للعباس ثم إنه من وسائل الثبات كذلك والاستقامة على هذا الطريق أن يتذكر الإنسان ما أعده الله للثابتين عليه من التمكين في الحياة الدنيا ومن التقريب في الآخرة فالذين ثبتوا على هذا الطريق ولو قتلوا عليه هم الذين يمكن الله لهم ويمكن لهم بالمحبة في قلوب عباد الله ، ألا ترون أن الذين قتلوا يوم أحد قد جعل الله لهم القبول في نفوس المؤمنين جميعا ، ولا يزالون يتعلقون بهم ويقتدون بهم ويحبونهم غاية المحبة ، وهذا هو التمكين ، فإن التمكين إنما يكون في قلوب أهل الإيمان وأهل الله عز وجل ، أما ما سوى ذلك فهو كله زائل منقطع والذين قتلوا يوم أحد والذين نجوا وعاشوا قد اداركوا جميعا ، فالمنافقون الذين رجعوا عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بنصف الجيش حين واجهوا المشركين يوم أحد لم يعمروا إلى زماننا هذا ولم ينالوا إلا أرزاقهم التي كتبت لهم ولم تزدد أعمارهم بشيء ، ولم يكن لهم أية مكانة ، فلم يكتب الله لهم الخير لا في الدنيا ولا في الآخرة ، والذين صمدوا وصبروا ومنهم عبد الله بن عمرو بن حرام حين رجع المنافقون عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وقف عليهم فقال: أي قومي لا تخذلوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في هذا الموقف فعسى أن لا يتكرر أن تدعوا إلى الدفع وأنتم قادرون عليه ، فقالوا: لو كنا نعلم قتالا لاتبعناكم ، فرجع وقال: أخزاكم الله وأغنى عنكم رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم فنزل فقاتل حتى قتل فدخل الجنة ، وعرض الله عليه أن يتمنى عليه ما شاء فتمنى أن يرده للحياة حتى يقاتل فيقتل في سبيل الله مرة أخرى ، وقد أخرج من قبره بعد ست و أربعين سنة قال جابر، بينا أنا في المسجد إذ جاءني مناد فقال: إن أباك قد أخرج من قبره فخرجت أشتد عدوا إلى الشهداء فإذا ستة عشر من الأنصار قد أخرجوا من قبورهم وذلك في أيام معاوية بن أبي سفيان رضي الله عنهما ، فإذا جراحهم تنزف بالدم ، قال فرفعت يد أحدهم عن خاصرته فخرج الدم ، فعادت يده فسكن الدم ، إنهم الذين أنزل الله فيهم: (ولا تحسبن الذين قتلوا في سبيل الله أمواتا بل أحياء عند ربهم يرزقون فرحين بما آتاهم الله من فضله ويستبشرون بالذين لم يلحقوا بهم من خلفهم أن لا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون يستبشرون بنعمة من الله وفضل وأن الله لا يضيع أجر المؤمنين الذين استجابوا لله والرسول من بعدما أصابهم القرح للذين أحسنوا منهم واتقوا أجر عظيم الذين قال لهم الناس إن الناس قد جمعوا لكم فاخشوهم فزادهم إيمانا وقالوا حسبنا الله ونعم الوكيل فانقلبوا بنعمة من الله وفضل لم يمسسهم سوء واتبعوا رضوان الله والله ذو فضل عظيم) كذلك من وسائل الثبات على دين الله أن يحرص الإنسان على الاستقامة على هذا الطريق في خلواته ، إذا خلى بنفسه أن يكون من الذاكرين الله كثيرا أن يحرص في خلواته على أن يري الله من نفسه خيرا ، فالله سبحانه وتعالى لعباده بالمرصاد ، وما تخطر في قلب إنسان خطرة ولا تنظر عينه نظرة إلا وهي مسجلة مكتوبة عند الله عز وجل ، فلذلك لا بد أن يستشعر المؤمن السالك لهذا الطريق مراقبة الله سبحانه وتعالى له وأنه أقرب إليه من حبل الوريد وأن أعماله جميعا معروضة عليه يقرأها عندما ينادى على رؤوس الأشهاد (اقرأ كتابك كفى بنفسك اليوم عليك حسيبا) كذلك فإن من وسائل الثبات على دين الله أن يجتهد الإنسان في الدعاء أن يثبته الله على طريق الاستقامة وقد كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يكثر أن يقول: \"اللهم يا مقلب القلوب ثبت قلوبنا على دينك\" \"اللهم يا مصرف القلوب صرف قلوبنا على طاعتك\" إن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو معصوم قد غفر الله له ما تقدم من ذنبه وما تأخر كان يحرص على الإكثار من هذا الدعاء ، أفليس جديرا بالمؤمن الذي سلك طريقه أن يحرص على الإكثار من هذا الدعاء وأن يتزود منه وهو يعلم أنه في كل وقت عرضة لأن يقلبه الله عز وجل نسأل الله الثبات والاستقامة على طريقه. يقول الله عز وجل (يثبت الله الذين آمنوا بالقول الثابت في الحياة الدنيا وفي الآخرة ويضل الله الظالمين ويفعل الله ما يشاء). عباد الله إن الله أمركم بأمر بدأ فيه بنفسه وثنى فيه بملائكته وثلث بكم معاشر المؤمنين فقال جل من قائل كريما: (إن الله وملائكته يصلون على النبي يا أيها الذين آمنوا صلوا عليه وسلموا تسليما). اللهم صل وسلم وزد وبارك على نبينا محمد عبدك ونبيك ورسولك النبي الأمي وعلى آله وصحبه وسلم تسليما. اللهم أعز الإسلام والمسلمين وأذل الشرك والمشركين وأوهن كيد الكافرين وانصرنا عليهم أجمعين ، اللهم أظهر دينك وكتابك على الدين كله ولو كره المشركون ، اللهم اخلف محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم في أمته بخير ، اللهم ارزقنا التمسك بسنته عند فساد أمته ، واحشرنا تحت لوائه وابعثنا في زمرته ، واسقنا من حوضه بيده الشريفة شربة هنيئة لا نظمأ بعدها أبدا ، وبيض وجوهنا يوم تبيض وجوه وتسود وجوه ، وآتنا كتبنا بأيماننا تلقاء وجوهنا وجوزنا على الصراط كالبرق الخاطف يا أرحم الراحمين ، اللهم إنا نسألك بوجهك الكريم الفردوس الأعلى من الجنة ، اللهم إنا نسألك بوجهك الكريم الفردوس الأعلى من الجنة ، اللهم من أرادنا أو أراد الإسلام بسوء فاشغله بنفسه واجعل تدبيره تدميره واجعل دائرة السوء عليه وأنزل به المثلات وأنزل به بأسك الذي لا يرد عن القوم المجرمين وأرنا فيه عجائب قدرتك عاجلا غير رائث إنك على كل شيء قدير. عباد الله (إن الله يأمر بالعدل والإحسان وإيتاء ذي القربى وينهى عن الفحشاء والمنكر والبغي يعظكم لعلكم تذكرون) فاذكروا الله العظيم الجليل يذكركم واشكروه على نعمه شكرا حقيقيا يزدكم ، ولذكر الله أكبر والله يعلم ما تصنعون.
body_en:
Praise belongs to God. We praise Him and we seek His help, and we seek refuge in God from the evils of our own selves and from the evil consequences of our deeds. Whomever God guides, there is none to lead him astray; and whomever He leads astray, there is none to guide him. I bear witness that there is no god but God alone, having no partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger — God bless him and his family and his Companions, and grant them abundant peace.

{O people, be conscious of your Lord, who created you from a single soul and created from it its mate, and from the two of them spread abroad many men and women. And be conscious of God, by whom you ask of one another, and of the ties of kinship. God is ever watchful over you} (Sūrat al-Nisāʾ 4:1).

{O you who believe, be conscious of God and speak a word that is straight (70). He will set right your deeds for you and forgive you your sins. And whoever obeys God and His Messenger has won a great victory} (Sūrat al-Aḥzāb 33:70–71).

To proceed: the best of speech is the Book of God, and the best guidance is the guidance of Muhammad, God bless him and grant him peace. The worst of matters are those newly invented in religion, and every innovation in religion (bidʿah) is misguidance.

Servants of God, God, glorified and exalted, guides whomever He wills to His straight path, and makes firm upon that path whomever He wills to make firm, and tests people and tries them upon it. Whoever God wills to make firm will be made firm.

God, glorified and exalted, has commanded the taking of means in all matters, and among those are the means of guidance and of uprightness. Among the means of guidance is learning what God has commanded, and acting upon what the Messenger of God, God bless him and grant him peace, brought, and taking the Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace, as one's model in words, deeds, beliefs and intentions. Among the means of guidance likewise is humble entreaty to God, glorified and exalted, in asking for guidance. And among the means of guidance is reflection and remembrance.

Then, after that, come the means of steadfastness in the religion of God, and these are greater, and more deserving that the Muslim should occupy himself with them.

Among the greatest of them is that the Muslim should remember that he is in this life within the pattern of mutual pushing back, and within a struggle in which a decisive outcome is unavoidable. This struggle is either uprightness upon the path of guidance until death, or turning back and reversing upon one's heels. People are of two divisions: either a person is of the God-conscious, or he is of the wretched. The God-conscious are the felicitous, whom God makes firm with the firm word in the life of this world and in the hereafter. If a person knows this struggle, and knows the division of people into the two divisions, and knows that this comes about neither by lineage nor by ancestry but only by the taking of means and by the choice of the Sovereign, the Judge, glorified and exalted, then he will be eager not to be of the wretched, and to be of the people of guidance, and to hold to that his whole life long.

Then, among the means of uprightness and steadfastness likewise, is that a person should know the length of this road and what lies upon it of hardships. For many people turn back at the first blow and retreat from the road of uprightness and guidance, and do not stand fast upon it and are not steadfast, because they are ignorant of what lies upon it of blows and obstacles.

You, servants of God, are upon a this-worldly path which is a representation of the path of the hereafter. You know that the path of the hereafter has upon it hooks like the thorns of the saʿdān plant, and that people differ upon it according to their deeds. So likewise this this-worldly path, the white clear way, has upon it hooks that catch hold of people; whoever is not steadfast upon it will turn away upon his heels. God, exalted be He, said: {And among people is he who worships God upon an edge. If good befalls him he is at ease with it, and if a trial befalls him he turns about upon his face. He has lost this world and the hereafter. That is the manifest loss} (Sūrat al-Ḥajj 22:11).

Likewise, among the means of steadfastness in this religion is not to be hasty in a person's attaining his reward in this life. The reward of God, glorified and exalted, is what He has prepared for His friends in the abode of lasting bliss. That reward is God's bringing His friends near, mighty and majestic is He, and His choosing them — when God whitens their faces, gives them their books in their right hands, places them in the first company, brings them near in the highest Firdaws of the Garden, and shades them with the shade of His throne on a day when there is no shade but His shade; for He has chosen them for that.

Therefore a person must be eager for the reward of the hereafter, and must know that what is hastened to him in this life is only a diminishing of his reward. It is established as sound (ṣaḥīḥ) from the Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: "No raiding party goes out in the path of God and takes spoils but that two thirds of its reward has been hastened to it; and no raiding party goes out in the path of God and fails but that it attains its reward in full."

Therefore we must be eager, servants of God, that the hereafter be the bulk of our concern, and that we be eager for the reward of the hereafter, and that we not be eager to hasten anything of our reward in this life.

Then know — may God have mercy on me and on you — that those to whom something is hastened in this life, even if they are among the best of the friends of God, always remain in wariness and fear. For that reason al-Bukhari and Muslim reported in the two Ṣaḥīḥ collections from Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, may God be pleased with him, that he was fasting, and the table was set before him, and there were on it various kinds of food, and he wept a severe weeping until he made those around him weep. They said: "Abu al-Mundhir, what makes you weep?" He said: "We were a people of ignorance and evil, and God sent to us His Messenger, God bless him and grant him peace, and we believed and affirmed the truth and followed. Among us are those who died and did not have anything of their reward hastened to them — among them my brother Musab ibn Umayr, who was killed on the day of Uhud and had nothing but his sword and a cloak upon him: if we covered his head with it his feet showed, and if we covered his feet his head showed. So the Messenger of God, God bless him and grant him peace, ordered us to cover his head and to put some idhkhir grass over his feet. So he died and had nothing of his reward hastened to him. And we remained after them, and this world opened its doors to us and we gather its fruit; so we fear that it may be said to us on the Day of Resurrection: {You used up your good things in your worldly life and took your enjoyment of them. So today you are recompensed with the punishment of humiliation for having been arrogant in the earth without right, and for having been rebellious} (Sūrat al-Aḥqāf 46:20)."

The like of this is established as sound from Khabbab ibn al-Aratt, may God be pleased with him.

And it is established that the Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace, went out of his house — nothing brought him out but hunger — and he met Abu Bakr and Umar and said: "What has brought the two of you out of your houses?" They said: "Hunger has brought us out." He said: "And I — nothing has brought me out but hunger." So they went to Abu al-Haytham ibn al-Tayyihan, and he received them as guests. When he took his knife, intending to slaughter a sheep, the Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace, forbade him the milk-bearing ones, that is, the milch animals. And when he set before them a cluster of dates and meat and cool water, the Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace, looked at that and said: "This is among the bounty you will be asked about." {Then you will certainly be asked on that day about the bounty} (Sūrat al-Takāthur 102:8).

It is upon us, servants of God, to beware of being among those whose rewards are hastened to them in this life, so that they reap them in matters that are cut off and in which there is no benefit. Those people are worth nothing with God, for their worth is what God hastens to them of the matters of this perishing world.

Then know — may God have mercy on me and on you — that among the means of uprightness and steadfastness in religion is that we remember that haste in obtaining the matters of this world is likewise a fault and a harm. Al-Bukhari reported in the Ṣaḥīḥ from the report of Khabbab ibn al-Aratt, may God be pleased with him, that the Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace, was reclining upon a cloak of his in the shade of the Kaʿbah. Khabbab said: I came to him and said: "Messenger of God, will you not seek victory for us? Will you not supplicate for us?" He said: "Among those before you a man would be brought and the saw would be placed upon the parting of his head and he would be split with it into two halves; then iron combs would be brought and he would be combed with them, what is below his bone of skin and flesh — and that would not turn him from his religion. And by Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, God will surely bring this affair to completion, until a rider travels from Sanaa to Hadramawt fearing none but God, and the wolf for his sheep. But you are a people who are hasty."

So the Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace, warned with an eloquent warning against this haste, and made clear its harm and its danger, and made clear that the future belongs to this religion inevitably, and that God will grant it victory and give it might, by the might of one who is mighty or by the abasement of one who is abased.

But whoever misses that opening, it is better for him. For the Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace — God gave him the treasures of Chosroes and Caesar, yet God took him before he attained anything of that; they were opened to his Companions after him and they spent them in the path of God. This is evidence that whoever misses the opening, it is better for him. And those who died before the opening are the ones who were true to what they had covenanted with God. For the Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace, eight days before his death, stood over the martyrs of Uhud and said: "I am a witness over these, that they were true to God in what they covenanted with Him."

And you know that the Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace, was taken by God without having eaten his fill for three consecutive days, and three months would pass in which no fire was seen in his houses. He used to sleep upon a reed mat and it would leave its mark in his side — may my father and mother be his ransom, God bless him and grant him peace.

Then know — may God have mercy on me and on you — that among the means of steadfastness upon this arduous road is that a person should remember the stories of those who went before and preceded him upon the road, and what they met with of harm in the path of God. Let us remember, my brothers, how people used to mock Noah, peace be upon him. And let us remember the conspiring together of the nearest kin against Abraham when they cast him into the fire, and let us remember their expelling him from their city. And let us remember likewise what Lot met with from his people. And let us remember what the prophets met with after that, down to our Prophet Muhammad, God bless him and grant him peace, of harm in the path of God, and what his Companions met with of harm.

For the Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace, was prostrating to his Lord at the Yemeni corner, and Uqbah ibn Abi Muayt came and put his foot upon the nape of the Messenger of God, God bless him and grant him peace — that is, the back of his head — and Uqbah was heavy and fat, and he kept pressing him with his foot, until he ordered one who came to him with the afterbirth of a she-camel that had given birth, and placed it between his shoulders while he was prostrating to his Lord.

And likewise Nawfal bound Abu Bakr and Talha ibn Ubayd Allah together with a leather thong and struck them upon their cheeks a severe striking until he made their cheeks bleed.

And likewise a number of the Companions of the Messenger of God, God bless him and grant him peace, were harmed with severe harm, in addition to what they met with of other pressures. Thus Sad ibn Abi Waqqas, when he accepted Islam and made his Islam public, his mother went on hunger strike and swore that she would not eat and would not drink until he turned back from his religion. When he feared death for her, he whispered in her ear and said: "Mother, if you had a hundred souls, and they went out one soul after another, on condition that I turn back from my religion, I would not turn back from it. So live or die."

Therefore we must know that we are being tested by this religion, and that we are in need of steadfastness in it; in need of knowing that whoever is not steadfast in his religion harms none but himself, and does not harm God or His religion in anything; and that this religion continues until God inherits the earth and whoever is upon it.

Then know likewise — may God have mercy on me and on you — that whoever remembers the stories of those who have passed and the condition they were in will always expect to meet with some of what they met with, according to his degree in faith and God-consciousness. For you are travelling a road which those pioneers who went before travelled, and you are not nobler in the sight of God than they were; so what they met with, you must inevitably receive your share of it. God, exalted be He, says: {In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate. Alif Lām Mīm. Do people reckon that they will be left to say "We believe" and not be tried? We tried those before them, and God will surely know those who are truthful and will surely know the liars} (Sūrat al-ʿAnkabūt 29:1–3).

May God bless me and you in the Mighty Qur'an, and may He benefit me and you by what is in it of verses and wise remembrance. And may He turn in forgiveness to me and to you; He is the Ever-Relenting, the Merciful.

Praise belongs to God for His beneficence, and thanks be to Him for His favour and His bounty. I bear witness that there is no god but God alone, having no partner, in magnification of His affair; and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger, the one who calls to His good pleasure — God bless him and his family, his Companions, his wives, his offspring and his brethren, and grant them peace.

Servants of God, among the means of steadfastness in the religion of God is that a person should read the stories of the prophets in the Qur'an. It is established as sound from Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak, may God be pleased with him, that he said: "The stories of the righteous are a host among the hosts of God, by which God makes firm the hearts of His servants." The confirmation of that from the Qur'an is the words of God, exalted be He: {And all that We relate to you of the tidings of the messengers is that by which We make your heart firm. And there has come to you in this the truth, and an admonition and a reminder for the believers} (Sūrat Hūd 11:120).

So it is upon us, servants of God, to remember what they were in and what they were harmed with in the path of God, and to know that the road is long, and that ahead of us is more than what we have met with, and that there remains of the road more than has passed.

Therefore know — may God have mercy on me and on you — that it is upon you to expect more trial for the religion of God, whether that be through adversity or through ease; and to know that not one of you has any guarantee of steadfastness in the religion of God, except whomever God, mighty and majestic, makes firm.

Then know likewise — may God have mercy on me and on you — that among the means of steadfastness in the religion of God is holding to the congregation (jamāʿah). For the Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace, said: "The hand of God is with the congregation, and whoever separates himself separates himself into the Fire." And he said: "The hand of God is over the congregation, and the wolf eats only the sheep that strays far off." And he said: "Whoever parts from the congregation by a handspan dies a death of ignorance." And he said: "Whoever parts from the congregation has cast off the collar of Islam from his neck." And he said to Hudhayfah: "You are to hold to the congregation of the Muslims and their imam." And he said: "The blood of a Muslim man is not lawful except by one of three: the married fornicator, a life for a life, and one who abandons his religion, parting from the congregation."

That is because the believer, when he is with his brothers, will feel shame before many matters; and his being in their midst will be a making-firm of him upon the truth; and he will likewise be open to being counselled if some lapse proceeds from him. Sincere counsel is part of the reminder, and the reminder benefits the believers. But he who cuts himself off from counsel, and finds no one to direct him in his state of weakness and no one to help him against his devil and his own soul in the state of weakness, is exposed to reversing upon his heels.

Then know likewise — may God have mercy on me and on you — that among the means of steadfastness in this religion is that a person should remember his responsibility. For we are now in a time in which we hold the banner of Islam; people have drawn back from it and left it in your hands, and God, glorified and exalted, has no need of you. So show God good from yourselves, and know that you attained this great honouring by God's granting of success and His choice, not of your own accord. Therefore you must stand fast upon it and be patient.

Then know likewise — may God have mercy on me and on you — that among the means of steadfastness and uprightness upon this road is that a person should remember those behind him who look to his conduct: if he is upright they are upright, and if he is crooked they are crooked. They hang their hopes upon you, and they look to your patience upon the road. You are their teachers and the ones taken as models upon the road of uprightness. So if you are patient, the people behind you are patient.

Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: "I grieved at the parting from al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib, and nothing made me firm except a bedouin who said:

*Be patient, and we shall be patient through you, for the patience of the flock is at the patience of the head. / Better than al-Abbas is your reward after him, and God is better for al-Abbas than you.*"

Then, among the means of steadfastness likewise and of uprightness upon this road, is that a person should remember what God has prepared for those steadfast upon it of establishment in the life of this world and of being brought near in the hereafter. For those who were steadfast upon this road, even if they were killed upon it, are the ones whom God establishes, and establishes for them by love in the hearts of the servants of God.

Do you not see that those who were killed on the day of Uhud — God has given them acceptance in the souls of all the believers, and they do not cease to be attached to them and to take them as models and to love them with the utmost love? This is establishment. For establishment is only in the hearts of the people of faith and the people of God, mighty and majestic. As for what is other than that, it is all passing away and cut off.

And those who were killed on the day of Uhud and those who escaped and lived have all alike come to their end. The hypocrites who turned back from the Messenger of God, God bless him and grant him peace, with half the army when they faced the idolaters on the day of Uhud did not live on to this time of ours, and attained nothing but their allotted provisions which had been written for them, and their lifespans were not increased by anything, and they had no standing whatever; God did not write good for them, neither in this world nor in the hereafter.

And those who stood fast and were patient — among them Abd Allah ibn Amr ibn Haram: when the hypocrites turned back from the Messenger of God, God bless him and grant him peace, he stood over them and said: "O my people, do not forsake the Messenger of God, God bless him and grant him peace, in this position; perhaps it will not happen again that you are called to the defence while you are able to it." They said: "If we knew there would be fighting we would have followed you." So he turned back and said: "May God disgrace you, and God will make His Messenger, God bless him and grant him peace, independent of you." Then he went down and fought until he was killed, and he entered the Garden. God offered him that he might wish for whatever he wished, and he wished that He would return him to life so that he might fight and be killed in the path of God a second time.

He was taken out of his grave after forty-six years. Jabir said: While I was in the mosque, a caller came to me and said: "Your father has been taken out of his grave." So I went out running hard to the martyrs, and there were sixteen of the Ansar who had been taken out of their graves — and that was in the days of Muawiyah ibn Abi Sufyan, may God be pleased with them both — and their wounds were flowing with blood. He said: I lifted the hand of one of them from his flank and the blood came out; and his hand returned and the blood was stilled.

They are the ones about whom God sent down: {And do not reckon those who were killed in the path of God as dead. Rather they are living with their Lord, provided for, rejoicing in what God has given them of His bounty, and receiving good tidings concerning those who have not yet joined them from behind them, that there shall be no fear upon them nor shall they grieve. They receive good tidings of a blessing from God and a bounty, and that God does not let the reward of the believers go to waste — those who responded to God and the Messenger after the wound had afflicted them. For those of them who did good and were God-conscious there is a great reward. Those to whom people said: The people have gathered against you, so fear them — and it increased them in faith and they said: God is sufficient for us, and an excellent Guardian is He. So they returned with a blessing from God and a bounty; no evil touched them, and they followed the good pleasure of God; and God is possessed of great bounty} (Sūrat Āl ʿImrān 3:169–174).

Likewise, among the means of steadfastness in the religion of God is that a person be eager for uprightness upon this road in his times of solitude: that when he is alone with himself he be among those who remember God much, and that he be eager in his solitude to show God good from himself. For God, glorified and exalted, is ever watchful over His servants; no thought passes in the heart of a person, and his eye does not cast a glance, but that it is recorded and written with God, mighty and majestic.

Therefore the believer who travels this road must be conscious of God's watching over him, glorified and exalted, and that He is nearer to him than the jugular vein, and that all his deeds are laid before Him and he will read them when he is called before the assembled witnesses: {Read your book. Sufficient is your own self against you this day as a reckoner} (Sūrat al-Isrāʾ 17:14).

Likewise, among the means of steadfastness in the religion of God is that a person strive in supplication that God make him firm upon the road of uprightness. The Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace, used often to say: "O God, Turner of hearts, make our hearts firm upon Your religion." "O God, Disposer of hearts, dispose our hearts to Your obedience."

The Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace — though he is protected from sin, and God had forgiven him what went before of his fault and what came after — used to be eager to say this supplication often. Is it not then fitting for the believer who travels his road to be eager to say this supplication often and to take provision from it, knowing that at every moment he is exposed to God's turning him about, mighty and majestic? We ask God for steadfastness and uprightness upon His road.

God, mighty and majestic, says: {God makes firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the hereafter; and God leads the wrongdoers astray; and God does what He wills} (Sūrat Ibrāhīm 14:27).

Servants of God, God has commanded you with a command in which He began with Himself, and made His angels second in it, and made you, company of believers, third. He said — and noble is He who speaks: {Indeed God and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet. O you who believe, send blessings upon him and greet him with peace} (Sūrat al-Aḥzāb 33:56).

O God, bless and grant peace and increase and blessing to our Prophet Muhammad, Your servant, Your prophet and Your messenger, the unlettered Prophet, and to his family and his Companions, and grant them peace.

O God, give might to Islam and the Muslims, and abase associating partners with God (shirk) and those who associate partners with Him. Weaken the scheming of the unbelievers and grant us victory over them all. O God, make Your religion and Your Book prevail over all religion, though those who associate partners with God be averse.

O God, succeed Muhammad, God bless him and grant him peace, in his community with good. O God, grant us to hold fast to his sunnah when his community is corrupted. Gather us under his banner and raise us in his company. Give us to drink from his pool, by his noble hand, a pleasant draught after which we shall never thirst again. Whiten our faces on the day when faces are whitened and faces are blackened. Give us our books in our right hands, before our faces, and bring us across the path like flashing lightning, O most Merciful of the merciful.

O God, we ask You by Your noble face for the highest Firdaws of the Garden. O God, we ask You by Your noble face for the highest Firdaws of the Garden.

O God, whoever intends evil against us or against Islam, occupy him with himself, make his scheming his own destruction, turn the turn of evil upon him, send down upon him exemplary punishments, and send down upon him Your might which is not turned back from the criminal people; and show us in him the wonders of Your power, soon and without delay — You have power over all things.

Servants of God: {Indeed God commands justice and excellence and giving to kinsfolk, and He forbids indecency and wrong and oppression. He admonishes you, that you may take heed} (Sūrat al-Naḥl 16:90). So remember God, the Mighty, the Majestic, and He will remember you; and thank Him for His blessings with a true thankfulness, and He will increase you. And the remembrance of God is greater, and God knows what you do.

flags.arabic: قال: \"ما من سرية تخرج في سبيل الله فتغنم…\"   /   \"يد الله مع الجماعة ومن شذ شذ في النار\"
flags.context: Quotation marks around quoted speech throughout this record.
options: Preserve the backslashes in body_ar and omit them from body_en, as done here
Strip them from body_ar as well, treating them as pure CMS noise
flags.note: An addslashes artifact from the CMS: literal backslashes stand before every quote mark in the stored Arabic. Style guide 11 requires that source defects be recorded rather than silently fixed, and notes that this one is corpus-wide and should be cleaned globally rather than per record. body_ar therefore preserves the backslashes exactly as served.

flags.arabic: فقالوا يا أبا المنذر وما يبكيك
flags.context: The narration of Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf weeping over the laid table.
options: Leave the kunya as the source gives it ('Abu al-Mundhir'), as done here
Correct to 'Abū Muḥammad', the kunya of Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf
flags.note: The narration is attributed in this record to Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, whose kunya is Abū Muḥammad. 'Abū al-Mundhir' is the kunya of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb. Either the kunya or the attribution appears to be an error in the source. Style guide 11 forbids silently fixing it, so the English carries the source reading and the defect is flagged. The Sheikh's argument does not depend on which is right, but the English as it stands names a Companion by another Companion's kunya.

flags.arabic: لا يصده ذلك عن دينه و والذي نفس محمد بيده … ولكنكم قوم تستعجلون\"
flags.context: The hadith of Khabbab ibn al-Aratt in the shade of the Kaʿbah.
options: Render the quotation whole and note the unbalanced marks, as done here
Reposition the opening quotation mark in body_ar
flags.note: The quotation of this hadith opens without a quotation mark but closes with one, so the extent of the Prophet's reported words is not marked in the source. The English takes the quotation to run from 'Among those before you' to 'you are a people who are hasty', which is the standard extent of this report. The source also carries a doubled conjunction ('wa wa-lladhī'). Neither has been corrected in body_ar.

flags.arabic: وقال: \"لا يحل دم امرئ مسلم إلا بإحدى ثلاث \"الثيب الزاني والنفس بالنفس والتارك لدينه المفارق للجماعة\"
flags.context: The last of the series of hadiths on holding to the congregation.
options: Render as a single continuous quotation, as done here
Treat the inner marks as a nested quotation
flags.note: The quotation marks in this sentence are malformed: a second opening mark appears in mid-quotation with no matching close, leaving three marks in all. The English renders the hadith as one continuous statement, which is how it is transmitted. body_ar preserves the malformed marks.

flags.arabic: والذين قتلوا يوم أحد والذين نجوا وعاشوا قد اداركوا جميعا
flags.context: Contrasting the fate of the martyrs of Uhud with that of the hypocrites who withdrew.
options: have all alike come to their end
have all caught up with one another
have all been overtaken together
flags.note: The verb as printed ('iddārakū') is ambiguous here and the sentence is elliptical. The sense required by what follows — that the hypocrites 'did not live on to this time of ours' — is that both groups alike have died, so that only the reward distinguishes them. A reviewer should confirm the reading before the English fixes one.

flags.arabic: اصبر نكن بك صابرين فإنما صبر الرعية عند صبر الراس خير من العباس أجرك بعده والله خير منك للعباس
flags.context: Ibn Abbas on what consoled him at the death of his father al-Abbas.
options: Render as two lines of verse, as done here
Render as continuous prose, as the source prints it
flags.note: The CMS has run two lines of verse into the surrounding prose without line breaks, so that the couplets are not visible. Style guide 4: rendered as prose in italics, with the Arabic retained in the bilingual pane. The source also spells 'al-raʾs' without its hamzah ('al-rās'). The bedouin who spoke the lines is not named.

flags.arabic: فإن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان ساجدا لربه عند الركن اليماني فجاء عقبة بن أبي معيط
flags.context: The account of the camel's afterbirth placed on the Prophet's back while he prostrated.
options: Render exactly as the Sheikh gives it, as done here
Harmonise the account with the wording in the Ṣaḥīḥ collections
flags.note: The Sheikh gives this account without naming a collection or a grading. In the better-known transmissions the instigator is Abu Jahl and the location is given simply as the Kaʿbah, and the detail of Uqbah pressing with his foot belongs to a separate report. Style guide 4 forbids adding a grading or an attribution he did not give, so nothing has been supplied; the account stands as he told it.

flags.arabic: وكذلك فإن نوفلا قرن أبا بكر وطلحة بن عبيد الله بنسع وضربهما على خديهما ضربا شديدا حتى أدما خديهما
flags.context: Examples of harm suffered by the Companions.
options: Render exactly as the Sheikh gives it, as done here
Separate the binding and the beating as two distinct reports
flags.note: The report of Nawfal ibn Khuwaylid binding Abu Bakr and Talha together with a thong — the origin of Talha's title 'the paired one' — and the report of their being beaten are usually transmitted separately. The Sheikh combines them and gives no source or grading. Nothing has been added or separated; a reviewer may wish to note the combination.

flags.arabic: (بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم ألم أحسب الناس أن يتركوا أن يقولوا آمنا وهم لا يفتنون …)
flags.context: The verse closing the first part of the sermon.
options: Keep the basmalah inside the quotation, as done here
Move the basmalah outside the quoted verse
flags.note: The source encloses the basmalah within the parentheses of the Qur'anic citation, so that it reads as part of the quoted verse. Sūrat al-ʿAnkabūt begins at 'Alif Lām Mīm'. Preserved as served and flagged rather than silently repositioned.

flags.arabic: ويثبت من أراد ثباته … وفي جدلية لا بد فيها من الحسم
flags.context: The framing of the whole sermon.
options: struggle in which a decisive outcome is unavoidable
dialectic which must be resolved
contest which must end in a settlement
flags.note: 'Jadaliyyah' here is used in a modern register ('dialectic'), unusually for this corpus, alongside 'sunnat al-tadāfuʿ' (the pattern of mutual pushing back, from Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:251). The English renders the sense rather than importing the philosophical term, but the register is distinctive and a reviewer may prefer to keep it.

translator_notes: Qur'anic renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic text of the Qur'an.

The CMS does not expose a section or category on the article view for this record, and the 2010 archive is not reachable through the site's section listings. section/category_ar/category_en are therefore left null rather than inferred.

The published page appends CMS chrome to the article text ('Tweet' plus the Arabic publication timestamp). That chrome has been removed from body_ar and body_en; the timestamp it carried is recorded in date/date_ar.

CMS escaping defect (style guide 11): this record carries literal backslashes before the quote marks around quoted speech, an addslashes artifact. They are preserved verbatim in body_ar and omitted from body_en. This is corpus-wide and should be cleaned globally, not per record.

This is a complete two-part Friday sermon. The first part closes with 'May God bless me and you in the Mighty Qur'an', the second opens with 'Praise belongs to God for His beneficence', and the whole ends with the customary closing verse of Sūrat al-Naḥl. Nothing is missing at either end.

The sermon is structured as an enumeration of the means (wasāʾil) of steadfastness. The Sheikh lists them in sequence, each introduced by 'then know' or 'likewise among the means'. That enumerative structure has been preserved in the English rather than smoothed into continuous argument, because the list is the form of the argument.

Several narrations here are given without a named collection or a grading, and two appear to combine reports that are usually transmitted separately. Style guide 4 forbids adding a grading the Sheikh did not give or dropping one he did, so the attributions stand exactly as he gives them and the points of difference are flagged for the reviewer rather than harmonised.

title_ar: حسن الخلق
title_en: Good Character
body_ar: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين وأصلي وأسلم على من بعث رحمة للعالمين وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين، السلام عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته. أما بعد فإن الله سبحانه وتعالى جعل الإنسان مؤلفا من ثلاثة عناصر هي العقل الذي به شرفه على سائر الحيوانات، والجسم الذي هو من تراب والروح التي هي نفخة غيبية من أمر الله، وكل واحد من هذه العناصر الثلاثة قابل للتربية والنماء والزكاء، والروح نماؤها وزكاؤها إنما هو باكتسابها للأخلاق الحميدة ومجانبتها للأخلاق السيئة وحسن أخلاق الإنسان دليل على تهذيب روحه وصفاء طبعه، وسوء أخلاقه دليل على خبث طويته وعلى خبث روحه نسأل الله السلامة والعافية. والخلق خلقان خلق فطري وخلق مكتسب، فمن الأخلاق ما هو فطري يفطر عليه الإنسان ويتعود عليه، كما قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: يقدم عليكم أهل اليمن هم أصفى أفئدة وأرق قلوبا، الإيمان يمان والحكمة يمانية. والمكتسب هو ما يتعود الإنسان عليه فيجاهد نفسه حتى يحصل له الخلق، وحسن الخلق مطلوب شرعا ومن المهمات العليا، ولذلك أثنى الله على رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم، بحسن الخلق، فقال:"وإنك لعلى خلق عظيم" فمن كان حسن الخلق فإنه لا بد أن يوفق للطاعات العلى، وكذلك يختار لجوار النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في الدرجات العلى من الجنة، ومن كان سيء الخلق نسأل الله السلامة والعافية لا يوفق للطاعات الكبرى، ولا يستطيع كذلك أن يكون من العابدين لأن سوء خلقه مقتض منه للنفرة والطرد عن الحضرة والمقام الرفيع، واكتساب الإنسان للخلق الحسن إنما يتم بمعرفته بأخلاق المؤمنين وبما يقابلها من أخلاق الكفار والمنافقين فيحاول الاتصاف بأخلاق المؤمنين، وقد بين النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ذلك فبين ما يكون من الأخلاق مجتمعا يمثل النفاق، فإذا اجتمع في الإنسان كان منافقا خالصا، وذلك في حديث عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاصي رضي الله عنهما أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: أربع من كن فيه كان منافقا خالصا، ومن كانت فيه خصلة منهن كانت فيه خصلة من النفاق حتى يدعها إذا حدث كذب وإذا ائتمن خان وإذا عاهد غدر وإذا خاصم فجر. وكذلك بين النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم صفات المنافق، فقال: آية المنافق ثلاث إذا حدث كذب وإذا وعد أخلف وإذا ائتمن خان، ففي مقابلها صفات أهل الإيمان فمنها الصدق فهو صفة من صفات الإيمان لما ثبت عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: إن الصدق يهدي إلى البر وإن البر يهدي إلى الجنة ولا يزال الرجل يصدق ويتحرى الصدق حتى يكتب عند الله صديقا، وإن الكذب يهدي إلى الفجور وإن الفجور يهدي إلى النار، ولا يزال الرجل يكذب ويتحرى الكذب حتى يكتب عند الله كذابا، وكذلك بين النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن خلق هذا الدين هو الحياء، فقال: لكل دين خلق وخلق الإسلام الحياء، وقال: للأنصاري الذي سمعه يعظ أخاه في الحياء، قال: دعه فإن الحياء من الإيمان. وكذلك ثبت عنه صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: الحياء شعبة من شعب الإيمان. وحض النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم على كثير من الأخلاق الرفيعة، كالحلم والأناة، فبين أنهما محبوبان لدى الله جل جلاله، فقد قال لأشج عبد القيس إن فيك لخصلتين يحبهما الله ورسوله: الحلم والأناة، وكذلك بين أن المؤمن لا يكذب أي لا يكون كذابا بطبعه، لما سئل: المؤمن يسرق: قال: نعم، قيل: المؤمن يزني قال: نعم، قيل: المؤمن يكذب: قال: لا، والمقصود بذلك أنه لا يكون كذابا، كثير الكذب، فذلك ليس من صفات المؤمنين وإنما هو من صفات المنافقين، فيغري بفعل المكرمات انبساطه ويحميك أن تأتي القبيح احترامه وكذلك فإن من فوائد حسن الخلق أنه مقتض أيضا لإحسان العشرة واستمرارها، فالعلاقات يمكن أن يبنيها الإنسان لكنها كثيرا ما تتقطع بسبب اختلاف المصالح وبسبب سوء الخلق أو غير ذلك، فإذا كان الإنسان حسن الخلق فإن علاقته التي بناها ستستمر سواء كان ذلك في داخل أسرته وعائلته أو في محيطه من حوله، فكل من كان حسن الخلق ستستمر علاقته بمعاشريه، وكل من كان سيئ الخلق فلن يصبر عليه أحد وسيشق التعامل معه، وحسن الخلق كذلك دليل على وفرة العقل وتمامه، فالإنسان الذي لديه عقل وافر لا يمكن أن يكون سيء الخلق مع الناس، لأن له من التفكير ما يستطيع به الوصول إلى ما يحبه الناس، وبذلك يؤثر عليهم، ولا يحتاج إلى إساءة الخلق في التعامل معهم لأنه ينال بالرفق ما يريد نيله الناس بما سواه. وكذلك فإن حسن الخلق أيضا يقتضي من الإنسان اجتناب كثير من الرذائل والسمو بنفسه عنها، وبذلك تعلو منزلته ويرتفع قدره، فالإنسان إذا كان سيء الخلق سينغمس في كثير من الرذائل بسبب سوء خلقه وسوء معاملته للناس، وإذا انغمس فيها فإنها تدعوه للانخفاض وهي منافية لرفع الدرجات، أما إذا حسن أخلاقه فإنه سيرضي الجميع، ولذلك فقد جاء: إنك لن تسع الناس بمالك فلتسعهم بحسن خلقك، يستطيع الإنسان أن يوزع حسن خلقه على الناس، فيكتسبهم جميعا ولو كان ماله قليلا، ولو كان ضعيف ذات اليد، فحسن خلقه كفيل بإرضاء الناس عنه، وحسن الخلق كذلك أهمه حسن الخلق مع الله جل جلاله، فالإنسان إذا ومن ما جرب أن الإنسان إذا كان له أصدقاء من أهل الصدق والنصح والإخلاص، فإنهم بالإمكان أن يعينوه على حسن الخلق وأن يهذبوا أخلاقه بإزالة الكلفة والتعود على الألفة، وهم بمثابة المرآة ينظر فيها فيرى ما في وجهه من الأوساخ وقد قال الحكيم: الخل كالماء يبدي لي ضمائره مع الصفاء ويخفيها مع الكدر وقراءة الإنسان لصفات الصالحين وما جاء في قصص الأنبياء في القرآن وما جاء أيضا في السنة من أحاديث الأنبياء و فمن كان بخيلا أو جبانا فهو متصف بسوء الخلق، ولذلك لا يصلح لسيادة الناس، ولا لرعاية التكاليف قبل علاجه من هذا الداء العضال الذي أصيب به، والإنسان إذا أورث أولاده هذا الخلق السيء فقد أساء إليهم إساءة مستمرة، وإذا عودهم على حسن الخلق ورباهم عليه فإنهم سيكونون امتدادا في عمره واستقامته، وقد أخرج مالك في الموطإ أن المسيح بن مريم عليه السلام مر من زقاق ضيق فاستقبله خنزير فقال: انفذ بسلام، فقيل: يا نبي الله أتقول هذا لخنزير؟ قال: أردت أن أعود لساني قول الخير. ومر هو وحواريون على جيفة كلب قد أنتن فقال: الحواريون ما أنت رائحته، فقال المسيح بن مريم ما أحسن بياض أسنانه، فقيل له في ذلك، فقال: ذكرته بأحسن ما فيه، وهذا هو تعويد النفس على أحسن الأخلاق وأتمها، وقد بين النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كذلك ما ارتضاه من الأخلاق في نساء قريش فقال: عليكم خير النساء صلح نساء قريش أحناه على ولد في صغره وأرعاه على زوج في ذات يده وأرضاه بالقليل، وهذه القناعة صفة حميدة، وقد أثنى الله كذلك على الأنصار بخلق حميد وهو الكرم، فقد قال الله تعالى: {والذين تبؤوا الدار والإيمان من قبلهم يحبون من هاجر إليهم ولا يجدون في صدورهم حاجة مما أوتوا ويؤثرون على أنفسهم ولو كان بهم خصاصة ومن يوق شح نفسه فأولئك هم المفلحون}. أي من وقي البخل فإنه سيكون من المفلحين لا محالة، لأن كرمه سيسعى به للتوفيق لأن الله آخذ بيد السخي فلا بد أن يوفق لكل الطاعات. وعندما وقف علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه على طلحة بن عبيد الله رضي الله عنه يوم الجمل وهو قتيل بكى وأنشأ يقول: فتى كان يدنيه الغنى من صديقه إذا ما هو استغنى ويبعده الفقر فتى لا يعد المال ربا وهذا الخلق الكريم الذي ذكره علي رضي الله عنه في طلحة بن عبيد الله رضي الله عنه كان الناس يعرفون أنه من الأخلاق الحميدة حتى في الجاهلية ولذلك يقول رجل من بني م يعاتبني في الدين قومي وإنما ديوني في أشياء تكسبهم حمدا ألم يدر قومي كيف أوسر مرة وأعسر حتى تبلغ العسرة الجهدا فما زادني الإقتار منهم تقربا ولا زادني فضل الغنى منهمُ بعدا أسد به ما قد أخلوا وضيعوا وإن الذي بيني وبين بني أبي وبين بني عمي لمختلف جدا أراهم إلى نصري بطاء وإن همُ دعوني إلى نصر أجبتهمُ شدا ولا أحمل الحقد القديم عليهمُ وليس زعيم القوم من يحمل الحقدا لهم جل مالي إن تتابع بي غنى وإن قل مالي لم أكلفهمُ رفدا وإن أكلوا لحمي وفرت لحومهم وإن هدموا مجدي بنيت لهم مجدا إلى آخره.. وقد كان العرب في جاهليتهم يتحلون ببعض الأوصاف الحميدة، التي أقرها الشرع وهي من حسن الخلق، فكرم الضيافة والشجاعة والعفة هي من الأخلاق الحميدة، ولذلك فإن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه كان يأمر بتحفظ أشعار العرب لما فيها من المروءة فمثلا قول عنترة بن شداد العبسي في وصف نفسه وعفته: إني امرؤ سمح الخليقة ماجد لا أتبع النفس اللجوج هواها وأغض طرفي إن بدت لي جارتي حتى يواري جارتي مأواها أبني إن أباك كارب يومه فإذا دعيت إلى المكارم فاعجل والله فاتقه وأوف بنذره وإذا حلفت مباليا فتحلل واستغن ما أغناك ربك بالغنى وهكذا وقد كان كثير من الحكماء يوصون بكثير من الأخلاق الحميدة حتى في العصر الجاهلي وقد أقر ذلك الإسلام، ولا شك أن وصايا زهير بن أبي سلمى ولبيد بن ربيعة العامري رضي الله عنه محفوظة لدى كثير من المستمعين، وهي كلها تدل على أن الأخلاق الحميدة محبوبة لدى جميع الناس من مسلمهم وكافرهم وبرهم وفاجرهم، فكلهم يحبون الخلق الحسن ويكرهون الخلق الذميم، وذلك فطرة فطر الله الناس عليها جميعا، فكل من كان سيئ الخلق كان بغيضا لدى الناس حتى لو كان مسلما، وكل من كان حسن الخلق يحبه الناس في تعاملهم معه حتى لو كان كافرا، وقد كان عدد من المتصفين بالكفر على خلق فأحبهم الناس من أجل ذلك، فهذا عبد الله بن جدعان التيمي من بني تيم بن مرة من قريش كان كريم الخلق فأحبه الناس حبا شديدا، وقد أثنوا عليه ثناء عطرا، ومن ذلك ثناء أمية بن أبي الصلت الثقفي عليه وقد سمع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كثيرا منه، وكذلك نسأل الله سبحانه وتعالى أن يوفقنا لأحسن الأخلاق وأرضاها وأن يصرف عنا سيئها لا يهدي لأحسنها ولا يصرف سيئها إلا هو وصلى الله وسلم على نبينا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه أجمعين.
body_en:
In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate. Praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds. I pray for blessing and peace upon him who was sent as a mercy to the worlds, and upon his family and his Companions and whoever is guided by his guidance and takes his sunnah as his way until the Day of Judgement. Peace be upon you, and the mercy of God and His blessings.

To proceed: God, glorified and exalted, made the human being composed of three elements. The first is the intellect, by which he is honoured above the rest of the animals; the second is the body, which is from dust; and the third is the spirit, which is an unseen breath from the command of God. Each one of these three elements is capable of cultivation, of growth and of purification. As for the spirit, its growth and its purification come about only through its acquiring praiseworthy character traits and keeping clear of evil ones. A person's good character is evidence of the refinement of his spirit and the purity of his nature, and his bad character is evidence of the foulness of his inward disposition and of the foulness of his spirit — we ask God for safety and well-being.

Character is of two kinds: innate character and acquired character. Among the character traits there is that which is innate, which a person is created disposed towards and grows accustomed to, as the Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace, said: "The people of Yemen are coming to you. They are the purest of heart and the most tender of heart. Faith is Yemeni and wisdom is Yemeni." The acquired kind is that which a person accustoms himself to, struggling against his own soul until the trait is attained by him.

Good character is required by the Sharia and is among the highest priorities. For that reason God praised His Messenger, God bless him and grant him peace, for good character, saying: {And you are indeed of a magnificent character} (Sūrat al-Qalam 68:4). So whoever is of good character must necessarily be granted success in the loftiest acts of obedience, and likewise is chosen for the neighbourhood of the Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace, in the loftiest degrees of the Garden. And whoever is of bad character — we ask God for safety and well-being — is not granted success in the greatest acts of obedience, nor is he able to be among the true worshippers, because his bad character entails aversion towards him and his being driven away from the Presence and from the elevated station.

A person's acquisition of good character is accomplished only through his knowing the character traits of the believers, and what stands opposite them among the character traits of the unbelievers and the hypocrites, so that he strives to be characterised by the traits of the believers. The Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace, made that clear: he set out those character traits which, when combined, constitute hypocrisy, so that when they combine in a person he is a pure hypocrite. That is in the report (ḥadīth) of Abd Allah ibn Amr ibn al-As, may God be pleased with them both, that the Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Four traits, whoever has them in him is a pure hypocrite; and whoever has one trait of them in him has in him a trait of hypocrisy until he abandons it: when he speaks he lies, when he is entrusted he betrays, when he makes a covenant he acts treacherously, and when he disputes he behaves outrageously."

The Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace, likewise set out the marks of the hypocrite, saying: "The sign of the hypocrite is three: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks his promise, and when he is entrusted he betrays."

Standing opposite these are the traits of the people of faith (īmān). Among them is truthfulness, for it is one of the traits of faith, in view of what is established from the Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: "Truthfulness guides to righteousness, and righteousness guides to the Garden. A man continues to be truthful and to seek out truthfulness until he is written down with God as one who is truthful. And lying guides to wickedness, and wickedness guides to the Fire. A man continues to lie and to seek out lying until he is written down with God as a liar."

The Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace, likewise made clear that the character of this religion is modesty (ḥayāʾ), saying: "Every religion has a character, and the character of Islam is modesty." And he said of the man of the Ansar whom he heard admonishing his brother concerning modesty: "Leave him, for modesty is part of faith." It is likewise established from him, God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: "Modesty is a branch among the branches of faith."

The Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace, urged many lofty character traits, such as forbearance and deliberateness, making clear that these two are beloved to God, glorified be His majesty. He said to al-Ashajj of Abd al-Qays: "In you are two traits that God and His Messenger love: forbearance and deliberateness."

He likewise made clear that the believer does not lie — that is, he is not a liar by his nature. When he was asked, "Does the believer steal?" he said, "Yes." It was said, "Does the believer commit fornication?" He said, "Yes." It was said, "Does the believer lie?" He said, "No." What is intended by that is that he is not a liar, one who lies much; for that is not among the traits of the believers, but rather among the traits of the hypocrites.

*His open-handedness of manner entices one to the doing of noble deeds, and respect for him guards you from committing what is base.*

Likewise, among the benefits of good character is that it also brings about good companionship and its continuance. Relationships are something a person can build, but they are often severed because of a divergence of interests, or because of bad character, or something other than that. So if a person is of good character, the relationship he has built will continue, whether that be within his household and his family or in the environment around him. Everyone who is of good character — his relationship with his associates will continue; and everyone who is of bad character — no one will bear with him, and dealing with him will be burdensome.

Good character is likewise evidence of abundance of intellect and its completeness. The person who possesses an abundant intellect cannot be of bad character with people, because he has enough reflection to reach by it what people love, and by that he has influence over them; and he has no need of bad character in dealing with them, because he attains by gentleness what people seek to attain by other means.

Likewise, good character also requires of a person that he keep clear of many vices and raise himself above them, and by that his station is elevated and his worth is raised. For if a person is of bad character he will plunge into many vices because of his bad character and his bad dealing with people; and if he plunges into them, they summon him downward, and they are contrary to the raising of degrees. But if his character is good, he will please everyone. For that reason it has come down: "You will not be able to encompass people with your wealth, so encompass them with your good character." A person is able to distribute his good character among people and so win them all, even though his wealth be little and his means weak; his good character suffices to make people pleased with him.

And as for good character, the most important of it is good character with God, glorified be His majesty. For a person, if he — [the Arabic breaks off here in mid-sentence; see flags] — and it has been found by experience that if a person has friends among the people of truthfulness, sincere counsel and sincerity, it is possible for them to assist him towards good character and to refine his character by the removal of constraint and by accustoming him to intimacy. They are in the position of a mirror into which he looks and sees what is on his face of dirt. The wise man has said:

*The true friend is like water: it shows me its inmost thoughts when it is clear, and conceals them when it is turbid.*

And a person's reading of the qualities of the righteous, and what has come in the stories of the prophets in the Qur'an, and what has also come in the sunnah of the reports of the prophets, and — [the Arabic breaks off here and resumes on a different point; see flags] — so whoever is miserly or cowardly is characterised by bad character, and for that reason he is not fit for the leadership of people, nor for taking charge of the obligations laid upon them, before he is cured of this chronic disease with which he has been afflicted.

If a person bequeaths this bad character to his children he has wronged them with a continuing wrong; and if he accustoms them to good character and raises them upon it, they will be an extension of his own lifespan and his own uprightness.

Malik reported in the Muwatta that the Messiah, son of Mary, peace be upon him, passed through a narrow alley and a pig came towards him, and he said: "Pass in peace." It was said: "O prophet of God, do you say this to a pig?" He said: "I wished to accustom my tongue to the speaking of good." And he and the disciples passed by the carcass of a dog that had turned putrid, and the disciples said: "How foul is its smell!" and the Messiah, son of Mary, said: "How beautiful is the whiteness of its teeth!" He was spoken to about that, and he said: "I mentioned it by the best of what was in it." This is the accustoming of the soul to the best and most complete of character traits.

The Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace, likewise made clear what he approved of the character traits of the women of Quraysh, saying: "Take to the best of women — the righteous women of Quraysh: the most tender of them towards a child in his infancy, and the most careful of them over a husband in respect of what his hand possesses, and the most content of them with little." This contentment is a praiseworthy trait.

God likewise praised the Ansar for a praiseworthy trait, namely generosity. God, exalted be He, said: {And those who settled in the abode and in faith before them love whoever emigrated to them, and find in their breasts no need for what they have been given, and prefer others above themselves even though poverty be their own lot. And whoever is guarded against the avarice of his own soul — those are the ones who prosper} (Sūrat al-Ḥashr 59:9). That is, whoever is guarded against miserliness will inevitably be among those who prosper, because his generosity will strive to bring him success, for God takes the hand of the generous man, so he must necessarily be granted success in all acts of obedience.

When Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, stood over Talha ibn Ubayd Allah, may God be pleased with him, on the Day of the Camel, and he lay slain, he wept and began to recite:

*A young man whom wealth would bring near to his friend when he was in easy circumstances, and whom poverty would take far from him; a young man who did not reckon wealth a lord...*

This noble trait which Ali, may God be pleased with him, mentioned of Talha ibn Ubayd Allah, may God be pleased with him, was one that people recognised as being among the praiseworthy character traits even in the age before Islam. For that reason a man of the Banu M— says:

*My people reproach me over debt, yet my debts are in matters that earn them praise. Did my people not know how I am at one time in easy circumstances and at another in straitened ones, until hardship reaches its utmost? Straitened means has not increased my drawing near to them, nor has abundance of wealth increased my distance from them. With it I repair what they have left undone and squandered. What is between me and my father's sons and my uncle's sons is greatly at variance: I see them slow to help me, yet if they call me to help them I answer them at a run. I do not bear the old rancour against them, and the chief of a people is not one who bears rancour. The greater part of my wealth is theirs if wealth comes to me in succession, and if my wealth is little I do not burden them with a gift. If they eat my flesh, I make their flesh abundant; and if they demolish my glory, I build glory for them* — and so on to the end.

The Arabs in the age before Islam used to adorn themselves with certain praiseworthy qualities which the Sharia affirmed and which are part of good character. Generosity in hospitality, courage and chastity are among the praiseworthy traits. For that reason Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, used to give the command that the poetry of the Arabs be memorised, for the manly virtue it contains. For example, the saying of Antarah ibn Shaddad al-Absi in describing himself and his chastity:

*I am a man of generous nature, noble; I do not follow the obstinate soul in its desire. I lower my gaze if my woman neighbour appears to me, until her dwelling conceals her.*

*My son, your father's day is drawing to its close, so when you are called to noble deeds, make haste. And fear God, and fulfil his vow; and if you have sworn an oath taking it seriously, then absolve yourself of it. And be free of want so long as your Lord has made you free of want by wealth* — and so on.

Many of the wise used to counsel many praiseworthy character traits even in the age before Islam, and Islam affirmed that. There is no doubt that the counsels of Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma and of Labid ibn Rabiah al-Amiri, may God be pleased with him, are memorised by many of the listeners. All of them indicate that praiseworthy character traits are beloved to all people — the Muslim among them and the unbeliever, the righteous among them and the corrupt. All of them love good character and hate blameworthy character, and that is a natural disposition (fiṭrah) upon which God created all people. So everyone who is of bad character is detestable to people even if he is a Muslim, and everyone who is of good character is loved by people in their dealings with him even if he is an unbeliever.

A number of those characterised by unbelief were possessed of character, and people loved them on that account. Thus Abd Allah ibn Judan al-Taymi, of the Banu Taym ibn Murrah of Quraysh, was of generous character, and people loved him with an intense love and praised him with fragrant praise. Among that is the praise of Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt al-Thaqafi for him, much of which the Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace, heard.

And likewise we ask God, glorified and exalted, to grant us success in the best of character traits and the most pleasing of them, and to turn away from us the evil of them — none guides to the best of them and none turns away the evil of them but He. And may God bless and grant peace to our Prophet Muhammad and to his family and his Companions all together.

This is a complete lecture transcript (dars), not a Friday sermon: it opens with the basmalah, the greeting of peace and 'ammā baʿd', and closes with a supplication and the prayer upon the Prophet. It has no two-part sermon structure and no closing sermon formulae, so it is typed as a transcript rather than a khuṭbah.

The source carries two lacunae where the transcript breaks off in mid-sentence and resumes on another point. Both are left visible in the English and flagged; nothing has been supplied to bridge them. The first is the more serious, because the passage lost is the one the Sheikh had just announced as the most important: good character towards God.

The Sheikh here reports praiseworthy conduct among the Arabs before Islam and among named non-Muslims (Abd Allah ibn Judan). These are reported as instances of character that the Sharia affirmed; they are not statements about the standing of those persons in the hereafter, and the English keeps them as descriptive reports.

title_ar: الوحدة الإسلامية وخطر التفرق
title_en: Islamic Unity and the Danger of Division
body_ar: إن الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينه ، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا ومن سيئات أعمالنا من يهده الله فلا مضل له ومن يضلل فلا هادي له ، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له وأشهد أن محمدا عبده ورسوله صلى الله عليه وعلى آله وأصحابه وسلم تسليما كثيرا (يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اتَّقُوا رَبَّكُمُ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ مِنْ نَفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ وَخَلَقَ مِنْهَا زَوْجَهَا وَبَثَّ مِنْهُمَا رِجَالًا كَثِيرًا وَنِسَاءً وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ الَّذِي تَسَاءَلُونَ بِهِ وَالْأَرْحَامَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَلَيْكُمْ رَقِيبًا) (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آَمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَقُولُوا قَوْلًا سَدِيدًا (70) يُصْلِحْ لَكُمْ أَعْمَالَكُمْ وَيَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ ذُنُوبَكُمْ وَمَنْ يُطِعِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ فَقَدْ فَازَ فَوْزًا عَظِيمًا)
body_en:
All praise belongs to God. We praise Him and seek His help, and we take refuge in God from the evil of our own selves and from our evil deeds. Whomever God guides, none can lead astray; whomever He leads astray, none can guide. I bear witness that there is no god but God alone, who has no partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger — may God bless him, his family and his Companions, and grant them abundant peace.

{O people, be mindful of your Lord, who created you from a single soul, and created from it its mate, and spread from the two of them many men and women. Be mindful of God, in whose name you make demands of one another, and of the ties of kinship. God is ever watching over you.} (Sūrat al-Nisāʾ 4:1)

{O you who believe, be mindful of God and speak with words that are true and sound (70). He will set your deeds right for you and forgive you your sins. Whoever obeys God and His Messenger has won a great triumph.} (Sūrat al-Aḥzāb 33:70–71)
