This is better for him, and this is what adheres to the sunnah of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.

(And in general, tawassul belongs properly to jurisprudence (fiqh) and not to the articles of creed.)

flags.arabic: و عموما فإن التوسل صريح في الفقه و ليس في العقائد
flags.context: The parenthesis closing the fatwa.
options: And in general, tawassul belongs properly to jurisprudence (fiqh) and not to the articles of creed.
And in general, tawassul is treated explicitly in the books of jurisprudence and not in the works of creed.
And in general, the question of tawassul is a clear-cut matter of jurisprudence rather than of creed.
flags.note: HIGH SIGNIFICANCE. صريح can mean 'belongs properly / is strictly' or 'is explicitly treated'. On reading 0 the Sheikh is placing the whole tawassul dispute outside creed — a substantive position with real consequences, since it bears on whether error in it touches a person's belief. On reading 1 he is only remarking where the topic is discussed in the literature. The two are not equivalent and the translator cannot settle between them. The Sheikh's office should confirm.

flags.context: لقد قدمت لأحد المشايخ طلبا لطريقته فأعطانيها مصحوبة بشروط
options: a request to be admitted to his Sufi order (ṭarīqah)
a request for his ṭarīqah (spiritual path)
a request for his method of devotion
flags.note: The conditions the questioner describes — a covenant, secrecy, a bond of service to the shaykh until his death — are the marks of initiation into a Sufi ṭarīqah. Option 2 is neutral but loses the institutional sense on which the question turns. The Sheikh himself does not name the order, and does not comment on ṭarīqah affiliation as such; nothing to that effect has been added.

flags.arabic: ويجب أيضا على المنصوح أن ينصح بها دائما
flags.context: فهذه النصائح تجب على الشيخ أن ينصح بها ويجب أيضا على المنصوح أن ينصح بها دائما
options: and the one counselled is obliged to be counselled with them always
and the one counselled is obliged to pass them on as counsel always
and the one counselled is obliged to keep being reminded of them
flags.note: The verb ينصح is used twice with different subjects and the second is ambiguous between passive ('be counselled') and active ('give counsel'). The sentence as printed is awkward and may be a transcription slip from a spoken original. Rendered literally; a reviewer with the audio should resolve it.

translator_notes: This is a complete written fatwa: the questioner's account followed by the Sheikh's answer. The two are not separated by any marker in the Arabic source — the answer begins at إن هذه النصائح. The labels QUESTION and ANSWER have been added in the English for legibility and are editorial, not the Sheikh's.

Rulings actually given here, with their exact force: visiting graves in general is 'recommended' (mandūb); the innovated visitation described is 'without doubt manifest shirk'; seeking nearness through another person's deeds is 'not lawful for you'. None has been strengthened or softened, and no ruling word has been supplied where he used none.
The hadith «Religion is sincere counsel» is given without a named collection; none has been added.
The source spells ذلك as ذالك throughout and omits some spaces (e.g. كنت.أما); body_ar preserves the source exactly.

title_ar: فتاوي في العقيدة
title_en: Fatwas on Creed
body_ar:
الجمع بين الحديث: إن الله لا يقبض العلم انتزاعا، والقول إن القرآن يمحى من المصاحف والصدور في ليلة من الليالي كيف يمكن الجمع بين الحديث: إن الله لا يقبض العلم انتزاعا، والقول إن القرآن يمحى من المصاحف والصدور في ليلة من الليالي؟

هذا إنما يكون في آخر الزمان عندما يرفع العلم ويكثر الجهل ويبقى القرآن للتبرك فقط ولا يبقى للعلم، فإن القرآن من رفعه أن يبقى للتبرك فقط فيبقى رقى تعلق على المجانين والمصابين أو زخارف تزين بها البيوت ويهجر العمل به والحكم به في النهار ويهجر القيام به في الليل، فهذا من رفعه وقد شاهدتم بعض ذلك.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

الختمة للميت

هل تجوز الختمة للميت أم لا و هي التي تسمى بالسلكة؟ إن وصول ثواب القرءان للميت بعد موته محل خلاف بين أهل العلم فمذهب مالك والشافعي أنه لا يصل وذلك أن الأصل قول الله تعالى ﴿أم لم ينبأ بما في صحف موسى وإبراهيم الذي وفى أن لا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى وأن ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى وأن سعيه سوف يرى ثم يجزاه الجزاء الأوفى﴾ فعلى هذا الأصل لا يصل هذا العمل بعد الموت أما أبو حنيفة وأحمد فذهبا إلى وصوله قياسا لقراءة القرءان على الصدقة و الحج و العمرة وغير ذلك من أنواع القرب وقد اتفق على أن الصدقة و الدعاء يصلان قطعا وما عداهما كله داخل في الخلاف لأن الصدقة والدعاء ثبت فيهما الأحاديث الصحيحة عن النبي صلى الله عليه و سلم وكذلك الحج و العمرة ثبت فيهما الأحاديث الصحيحة أما ما سوى ذلك كله فلم يرد فيه نص عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ويبقي الخلاف هل هذا من المقدرات التي لا يدخلها القياس أو ليس من المقدرات فيمكن القياس فيه هذا محل خلاف أصولي لا يمكن حسمه و على هذا فالذين يفعلون الختمة عن دبر الميت ويريدون إيصالها إليه فالأحوط بهم والأفضل لهم أن يتصدقوا عنه و أن يدعوا له فهذا الذي يصل بلا خلاف.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

الخسف الذي سيقع في الشرق والغرب وجزيرة العرب

ما هو الخسف الذي سيقع في الشرق والغرب وجزيرة العرب؟

الخسف هو الزلزال الذي يقتضي أن يدخل وجه الأرض تحت بعض طبقاتها وهذا من أشد أنواع الزلازل، ووقع كثير من الخسوف في مشارق الأرض ومغاربها، ولكن لا يمكن الجزم بأن خسفا من هذه الخسوف هو المقصود في الحديث، وإن كانت ثلاثة خسوف قد جاءت متقاربة أحدها بالمشرق والآخر بالمغرب والآخر بجزيرة العرب، فالذي حصل في المشرق هو الخسف الذي سمعتم به في إيران والخسف الذي حصل بالمغرب هو خسف مدينة الأصنام بالجزائر، والخسف الذي بجزيرة العرب هو خسف مدينة الذمار باليمن، ولكن لا يمكن الجزم بأنها هي المقصودة في الحديث بل هذه آيات كلها ومواعظ، والله تعالى يقول: {وَمَا نُرْسِلُ بِالْآَيَاتِ إِلَّا تَخْوِيفًا (59)} [الإسراء] وهي تذكير للعباد بالإيمان بالله سبحانه وتعالى وحده، ولكن لا يجزم بأنها هي المقصودة بالحديث لأنه لم يرد ما يدل على خصوص ذلك.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

الذكر عند شيخ مخصوص

اشتراط أخذ الذكر عن شيخ واحد مخصوص؟ أن الذكر مثل غيره من أمور الدين يؤخذ عن كل من رواه و كل من نقله والآن يؤخذ من الكتب أيضا فإذا رجع الإنسان إلى صحيح البخاري أو صحيح مسلم أو الموطأ أو إلى كتب الأذكار فأخذ منها هذه الأذكار فذلك كاف فليس هو ذا خصوصية زائدة على ما في الأحكام كلها.
body_en:
Reconciling the hadith 'God does not take knowledge away by snatching it out' with the statement that the Qur'an will be erased from the written copies and from people's breasts on one of the nights. How can one reconcile the hadith 'God does not take knowledge away by snatching it out' with the statement that the Qur'an will be erased from the written copies and from people's breasts on one of the nights?

This will only be at the end of time, when knowledge is taken up and ignorance becomes widespread, and the Qur'an remains only as a thing to seek blessing by and no longer remains for knowledge. For part of the Qur'an's being taken up is that it should remain only as a thing to seek blessing by — so that it remains as charms hung on the insane and the afflicted, or as ornaments with which houses are decorated, while acting by it and judging by it in the daytime is abandoned, and standing in prayer with it at night is abandoned. This is part of its being taken up; and you have witnessed some of that.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The khatmah for the deceased

Is the khatmah for the deceased permissible or not — the one that is called al-salkah?

Whether the reward of [reciting] the Qur'an reaches the deceased after his death is a point on which the scholars differ. The position (madhhab) of Malik and al-Shafi'i is that it does not reach him, on the ground that the governing principle is the words of God, exalted is He: {Or has he not been told of what is in the scrolls of Moses, and of Abraham who fulfilled [what he was charged with] — that no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another, and that a person shall have nothing but what he has striven for, and that his striving shall be seen, and then he shall be repaid for it with the fullest repayment} (Sūrat al-Najm 53:36–41). On this principle, this act does not reach him after death. As for Abu Hanifah and Ahmad, they held that it does reach him, by analogical reasoning (qiyās) from the recitation of the Qur'an to voluntary charity (ṣadaqah), to hajj, to the lesser pilgrimage (ʿumrah), and to the other kinds of acts of nearness to God. There is agreement that charity and supplication reach [the deceased] with certainty, and everything besides these two falls within the disagreement — because for charity and supplication sound hadiths (ṣaḥīḥ) from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, are established, and likewise for hajj and ʿumrah sound hadiths are established, whereas for everything other than all of that no explicit text (naṣṣ) has come from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. So the disagreement remains: is this among the fixed, quantified matters (al-muqaddarāt), into which analogical reasoning does not enter, or is it not among the fixed matters, so that analogy is possible in it? This is a point of disagreement in legal theory (uṣūl) that cannot be settled. Accordingly, those who perform the khatmah following upon the death of the deceased and wish to convey it to him — the more cautious and the better course for them is to give charity on his behalf and to supplicate for him, for that is what reaches him with no disagreement at all.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The sinking of the earth that will occur in the East, in the West and in the Arabian Peninsula

What is the sinking of the earth that will occur in the East, in the West and in the Arabian Peninsula?

The khasf is the earthquake that causes the face of the earth to go down beneath some of its own layers, and this is among the most severe kinds of earthquake. Many such sinkings have occurred in the easts and the wests of the earth, but it is not possible to assert with certainty that any one of these sinkings is the one meant in the hadith — even though three sinkings did come close together, one of them in the East, another in the West and another in the Arabian Peninsula. The one that occurred in the East is the sinking you have heard of in Iran; the sinking that occurred in the West is the sinking of the city of al-Asnam in Algeria; and the sinking in the Arabian Peninsula is the sinking of the city of Dhamar in Yemen. But it is not possible to assert with certainty that these are the ones meant in the hadith. Rather, these are all of them signs and admonitions, and God, exalted is He, says: {And We do not send the signs except to instil fear (59)} [Sūrat al-Isrāʾ 17:59]. They are a reminder to God's servants to believe in God, glorified and exalted, alone. But one does not assert with certainty that they are the ones meant by the hadith, because nothing has come that would indicate that specifically.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Taking the formulae of remembrance from one particular shaykh

On making it a condition that the formulae of remembrance (dhikr) be taken from one single, particular shaykh?

The remembrance of God is like the other matters of religion: it is taken from everyone who has narrated it and everyone who has transmitted it, and nowadays it is taken from books as well. So if a person turns to Sahih al-Bukhari, or Sahih Muslim, or the Muwatta', or to the books of the formulae of remembrance, and takes these formulae from them, that is sufficient. It has no special character over and above what holds for all the rulings.

flags.context: هل تجوز الختمة للميت أم لا و هي التي تسمى بالسلكة؟
options: al-salkah — a complete recitation of the Qur'an dedicated to a deceased person
the 'threading' — a communal recitation in which the Qur'an is divided among those present and completed in one sitting
a Qur'an-completion gathering held for the dead
flags.note: Mauritanian/Shinqiti regional term, glossed by the questioner himself as the local name for the khatmah. Whether it denotes specifically the practice of dividing the text among a gathering so that it is completed at once (the sense the root س-ل-ك, 'to thread', suggests), or any dedicated completion, determines whether the term should be translated or kept in transliteration. The Sheikh's office should confirm the local practice before a fixed rendering is chosen. Comparable to the الكيص case in the style guide.

flags.arabic: هذا محل خلاف أصولي لا يمكن حسمه
flags.context: هل هذا من المقدرات التي لا يدخلها القياس أو ليس من المقدرات فيمكن القياس فيه هذا محل خلاف أصولي لا يمكن حسمه
options: This is a point of disagreement in legal theory that cannot be settled
This is a disagreement in legal theory that admits of no decisive resolution
This is a theoretical disagreement on which no ruling can be given
flags.note: CRITICAL FOR DISPLAY. The Sheikh explicitly declines to settle this question. His closing advice — that charity and supplication are 'the more cautious and the better course' (al-aḥwaṭ ... wa-l-afḍal) — is a recommendation, NOT a ruling that the khatmah is forbidden or invalid. The English must not be presented or summarised in any way that converts it into a prohibition. Option 2 is rejected because it overstates: he declines to settle the uṣūl question, not to give any guidance at all.

flags.context: فالذين يفعلون الختمة عن دبر الميت ويريدون إيصالها إليه
options: following upon the death of the deceased
on behalf of the deceased after his death
at the conclusion of the rites for the deceased
flags.note: عن دبر idiomatically means 'immediately following'. Whether it points to the moment of death or to the end of the funeral rites is not determinable from the text, and the difference matters for describing the practice accurately.

flags.context: هل هذا من المقدرات التي لا يدخلها القياس
options: the fixed, quantified matters (al-muqaddarāt)
the matters whose measure is divinely fixed and so closed to analogy
the prescribed quantities
flags.note: A technical uṣūl category not in the project glossary: rulings whose amounts or forms are set by revelation and therefore, on one view, not extendable by qiyās. It should be added to the glossary, since the whole argument of this fatwa turns on it.

translator_notes: Qur'anic renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic text of the Qur'an.

Four separate fatwas on one page, divided in the source by rules of hyphens. The rules are preserved in both body_ar and body_en so the boundaries survive; the site should render them as four separate items.
In the first item the heading and the question are identical in the Arabic and are printed one after the other. This duplication is in the source and has been kept.

Attribution of positions on the khatmah is load-bearing and has been kept exact: NOT reaching the deceased is attributed to Malik and al-Shafi'i; reaching him by analogy is attributed to Abu Hanifah and Ahmad; charity and supplication reaching him is reported as agreed by all. None of these is presented as the Sheikh's own position, and he states that the underlying question cannot be settled.

In the second and fourth items the question and the answer run together in a single paragraph with no marker in the Arabic. A paragraph break has been introduced in the English at the point where the answer begins; this is editorial.
Al-Asnam is the Algerian city now called Chlef, and Dhamar is in Yemen. The Sheikh names them without dates, and no dates or identifications of the earthquakes have been added.
مدينة الذمار in the source carries a definite article not normally written with the place name Dhamar; body_ar preserves the source.

title_ar: الذي يصل للميت و الذي لا يصله
title_en: What Reaches the Dead and What Does Not
body_ar:
ما يعرف عندنا بالتوفية للأموات أي قراءة سورة الإخلاص إحدى عشرة مرة ليلة الجمعة و إرسال ثوابها للأموات هل يصل إليهم؟و هل هو ثابت في السنة أم لا؟

هذا لم يرد في السنة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم و من المعلوم أن الخير هو ما جاء به النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من عند الله و أن ما لم يأت به لا خير فيه و قراءة القرآن و إهداء ثوابه للأموات محل خلاف بين أهل العلم فمذهب مالك و الشافعي أنه لا يصل و الغريب أن أهل هذه البلاد مالكيون و مع ذلك نجد هذه العادة منتشرة فيهم و مذهب مالك أنه لا يصل مذهب مالك أن القرآءة لا تصل الأموات والذي يصل هو الدعاء و الصدقة و قد قال مولود رحمه الله: أجر الطعام و الدعا إن بذلا للميت لا خلاف في أن يصلا

و مع ذلك مذهب أبي حنيفة و ابن حنبل أن قراءة القرآن و إهداء ثوابه للميت إذا كان الإهداء سابقا على القراءة فإنه يصل قياسا على الصدقة و الدعاء و هذا الذي يسمى بالتلحيق عندهم و هو أن يقول الإنسان قبل قراءته اللهم اجعل ثواب ما سأقرأ و بركة ما سأتلو هدية مني نازلة و رحمة منك واصلة إلى فلان و يذكره فيكون هذا إهداء لذلك العمل إليه

و الحنابلة و الحنفية قاسوا هذا على الحج و العمرة فقد أذن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بالحج و العمرة عن الأموات فقد أخرج البخاري في الصحيح من حديث أنس بن مالك رضي الله عنه أن رجلا من الأنصار أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: إن أمي ماتت و لم تحج أفأحج عنها ؟ قال: حج عن أمك و في رواية حج عن أمك و اعتمر و هي لأبي داوود في السنن و كذلك في حديث الخثعمية أنها قالت: يارسول الله : إن فريضة الله بالحج أدركت أبي شيخا كبيرا لا يمسك نفسه على الرحل أفأحج عنه قال: أرايت لو كان على أبيك دين أكنت قاضيته قالت نعم قال: فأدوا الذي عليه فدين الله أحق بالوفاء و سمع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم رجلا يقول: لبيك اللهم عن شبرمة فقال: أحججت عن نفسك قال: لا قال:فاحجج عن نفسك ثم عن شبرمة و سمع آخر يقول لبيك اللهم عن عرفطة فقال: أحججت عن نفسك قال: لا قال: فاحجج عن نفسك ثم عن عرفطة

و هذا يقتضي جواز الحج عن الأموات و الأحياء أيضا بالنيابة إذا كانوا عاجزين عن الوصول لكن قياس القراءة على الحج مشكل لأن الحج فيه عمل بدني و عمل قلبي و عمل قولي و عمل مالي و القراءة هي مجرد عمل قولي و عمل قلبي و ليس فيها شيء من عمل بقية البدن و لا شيء من المال فلذلك قياسها قياس مع وجود الفارق فالراحج عدم وصولها
body_en:
What is known among us as al-tawfiyah for the dead — that is, reciting Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ eleven times on the night before Friday and sending its reward to the dead: does it reach them? And is it established in the sunnah or not?

This has not come down in the sunnah from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. It is well known that the good is what the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought from God, and that whatever he did not bring has no good in it. Reciting the Qur'an and making a gift of its reward to the dead is a point of disagreement among the scholars. The position of Malik and al-Shafi'i is that it does not reach them. What is strange is that the people of this country are Malikis, and yet we find this custom widespread among them, while Malik's position is that it does not reach. Malik's position is that the recitation does not reach the dead, and that what does reach them is supplication and voluntary charity (ṣadaqah). Mawlud, may God have mercy on him, said: *The reward of food and of supplication, if they are given on the dead man's behalf — there is no disagreement that the two reach him.*

Even so, the position of Abu Hanifah and Ibn Hanbal is that reciting the Qur'an and making a gift of its reward to the deceased does reach him, if the gift precedes the recitation, by analogical reasoning (qiyās) from charity and supplication. This is what they call al-talḥīq, namely that a person says, before he recites: 'O God, make the reward of what I am about to recite and the blessing of what I am about to recite a gift from me, sent down, and a mercy from You, arriving, to so-and-so' — and he names him. This then constitutes a gift of that act to him.

The Hanbalis and the Hanafis drew this analogy from hajj and the lesser pilgrimage (ʿumrah), for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, permitted hajj and ʿumrah on behalf of the dead. Al-Bukhari recorded in the Ṣaḥīḥ, from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik, may God be pleased with him, that a man of the Ansar came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: 'My mother has died and did not perform hajj; shall I perform hajj on her behalf?' He said: 'Perform hajj on behalf of your mother.' In another narration: 'Perform hajj on behalf of your mother, and perform ʿumrah' — and that narration is Abu Dawud's, in the Sunan. Likewise in the hadith of the woman of Khathʿam, that she said: 'O Messenger of God, God's obligation of hajj has come upon my father as a very old man who cannot hold himself up on the mount; shall I perform hajj on his behalf?' He said: 'Tell me: if your father owed a debt, would you not have paid it?' She said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Then discharge what is owed by him, for God's debt has the better right to be discharged.' And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard a man saying: 'Here I am, O God, on behalf of Shubrumah.' He said: 'Have you performed hajj for yourself?' He said: 'No.' He said: 'Then perform hajj for yourself, and then for Shubrumah.' And he heard another saying: 'Here I am, O God, on behalf of ʿArfaṭah.' He said: 'Have you performed hajj for yourself?' He said: 'No.' He said: 'Then perform hajj for yourself, and then for ʿArfaṭah.'

This entails the permissibility of performing hajj on behalf of the dead, and on behalf of the living as well, by proxy, when they are unable to make the journey. But the analogy of recitation to hajj is problematic, because hajj contains bodily action, action of the heart, verbal action and financial action, whereas recitation is merely verbal action and action of the heart: there is nothing in it of the action of the rest of the body, and nothing of wealth. Its analogy is therefore an analogy drawn where a relevant difference is present. So the stronger view is that it does not reach them.

flags.context: ما يعرف عندنا بالتوفية للأموات أي قراءة سورة الإخلاص إحدى عشرة مرة ليلة الجمعة و إرسال ثوابها للأموات
options: al-tawfiyah — the local name for reciting Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ eleven times on the night before Friday and dedicating the reward to the dead
the 'discharging' (al-tawfiyah) — a reward-dedication rite performed for the dead
the completion-recitation for the dead
flags.note: Mauritanian regional term, glossed by the questioner himself ('what is known among us as…'). The English keeps the Arabic term because there is no settled English name for the practice. The Sheikh's office should confirm whether al-tawfiyah names this specific eleven-fold recitation or a wider family of rites.

flags.context: و هذا الذي يسمى بالتلحيق عندهم و هو أن يقول الإنسان قبل قراءته اللهم اجعل ثواب ما سأقرأ
options: al-talḥīq — dedicating the reward in advance of the recitation
the 'attaching' of the reward
prior assignment of the reward
flags.note: A Hanafi/Hanbali term of art reported here by the Sheikh, not his own usage ('what they call'). The attribution must remain visible in any rendering.

flags.context: و قد قال مولود رحمه الله: أجر الطعام و الدعا إن بذلا للميت لا خلاف في أن يصلا
options: Mawlud — a Mauritanian author of didactic verse, cited by first name only
Muhammad Mawlud al-Yaqubi al-Shinqiti, the Mauritanian versifier
an unidentified scholar named Mawlud
flags.note: The Sheikh cites the poet by a single name, as is normal in the Shinqiti tradition where the naẓm is common knowledge. The English does not supply an identification; the Sheikh's office should confirm which Mawlud and which naẓm the line comes from before any note is added for readers.

translator_notes: Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.
The single line of verse quoted from Mawlud is rendered as prose in italics per house style; no attempt has been made at rhymed English. The Arabic should be displayed alongside it.

Three spelling slips in the source have been preserved verbatim in body_ar and not carried into the English: القرآءة for القراءة, الدعا for الدعاء (inside the line of verse, where it may be metrical licence), and فالراحج for فالراجح in the closing sentence. The last of these is the word that carries the Sheikh's own conclusion, so it should be confirmed against another copy before publication.

The clause 'و مذهب مالك أنه لا يصل مذهب مالك أن القرآءة لا تصل الأموات' repeats itself in the source. The repetition has been kept in the Arabic and rendered once as a restatement in the English, which is how it reads.
The Sheikh gives al-Bukhari for the hadith of Anas and Abu Dawud's Sunan for the second narration, and gives no grading for the remaining reports. No grading has been supplied.

title_ar: الرقى والتمائم
title_en: Incantations and Amulets
body_ar:
سائلة عن مرض (السَّل المَصْ) الشعبي وعندها قرن كبش وفيه حكمة سوداء ومعه تزلوميت، فالقرن يدخل في ماء ويشربه المصاب بالسَّل، فيشفى بإذن الله، وأما التزلوميت فتستعمل للمرأة التي استعصى عليها النفاس فما هو حكم الشرع في ذلك مع العلم أنها تستخدمه لمنافع المسلمين وهي تعلم عدم مضرته أو نفعه إلا بإذن الله؟

أن هذه الرقى كانت قديمة وكانت من أمر الجاهلية فقال النبي (ص): «اعرضوا علي رقاكم» فما كان فيها فيه تعظيم لله وذكر له أقره النبي (ص)، وما كان غير ذلك رده ونهى عنه، فكل ما لا يعرف الإنسان معناه لا يحل له الرقية به،

وبالنسبة لهذه الأمور المجسمات كالقرون وما يسمى بالتزلوميت ونحو ذلك لا يحل استعماله لأن الإنسان لا يدري ما فيه، وإذا دراه فهو أمور ظاهرها مثل ظاهر السحر لأنها مجسمات وأمور من هذا القبيل، فلذلك هذا النوع يضر ولا ينفع، وما يشاهد منه من النفع العاجل كالشفاء من مرض من الأمراض إنما هو فتنة لأن الإنسان سيتعلق به ويظن أنه يشفي أو ينفع فهو فتنة يفتن الله بها،

ونحن الآن ننتظر الدجال فعلينا أن نحذر من مثل هذه الأمور، فإذا كان الإنسان يحذر فتنة المسيح الدجال فليعلم أن الدجال يحيي الموتى، يناديهم فيقومون من قبورهم، ويمر بالقرية الخربة فتتبعه كنوزها كيعاسيب النحل، ويأتي أهل قرية وهم مسنتون في غاية الجهد فيصدقونه فيأمر السماء فتمطر ويأمر الأرض فتنبت، فتروح عليهم مواشيهم أسمن ما كانت ضروعا، ويمر على أهل قرية مخصبين فيكذبونه، فيأمر السماء فتمسك ويأمر الأرض فتقحل فتروح عليهم مواشيهم وهي أشد ما تكون لأواء،

فإذا عرفنا هذا وعرفنا أن هذه الأمور المشاهدات الدنيوية إنما هي فتن يجريها الله تعالى كما يجري أشد منها على يد المسيح الدجال، فعلى الإنسان أن لا يغتر بها وأن يعلم أن الفتن موجودة، وأن تقليد الإنسان في اتباعها، وشهادته بأن القضية هي مجرد مشاهدة أن هذا شربه فلان فبرئ وعلق على فلانة فبرئت، فهذا النوع إنما هو من الفتن التي على الإنسان أن يحذرها لأنه لو كان كل من يبرئ مريضا يتبع لكان الدجال أحق بهذا فهو يحيي الموتى، فلذلك لا بد من الحذر غاية الحذر من هذا النوع ومن خطره العقدي المؤثر على عقائد الناس،

ولنعلم أن الله سبحانه وتعالى آتانا ما فيه الشفاء والنور، فأنزل علينا هذا القرآن المبين الذي لا يأتيه الباطل من بين يديه ولا من خلفه تنزيل من حكيم حميد، وهو حبل الله المتين وصراطه المستقيم، من تمسك به عصم، ومن تركه من جبار قصم الله ظهره، وقد قال الله تعالى: { وَنُنَزِّلُ مِنَ الْقُرْآَنِ مَا هُوَ شِفَاءٌ وَرَحْمَةٌ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ} وقال: {وَإِذَا قَرَأْتَ الْقُرْآَنَ جَعَلْنَا بَيْنَكَ وَبَيْنَ الَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْآَخِرَةِ حِجَابًا مَسْتُورًا وَجَعَلْنَا عَلَى قُلُوبِهِمْ أَكِنَّةً أَنْ يَفْقَهُوهُ وَفِي آَذَانِهِمْ وَقْرًا وَإِذَا ذَكَرْتَ رَبَّكَ فِي الْقُرْآَنِ وَحْدَهُ وَلَّوْا عَلَى أَدْبَارِهِمْ نُفُورًا} وقال تعالى: { وَلَوْ أَنَّ قُرْآَنًا سُيِّرَتْ بِهِ الْجِبَالُ أَوْ قُطِّعَتْ بِهِ الْأَرْضُ أَوْ كُلِّمَ بِهِ الْمَوْتَى بَلْ لِلَّهِ الْأَمْرُ جَمِيعًا} فلذلك علينا أن نكتفي بكتاب الله تعالى، وأن نلتمس فيه الهدى، وأن نحذر من هذه الشواغل التي تشغل عنه.
body_en:
A woman asks about the folk illness (al-sall al-maṣṣ). She has a ram's horn with a black ḥikmah in it, and with it a tazlūmīt. The horn is put into water and the one afflicted with al-sall drinks it and is cured, by God's leave. As for the tazlūmīt, it is used for a woman whose post-natal period has become obstructed. What is the ruling of the Sharia on that, bearing in mind that she uses it for the benefit of Muslims and knows that it neither harms nor benefits except by God's leave?

These incantations (ruqā) are old, and were part of the business of the age of ignorance. The Prophet, upon whom be peace, said: 'Present your incantations to me.' Whatever in them contained the magnification of God and remembrance of Him, the Prophet, upon whom be peace, confirmed; and whatever was otherwise, he rejected and forbade. So everything whose meaning a person does not know, it is not lawful for him to use as an incantation.

As for these physical objects — such as horns, and what is called the tazlūmīt, and the like — it is not lawful to use them, because a person does not know what is in them; and if he does know, they are things whose outward appearance is like the outward appearance of sorcery, because they are physical objects and matters of that sort. This kind of thing therefore harms and does not benefit. And whatever immediate benefit is observed from it, such as recovery from one illness or another, is only a trial, because a person will become attached to it and suppose that it heals or benefits. It is a trial by which God tries people.

We are now awaiting the Dajjal, so we must be on our guard against things of this kind. If a person is to be on his guard against the trial of the False Messiah, let him know that the Dajjal brings the dead to life: he calls them and they rise from their graves; he passes by the ruined village and its treasures follow him like swarms of bees; he comes to the people of a village who are in drought and in the utmost distress, and they believe him, so he commands the sky and it rains, and commands the earth and it brings forth growth, and their livestock come home to them in the evening with their udders fuller than they have ever been; and he passes by the people of a village who are in plenty, and they call him a liar, so he commands the sky and it withholds, and commands the earth and it goes barren, and their livestock come home to them in the evening in the worst hardship they have ever known.

So when we know this, and know that these worldly things that are seen are only trials that God, exalted, brings about — just as He brings about what is far graver than them at the hand of the False Messiah — then a person must not be deceived by them, and must know that trials exist. A person's following them without examination, and his testimony that the matter is simply something observed — that so-and-so drank this and recovered, and it was hung on such-and-such a woman and she recovered — this kind of thing is only one of the trials a person must be on his guard against; for if everyone who cures a sick person were to be followed, the Dajjal would have the better claim to that, since he brings the dead to life. Hence the utmost caution is required against this kind of thing, and against its danger to creed, which affects what people believe.

And let us know that God, glorified and exalted, has given us that in which there is healing and light, and has sent down upon us this clear Qur'an, which falsehood does not approach from before it or from behind it, a revelation from One All-Wise, Praiseworthy. It is God's firm rope and His straight path: whoever holds fast to it is preserved, and whoever abandons it — any tyrant who does so — God breaks his back. God, exalted, has said: {And We send down of the Qur'an that which is a healing and a mercy for the believers} (Sūrat al-Isrāʾ 17:82). And He said: {And when you recite the Qur'an, We place between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter a concealed veil; and We have placed coverings over their hearts, lest they understand it, and in their ears a deafness. And when you mention your Lord alone in the Qur'an, they turn their backs in aversion} (Sūrat al-Isrāʾ 17:45–46). And He, exalted, said: {And if there were a Qur'an by which the mountains were moved, or the earth were cloven apart, or the dead were spoken to — rather, to God belongs the affair entirely} (Sūrat al-Raʿd 13:31). So we must content ourselves with the Book of God, exalted, and seek guidance in it, and beware of these preoccupations that divert us from it.

flags.context: سائلة عن مرض (السَّل المَصْ) الشعبي
options: al-sall al-maṣṣ — a folk illness name, left untranslated
a wasting illness known in local folk medicine as al-sall al-maṣṣ
consumption (tuberculosis) as named in Mauritanian folk medicine
flags.note: Hassaniya folk-medicine term; the questioner marks it as popular usage (الشعبي) and puts it in brackets herself. السل on its own is consumption/tuberculosis, but المص ('the sucking') is a local qualifier of unknown extension, so identifying it with tuberculosis would be a guess. Left untranslated pending the Sheikh's office.

flags.context: وعندها قرن كبش وفيه حكمة سوداء ومعه تزلوميت … وأما التزلوميت فتستعمل للمرأة التي استعصى عليها النفاس
options: tazlūmīt — a Mauritanian amulet object, left untranslated
a charm or talisman known as tazlūmīt
an inscribed or knotted amulet (tazlūmīt)
flags.note: Hassaniya dialect term for a physical object used in folk healing. The Sheikh treats it as a مجسم (a physical object) alongside horns, but neither he nor the questioner describes its form. Any English gloss would state more than the source does.

flags.context: وعندها قرن كبش وفيه حكمة سوداء
options: a black ḥikmah — an object placed inside the horn; sense uncertain
a black bead
a black knot or binding
flags.note: IMPORTANT: this is not the usul term ḥikmah ('underlying wisdom') in the glossary. Here it names a physical thing inside the ram's horn. The referent is not established by the source and has deliberately not been guessed.

flags.context: وأما التزلوميت فتستعمل للمرأة التي استعصى عليها النفاس
options: a woman whose post-natal period (nifās) has become obstructed
a woman whose childbirth has become difficult
a woman whose post-natal bleeding will not stop
flags.note: استعصى عليها النفاس can point to obstructed labour, to retained lochia, or to bleeding that will not cease. The Arabic does not decide between them, and the medical referent matters for how the fatwa reads. Left deliberately general in the English.

translator_notes: Qur'anic renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.

The words 'لا يأتيه الباطل من بين يديه ولا من خلفه تنزيل من حكيم حميد' are Qur'an (Sūrat Fuṣṣilat 41:42) woven into the Sheikh's own prose without quotation marks in the source. They have been left unbraced in the English, matching the source, rather than promoted to a marked quotation.
The description of the Dajjal reproduces the wording of the well-known long hadith of al-Nawwas ibn Samʿan, but the Sheikh gives no narrator, collection or grading here, and none has been supplied.
لا يحل is rendered 'it is not lawful', not 'it is not permissible', so that 'permissible' remains reserved for mubāḥ per the five-rulings table.

The Sheikh's ruling on the objects is given as لا يحل استعماله ('it is not lawful to use them'), and his ruling on incantations of unknown meaning likewise. He does not use ḥarām or makrūh here, and no ruling word has been supplied for him.

title_ar: الفرق بين الإسلام والإيمان
title_en: The Difference Between islām and īmān
body_ar:
لقد فسر رسول الله (ص) الإيمان في حديث وفد عبد القيس بما فسر به الإسلام في حديث جبريل فما وجه الجمع بين التفسيرين؟

أن الإيمان والإسلام لفظان شرعيان إذا اجتمعا افترقا وإذا افترقا اجتمعا، فإذا جاءا في سياق واحد اختلف معناهما كحديث جبريل، وإذا جاءا في سياقين مختلفين اتحد معناهما كحديث وفد عبد القيس،

فإن حديث وفد عبد القيس حين قالوا لرسول الله (ص) إنا لا نصل إليك إلا في الشهر الحرام وبيننا وبينك هذا الحي من كفار مضر فأمرنا بأمر فصل نعمل به ونخبر به من وراءنا وندخل به الجنة، فأمرهم بأربع ونهاهم عن أربع قال: «آمركم بالإيمان بالله وحده أتدرون ما الإيمان بالله وحده؟» وشرح لهم الإيمان بالله وحده بأن يشهدوا أن لا إله إلا الله وأن محمدا رسول الله ويقيموا الصلاة ويؤدوا خمس المغنم، وبين لهم الأربع التي يتركونها من الأشربة، فشرح لهم مفهوم الإيمان ببعض مفهوم الإسلام مما يدل على أن الإيمان والإسلام إذا جاءا منفردين اتحد معناهما،

أما إذا جاءا في سياق واحد كآية سورة الحجرات وهي قول الله تعالى: {قَالَتِ الْأَعْرَابُ آَمَنَّا قُلْ لَمْ تُؤْمِنُوا وَلَكِنْ قُولُوا أَسْلَمْنَا} [14] فإن معناهما يختلف كحديث جبريل، وكذلك حديث سعد بن أبي وقاص في الصحيحين أن رسول الله (ص) أعطى رجالا فترك رجلا وهو أعجبهم إلي فغلبني ما أعرف فيه، فقلت: يا رسول الله، مالك عن فلان فإني والله لأراه مؤمنا؟ فقال: أو مسلما، ففرق الرسول (ص) بين الكلمتين عندما وردتا في سياق واحد.
body_en:
The Messenger of God, upon whom be peace, explained faith (īmān) in the hadith of the delegation of ʿAbd al-Qays with the very thing by which he explained submission (islām) in the hadith of Gabriel. How are the two explanations to be reconciled?

Faith (īmān) and submission (islām) are two terms of the revealed law: when they are brought together they part, and when they are parted they come together. If they occur within a single context, their meanings differ, as in the hadith of Gabriel; and if they occur in two different contexts, their meaning is one, as in the hadith of the delegation of ʿAbd al-Qays.

As for the hadith of the delegation of ʿAbd al-Qays: when they said to the Messenger of God, upon whom be peace, 'We cannot reach you except in the sacred month, and between us and you is this clan of the unbelievers of Mudar, so command us with a decisive command which we may act upon and may pass on to those we have left behind, and by which we may enter the Garden' — he commanded them four things and forbade them four. He said: 'I command you to believe in God alone. Do you know what belief in God alone is?' And he explained belief in God alone to them as: that they bear witness that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, that they establish the prayer, and that they render a fifth of the spoils. And he set out for them the four things they were to abandon, among the drinks. So he explained the concept of īmān to them by part of the concept of islām — which shows that when īmān and islām occur singly, their meaning is one.

As for when they occur within a single context — like the verse of Sūrat al-Ḥujurāt, God's words, exalted is He: {The Bedouins said: we have believed. Say: you have not believed; rather say: we have submitted} (Sūrat al-Ḥujurāt 49:14) — then their meanings differ, as in the hadith of Gabriel. So too the hadith of Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas in the two Ṣaḥīḥs: that the Messenger of God, upon whom be peace, gave to a number of men and left out one man, who was the most pleasing of them to me; and what I knew of him overcame me, so I said: 'O Messenger of God, what is it with you and so-and-so? By God, I consider him a believer.' He said: 'Or a Muslim.' So the Messenger, upon whom be peace, distinguished between the two words when they occurred within a single context.

flags.context: وبين لهم الأربع التي يتركونها من الأشربة
options: the four things they were to abandon, among the drinks
the four drinking vessels they were to abandon
the four intoxicating drinks they were to abandon
flags.note: The Sheikh does not name the four, and the received wording of the hadith of the delegation of ʿAbd al-Qays lists four VESSELS (al-ḥantam, al-dubbāʾ, al-naqīr, al-muzaffat), not four drinks. His phrasing من الأشربة points to drinks. The English keeps his wording rather than substituting the familiar list, and the discrepancy is recorded here rather than resolved.

flags.arabic: إذا اجتمعا افترقا وإذا افترقا اجتمعا
flags.context: أن الإيمان والإسلام لفظان شرعيان إذا اجتمعا افترقا وإذا افترقا اجتمعا
options: when they are brought together they part, and when they are parted they come together
when they are mentioned together they differ, and when mentioned separately they coincide
united in expression they divide in meaning; divided in expression they unite in meaning
flags.note: A standing maxim of the usul tradition whose force lies in its symmetry. Option 0 keeps the shape at the cost of some immediate clarity; option 1 reads more plainly but loses the aphorism. The Sheikh's own gloss follows immediately in the text either way.

translator_notes: Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.

The source marks the Qur'anic quotation with its own brace brackets and gives only the bare verse number '[14]'; the sura name and full reference have been supplied in the English per house style, and the Arabic has not been altered.
The source writes the honorific as (ص) throughout. It is rendered in full in the English as 'upon whom be peace'.

In the hadith of Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas the Sheikh moves mid-sentence from third-person narration into Saʿd's own first-person voice, exactly as the report runs. The shift has been kept rather than smoothed out.
The Sheikh attributes the hadith of Saʿd to 'the two Ṣaḥīḥs' and gives no grading for the hadith of the delegation of ʿAbd al-Qays or the hadith of Gabriel. No grading has been supplied.

title_ar: فتاوي متنوعة
title_en: Various Fatwas
body_ar:
الفرق بين النفس والروح

ما الفرق بين النفس والروح؟

هذا محل خلاف بين أهل العلم، والراجح أن الروح تطلق على القوة التي بها الحياة، وأن النفس تطلق على باطن الإنسان، فالنفس هي ما يسمى بالقلب مثلا، والروح تشمل كل القوى الباطنية فيدخل فيها النفس القلب والعقل والبصيرة وغير ذلك؟ ولهذا فالحيوانات لها أرواح وتقبض عند الموت، ولكن ليس لها تلك القوى ليس لها عقل مثلا، هذا يختص بالإنسان.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

الفرق بين أهل السنة والجماعة

أهل السنة والجماعة ما الفرق بينهما؟

هذا مصطلح لم يرد في الكتاب ولا في السنة، وإنما جاءت أحاديث فيها الأمر بالسنة وأحاديث فيها الأمر بالجماعة، فقد ثبت عن رسول الله (ص) في وصيته التي رواها عنه العرباض بن سارية رضي الله عنه أنه قال: «فمن يعش منكم فسيرى اختلافا كثيرا فعليكم بسنتي وسنة الخلفاء الراشدين المهديين، عضوا عليها بالنواجذ» وهذا أمر منه باتباع السنة، وكذلك جاء عن النبي (ص) الحض على التزام سنته في كثير من الأحاديث مثل حديث المقدام بن معدي كرب رضي الله عنه أن رسول الله (ص) قال: «ألا هل يوشك رجل شعبان متكئ على أريكته يأتيه الأمر من أمري مما أمرت به أو نهيت عنه فيقول: بيننا وبينكم كتاب الله، ما وجدنا فيه من حلال استحللناه وما وجدنا فيه من حرام حرمناه، ألا وإنما حرم رسول الله مثل ما حرم الله، ألا إني أوتيت القرآن ومثله معه».

وكذلك جاء عنه (ص) الحض على الجماعة في أحاديث كثيرة مثل قوله لحذيفة بن اليمان: تلزم جماعة المسلمين وإمامهم، ومثل قوله (ص): لا يحل دم امرئ مسلم إلا بإحدى ثلاث، الثيب الزاني والنفس بالنفس والتارك لدينه المفارق للجماعة، ومثل قوله (ص): من فارق الجماعة شبرا مات ميتة جاهلية، ومثل قوله (ص): من فارق الجماعة فقد خلع ربقة الإسلام من عنقه، ومثل قوله (ص): يد الله مع الجماعة ومن شذ شذ في النار، ومثل قوله (ص): من أراد بحبوحة الجنة فليلزم الجماعة، ومثل قوله (ص): يد الله على الجماعة وإنما يأكل الذئب من الغنم القاصية، وكذلك نهيه عن التعرب بعد الهجرة، والأحاديث كثيرة في هذا الباب

فهذه الأحاديث بمجموعها الأحاديث الأولى الدالة على التزام السنة، والأحاديث الثانية الدالة على التزام الجماعة لفق بينهما العلماء فجعلوا المحجة البيضاء التي كان عليها النبي (ص) وأصحابه السنة والجماعة، فليس المقصود بالسنة مجرد ما يسمى بالسنة في عرف الفقهاء، وهو هيئة الأمر الشرعي المأمور به أمرا غير جازم بحيث يثاب فاعله ولا يعاقب تاركه، هذه السنة عند الفقهاء والأصوليين وليست هي المقصودة هنا، كذلك ليس المقصود بالجماعة الأفراد الكثر والسواد الأعظم فقط، بل يقول الله تعالى: {وَإِنْ تُطِعْ أَكْثَرَ مَنْ فِي الْأَرْضِ يُضِلُّوكَ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ} [الأنعام 116] فالمقصود ما كان عليه الرسول (ص) وأصحابه فهذا نسميه سنة وجماعة اصطلاحا فقط، ولا مشاحة في الاصطلاح.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

الفرق بين كرامة الأولياء وغيرها

هناك خوارق للعادة بعضها يكون كرامة من الله سبحانه وتعالى لأوليائه وبعضها يكون شيطانيا كيف نفرق بين ذلك؟

إنما يفرق بين ذلك بحال الإنسان نفسه، فمن كان ملتزما بالشرع مطابقا في ظاهره وباطنه لشرع الله، فما يناله من ذلك هو كرامة أكرمه الله بها، ومن كان مخالفا للشرع عاصيا مبتدعا فما يناله من ذلك من قبل الشيطان، أو ابتلاء من الله تعالى وامتحان.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

القول بفناء النار

ما القول في فناء النار و هل قال به أحد من السلف و إذا كان الجواب نعم فما تأويله للآيات الدالة على خلود أصحابها فيها؟

الجواب أن ذلك لم يقل به أحد من الصحابة أو التابعين أو أتباعهم صراحة و إنما رويت عنهم بعض الآثار التي تدل على ذلك التي يمكن أن يفهم منها ذلك كأثر عمر بن الخطاب و أثر بن مسعود في أن أهل النار لو داموا فيها قدر رمل عالج لكان لهم يوم يخرجون فيه منها و أنها يوشك أن يمر عليها يوم تصفق فيه أبوابها من قلة الداخلين و المقصود حينئذ بفنائها خروج أكثر أهلها منها لكن لا يقصد به فناؤها المطلق فناؤها هي في نفسها

و عموما فلا شك أن من كان في قلبه مثقال ذرة من إيمان أو من قال لا إله إلا الله فسيخرج منها و لو مكث فيها مليارات المليارات من السنين فسيخرج منها على كل حال فالله سبحانه و تعالى يقول يوم القيامة بعد أن تنتهي شفاعات الشافعين: إنتهت شفاعات الشافعين و بقيت شفاعة أرحم الراحمين فيقول لملائكته أخرجوا من النار من قال لا إله إلا الله و بذلك يخرجون منها قد اسودوا و امتحشوا فيلقون في نهر الحياة فتنبت أجسامهم كما تنبت الحبة في حميل السيل ثم يأمر بهم إلى الجنة

فالنار إذن لا تفنى بل هي مبقاة و لا شك سيبقى فيها من مات على الكفر و ليس في قلبه مثقال حبة من خردل من خير و لم يقل لا إله إلا الله قط فأولائك الذين يخلدون في النار و لا يخرجون منها. (و ما هم بخارجين منها)

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

الكتب التي ينبغي الاعتناء بها من حيث الفهم للعقيدة الصحيحة

بما ذا ترشدون من الكتب التي ينبغي الاعتناء بها من حيث الفهم للعقيدة الصحيحة و جزاكم الله خيرا؟

اٍن الكتب التي ألفها السلف الصالح في هذا المجال فيها غنية للمسلمين و من هذه الكتب مثلا كتاب الإيمان لأبي بكر ابن أبي شيبة وكتاب الإيمان لأبي خيثمة زهير ابن حرب شيخ مسلم ومثل ذلك كتاب البخاري رحمه الله خلق أفعال العباد ومثل ذلك أيضا كتاب اللالكائي شرح أصول السنة وهكذا فهذه الكتب نافعة مهمة.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

الكلام على ادعاء بعض الأحياء للقاء الأموات

ما تعليقكم على من يدعي لقاء الموتى ومعرفة أهل الجنة منهم من أهل النار ونحو ذلك؟

أن حال الأموات وراء البرزخ الذي هو دونهم إلى يوم القيامة هو من الغيوب التي لا نطلع عليها إلا بوحي، قد يطلع الإنسان بتخييل أو نحوه أو بسماع في بعض الأحيان لتعذيب الأموات في قبورهم لكن قد ينقطع عنهم ذلك فينعمون أيضا فهذا من الأمور التي لا تقتضي قطعا،

فقد كان أصحاب النبي (ص) عنده ذات ليلة فسمعوا أصواتا مروعة فقال: تلك يهود تعذب في قبورها، فبين لهم أن هذا عذاب القبر عذاب بني قريظة الذين قتلهم رسول الله (ص) فهم يعذبون في قبورهم فسمع أصحابه أصواتهم، وهذا غيب كشفه الله لهم في ذلك الوقت ليزدادوا خشية لله وتوكلا عليه،

وكذلك فإن ابن عمر خرج في سفر في عهد النبي (ص) وحده فمر على قبر فخرج له صاحبه من قبره يقول: يا عبد الله اسقني، فيقول: ما عرفت هل عرف اسمي أو هي كلمة تقولها العرب، فخرج في أثره شيء فجره بعنف وقال: يا عبد الله لا تسقه، فحم عبد الله أي أصابته حمى النافض وهي حمى شديدة فنهى رسول الله (ص) عن الوحدة في السفر بسبب ذلك،

وقد بين النبي (ص) بعض أحوال أهل القبور في قبورهم، فهو يسمع منها ما لا نسمعه نحن ويراه، فيرى عذاب القبر ويرى نعيمه لكن ذلك بالوحي كما صح عنه في الصحيحين أنه مر بقبرين جديدين فقال: أما إنهما ليعذبان وما يعذبان في كبير، ثم قال: بلى أما أحدهما فكان لا يستتر من البول، وأما الآخر فكان يمشي بالنميمة، وكذلك فإنه قال: إن هذه القبور مظلمة على أهلها وإن الله ينورها بصلاتي ودعائي، وقد أخبر بمواضع الفتن وبغير ذلك من الأمور المتعلقة بعذاب القبر، فكل ذلك عن طريق الوحي،

فلذلك لا يستطيع إنسان أن يدعي ذلك إلا إذا كان سمع أصواتا من باب التخييل كما حصل للصحابة، فيدل ذلك على أن ذلك الوقت يمكن أن يكون الصوت الصادر فيه من عذاب القبر ثم يزول، فعذاب القبر ليس عذابا دائما مثل عذاب الآخرة، ليس مثل عذاب الكفار في النار بل ينقطع، قد يعذب الإنسان للحظات ثم ينقطع عنه ذلك، وعذاب القبر من مكفرات الذنوب فهو معدود في مكفرات الذنوب، لأن الإنسان إذا كان يستحق عذابا في مقابل ذنب من الذنوب فعجل له عذابه في القبر يبعث يوم القيامة وليس عليه ذلك الذنب فيستحق الجنة دون عقاب، وقد عده العلامة سيد عبد الله بن الحاج ابراهيم في مكفرات الذنوب وعده بعض أهل العلم قبله كذلك.
body_en:
The difference between the soul (nafs) and the spirit (rūḥ)

What is the difference between the soul (nafs) and the spirit (rūḥ)?

This is a point of disagreement among the scholars. The stronger view is that 'spirit' is applied to the power by which there is life, and that 'soul' is applied to the inward dimension of the human being. So the soul is what is called, for example, the heart, while the spirit takes in all the inward faculties, so that the soul, the heart, the intellect, discernment and the rest fall under it. For this reason animals have spirits, which are taken at death, but they do not have those faculties — they have no intellect, for instance; that belongs to the human being alone.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------

The difference between ahl al-sunnah and al-jamāʿah

Ahl al-Sunnah wa-l-Jamāʿah — what is the difference between the two?

This is a technical term which has not come down in the Book or in the sunnah. What came were hadiths containing the command to [hold to] the sunnah, and hadiths containing the command to [hold to] the congregation (jamāʿah). It is established from the Messenger of God, upon whom be peace, in his counsel narrated from him by al-Irbad ibn Sariyah, may God be pleased with him, that he said: 'Whoever of you lives will see much disagreement, so you must keep to my sunnah and to the sunnah of the rightly guided caliphs; bite onto it with your back teeth.' This is a command from him to follow the sunnah. Likewise there came from the Prophet, upon whom be peace, the urging to hold to his sunnah in many hadiths, such as the hadith of al-Miqdam ibn Madikarib, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, upon whom be peace, said: 'Is it not near that a man, full-fed, reclining on his couch, to whom there comes a matter of my command — of what I have commanded or what I have forbidden — will say: between us and you is the Book of God; whatever we find in it of the lawful we hold lawful, and whatever we find in it of the forbidden we hold forbidden. Truly, what the Messenger of God has forbidden is like what God has forbidden. Truly, I have been given the Qur'an and the like of it along with it.'

Likewise there came from him, upon whom be peace, the urging to [hold to] the congregation in many hadiths, such as his words to Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman: 'Keep to the congregation of the Muslims and their leader'; and his words, upon whom be peace: 'The blood of a Muslim is not lawful except for one of three: the previously married person who commits adultery, a life for a life, and the one who abandons his religion and separates from the congregation'; and his words, upon whom be peace: 'Whoever separates from the congregation by a handspan dies the death of the age of ignorance'; and his words, upon whom be peace: 'Whoever separates from the congregation has cast the yoke of Islam from his neck'; and his words, upon whom be peace: 'The hand of God is with the congregation, and whoever breaks away, breaks away into the Fire'; and his words, upon whom be peace: 'Whoever desires the very heart of the Garden, let him keep to the congregation'; and his words, upon whom be peace: 'The hand of God is over the congregation, and the wolf eats only the sheep that has strayed far off'; and likewise his prohibition of reverting to desert life after the emigration. The hadiths in this chapter are many.

So these hadiths taken all together — the first set, indicating adherence to the sunnah, and the second set, indicating adherence to the congregation — the scholars joined the two and made the white, clear road which the Prophet, upon whom be peace, and his Companions were upon 'the sunnah and the congregation'. What is meant by 'the sunnah' here is therefore not merely what is called sunnah in the jurists' usage — that is, the status of a legally commanded act which is commanded in a non-binding way, such that the one who performs it is rewarded and the one who omits it is not punished. That is the sunnah of the jurists and the legal theorists, and it is not what is intended here. Likewise, what is meant by 'the congregation' is not simply the numerous individuals and the great mass; rather, God, exalted, says: {And if you obey most of those on earth, they will lead you astray from the path of God} [al-Anʿām 116] (Sūrat al-Anʿām 6:116). What is meant is what the Messenger, upon whom be peace, and his Companions were upon. This we call 'sunnah and congregation' only as a technical term, and there is no quarrelling over technical terms.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------

The difference between the charisms of God's friends and other [extraordinary events]

There are breaks in the customary order, some of which are a charism (karāmah) from God, glorified and exalted, to His friends, and some of which are satanic. How do we distinguish between them?

The distinction is drawn only by the state of the person himself. Whoever is committed to the revealed law, conforming in his outward and his inward to the law of God — then what he attains of that is a charism with which God has honoured him. And whoever is at variance with the law, disobedient and an innovator — then what he attains of that is from the side of Satan, or is an affliction and a test from God, exalted.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------

The view that the Fire will pass away

What is the view concerning the passing away of the Fire, and did any of the salaf hold it? And if the answer is yes, how does he interpret the verses indicating the eternal abiding of its people in it?

The answer is that none of the Companions, nor the Successors, nor those who followed them said this explicitly. Rather, certain reports have been narrated from them that point to it, or from which that can be understood — such as the report of Umar ibn al-Khattab and the report of Ibn Masud that if the people of the Fire were to remain in it for as long as the sands of Alij, they would still have a day on which they would come out of it, and that a day is near to come upon it on which its gates will slam shut for the fewness of those entering. What is meant by its 'passing away' in that case is the exit of most of its people from it; it is not meant to mean its absolute passing away, its passing away in itself.

In general, there is no doubt that whoever has in his heart the weight of an atom of faith, or who has said 'there is no god but God', will come out of it. Even if he remains in it for billions upon billions of years, he will come out of it in any case. For God, glorified and exalted, says on the Day of Resurrection, after the intercessions of the intercessors have come to an end: 'The intercessions of the intercessors have ended, and there remains the intercession of the Most Merciful of the merciful.' And He says to His angels: 'Bring out of the Fire whoever said "there is no god but God".' By that they come out of it, blackened and charred, and are cast into the river of life, and their bodies grow as a seed grows in the silt carried down by a torrent; then He commands that they be brought to the Garden.

The Fire, then, does not pass away; rather it is kept in being. And there will without doubt remain in it whoever died upon unbelief, having not in his heart the weight of a mustard seed of good and never having said 'there is no god but God'. Those are the ones who abide for ever in the Fire and do not come out of it: {and they will not be coming out of it} (Sūrat al-Māʾidah 5:37).

---------------------------------------------------------------------------

The books that ought to be given attention for the understanding of sound creed

Which books do you direct us to that ought to be given attention for the understanding of sound creed? May God reward you well.

The books which the righteous predecessors composed in this field contain sufficiency for the Muslims. Among these books are, for example, the Book of Faith (Kitāb al-Īmān) of Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah; the Book of Faith of Abu Khaythamah Zuhayr ibn Harb, the teacher of Muslim; and likewise the book of al-Bukhari, may God have mercy on him, Khalq Afʿāl al-ʿIbād; and likewise the book of al-Lalakaʾi, Sharḥ Uṣūl al-Sunnah; and so on. These books are beneficial and important.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------

On the claim of some of the living to meet the dead

What is your comment on one who claims to meet the dead, and to know which of them are of the people of the Garden and which of the people of the Fire, and the like?

The condition of the dead beyond the intermediate realm (barzakh), which lies before them until the Day of Resurrection, is among the unseen matters which we come to know only by revelation. A person may at times come upon something — by a mental impression or the like, or by hearing — of the punishment of the dead in their graves; but that may be cut off from them and they may be in ease as well. So this is among the matters that do not yield certainty.

The Companions of the Prophet, upon whom be peace, were with him one night and heard terrifying sounds, and he said: 'Those are Jews being punished in their graves.' So he made clear to them that this was the punishment of the grave — the punishment of the Banu Qurayzah whom the Messenger of God, upon whom be peace, had killed; they are being punished in their graves, and his Companions heard their voices. This is an unseen matter that God disclosed to them at that moment so that they might increase in fear of God and in reliance upon Him.

Likewise, Ibn Umar went out on a journey alone in the time of the Prophet, upon whom be peace, and passed by a grave, and its occupant came out to him from his grave saying: 'O servant of God, give me water.' He says: 'I did not know whether he knew my name, or whether it is a phrase the Arabs use.' Then something came out after him and dragged him back violently and said: 'O servant of God, do not give him water.' So Abd Allah took a fever — that is, the shivering fever came upon him, which is a severe fever. Because of that the Messenger of God, upon whom be peace, forbade being alone on a journey.

The Prophet, upon whom be peace, made clear some of the states of the people of the graves in their graves; he hears from them what we do not hear, and he sees it. He sees the punishment of the grave and he sees its bliss, but that is by revelation, as is soundly established from him in the two Ṣaḥīḥs, that he passed by two fresh graves and said: 'Indeed, these two are being punished, and they are not being punished for something great.' Then he said: 'Rather — as for one of them, he did not shield himself from urine; and as for the other, he used to go about with slander.' Likewise he said: 'These graves are darkness upon their people, and God illuminates them by my prayer and my supplication.' And he gave news of the places of trials, and of other matters connected with the punishment of the grave; all of that was by way of revelation.

For that reason no one is able to claim such a thing, unless he has heard sounds by way of a mental impression, as happened to the Companions. That indicates that at that time the sound produced may come from the punishment of the grave and then pass away. For the punishment of the grave is not a perpetual punishment like the punishment of the Hereafter; it is not like the punishment of the unbelievers in the Fire — rather it is interrupted. A person may be punished for moments and then it ceases from him. The punishment of the grave is among the expiators of sins; it is counted among the expiators of sins, because if a person deserves a punishment in return for one of his sins, and his punishment is brought forward for him in the grave, he is raised on the Day of Resurrection with that sin no longer upon him, and so deserves the Garden without chastisement. The erudite scholar Sidi Abd Allah ibn al-Hajj Ibrahim counted it among the expiators of sins, and some of the scholars before him counted it likewise.

flags.context: والراجح أن الروح تطلق على القوة التي بها الحياة، وأن النفس تطلق على باطن الإنسان

flags.note: English 'soul' and 'spirit' do not divide the way nafs and rūḥ do here, and the Sheikh's distinction is the point of the answer: rūḥ is the wider term (the animating power, which animals also possess), nafs the narrower inward faculty. Whichever pair is fixed must be used consistently across the corpus, since the two words recur constantly.

title_ar: الكلام على الوسوسة في الطهارة والصلاة وطرق علاجها
title_en: On Obsessive Whispering in Purification and Prayer, and How to Treat It
body_ar:
عندي ولد تأخذه الوسوسة في الطهارة و الصلاة فإذا ذهب إلى الخلاء و تطهر من البول يتوضأ حتى ينتهي فيقول أنا لم أخلص من البول و لا أقدر على أن أصلي بالنجاسة و ينزع لباسه كله و يأخذ لباسا آخر و يصلي؟

أن هذا النوع هو من عمل الشيطان و قد قال الله تعالى:﴿يأيها الذين آمنوا لا تتبعوا خطوات الشيطان﴾ فعليه أن يتعالج من هذا المرض بأسباب الشفاء الشرعية و منها الإكثار من الإستغفار و منها كذلك أذكار دخول الخلاء و الخروج منه و الحفاظ عليها و منها أيضا عدم إتعاب النفس في التفكير كثيرا في هذا الأمر فيجب عليه أن يصرفه عن نفسه و منها أيضا الرقية الشرعية أن يقرأ القرآن على نفسه و أن يقرأه عليه غيره و منها الحفاظ على أذكار النوم و الإستيقاظ و الصباح و المساء و منها الصدقة التي يعالج بها المرض «عالجوا مرضاكم بالصدقة» فكل ذلك يزيل عنه هذا الوسواس بإذن الله
body_en:
I have a son who is seized by obsessive whispering (waswasah) in purification (ṭahārah) and prayer. When he goes to the lavatory and cleans himself of urine, he performs ablution right through to the end, and then says: I have not got free of the urine, and I cannot pray with substantive impurity (najāsah) on me — and he takes off all his clothing, takes other clothing, and prays.

This kind of thing is from the work of Satan. God, exalted, has said: {O you who believe, do not follow the footsteps of Satan} (Sūrat al-Nūr 24:21). So he must treat himself for this illness with the means of healing given in the revealed law. Among them: frequent seeking of forgiveness. Among them likewise: the remembrances for entering the lavatory and for leaving it, and keeping to them. Among them also: not wearying himself by thinking much about this matter — he is obliged to turn it away from himself. Among them also: the lawful incantation (ruqyah), that he recite the Qur'an over himself and that someone else recite it over him. Among them: keeping to the remembrances for sleeping and waking, and for morning and evening. And among them: the voluntary charity (ṣadaqah) by which illness is treated — 'Treat your sick with charity.' All of that will remove this obsessive whispering from him, by God's leave.

flags.context: عندي ولد تأخذه الوسوسة في الطهارة و الصلاة … فكل ذلك يزيل عنه هذا الوسواس بإذن الله
options: obsessive whispering (waswasah)
compulsive doubt in matters of worship (waswasah)
satanic insinuation (waswasah)
flags.note: waswasah covers both the satanic insinuation and the sufferer's compulsive doubt, and the Sheikh's answer works on both levels at once: he names it 'the work of Satan' and also calls it 'this illness' to be treated. Option 2 keeps only the first sense and option 1 only the second. Note also that the Sheikh prescribes only religious remedies here; he neither recommends nor rules out medical treatment, and nothing on that has been added.

title_ar: الكلام على خوارق العادات
title_en: On Breaks in the Customary Order
body_ar:
ما يظهر من الخوارق على يد الولي وما يظهر على يد الساحر ما الفرق بينهما؟

أن أهل العلم ذكروا أن خوارق العادات سبعة أقسام، أربع منها للخير وثلاث للشر، فالأربع التي للخير هي أولا الإرهاصات التي تظهر عند ميلاد الأنبياء وفي صباهم كتصدع إيوان كسرى وخمود نار الفرس وما شاهدته حليمة من الخوارق في صبا النبي (ص) وشق صدره ونحوه فهذه أمور ليست من المعجزات ولكنها من الإرهاصات فهي تدل على بعثته، فهو إذ ذاك لم يبعث بعد، وإنما بعث على رأس أربعين سنة،

والنوع الثاني هو المعجزات، وهي ما يظهر على يد الأنبياء عند التحدي عند تبليغ رسالات ربهم، كنزول الوحي، وكالمعراج والإسراء وشق القمر ونحو ذلك وكناقة صالح وعصا موسى فهذا هو المعجزة وهي مختصة بالأنبياء،

القسم الثالث ما يسمى بكرامات الأولياء، وهو ما يكرم الله به من كان من أهل الطاعة والتقوى والإيمان مما يعينه على الطاعة، كقوة البدن بحيث يستطيع الإنسان الدوام على الوضوء والغسل، فهذا كرامة يكرم الله بها أولياءه، ومثل ذلك الحفاظ على الصف الأول أو على إجابة المنادي أو على الصلاة في الجماعة أو على ختم القرآن في كل يوم وليلة مثلا أو الحفاظ على قيام الليل في طيلة السنة، فهذا كرامة يكرم الله بها من شاء من أوليائه وهي خارقة لعادة جمهور الناس، فهذا النوع يسمى الكرامات، وأغلبها لا يتجه إلى الدنيا إنما يتجه إلى أمور الآخرة، فالكرامات في أغلبها لا تتجه إلى أمور الدنيا كأن يجد الإنسان نقودا أو سيارة أو هاتفا أو نحو ذلك فهذه أمور دنيوية تافهة وإكرام الله تعالى للعباد يتعلق بأمور أكبر من هذا كإكرامه لأوليائه بما يعينهم على عبادته وطاعته وما يزيدهم إيمانا وخشية وتقوى،

النوع الرابع هو ما يسمى بالعون، وهو ما يناله أواسط المسلمين ممن ليس مشهورا بالطاعة ولا بالعبادة فيقيض الله له أمرا خارقا للعادة بسبب إيمانه، كمن نفرت منه راحلته بخلاء من الأرض فأمسكتها عليه شجرة، فهذا النوع مما يعين على أمور الدنيا ليس داخلا في نطاق الكرامة ولكنه من العون يعين الله بها عباده، فيقيض لهم ما يعينهم على أمور دنياهم مما هو خارق للعادة،

هذه الأربع للخير أما الثلاث التي للشر فهي أولا ما يسمى بالإهانة، وهو ما يظهر من الخوارق على يد مدعي الرسالة الكاذب على خلاف دعواه، فمسيلمة الكذاب سمع أن النبي (ص) مسح على رأس صبي فلم يشب، بقي شعره أسود إلى أن مات وهو شيخ كبير، فمسح هو على رأس صبي فقرع، وسمع أن النبي (ص) بصق في بير كانت ملحا فصارت عذبا، فبصق هو في بير فيبست، فهذا النوع يسمى إهانة هو خارق للعادة فعلا، هذا خارق للعادة لكنه إهانة لأنه ليس على الوجه المطلوب وهو خلاف الوجه الذي يطلبه الإنسان،

النوع الثاني من هذه الخوارق التي هي للشر السحر، والسحر هو ما سبق تعريفه بقسميه، ما كان منه تخييلا وما كان تأثيرا، فهذا يحصل به خرق للعادة وهو للشر فهو كفر بصاحبه،

والنوع الثالث من الخوارق التي هي للشر ما كان مما يسمى بالكهانة ومخالطة الجن، فالجن يخرقون العادة للإنسان فيسمعون الكلمة الواحدة من الغيب فيضيفون إليها تسعا وتسعين كذبة، فيأتونه بمائة كلمة فيها كلمة واحدة صدق وتسعة وتسعون كذبة، فيخبر هو بما أخبروه به، فتارة يأتيه صادق وتارة يأتيه كاذب، كما قال صاف بن صياد لرسول الله (ص) عندما سأله كما في الصحيح، قال: ماذا يأتيك يا صاف؟ قال: يأتيني صادق وكاذب، قال: اخسأ فلن تعدو قدرك، فعرف النبي (ص) أنما يأتيه هو من الشيطان لأن ما كان من عند الله لا يكون فيه كاذب، لا بد أن يكون صادقا، فقال: يأتيني صادق وكاذب فقال: اخسأ فلن تعدو قدرك،

فإذن هذه هي خوارق العادة وأقسامها واضحة والتمييز بينها بين، وإنما يشكل على بعض الناس ما يحصل لبعض الأولياء من الإخبار ببعض المغيبات وهم أهل استقامة وصلاح وتارة يصدقون في ذلك وتارة يكذبون، والجواب عن هذا أنه يجب عليهم أن لا يخبروا بما اطلعوا عليه من ذلك، ويحرم عليهم الإخبار به، وإذا أخبروا ببعضه فكان صادقا فعلى أهل الإيمان أن لا يغتروا به وأن يعلموا أن هذا يحصل للصالح والطالح ويحصل للمؤمن وغيره،

ولذلك سئل الإمام الجنيد رحمه الله فقيل له: الولي هو الذي يطير في الهواء؟ قال: الغراب يطير في الهواء وينقر الدبر، قيل له: أهو الذي يمشي على الماء؟ قال: الحوت يمشي على الماء وتؤكل ميتته، قيل: أهو الذي يجمع بين المشرق والمغرب في آن واحد؟ قال: إبليس يجمع بين المشرق والمغرب في آن واحد وهو أخس خلق الله، قيل: فما الولي إذن؟ قال: من استقام حاله على وفق ما جاء به رسول الله (ص) من عند الله تعالى فهذا هو الولي وهذه هي الولاية التي يحرص عليها هي ولاية الله.
body_en:
What appears of extraordinary events at the hand of the friend of God, and what appears at the hand of the sorcerer — what is the difference between them?

The scholars have mentioned that breaks in the customary order are of seven kinds: four of them for good and three of them for evil.

The four that are for good are, first, the precursors (irhāṣāt) that appear at the birth of the prophets and in their childhood — such as the cracking of the arch of Chosroes, the dying down of the fire of the Persians, what Halimah witnessed of extraordinary things in the childhood of the Prophet, upon whom be peace, the opening of his breast, and the like. These are not miracles (muʿjizāt) but precursors; they point to his being sent, since at that time he had not yet been sent — he was sent at the completion of forty years.

The second kind is the miracles: what appears at the hand of the prophets at the point of challenge, in conveying the messages of their Lord — such as the descent of revelation, the Ascension and the Night Journey, the splitting of the moon and the like, and such as the she-camel of Salih and the staff of Moses. This is the miracle, and it belongs to the prophets alone.

The third kind is what is called the charisms of the friends of God (karāmāt al-awliyāʾ): what God honours with it whoever is of the people of obedience, God-consciousness (taqwā) and faith, from among the things that help him toward obedience — such as bodily strength, so that a person is able to keep up ablution and full washing; this is a charism with which God honours His friends. Of the same kind is keeping to the first row, or to answering the one who calls to prayer, or to praying in congregation, or to completing the Qur'an every day and night, for example, or keeping to the night prayer through the whole year. This is a charism with which God honours whom He wills of His friends, and it is a break with the custom of most people. This kind is called the charisms, and most of them are not directed toward this world but toward the affairs of the Hereafter. Charisms are in most cases not directed toward worldly matters, such as a person finding money or a car or a telephone or the like; those are trivial worldly matters, whereas God's honouring of His servants is bound up with matters greater than this — as when He honours His friends with what helps them toward His worship and His obedience, and with what increases them in faith, awe and God-consciousness.

The fourth kind is what is called assistance (ʿawn): what is attained by the middling sort of Muslims, who are not renowned for obedience or for worship, so that God ordains for such a person something that breaks the customary order on account of his faith — like one whose mount bolted from him in an empty tract of land and a tree held it back for him. This kind is among what gives help in worldly matters; it does not fall within the scope of the charism, but is of the assistance by which God assists His servants, ordaining for them what helps them in their worldly affairs, of what breaks the customary order.

These are the four for good. As for the three that are for evil: the first is what is called humiliation (ihānah), namely the extraordinary events that appear at the hand of a false claimant to messengerhood, contrary to his claim. Musaylimah the Liar heard that the Prophet, upon whom be peace, had wiped the head of a boy and that the boy did not go grey — his hair stayed black until he died an old man. So Musaylimah wiped the head of a boy, and the boy went bald. And he heard that the Prophet, upon whom be peace, spat into a well that was salt and it became sweet; so he spat into a well and it dried up. This kind is called humiliation: it is in fact a break in the customary order — this is a break in the customary order, but it is a humiliation, because it is not in the manner sought, and is the opposite of the manner the person seeks.

The second kind of these breaks that are for evil is sorcery (siḥr). Sorcery is what has already been defined, in its two kinds: what is illusion, and what is actual effect. By it a break in the customary order comes about, and it is for evil; it is unbelief on the part of the one who does it.

The third kind of the breaks that are for evil is what is called soothsaying (kihānah) and consorting with the jinn. The jinn break the customary order for the human being: they hear a single word from the unseen and add to it ninety-nine lies, so they bring him a hundred words, among which is one word of truth and ninety-nine lies. Then he reports what they have reported to him, so that at one time a truthful one comes to him and at another a lying one — as Saf ibn Sayyad said to the Messenger of God, upon whom be peace, when he asked him, as is in the Ṣaḥīḥ. He said: 'What comes to you, Saf?' He said: 'A truthful one and a lying one come to me.' He said: 'Be off with you; you will never go beyond your measure.' So the Prophet, upon whom be peace, knew that what comes to him is from Satan, because what is from God has no liar in it — it must be truthful. So he said, 'A truthful one and a lying one come to me', and he said: 'Be off with you; you will never go beyond your measure.'

These, then, are the breaks in the customary order. Their divisions are clear and the distinction between them is plain. What causes difficulty for some people is only what happens to some of the friends of God: that they report certain things of the unseen, being people of uprightness and righteousness, and at times they are right in that and at times they are wrong. The answer to this is that they are obliged not to report what they have come upon of that; it is forbidden (ḥarām) for them to report it. And if they do report some of it and it turns out true, the people of faith must not be taken in by it, and must know that this happens to the righteous and to the corrupt, and happens to the believer and to others.

That is why Imam al-Junayd, may God have mercy on him, was asked. It was said to him: 'Is the friend of God the one who flies through the air?' He said: 'The crow flies through the air and pecks at sores.' It was said to him: 'Is he the one who walks on water?' He said: 'The fish walks on water, and its carrion is eaten.' It was said: 'Is he the one who joins east and west in a single moment?' He said: 'Iblis joins east and west in a single moment, and he is the basest of God's creation.' It was said: 'What, then, is the friend of God?' He said: 'One whose state is upright in accordance with what the Messenger of God, upon whom be peace, brought from God, exalted.' This is the friend of God, and this is the friendship to be striven for: the friendship of God.
