title_ar: فتاوي في العقيدة
title_en: Fatwas on Creed
body_ar:
الوسوسة في العقيدة

ما حكم من يتعرض لوساوس الشيطان في عقيدته؟ بما ذا ينصح؟

على الإنسان إذا أحس بشيء من وسوسة الشيطان في اعتقاده أن يعلم أن ذلك من خطوات الشيطان التي نهانا الله تعالى عن اتباعها فقد قال الله تعالى:﴿يأيها الذين آمنوا لا تتبعوا خطوات الشيطان﴾ . و عليه أن يكثر من ذكر الله تعالى فإن ذلك يطرد الشيطان فليكثر من الإستغفار و ليقل \"لا إله إلا الله\" فهذا يقطع على الشيطان السبيل و يزيل تلك الوساوس بالكلية و عليه أن لا يتبع التفكير التفكير، إذا جاءت فكرة خاطرة عليه أن لا يرددها، بل يقطعها بذكر الله تعالى...

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

بما تثبت العقيدة وأصول الدين؟

هل تثبت العقيدة وأصول الدين بخبر الآحاد؟

أن خبر الآحاد أربعة أنواع لدى أهل الحديث، القسم الأول منه المستفيض وهو الذي يقترب من المتواتر والفصل بينهما شاق وهذا تثبت به العقائد بدون خلاف، القسم الثاني المشهور وهو الذي رواه عدد في كل طبقة لا يزيدون على العشرة ولا ينقصون عن الثلاثة أو الأربعة، ثم يليه العزيز وهو الذي انفرد به في طبقة من الطبقات اثنان أو ثلاثة، ثم يليه الغريب وهو الذي انفرد به واحد في طبقة من الطبقات في أي طبقة من طبقاته،

وهذه الثلاثة اختلف فيها الناس هل تقتضي القطع أم لا، فذهب جمهور الأصوليين إلى أن خبر الآحاد إذا كان مشهورا أو عزيزا أو غريبا لا يقتضي القطع، وذهب المحققون منهم إلى أنه يقتضي القطع إن احتف بالقرائن التي تدل عليه، وذهب آخرون إلى أنه يقتضي القطع مطلقا وروي هذا عن جمهور أهل الحديث، ولكن القول الصحيح أن أخبار الآحاد إن احتفت بالقرائن اقتضت القطع ويمثل لذلك أهل الحديث بما يرويه مالك عن نافع عن ابن عمر عن رسول الله (ص)، فإنه يقتضي القطع لما احتف به من القرائن،

وعلى هذا الخلاف اختلف في الاستدلال بأخبار الآحاد في العقائد، والعقائد تنقسم إلى قسمين ما يطلب فيه القطع وهو أصول العقائد والديانات، وما لا يطلب فيه القطع وهو تفاصيلها، كتفصيل صفات الله سبحانه وتعالى ونحو ذلك، فتفاصيل الصفات على الراجح لا يشترط فيها القطع ولذلك يقبل فيها أخبار الآحاد، فيمكن أن تثبت صفة لله عز وجل بخبر الآحاد ويمكن أن يثبت له الاسم بذلك،

ولهذا يقول السيوطي رحمه الله: أسماؤه سبحانه موقفة** ثالثها الاسم فقط دون الصفه ويكتفى بمرة والمصدر** والفعل والظنون في المعتبر الظنون أخبار الآحاد،

أما الأمور القطعية والأصول أصول الديانات فلا بد فيها من القطع، فعلى القول بأن خبر الآحاد يفيد القطع مطلقا فلا إشكال في ثبوتها بذلك، وعلى القول بأنه يفيد القطع إن احتف بالقرائن فكذلك مثل ما رواه البخاري في الصحيح أو رواه مسلم في الصحيح حتى لو كان غريبا أو عزيزا فإنه احتف به من القرائن ما يقتضي القطع به، وإن شرط فيها القطع فإنه لا يؤخذ فيها بخبر الآحاد،

وحكمنا بالصحة على ما في الصحيحين لا يقصد به القطع عند الأصوليين وإنما يقصد به القطع عند المحدثين فقط، ولهذا قال العراقي رحمه الله في ألفية المصطلح: وبالصحيح والضعيف قصدوا** في ظاهر لا القطع والمعتمد إمساكنا عن حكمنا على سند** بأنه أصح مطلقا وقد خاض به قوم فقيل مالك** عن نافع فيما رواه الناسك مولاه واختر حيث عنه يسند** الشافعي قلت فعنه أحمد
body_en:
Obsessive whispering concerning creed

What is the ruling concerning one who is exposed to Satan's obsessive whisperings in his creed? What is he advised to do?

When a person senses anything of Satan's whispering in what he believes, he must know that this is one of the footsteps of Satan, which God, exalted, has forbidden us to follow, for God, exalted, has said: {O you who believe, do not follow the footsteps of Satan} (Sūrat al-Nūr 24:21). He must make much remembrance of God, exalted, for that drives Satan away. So let him make much seeking of forgiveness, and let him say 'there is no god but God', for this cuts off Satan's path and removes those whisperings entirely. And he must not pursue the thought: if a passing thought comes, he must not turn it over again, but should cut it off with the remembrance of God, exalted...

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

By what are creed and the foundations of religion established?

Are creed and the foundations of religion established by a singly transmitted report (khabar al-āḥād)?

The singly transmitted report is of four types in the usage of the hadith scholars. The first of them is the widespread (mustafīḍ), which comes close to the mass-transmitted (mutawātir); separating the two is laborious. By this, creedal doctrines are established without disagreement. The second is the well-known (mashhūr), which is what a number narrated in every layer, not exceeding ten and not falling below three or four. Next to it is the strong (ʿazīz), which is what two or three alone narrated in one of the layers. Next to it is the singular (gharīb), which is what one narrator alone narrated in one layer, in whichever of its layers that may be.

Over these three, people differed as to whether they yield certainty or not. The majority of the legal theorists held that a singly transmitted report, whether well-known, strong or singular, does not yield certainty. The verifying scholars among them held that it does yield certainty if it is attended by indications that point to it. Others held that it yields certainty absolutely, and this is narrated from the majority of the hadith scholars. But the correct position is that singly transmitted reports, if they are attended by indications, do yield certainty; and the hadith scholars give as their example of this what Malik narrates from Nafi from Ibn Umar from the Messenger of God, upon whom be peace, for it yields certainty on account of the indications attending it.

On this disagreement, they differed over taking singly transmitted reports as evidence in creedal doctrines. Creedal doctrines divide into two kinds: what certainty is required in, namely the foundations of the creeds and of the religions; and what certainty is not required in, namely their details — such as the details of the attributes of God, glorified and exalted, and the like. The details of the attributes, on the stronger view, do not have certainty as a condition, and therefore singly transmitted reports are accepted in them. So it is possible for an attribute to be established for God, mighty and majestic, by a singly transmitted report, and it is possible for a name to be established for Him by that.

That is why al-Suyuti, may God have mercy on him, says: *His names, glorified be He, are fixed by revelation; a third position holds it of the name only, not of the attribute. And a single instance suffices, and the verbal noun, and the verb, and the suppositions, in the view of the one whose opinion counts.* 'The suppositions' means singly transmitted reports.

As for matters of certainty, and the foundations — the foundations of the religions — certainty is indispensable in them. So on the view that a singly transmitted report yields certainty absolutely, there is no difficulty in their being established by it. And on the view that it yields certainty if attended by indications, the same holds — as with what al-Bukhari narrated in the Ṣaḥīḥ, or what Muslim narrated in the Ṣaḥīḥ: even if it were singular or strong, there attend it such indications as require certainty about it. And if certainty is stipulated in them, then a singly transmitted report is not taken in them.

Our ruling of soundness on what is in the two Ṣaḥīḥs is not intended as certainty in the view of the legal theorists; it is intended as certainty only in the view of the hadith scholars. That is why al-Iraqi, may God have mercy on him, said in the Alfiyyah on hadith terminology: *By 'sound' and 'weak' they intended [a judgement] on the outward, not certainty; and what is relied upon is our refraining from ruling of any chain that it is the soundest absolutely. Some people have ventured upon it, and it was said: Malik, from Nafi, the client of the devout one, in what the latter narrated. And choose, where it is given with a chain from him, al-Shafi'i; I said: and from him, Ahmad.*

title_ar: تعريف أهل الكلام
title_en: Defining the People of Kalām
body_ar:
من هم أهل الكلام وماذا تعنون بهم؟

أهل الكلام اسم اشتهر إطلاقه على طائفة من هذه الأمة وضعت قواعد لضوابط العقول، وذلك أن الشارع أحال علم بعض الأمور على العقل وعلوم الناس متفاوتة متباينة، ولا يمكن أن يجعل واحد منها حجة على باقيها، فاحتيج إلى وضع معايير وضوابط يرجع إليها الناس عند تخالف عقولهم

وأنتم تعلمون أن توزيع الله سبحانه وتعالى للعقول بين الناس متباين، ولذلك يقول الحكماء: ما من أحد إلا وهو راض عن الله في عقله، وأقلهم عقلا أرضاهم به، أقل الناس نصيبا من العقل يظن أنه أعقل الناس، وهذا من حكمة الله تعالى ولطفه، فكيف يتحاكم إلى هذا العقل الذي يتفاوت الناس فيه لا بد من وضع ضوابط يرجع إليها،

وهذه الضوابط هي التي سميت بالحجج والبراهين وبالقضايا التي هي الدعاوي، ومبناها على التفريق بين التصديق والتصور، فالتصور هو إدراك المفرد والتصديق هو إدراك النسبة أي إثبات أمر لأمر أو نفيه عنه،

وهذه القواعد العقلية هي من الاجتهاد المحض، ولا يمكن أن تكون خطأ مائة بالمائة ولا صوابا مائة بالمائة، وقد حصل الخطأ في كثير من جوانبها وبالأخص حين ترجمت إليها نظريات اليونان الإغريق ونظريات الرومان، ولا شك أن نظريات هذه الأمم السابقة يخالطها كثير من الوثنيات والشركيات،

وكذلك فإن كثيرا من الذين درسوا علم الكلام وتعمقوا في هذه القواعد غلوا في العقل حتى أخرجوه عن طوره، والعقل جارحة من جوارح الإنسان فهو مثل عينه وأذنه ويده ولا يمكن الغلو فيه لأن له حدودا إلى أعلى وحدودا إلى أسفل، فحدوده إلى أسفل هي الأوليات والمشاهدات والحدسيات والمحسوسات والمشهورات فهذه هي الحد الأدنى للعقل والسقف الأعلى له هي مواقف العقول التسعة التي يجمعها قوله: عجل وقتب، فالعين للعرو من النقيضين، والجيم لجمعهما، واللام للزوم الدور أوالتسلسل والواو لوقوع عدد لا نهاية له، والقاف لقلب الحقيقة، والتاء لتعدد الفاعل وتحصيل الحاصل وكذلك لترجيح بلا مرجح، والباء لبطلان الحصر،

فهذه تسعة هي مواقف العقول التي تقف عندها فإذا كانت العقول كذلك فلا يمكن أن نغلو فيها أو نجعلها يتحاكم إليها في كل الأمور بل الحكم للشخص هو خطاب الله لا خطاب العقل،

ومن هنا فإن كثيرا من المتكلمين يغلطون في تصور العقل، ولذلك قال الغزالي رحمه الله: الوحي عقل من الخارج والعقل وحي من الداخل، ولا شك أن هذا من الغلو في العقل، لأن العقل الذي يتكلم عنه الغزالي ليس متمثلا في عقل شخص بعينه، فلا يقصد عقل أبي حامد الغزالي مثلا، أو عقل إنسان بعينه،بل يقصد الوجود المطلق الذي هو الوجود الذهني للعقل، ولا يقصد الوجود الخارجي المتمثل في عقل شخص من الأشخاص أو جماعة من الجماعات، وإذا كان الحكم على ماهية ذهنية غير خارجية فهو حكم غير دقيق،

كذلك فإن مما خالط ما يسمى بعلم الكلام الخوض في صفات الله تعالى بغير علم، وهذا من الخطر الماحق، لأن الله تعالى: {لَا تُدْرِكُهُ الْأَبْصَارُ وَهُوَ يُدْرِكُ الْأَبْصَارَ وَهُوَ اللَّطِيفُ الْخَبِيرُ (103)} [الأنعام] وقد ذكرنا في الدرس الماضي أنه لا يمكن أن يثبت له إلا ما أثبته لنفسه أو أثبته له رسوله (ص) فلا يمكن أن يصل علم الحادث إليه، بل لا يمكن أن يعلم عنه إلا ما أوحى به، وإذا كان الأمر كذلك فلا مجال للعقل في هذا الباب،

وأهل الكلام فرق كثيرة دخلت علوما متعددة، ففي علوم اللغة طائفة متكلمة وهي التي تسمى بأهل التقعيد العقلي وهم أهل الكوفة، فأهل الكوفة مثلا إذا وجدوا أي نادرة لغوية قاسوا عليها وجعلوها قاعدة، وأهل البصرة يضعون قاعدة بالأكثرية وما خالفها جعلوه من الشواذ، أو بحثوا له عن تأويل يرده إلى القاعدة الأصلية، مثل خلافهم في تقدم الفاعل، فإن أهل البصرة يقولون الفاعل لا يتقدم: وبعد فعل فاعل فإن ظهر** فهو وإلا فضمير استتر لكن الكوفيين يقولون لا، بل يوجد فاعل متقدم، والبصريون يقولون: إذا وجد فإنه فاعل فعل محذوف يدل عليه ما بعده،

وكذلك في الأصول، ففي الأصول مدرسة تسمى المدرسة الكلامية وهي التي تبني القواعد الأصولية وقواعد الاستنباط واستغلال النصوص الشرعية على مقتضى القوانين العقلية، وهذه المدرسة هي التي سلكت في المذاهب الثلاثة المذهب المالكي والمذهب الشافعي والمذهب الحنبلي، وخالفتها مدرسة تسمى مدرسة الفقهاء وهي مدرسة الحنفية، فإنهم اعتمدوا على التفريع الفقهي ولم يعتمدوا على ترتيب المقدمات المنطقية العقلية،

وكذلك دخل هذا العلم في علم العقائد ووضع فيه كثير من الكتب واشتهر كثير من الفرق الداخلة في مسمى الكلام، مثل الكَلَّابية أصحاب ابن كَلَّاب، والكَرَّامية أصحاب ابن كَرَّام، وكذلك إلى حد ما الماتُريدِيَة والأشعرية أي أتباع هذين الإمامين، فكثير منهم أيضا دخلوا في علم الكلام وتوغلوا فيه،

وكذلك في التفسير فإن بعض المفسرين يدخلون في مسمى أهل الكلام لانشغالهم بالتفسير العقلي بالرأي المحض، ومن ذلك التفسير الإشاري الذي اشتغل به الألوسي رحمه الله تعالى وأدرجه في آخر تفسير كل آية من تفسيره تقريبا.
body_en:
Who are the people of kalām, and what do you mean by them?

'The people of kalām' is a name that has become well known as applied to a group of this community who laid down rules for the standards that govern the intellect. That is because the Lawgiver referred knowledge of some matters to the intellect, while people's understandings are disparate and divergent, and it is not possible to make any one of them a proof against the rest. So there was a need to lay down criteria and controls to which people could refer when their intellects diverge.

You know that God's distribution of intellects among people is uneven. That is why the sages say: there is no one who is not content with God as regards his own intellect, and those with the least intellect are the most content with it. The person with the smallest share of intellect thinks he is the most intelligent of people — and this is part of God's wisdom, exalted, and His kindness. So how can judgement be referred to this intellect, in which people vary? Controls must be laid down to which reference can be made.

These controls are what are called the proofs and the demonstrations, and the propositions, which are the claims. Their basis is the distinction between assent (taṣdīq) and conception (taṣawwur): conception is the grasping of a single notion, and assent is the grasping of a relation — that is, the affirming of one thing of another, or the denying of it.

These rational rules are pure exercise of reasoning; they cannot be a hundred per cent wrong, nor a hundred per cent right. Error has occurred in many of their aspects, and especially when the theories of the Greeks and the theories of the Romans were translated into them; and there is no doubt that the theories of these earlier nations are mixed with much that is pagan and much that associates partners with God.

Likewise, many of those who studied the science of kalām and went deep into these rules went to excess concerning the intellect, until they took it out of its proper bounds. The intellect is one of the faculties of the human being; it is like his eye, his ear and his hand, and there can be no going to excess in it, because it has limits at the upper end and limits at the lower end. Its limits at the lower end are the primary truths, the observed, the intuited, the sensed and the widely held — these are the lower bound of the intellect. Its upper ceiling is the nine points at which intellects come to a halt, which are gathered in the phrase 'ʿajil wa-qatab': the ʿayn is for the absence of both contradictories; the jīm is for joining the two together; the lām is for the necessity of circularity or of infinite regress; the wāw is for the occurrence of a number without end; the qāf is for the reversal of a reality; the tāʾ is for the multiplicity of the agent, and for the obtaining of what already obtains, and likewise for preponderance without a preponderating factor; and the bāʾ is for the collapse of an exhaustive division.

These are nine: they are the points at which intellects come to a halt. And if intellects are like this, then we cannot go to excess concerning them, nor make them the thing to which judgement is referred in all matters. Rather, the ruling upon a person is God's address, not the address of the intellect.

From here, many of the theologians err in how they conceive the intellect. That is why al-Ghazali, may God have mercy on him, said: revelation is an intellect from without, and the intellect is a revelation from within. There is no doubt that this is part of going to excess concerning the intellect, because the intellect al-Ghazali is speaking of is not embodied in the intellect of any particular person — he does not mean the intellect of Abu Hamid al-Ghazali, for instance, or the intellect of a particular human being; rather he means absolute existence, which is the mental existence of the intellect, and he does not mean external existence, embodied in the intellect of one person among persons or one group among groups. And when a judgement is passed on a mental quiddity rather than an external one, it is not a precise judgement.

Likewise, part of what has become mixed into what is called the science of kalām is plunging into the attributes of God, exalted, without knowledge — and this is an obliterating danger, because God, exalted: {Vision does not grasp Him, and He grasps vision; and He is the Subtle, the Aware (103)} [الأنعام] (Sūrat al-Anʿām 6:103). We mentioned in the previous lesson that nothing can be affirmed of Him except what He has affirmed of Himself, or what His Messenger, upon whom be peace, affirmed of Him; so the knowledge of an originated being cannot reach Him — indeed nothing can be known about Him except what He has revealed. And if the matter is so, then there is no scope for the intellect in this chapter.

The people of kalām are many groups, and they entered a number of sciences. In the language sciences there is a theologising faction, the one called the people of rational rule-making, and they are the people of Kufa. The people of Kufa, for instance, when they find any rare linguistic form, draw an analogy upon it and make it a rule; whereas the people of Basra lay down a rule by the majority usage, and whatever contradicts it they treat as anomalous, or else they seek an interpretation of it that returns it to the original rule. An example is their disagreement over whether the agent may precede. The people of Basra say the agent does not precede: *and after a verb comes an agent; if it appears, that is it, and otherwise a pronoun lies concealed.* But the Kufans say no, a preceding agent does exist; and the Basrans say that where such a thing is found, it is the agent of an omitted verb indicated by what comes after it.

Likewise in legal theory (uṣūl al-fiqh). In legal theory there is a school called the theological school, which builds the principles of legal theory, and the rules of derivation and of drawing on the texts of the revealed law, upon what the laws of the intellect require. This is the school that was followed in three of the schools of law — the Maliki, the Shafi'i and the Hanbali — and opposed to it is a school called the school of the jurists, which is the school of the Hanafis, for they relied upon the ramification of legal cases and did not rely upon the arranging of rational, logical premises.

Likewise this science entered the science of creed, and many books were composed in it, and many groups falling under the name of kalām became well known — such as the Kullabiyyah, the followers of Ibn Kullab; the Karramiyyah, the followers of Ibn Karram; and likewise, to a degree, the Maturidiyyah and the Ashariyyah, that is, the followers of these two imams, for many of them too entered the science of kalām and went far into it.

Likewise in exegesis: some of the exegetes fall under the name of the people of kalām, because of their occupation with rational exegesis by pure opinion. Of that is the allusive exegesis which al-Alusi, may God have mercy on him, occupied himself with, and which he appended at the end of his exegesis of almost every verse.

flags.context: the mnemonic and the nine impossibilities it encodes
options: keep the Arabic mnemonic transliterated and translate each of the nine, as done here
translate the nine and drop the mnemonic, which does not work in English

flags.note: The mnemonic ʿajil wa-qatab works only in Arabic: each consonant is the first letter of one of the nine impossibilities, and the tāʾ carries three of them, which is how seven letters yield nine items. The English keeps the letters so the structure is visible, but a reader without Arabic will not see why the letters are those letters. The list itself is the standard one of the logicians: the two contradictories both false, the two contradictories both true, circularity or infinite regress, an actual infinite, the reversal of a thing's reality, two agents for one effect, the obtaining of what already obtains, preponderance without a preponderating factor, and the failure of an exhaustive division.

flags.context: the first of the nine
options: the absence of both contradictories
being devoid of both contradictories
the removal of the two contradictories
flags.note: العُرُوّ (from عري, to be bare) here means that neither of two contradictories holds — the technical impossibility usually named as الخلو من النقيضين, 'the vacating of both contradictories', paired with the jīm which is their conjunction. 'Removal' would suggest an act performed on them rather than a state of affairs.

title_ar: حقيقة الكشف
title_en: The Reality of Unveiling
body_ar:
ما هي حقيقة الكشف ولمن يكون؟

أن الكشف معناه أن يكشف الله تعالى لبعض عباده شيئا من الغيوب النسبية، فالغيب قسمان غيب حقيقي وهذا لا يكشف لأحد لأنه من علم الله الذي استأثر به كما قال الله تعالى: {وَعِنْدَهُ مَفَاتِحُ الْغَيْبِ لَا يَعْلَمُهَا إِلَّا هُوَ}[الأنعام 59] وقال النبي (ص) في خمس لا يعلمهن إلا الله: {إِنَّ اللَّهَ عِنْدَهُ عِلْمُ السَّاعَةِ وَيُنَزِّلُ الْغَيْثَ وَيَعْلَمُ مَا فِي الْأَرْحَامِ وَمَا تَدْرِي نَفْسٌ مَاذَا تَكْسِبُ غَدًا وَمَا تَدْرِي نَفْسٌ بِأَيِّ أَرْضٍ تَمُوتُ}[لقمان 34] فهذا الغيب الحقيقي لا اطلاع لأحد من المخلوقات عليه وهو من خصائص الإله جل جلاله،

النوع الثاني هو الغيب النسبي وهو الذي يطلع عليه بعض العباد دون بعض، فالاطلاع عليه بالوسائل المعهودة غير خارق للعادة، كاطلاع الطبيب على حال الجنين في بطن أمه أنه حي يتنفس، أو أنه ذكر أو أنثى أو نحو ذلك بواسطة الأشعة فهذا اطلاع بأمور عادية كما إذا ذبحت الشاة وسلخت فشق بطنها فإذا فيه جنين فقد كان قبل الكشف عليه غيبا نسبيا وبعد الكشف عليه أصبح من عالم الشهادة، فهذا النوع من الغيوب النسبية،

ومثل ذلك من كان وراء هذا الجدار الآن لا يرى من دونه، لكن هذا الغيب غيب نسبي لأنه إذا دخل من الباب رآهم فانكشف له ما كان مغيبا عنه، ومثل ذلك ما يحصل عن طريق الأجهزة كالكلام بالهاتف مع إنسان بعيد، أو رؤيته عن طريق الأقمار الصناعة، أو بالهاتف المرئي فهذا من الغيب النسبي واكتشافه حينئذ بالوسائل المعتادة غير خارق للعادة،

أما انكشافه بالخارق للعادة من غير وسائل أصلا نراها، فهذا هو الكشف بمعنى خرق العادة، أن يرى الإنسان ما لا يراه غيره في الأمور العادية، مثلا إذا نظر الإنسان بمكبر فرأى هلالا أو نجما بعيدا هذا غير خارق للعادة لأنه كشف له غيب نسبي بآلة ووسيلة إذا رآه من غير آلة فهذا خارق للعادة فهو كشف لذلك الغيب النسبي،

وهذا الكشف قد يكون كرامة يكرم الله بها بعض أوليائه فيطلعهم على بعض الأمور التي تزيدهم إيمانا وخشية لله وزيادة توكل عليه ومحبة له، وقد يكون فتنة كما يبتلي الله به بعض المخرفين فيطلعهم على بعض الغيوب النسبية فيرون بذلك أنهم يتصرفون في الكون أو أنهم يؤثرون بما ليس لهم، فيدعون الدعاوي الباطلة الكاذبة فهذا فتنة عليهم،

ومثل ذلك يحصل للمؤمن والكافر، فهذا الكشف يحصل للمؤمنين ويحصل للكافرين ويحصل لمن لا يدعي الإسلام أصلا، كثير من النصارى واليهود يحصل لهم هذا النوع من الكشوف، وأعظمه فتنة على أهل الأرض ما يحصل منه للمسيح الدجال،

فالمسيح الدجال يحصل له من الكشوف الشيء العجيب جدا، فيري الإنسان والده وأمه وقد ماتا من فترة ويسمعه كلامهما ويمر على القرية الخربة فتتبعه كنوزها كيعاسيب النحل ويأتي أهل القرية وهم مسنتون فيصدقونه فيأمر السماء فتمطر ويأمر الأرض فتنبت، فتروح عليهم ماشيتهم أسمن ما كانت ضروعا، ويمر على أهل قرية وهم في خصب فيكذبونه فيأمر السماء فتمسك ويأمر الأرض فتقلع فتروح عليهم ماشيتهم وهي في أشد اللأواء، فهذا من الكشوفات التي تحصل للمسيح الدجال،

وبهذا يعلم أن الكشف ليس علامة من علامات الولاية لله، أنه يحصل للمؤمنين ويحصل للكافرين ويحصل لأعداء الله ويحصل لأولياء الله كل بحسب ما يؤتيه الله منه، وما يحصل منه لأولياء الله هو ما يزيدهم إيمانا وتوكلا على الله ومحبة له فهذا هو الذي يكون كرامة، أما ما ليس كذلك كما يزيد الإنسان طغيانا وأن يدعي أنه يتصرف في الكون فهذا ليس كشفا محمودا وليس كرامة.
body_en:
What is the reality of unveiling (kashf), and to whom does it occur?

Unveiling means that God, exalted, unveils to some of His servants something of the relative unseen. The unseen is of two kinds. There is a real unseen, and this is not unveiled to anyone, because it is of God's knowledge which He has kept to Himself, as God, exalted, said: {And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them but He} [الأنعام 59] (Sūrat al-Anʿām 6:59). And the Prophet, upon whom be peace, said, concerning five which none knows but God: {Indeed, God — with Him is knowledge of the Hour; and He sends down the rain; and He knows what is in the wombs. And no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die} [لقمان 34] (Sūrat Luqmān 31:34). This real unseen — no created being has any access to it, and it is among the exclusive properties of the Deity, majestic is His majesty.

The second kind is the relative unseen: that which some servants come to know and others do not. Coming to know it by the accustomed means is not a break with the customary order — as with a physician's coming to know the state of the foetus in its mother's belly, that it is alive and breathing, or that it is male or female, or the like, by means of imaging. This is coming to know by ordinary things; just as when a sheep is slaughtered and skinned and its belly is opened and there is a foetus in it: before it was uncovered it was a relative unseen, and after it was uncovered it became part of the world of the witnessed. This is of the kind of the relative unseen.

Likewise, whoever is behind this wall now is not seen by the one on the other side of it; but this unseen is a relative unseen, because if he comes in through the door he sees them, and what had been hidden from him is unveiled to him. And likewise what occurs by means of devices, such as speaking by telephone with a distant person, or seeing him by means of satellites, or by video telephone. This is of the relative unseen, and its discovery in that case, by the accustomed means, is not a break with the customary order.

But its being unveiled by a break with the customary order, with no means at all that we can see — this is unveiling in the sense of a break with the customary order: that a person sees what others do not see in ordinary matters. For instance, if a person looks through a magnifying glass and sees a crescent moon or a distant star, that is not a break with the customary order, because a relative unseen was unveiled to him by an instrument and a means; but if he sees it without an instrument, then that is a break with the customary order, and it is an unveiling of that relative unseen.

This unveiling may be a charism with which God honours some of His friends, disclosing to them certain matters that increase them in faith and in awe of God, and in greater reliance upon Him and love for Him. And it may be a trial, as God tries with it some of the deluded, disclosing to them some of the relative unseen, so that they take themselves to be disposing of the universe, or to be exercising an influence that is not theirs, and so make false and lying claims. This is a trial upon them.

The like of this happens to the believer and to the unbeliever. This unveiling happens to believers, and happens to unbelievers, and happens to one who makes no claim to Islam at all: many of the Christians and the Jews have this kind of unveiling happen to them. And the greatest of it as a trial upon the people of the earth is what happens of it to the False Messiah.

For the False Messiah has the most astonishing unveilings happen to him. He shows a person his father and his mother, who died some time ago, and lets him hear their speech. He passes by the ruined village and its treasures follow him like swarms of bees. He comes to the people of a village who are in drought and they believe him, so he commands the sky and it rains, and commands the earth and it brings forth growth, and their livestock come home to them in the evening with their udders fuller than they have ever been. And he passes by the people of a village who are in plenty and they call him a liar, so he commands the sky and it withholds, and commands the earth and it is stripped bare, and their livestock come home to them in the severest hardship. This is of the unveilings that happen to the False Messiah.

By this it is known that unveiling is not one of the signs of friendship with God — that it happens to believers and happens to unbelievers, and happens to the enemies of God and happens to the friends of God, each according to what God gives him of it. What happens of it to the friends of God is what increases them in faith, in reliance upon God and in love for Him; this is what constitutes a charism. As for what is not like that — such as what increases a person in overweening insolence, and his claiming that he disposes of the universe — this is not a praiseworthy unveiling, and is not a charism.

flags.context: أن الكشف معناه أن يكشف الله تعالى لبعض عباده شيئا من الغيوب النسبية
options: unveiling (kashf)
disclosure (kashf)
mystical unveiling
flags.note: kashf is the organising term of the whole answer and recurs throughout. Option 2 must be avoided: the Sheikh's entire point is that kashf is NOT a mark of sainthood and occurs to unbelievers and to the Dajjal, so a rendering that builds a Sufi valuation into the word would reverse his argument. Whichever is fixed must be used consistently wherever kashf appears in the corpus.

flags.context: وقد يكون فتنة كما يبتلي الله به بعض المخرفين
options: the deluded
those who talk nonsense
charlatans
flags.note: Unvowelled in the source. Read as al-mukharrifīn (from خرف, to drivel or be senile) it means those whose talk is delusion, which is how it has been rendered; read as al-mukharrifīn in the sense of fabricators it would come closer to 'charlatans', which implies deliberate deceit. The difference matters: the Sheikh is describing people who are themselves taken in by what is shown to them ('this is a trial upon them'), which tells against the deliberate-deceit reading.

flags.context: ويمر على أهل قرية وهم في خصب فيكذبونه فيأمر السماء فتمسك ويأمر الأرض فتقلع
options: and commands the earth and it is stripped bare
and commands the earth and it withholds its growth
and commands the earth and it becomes barren
flags.note: SOURCE VARIATION. The same clause of the same hadith appears three times in this slice with three different verbs: فتقحل in article 522, فتقلع here, and فتقحط in article 539. قحل and قحط both mean to dry up or suffer drought; قلع does not, and is most likely a copying slip for one of them. The source reading has been kept and the English chosen to fit the sense of the passage. A reviewer should decide whether to standardise across the three articles.

flags.arabic: وقال النبي (ص) في خمس لا يعلمهن إلا الله: {إِنَّ اللَّهَ عِنْدَهُ عِلْمُ السَّاعَةِ …}
flags.context: the attribution of the verse of Luqman
options: translate as given — the Prophet said this concerning the five
render so that the words quoted are clearly the Qur'anic verse rather than the Prophet's own words
attribute the verse to God and the framing to the Prophet
flags.note: As printed, the sentence introduces a Qur'anic verse with 'and the Prophet said'. The hadith on 'the keys of the unseen are five' recites this verse, so the Sheikh's phrasing is compressed rather than mistaken — but in English it can read as attributing the words of the Qur'an to the Prophet. The braces mark it as Qur'an, and the reference is supplied, which is why option 1 is recommended over a bare literal rendering.

translator_notes: Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.
The source supplies its own sura markers for both Qur'anic quotations ('[الأنعام 59]' and '[لقمان 34]'). Those markers have been kept and the full house references added beside them.
The Sheikh's contemporary examples — ultrasound imaging, the telephone, satellites, video calling, the magnifying glass — are his own and are part of the argument, not glosses added in translation.

The description of the Dajjal reproduces the wording of the long hadith of al-Nawwas ibn Samʿan, given here without narrator, collection or grading. None has been supplied. The same passage recurs in articles 522 and 539 of this slice, each time with small differences of wording; see the flag on فتقلع.
Source spelling preserved verbatim in body_ar: الأقمار الصناعة for الأقمار الصناعية, and الدعاوي for الدعاوى.

title_ar: فتاوي متنوعة
title_en: Various Fatwas
body_ar:
حكم أمر المرأة بالمعروف ونهيها عن المنكر

هل يجوز أمر المرأة بالمعروف ونهيها عن المنكر؟

نعم، بل يجب عليها أن تأمر بالمعروف وتنهى عن المنكر، ويجب كذلك أمرها هي يجب على الرجال إذا رأوا من النساء منكرا أن ينهوا عن المنكر وأن يأمروا بالمعروف، وقد كان رسول الله (ص) يباشر ذلك، ففي الصحيحين أنه خطب خطبة العيد فظن أنه لم يسمع النساء فتوكأ على بلال فوقف على النساء ووعظهن وقال يا معشر النساء تصدقن فإني رأيتكن أكثر أهل النار، فبكى النساء فألقى بلال ثوبه فجعل النساء يهوين بأيديهن إلى حليهن ويرمينه في ثوب بلال.

---------------------------------------------------------

حكم بعض الأذكار غير الواردة عن رسول الله r والمرتبطة بمناسبات

هنا ورقة كتب فيها أذكار وهي توزع مصورة وفيها أنها تسبيح شهر رمضان واليوم الأول يقال فيه: سبحان من سبحت له السماوات بأطرافها مائة مرة؟

أن هذا النوع هو من الابتداع ومما لم يأذن به الله ولم يأت به رسول الله (ص) فلذلك لا بد من هجرانه وتركه وفيما جاء به رسول الله (ص) غنية عن مثل هذا...

-------------------------------------------------------------

حكم تعليق التمائم

هل معلق التميمة مشرك؟

هذا شرك أصغر ليس شركا أكبر، إلا إذا اعتقد أنها تنفعه وترفع عنه الضر فذلك شرك أكبر بالاعتقاد، لكن مجرد تعليقها شرك أصغر غير مخرج من الملة كالحلف بغير الله ونحو ذلك فإن النبي (ص) قال: من تعلق تميمة وكل إليها، وقال: من تعلق تميمة فلا أتم الله له، وقال: من تعلق شيئا وكل إليه، وقال كذلك: إن الرقى والتمائم والتِّوَلَة شرك، فالمقصود بذلك شرك دون شرك وهو لا يخرج من الملة.

-------------------------------------------------------------

حكم لكزانة

ما حكم ما يسمى بالكزانة أيا كان نوعها؟

أن الغيب قد استأثر الله به، وقال: ﴿عالم الغيب فلا يظهر على غيبه أحدا﴾، وقال: ﴿قل لا يعلم من في السماوات ومن في الأرض الغيب إلا الله﴾، وقد بين النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن مفاتيح الغيب وهي مقاليد الغيب خمس لا يعلمهن إلا الله، والله تعالى يقول: ﴿وعنده مفاتح الغيب لا يعلمها إلا هو﴾، وهذه الخمس: ﴿إن الله عنده علم الساعة وينزل الغيث ويعلم ما في الأرحام، وما تدري نفس ماذا تكسب غدا وما تدري نفس بأي أرض تموت﴾،

ومحاولة التطلع عليها كأن يريد الإنسان الإطلاع على أجله أو على رزقه وما يرزق غدا، أو على وقت نزول المطر أو مجيء الغائب أو نحو ذلك فهذا من الكبائر، وصاحبه ربما أصيب بالفتن نسأل الله السلامة والعافية، كثيرا ما يكون المتطلع إلى ذلك عرضة للفتن فيسلط عليه الجن، ويفتن في دينه، والفتنة في الدين هي شر البلاء، شر البلية البلاء في الدين، والذي يبتلى في دينه يظهر له بعض الصدق فيما يخبر به الجان، أو ما يطلع عليه عن طريق هذه الوسائل، فيفتن بذلك ويظن أن كل ما يخبر به عن هذا الوجه صدق، فيتبع ذلك السبيل المظلم وبذلك تزل قدم بعد ثبوتها ويضل عن سواء الصراط نسأل الله السلامة والعافية.

يجب على المؤمن أن يستسلم لقدر الله خيره وشره، وأن يؤمن بذلك، وأن يعلم أن ما أصابه لم يكن ليخطئه وأن ما أخطأه لم يكن ليصيبه، وأنه رفعت الأقلام وجفت الصحف عما هو كائن، وأنه لا يقع في الكون شيء إلا بأمر الله وتدبيره، فيرضى حينئذ بكل ما كتب له، ولا يكون حينئذ صاحب تطلع إلى ما حجب عنه، وكلما كان الإنسان أوثق صلة بالله وأقوى إيمانا به كلما زهد في البحث عن المغيبات والأمور التي لا يطلع عليها.

وأعرف شيخا كبيرا من العلماء وهو الشيخ محمد يَبْرَ ولد بيه رحمة الله عليه كان أصم لا يسمع، وإنما يكتب له محدثه في الهواء فيفقه بالكتابة، فكتبت له: أن جهازا يوضع على الأذن يمكن عن طريقه السمع، وأني مستعد لأن أوفره له، فقال: أنا لا أريد أن أطلع على ما كتم ربي عني، فلم يرض أبدا باستعمال هذا الجهاز مع أنه من الأمور الجائزة، وليس من التطلع على الغيبيات، لكن من أهل العلم من يبلغ مستوى من التوكل على الله سبحانه وتعالى يظن أن هذا النوع من المعالجة هو مثل الكي، والنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «ما أحب أن أكتوي»، فيصل إلى هذا المستوى،

ولذلك فالكزانة إذا كانت هي الخط، فقد كان نبي من أنبياء الله في الماضي يخط، فمن وافق خطه خط ذلك النبي فلا بأس، وإلا فلا خير فيها، كما بين النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ذلك، ونحن الآن لا نستطيع أبدا أن نجزم بأن أي شيء منها موافق لما كان ذلك النبي يخطه، لأنه لا إسناد لنا في ذلك، فدل ذلك على حرمة الإشتغال بها مطلقا بجميع أنواعها وجميع هيئاتها، وأنه لا يحل التطلع على الغيبيات مطلقا بأي وسيلة من الوسائل.
body_en:
The ruling on enjoining right and forbidding wrong where a woman is concerned

Is it permissible for a woman to enjoin right and forbid wrong?

Yes; rather she is obliged to enjoin right and forbid wrong. And it is likewise obligatory that right be enjoined upon her: it is obligatory upon men, if they see a wrong among the women, to forbid the wrong and to enjoin the right. The Messenger of God, upon whom be peace, used to undertake that himself. In the two Ṣaḥīḥs: he delivered the Eid sermon, and thought that the women had not heard him, so he leaned upon Bilal and stood over the women and admonished them, and said: 'O company of women, give charity, for I have seen you to be the majority of the people of the Fire.' So the women wept, and Bilal spread out his garment, and the women began reaching with their hands to their jewellery and throwing it into Bilal's garment.

------------------------------------------------------------

The ruling on certain remembrances not transmitted from the Messenger of God ﷺ and tied to particular occasions

Here is a sheet with remembrances written on it, distributed as photocopies, and on it is that this is the glorification for the month of Ramadan, and that on the first day one says, a hundred times: 'Glory be to the One whom the heavens glorify with their farthest reaches.'

This kind of thing is innovation (bidʿah), and is among what God has not given leave for and what the Messenger of God, upon whom be peace, did not bring. For that reason it must be abandoned and left, and in what the Messenger of God, upon whom be peace, brought there is sufficiency to dispense with the like of this...

------------------------------------------------------------

The ruling on hanging amulets

Is the one who hangs an amulet an associator of partners with God?

This is lesser association (shirk aṣghar), not greater association — unless he believes that it benefits him and lifts harm from him, in which case that is greater association, by virtue of the belief. But merely hanging it is lesser association, which does not take one out of the religion, like swearing by other than God and the like. For the Prophet, upon whom be peace, said: 'Whoever hangs an amulet is consigned to it'; and he said: 'Whoever hangs an amulet — may God not bring anything to completion for him'; and he said: 'Whoever hangs anything is consigned to it'; and he likewise said: 'Incantations, amulets and love-charms are association.' What is meant by that is an association below association, and it does not take one out of the religion.

------------------------------------------------------------

The ruling on al-kazānah

What is the ruling on what is called al-kazānah, of whatever kind it may be?

God has kept the unseen to Himself. He said: {Knower of the unseen; and He does not disclose His unseen to anyone} (Sūrat al-Jinn 72:26). And He said: {Say: none in the heavens or the earth knows the unseen except God} (Sūrat al-Naml 27:65). The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, made clear that the keys of the unseen — which are the locks of the unseen — are five, which none knows but God. And God, exalted, says: {And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them but He} (Sūrat al-Anʿām 6:59). And these five are: {Indeed, God — with Him is knowledge of the Hour; and He sends down the rain; and He knows what is in the wombs. And no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die} (Sūrat Luqmān 31:34).

Attempting to look into them — as when a person wants to know his appointed term, or his provision and what he will be provided with tomorrow, or the time the rain will fall, or the coming of one who is absent, or the like — this is among the grave sins. Its perpetrator may well be struck with trials; we ask God for safety and well-being. Very often the one who seeks to look into that becomes exposed to trials, so that the jinn are set upon him and he is tried in his religion. Trial in one's religion is the worst of afflictions; the worst of calamities is calamity in religion. The one who is tried in his religion has some truth appear to him in what the jinn tell him, or in what he comes to know by these means, and so he is put to trial by it and supposes that everything he is told from that quarter is true; and so he follows that dark path, and by it a foot slips after being firm, and he strays from the evenness of the way — we ask God for safety and well-being.

The believer is obliged to submit to God's decree, its good and its evil, and to believe in that; and to know that what has befallen him could not have missed him and what has missed him could not have befallen him; and that the pens have been lifted and the pages have dried over what is to be; and that nothing occurs in the universe except by God's command and His ordering. Then he is content with everything that has been written for him, and is not one who reaches after what has been veiled from him. The more firmly bound a person is to God, and the stronger his faith in Him, the less he cares to search out things of the unseen and matters he is not given to know.

I know a great old scholar, Shaykh Muhammad Yabra Ould Bayyah, God's mercy be upon him, who was deaf and could not hear; whoever spoke with him would write for him in the air, and he would understand by the writing. I wrote to him that there is a device placed on the ear by means of which hearing is possible, and that I was ready to provide it for him. He said: I do not wish to come to know what my Lord has kept from me. He never consented to use this device, even though it is among the permissible things and is not a matter of seeking to look into things of the unseen; but among the scholars there are those who reach a level of reliance upon God, glorified and exalted, at which they hold this kind of treatment to be like cauterisation — and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: 'I do not like to be cauterised.' So he reaches this level.

Therefore al-kazānah, if it is the drawing of lines: a prophet among the prophets of God in the past used to draw lines, so whoever's drawing coincides with the drawing of that prophet, there is no harm in it, and otherwise there is no good in it — as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, made clear. And we today can never assert with certainty that any of it coincides with what that prophet used to draw, because we have no chain of transmission for that. This indicates the prohibition of occupying oneself with it absolutely, in all its kinds and all its forms, and that it is not lawful to seek to look into things of the unseen at all, by any means whatsoever.

flags.arabic: هل يجوز أمر المرأة بالمعروف ونهيها عن المنكر؟
flags.context: the first item
options: the ruling on enjoining right and forbidding wrong where a woman is concerned — keeping the ambiguity
is it permissible for a woman to enjoin right and forbid wrong?
is it permissible to enjoin right upon a woman and forbid her wrong?
flags.note: The Arabic genitive أمر المرأة is ambiguous between the woman as the one who enjoins and the woman as the one enjoined, and the Sheikh answers BOTH senses in a single breath: she is obliged to enjoin right, and it is obligatory that right be enjoined upon her. English cannot hold both in one clause, so the heading has been kept deliberately open and the body spells out the two halves as he does. A rendering that picks only one sense would lose half of his answer.

flags.arabic: غير الواردة عن رسول الله r
flags.context: the heading of the second item
options: read the stray 'r' as the honorific ﷺ lost in font conversion, and render it as such (done here)
reproduce the stray character as printed
omit the character
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT (style guide §11). A bare Latin 'r' stands where the honorific belongs. This is the well-known artifact of Arabic symbol fonts in which the glyph ﷺ is mapped to the character 'r'; the CMS has stored the character rather than the glyph. The stray letter is preserved in body_ar and rendered as the honorific in body_en. Worth checking corpus-wide, since the same font mapping will have produced the same artifact elsewhere.

flags.context: حكم لكزانة … ما حكم ما يسمى بالكزانة أيا كان نوعها؟
options: al-kazānah — the same Mauritanian term as al-gazzānah elsewhere in the corpus
sand-divination (al-kazānah)
geomancy
flags.note: A third spelling of the same Hassaniya word: الگزانه in article 526, لكْزانَه in article 540, and الكزانة / لكزانة here. All three should be recognised as one term when the corpus is indexed. Note that the Sheikh's ruling here is firmer than in article 526: here he concludes that occupying oneself with it is prohibited absolutely, in every kind and form, because no chain to the prophet who drew lines survives.

flags.arabic: فلم يرض أبدا باستعمال هذا الجهاز مع أنه من الأمور الجائزة
flags.context: the anecdote about the hearing aid
options: keep the Sheikh's explicit statement that the device is permissible
render the anecdote without the qualification
render the anecdote as a recommendation
flags.note: IMPORTANT FOR DISPLAY. The Sheikh tells this story in praise of the old scholar's reliance on God, but he states plainly, in the same sentence, that the hearing aid is among the permissible things and that using it is not a matter of prying into the unseen. Detached from that qualification the anecdote would read as a ruling against hearing aids, which is the opposite of what he says. The qualification must never be dropped in any excerpt or summary of this item.

flags.arabic: هذا شرك أصغر ليس شركا أكبر
flags.context: the third item
options: lesser association (shirk aṣghar) / greater association (shirk akbar)
minor shirk / major shirk
lesser idolatry / greater idolatry
flags.note: CROSS-REFERENCE. In article 537 of this slice the Sheikh says of the same practice that the Prophet 'counted it as associating partners with God' and that hanging amulets is forbidden (ḥarām), without distinguishing the two degrees. Here he distinguishes them and states that merely hanging an amulet does not take a person out of the religion. The two answers are not in conflict but they read very differently in isolation, and neither has been adjusted to the other. A reviewer should decide whether the site links them.

Four separate fatwas are published on this one page, divided in the source by rules of hyphens. The rules are preserved in both body_ar and body_en so the boundaries survive; the site should render them as four separate items. Each item's own heading is part of the source text and has been kept.
The second item breaks off with an ellipsis in the source ('غنية عن مثل هذا...'). The ellipsis has been reproduced; it is not a truncation introduced in extraction.

The Sheikh quotes the Qur'an in the fourth item without references; the references have been supplied in the English per house style and the Arabic has not been altered. The four hadiths on amulets in the third item are given without collection or grading, and none has been supplied.
'The pens have been lifted and the pages have dried' renders رفعت الأقلام وجفت الصحف, the formula of the hadith on the decree; the Sheikh gives it without attribution.
Source spellings preserved verbatim in body_ar: الإطلاع and الإشتغال written with connecting hamzas, and the vowelled proper name محمد يَبْرَ ولد بيه.

title_ar: عبارة أضمن على الله
title_en: The Expression 'I Guarantee upon God'
body_ar:
إن الناس ألفوا أن يقولوا أضمن على الله لك كذا، فهل هذه العبارة مستساغة شرعا؟

أن هذه العبارة مبناها في الأصل على حديث موضوع وقد جاء فيه: «البخيل من لا يضمن على الله» لكن هذا لا يصح عن النبي (ص)، وهو من الموضوعات، فلذلك لا ينبغي أن يقولها الإنسان إلا إذا كان المقصود عنده أن صاحب الفعل إن فعل ذلك ابتغاء مرضاة الله فقد وعده الله خيرا على ذلك الفعل، فهذا القصد، فإنك تستطيع ضمان ما ضمنه الله في كتابه، كل ما تعهد الله به في كتابه أو تعهد به رسوله (ص) فأنت تعلم أنه سيقع فيمكن أن تضمن وقوعه.
body_en:
People have grown accustomed to saying, 'I guarantee upon God that you will have such-and-such.' Is this expression acceptable in the revealed law?

This expression rests, in origin, upon a fabricated hadith (mawḍūʿ), in which it comes: 'The miser is the one who does not guarantee upon God.' But this is not sound from the Prophet, upon whom be peace; it is among the fabrications. For that reason a person should not say it — unless what he means by it is that the one who does the deed, if he does it seeking God's good pleasure, has been promised good by God for that deed. That is the intention that would make it acceptable; for you are able to guarantee what God has guaranteed in His Book. Everything that God has undertaken in His Book, or that His Messenger, upon whom be peace, has undertaken, you know will come to pass — so you can guarantee that it will occur.

flags.context: إن الناس ألفوا أن يقولوا أضمن على الله لك كذا
options: I guarantee upon God that you will have such-and-such
I stand surety with God that you will have such-and-such
I vouch for it with God that you will have such-and-such
flags.note: The whole fatwa turns on the preposition: ضمن على الله is to make oneself guarantor of something AGAINST God, as a debt is guaranteed against a debtor — which is precisely what makes the phrase objectionable, and why the Sheikh permits it only where it means guaranteeing what God has already undertaken in His own Book. A smoother English idiom such as 'I promise you in God's name' would lose the surety relation the answer depends on. The literal rendering has been kept for that reason.

flags.arabic: البخيل من لا يضمن على الله
flags.context: مبناها في الأصل على حديث موضوع وقد جاء فيه: «البخيل من لا يضمن على الله»
options: The miser is the one who does not guarantee upon God
The miser is the one who will not stand surety with God
The niggardly man is he who does not vouch for God
flags.note: The wording is quoted only in order to be rejected: the Sheikh grades it fabricated (mawḍūʿ) and says explicitly that it is not sound from the Prophet. Any display of this article must keep the grading attached to the quotation, since the sentence is quotable on its own and would circulate as a hadith. The Sheikh names no collection and no one who fabricated it.

translator_notes: Hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.
The Sheikh's grading has been carried exactly: the report is fabricated and not soundly established from the Prophet. Nothing has been added and nothing softened.

His ruling on the expression is لا ينبغي, 'should not', with a stated exception — not ḥarām and not makrūh. No ruling word has been supplied for him, and the exception has not been dropped: on his account the phrase is acceptable where the speaker means only to guarantee what God has already undertaken in His Book.
The question is put by the questioner about common usage ('people have grown accustomed'), and the answer is about the phrase, not about any individual.

title_ar: علاقة علم المنطق بالتوحيد
title_en: The Relation of the Science of Logic to the Affirmation of God's Oneness
body_ar:
ما علاقة علم المنطق بالتوحيد؟

أن علم المنطق هو علم المقاييس العقلية التي يدرك بها الإنسان الأدلة العقلية، فمرجع المنطق إلى التفريق بين التصور والتصديق، والتصور هو إدراك المفردات والتصديق هو إدراك النسب، والتصور إنما يوصل إليه بالمعرفات والتصديق إنما يوصل إليه بالحجج، وهذه الأمور إذا عرفها الإنسان عرف ما هو دليل عقلا وما يحتاج إلى الإثبات وما لا يحتاج إليه وعرف الخطأ في الأدلة وطريقة تركيب الأدلة، فهو معيار ليس فيه محذور شرعا في التوحيد ولا في غيره، لكن يمكن أن يستغل في الخير ويمكن أن يستغل في الشر، فتعلمه مثل تعلم الرياضيات مثل تعلم الحساب مثل تعلم الكتابة هو من المعايير التي يمكن أن يكال بها السمن ويكال بها الخمر ويكال بها اللبن، فبحسب استغلاله.
body_en:
What is the relation of the science of logic to the affirmation of God's oneness (tawḥīd)?

The science of logic is the science of the rational measures by which a person grasps rational proofs. Logic comes back to the distinction between conception (taṣawwur) and assent (taṣdīq). Conception is the grasp of single terms; assent is the grasp of the relations between them. Conception is arrived at only by way of definitions (muʿarrifāt), and assent only by way of proofs (ḥujaj). When a person knows these matters, he knows what counts as a proof rationally, what stands in need of demonstration and what does not; and he knows where error enters into proofs, and how proofs are put together. So it is an instrument of measurement in which there is nothing objectionable in the revealed law, neither in tawḥīd nor in anything else — but it can be turned to good use and it can be turned to evil use. Learning it is like learning mathematics, like learning arithmetic, like learning writing: it is one of those measures with which clarified butter may be measured out, and wine may be measured out, and milk may be measured out. It goes according to the use that is made of it.

flags.arabic: فهو معيار ليس فيه محذور شرعا
flags.context: the Sheikh's own verdict on studying logic
options: render literally as 'there is nothing objectionable in it in the revealed law'
render as 'it is permissible (mubāḥ)'
render as 'it is allowed'
flags.note: The Sheikh deliberately does not use any of the five ruling terms here. He says there is no maḥdhūr (nothing to be guarded against) in it in the revealed law, and then makes the verdict depend entirely on use. Rendering this as 'permissible (mubāḥ)' would assign a five-rulings category he did not assign, and would lose the conditionality of his answer.

flags.arabic: معيار / المعايير ... يكال بها السمن ويكال بها الخمر ويكال بها اللبن
flags.context: the closing image comparing logic to a measuring vessel
options: instrument of measurement / measures (with which ghee, wine and milk may be measured out)
standard / criterion
yardstick
flags.note: miʿyār here is the concrete measuring vessel, not an abstract criterion: the point of the image is that the same vessel measures out a lawful substance and an unlawful one. 'Criterion' or 'yardstick' loses the concrete figure and with it the argument.

translator_notes: The date carried here is the CMS record date. Across this whole slice the site serves a bulk-upload timestamp of 19-21 December 2010, which is when the written archive was loaded into the site, not when the Sheikh gave the answer. date_is_cms_upload is set true. The real date of composition is not recoverable from the page and has not been guessed.
The question is stated in the body itself; the title restates it. Nothing has been supplied.
taṣawwur and taṣdīq are the standard pair in Arabic logic. They have been rendered 'conception' and 'assent' and the Arabic kept in brackets, since no settled English pair exists.
The Sheikh gives no ruling on the five-rulings scale and none has been supplied. See the flag.

title_ar: محبة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ومحبة ما جاء به
title_en: Love of the Messenger of God, Peace and Blessings Be upon Him, and Love of What He Brought
body_ar:
بأي طريقة يحب الإنسان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم محبة كاملة ويحب كل ما جاء به؟

أن من أراد أن يحب رسول الله (ص) فعليه أن يتعرف عليه أولا، أن يعرف من هو رسول الله (ص)، فإذا درس الإنسان سيرته وشخصيته وحياته فلا بد أن يحبه حبا شديدا، ولذلك فإن أهل الأندلس لما ألف القاضي عياض رحمه الله كتاب الشفا في التعريف بحقوق المصطفى (ص) فقرأوه قالوا: لولا الشفا لما عرف المصطفى (ص)، فلا بد أن يتعرف الإنسان إلى النبي (ص) وأن يدرس سيرته، وحياته وشمائله حتى يحبه حبا شديدا، ثم بعد ذلك أن يتعود على هذه المحبة لعلمه أنها شرط لإيمانه كما قال النبي (ص): «لا يؤمن أحدكم حتى أكون أحب إليه من والده وولده والناس أجمعين» فلا بد أن يتدرب على محبته وإيثاره وتقديمه على كل من سواه.
body_en:
By what means does a person come to love the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, with a complete love, and to love everything he brought?

Whoever wishes to love the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, must first come to know him — to know who the Messenger of God is. If a person studies his biography (sīrah), his character and his life, he cannot but come to love him intensely. That is why, when Qadi ʿIyad, God have mercy on him, composed the book al-Shifāʾ fī l-taʿrīf bi-ḥuqūq al-Muṣṭafā ('The Cure: On Making Known the Rights of the Chosen One'), the people of Andalusia read it and said: 'Were it not for al-Shifāʾ, the Chosen One would not be known.' So a person must come to know the Prophet, and must study his biography, his life and his personal qualities (shamāʾil), until he loves him intensely. Then after that he should accustom himself to this love, knowing that it is a condition (sharṭ) of his faith (īmān), as the Prophet said: 'None of you believes until I am more beloved to him than his father, his child and all people.' So he must train himself in loving him, in giving him preference, and in putting him ahead of everyone besides him.

flags.context: the saying the Sheikh attributes to the people of Andalusia about Qadi ʿIyad's al-Shifāʾ
options: Were it not for al-Shifāʾ, the Chosen One would not be known
But for al-Shifāʾ, al-Muṣṭafā would not have been recognised
Without al-Shifāʾ, the Chosen One would have gone unknown
flags.note: The Arabic is a rhymed saying (al-Shifā / al-Muṣṭafā) and the rhyme cannot be carried into English without distorting the sense; it has been rendered as plain prose per the house rule against rhymed English. The saying is proverbial in the Maghrib; the Sheikh reports it of 'the people of Andalusia' and gives no source, and none has been supplied.

flags.context: وأن يدرس سيرته، وحياته وشمائله
options: his personal qualities (shamāʾil)
his character traits
his noble characteristics
flags.note: shamāʾil is a genre term as much as a common noun — the literature on the Prophet's physical description, manners and habits, of which al-Tirmidhi's al-Shamāʾil is the type. The Sheikh is listing three fields of study side by side (sīrah, life, shamāʾil), so the English should read as a field of study and not as a loose synonym for 'character', which he has already used in the previous sentence.

Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.

The source writes the eulogy after the Prophet's name sometimes in full (صلى الله عليه وسلم) and sometimes as the abbreviation (ص). Both are rendered in English as 'peace and blessings be upon him'; the abbreviation is preserved in body_ar.

The full title of Qadi ʿIyad's work is given in the source in a shortened form (كتاب الشفا في التعريف بحقوق المصطفى). title_ar: هل ما جاز أن يكون معجزة لنبي جاز أن يكون كرامة لولي؟
title_en: May Whatever Could Be a Miracle for a Prophet Also Be a Wonder for a Friend of God?
body_ar:
لا ولا يمكن أن يقع ذلك بحال من الأحوال لو كان كذلك لجاز أن ينزل الوحي على الأولياء الذين ليسوا بأنبياء فمعجزة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم الوحي المنزل إليه فلو كان كلما جاز أن يكون معجزة لنبي يجوز أن يكون كرامة لولي لادعى كثير من الناس أنهم أنزل إليهم قرءان يتلى وهذا لا يمكن أن يقع أصلا و لا يمكن أن يتصوره مؤمن لكن البحث في المسألة هو ما تصل إليه كرامات الأولياء فكرامات الأولياء حق ومن عقيدة أهل السنة والجماعة إثباتها وهي أن الله يكرم من أطاعه فالله أكرم الأكرمين وأرحم الراحمين ولا يمكن أن يتساوى لديه أهل الإيمان وأهل الكفر وهو الذي يقول في كتابه﴿أفنجعل المسلمين كالمجرمين ما لكم كيف تحكمون﴾

فمن كان من أهل التقوى والورع و العبادة والصلاح لا يمكن أن يستوي مع الفاسق المجاهر أبدا لا يمكن أن يستويا عند الله تعالى فلذلك يكرم أولياءه بما يعينهم عليه من طاعته و يشرفهم بأنواع التشريف الذي منه العلم النافع والعمل الصالح وهذه الكرامات أعظمها الاستقامة على الدين أعظم كرامة يكرم الله بها الولي استقامته على أمر الدين بحيث يملك جوارحه عما حرم الله عليه والكرامات حق لكن اختلف في مبلغها إلى أي شيء تبلغ واتفقوا على أنها لا تبلغ نزول الوحي أو وجود ولد من غير والد أو إحياء الموتى لكنها تبلغ ما دون ذلك كالعلم من غير تعلم وكالعون على الطاعة كطي المسافات ووجود الأموال من غير تسبب ونحو ذلك فهذا حاصل فعمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه طوي صوته مسافة شاسعة ما بين المدينة و بين فارس حين نادى سارية ابن زنيم فقال يا سارية الجبل الجبل وهذا الحديث أخرجه أحمد في فضائل الصحابة بعدة أسانيد أحدها إسناد صحيح وقد أخرجه ابن وهب في الجامع و عدد من المؤلفين في دواوين الحديث وهو حديث صحيح وكذلك فإن عثمان رضي الله عنه كان يرى أثر المعصية في وجه صاحبها فقد كان عنده أنس ابن مالك فدخل عليه رجل فقال: ما بال أحدكم يدخل علي وفي عينيه أثر الزنا فأقر الرجل فقال له أنس أوحي بعد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لا ولكنها فراسة المؤمن وكذلك الحال بالنسبة لعدد من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حصلت لهم كرامات عظيمة فالعلاء ابن الحضرمي رضي الله عنه خاض البحر فيبس أمامه حتى قطعه وكذلك فإن المرأة المهاجرة تدلى لها دلو من السماء حتى شربت منه حين ظمأها أهلها، وكذلك فإن من دونهم من التابعين حصل لهم أيضا شيء كثير من هذا بل قد قال شيخ الإسلام ابن تيمية رحمه الله إن الكرامات كلما انتقص الإيمان والعبادة في الناس وكلما انتقص العلم كلما ازدادت هي لأن الناس إذا كانوا أهل إيمان و ورع وتقوى لا يحتاجون إلى هذه الكرامات التي تزيد إيمانهم بالغيب وإذا نقص لديهم الإيمان بالغيب كثرت فيهم هذه الكرامات لأولياء الله أصحاب الإستقامة و الإلتزام بالحق ومع هذا فإن كثيرا من الناس تلتبس عليهم الكرامة بما ليس بكرامة.
body_en:
No. That cannot occur under any circumstance. If it were so, it would be possible for revelation to come down upon friends of God (awliyāʾ) who are not prophets — for the miracle of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, is the revelation sent down to him. If everything that could be a miracle for a prophet could be a wonder (karāmah) for a friend of God, then many people would claim that a Qur'an to be recited had been sent down to them; and this cannot occur at all, and no believer can conceive of it.

But the point of inquiry in the question is how far the wonders of the friends of God extend. The wonders of the friends of God are real, and affirming them is part of the creed of the people of the sunnah and the community: namely that God honours those who obey Him. For God is the most generous of the generous and the most merciful of the merciful, and it is not possible that the people of faith and the people of unbelief should be equal in His sight — He who says in His Book: {Shall We then treat those who submit like the criminals? What is the matter with you? How do you judge?} (Sūrat al-Qalam 68:35–36).

So one who is of the people of God-consciousness, scrupulousness, worship and uprightness cannot ever be the equal of the open transgressor; they cannot be equal in the sight of God, exalted. For that reason He honours His friends with what helps them to obey Him, and ennobles them with kinds of ennoblement, among which are beneficial knowledge and righteous action. The greatest of these wonders is steadfastness upon the religion: the greatest wonder with which God honours a friend of His is his steadfastness in the matter of religion, such that he has mastery over his own limbs where God has made something forbidden to him. The wonders are real, but there is disagreement over their extent — how far they reach. They agreed that they do not reach the descent of revelation, nor the coming to be of a child without a father, nor the raising of the dead; but they do reach what is below that, such as knowledge without learning, and help towards obedience, such as the folding up of distances, and the appearing of money without any means being taken to it, and the like. This does occur.

ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, God be pleased with him, had his voice folded across a vast distance between Medina and Persia, when he called out to Sariyah ibn Zunaym and said: 'Sariyah, the mountain! The mountain!' This report was brought out by Ahmad in Faḍāʾil al-Ṣaḥābah by several chains of transmission, one of them a sound chain; and Ibn Wahb brought it out in al-Jāmiʿ, and a number of authors in the collections of hadith; and it is a sound report. Likewise ʿUthman, God be pleased with him, used to see the trace of a sin on the face of the one who had committed it. Anas ibn Malik was with him, and a man came in upon him, and he said: 'What is the matter with one of you, that he comes in upon me with the trace of fornication in his eyes?' And the man confessed. So Anas said to him: 'Is there revelation after the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him?' He said: 'No — but it is the discernment of the believer.'

It is the same in the case of a number of the Companions of the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him: great wonders occurred for them. Al-ʿAla ibn al-Hadrami, God be pleased with him, waded into the sea and it dried before him until he crossed it. And likewise the emigrant woman, for whom a bucket was let down from heaven so that she drank from it, when her own people left her thirsty. Likewise those below them among the Successors — much of this occurred for them too. Indeed the Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, God have mercy on him, said that the more faith and worship are diminished among people, and the more knowledge is diminished, the more the wonders increase — because when people are people of faith and scrupulousness and God-consciousness, they have no need of these wonders that increase their faith in the unseen; and when their faith in the unseen is diminished, these wonders become frequent among them, for the friends of God who are the people of steadfastness and of holding fast to the truth. And even so, many people confuse a wonder with what is no wonder at all.

flags.context: the pair the whole answer turns on
options: wonder (karāmah) for a friend of God, against miracle (muʿjizah) for a prophet
charism against miracle
saintly marvel against prophetic miracle
flags.note: Neither term is in the glossary and both should be added, since the distinction is the substance of the answer and will recur across the corpus. A muʿjizah is evidentiary, establishing prophethood; a karāmah is not. 'Saint' for walī has been avoided throughout because it imports a Christian institution of canonisation that has no counterpart here; 'friend of God' is the literal sense and is what the Sheikh's argument uses.

flags.arabic: واتفقوا على أنها لا تبلغ نزول الوحي أو وجود ولد من غير والد أو إحياء الموتى … لكن اختلف في مبلغها
flags.context: the scope of the agreement and of the disagreement
options: keep the agreed limits and the open disagreement clearly separate, as done here
present the whole passage as settled
present the whole passage as disputed
flags.note: IMPORTANT — DO NOT CLOSE WHAT HE LEFT OPEN. The Sheikh marks a precise boundary: there is consensus that wonders do not reach revelation, virgin birth or raising the dead; and there is unresolved disagreement about exactly how far below that they do reach. He gives examples of what he says does occur but does not claim the disagreement is settled. The English must keep the agreement and the disagreement apart, and must not let his examples read as a ruling on the disputed extent.

flags.arabic: فقد كان عنده أنس ابن مالك فدخل عليه رجل فقال

clarify who speaks each line

flags.note: The pronouns in this account are hard to follow as printed: it is not made explicit that the man who confesses is the one who entered, nor that 'he said: No — but it is the discernment of the believer' is ʿUthman answering Anas. The English keeps the Arabic's own looseness rather than resolving it by inserting names. The Sheikh gives no narrator, collection or grading for this account, unlike the preceding one, and none has been supplied.

flags.arabic: وهذا الحديث أخرجه أحمد في فضائل الصحابة بعدة أسانيد أحدها إسناد صحيح … وهو حديث صحيح

options: reproduce the attribution and grading exactly as he gives them

title_ar: هل هذا زمان الخويصة ؟
title_en: Is This the Time of al-Khuwayṣṣah?
body_ar:
لا فزمان الخويصة هو الزمان الذي لا يطاع فيه الإنسان إذا أمر، إذا نهى عن منكر لم يطع و إذا أمر بمعروف لم يطع و هذا الزمان ما زال الناس و لله الحمد فيهم خير كثير فلم يأت ذلك الزمان بعد و ذلك الزمان لا يكون أيضا مستمرا لوقت طويل كما يتوهمه بعض الناس يظن أن زمان الخويصة هو آخر هذه الأمة أو زمان مستمر منها وهذا غير صحيح زمان الخويصة فترة تمر بالقرى إذا أراد الله إهلاكها فإن الله تعالى تعهد بإهلاك كل قرية قبل قيام الساعة فقال تعالى:﴿و إن من قرية إلا نحن مهلكوها قبل يوم القيامة أو معذبوها عذابا شديدا كان ذلك في الكتاب مسطورا﴾

و قد بين الله علامة ذلك الإهلاك و هو أن يسلط عليها مترفي أهلها فيأمرهم فيها فيكثروا فيها الفساد فلا يستطيع أحد التغيير عليهم و لا الإنكار عليهم لأنهم يخوفون الناس فيستسلم لهم الجميع فيمدحونهم في وجوههم و يذمونهم في قفاهم و لا ينكرون عليهم شيئا مما يفعلونه فإذا ظهر ذلك و لم يوجد منكر للمنكر فذلك وقت الخويصة يعتزل أهل الخير حتى يأتي العذاب فيهلك تلك القرية و لذلك قال الله تعالى: ﴿و إذا أردنا أن نهلك قرية أمرنا مترفيها﴾، أمرنا بمعنى جعلناهم أمراء و لذلك في القراءة الأخرى ﴿أمَّرنا﴾ ﴿ففسقوا فيها فحق عليها القول فدمرناها تدميرا﴾ وهذه الأمور متقاربة لأن الفاء للترتيب و التعقيب فإذا جاء العطف بالفاء فإنه يقتضي القرب: ﴿أمرنا مترفيها ففسقوا فيها فحق عليها القول فدمرناها تدميرا﴾ أمور متفاوتة جدا و هذه الأمور وقتها هو وقت الخويصة إذا حصل ذلك لكن هذه الأمة ما زالت بخير و فيها كثير من أهل الاستقامة و الصلاح وفيها كثير من الذين يحبون الخير و يحبون أهله و لذلك لا يغتر أحد بأن العزلة أفضل في هذا الزمان فهذا غير صحيح فالمؤمن الذي يخالط الناس ويصبر على أذاهم خير من المؤمن الذي لا يخالط الناس و لا يصبر على أذاهم.
body_en:
No. The time of al-khuwayṣṣah is the time in which a person is not obeyed when he commands: when he forbids a wrong he is not obeyed, and when he enjoins a right he is not obeyed. In this time of ours people still — praise be to God — have much good in them, so that time has not yet come. Nor is that time continuous for a long period, as some people imagine: they suppose that the time of al-khuwayṣṣah is the end of this community, or a continuous stretch of it, and this is not correct. The time of al-khuwayṣṣah is a period that passes over towns when God wills to destroy them; for God, exalted, has undertaken the destruction of every town before the coming of the Hour, saying, exalted: {And there is no town but that We shall destroy it before the Day of Resurrection, or punish it with a severe punishment; that is written in the Book} (Sūrat al-Isrāʾ 17:58).

And God has set out the sign of that destruction: that He gives power over the town to the luxurious among its people, so that they command in it and multiply corruption in it, and no one is able to change what they do or to denounce them — because they make people afraid, so that everyone submits to them and praises them to their faces and blames them behind their backs, and denounces nothing of what they do. So when that appears, and there is no one to denounce the wrong, that is the time of al-khuwayṣṣah: the people of good withdraw, until the punishment comes and destroys that town. That is why God, exalted, said: {And when We will to destroy a town, We command its luxurious ones} (Sūrat al-Isrāʾ 17:16) — 'We command' meaning We made them commanders, which is why in the other canonical reading it is {We appointed as commanders}; {so they transgress in it, and the word comes due against it, and We destroy it utterly}. These things follow closely on one another, because the connective fa indicates sequence and immediate succession, so when the linkage comes with fa it implies closeness: {We command its luxurious ones, so they transgress in it, so the word comes due against it, so We destroy it utterly}. They are matters very different from one another. These things — their time is the time of al-khuwayṣṣah, if that happens.

But this community is still in a good state, and there are in it many of the people of steadfastness and uprightness, and many who love good and love its people. So let no one be deluded into thinking that withdrawal is better in this time of ours; that is not correct. The believer who mixes with people and bears their harm patiently is better than the believer who does not mix with people and does not bear their harm patiently.

flags.context: the term the whole record is built on, used five times
options: keep in transliteration as al-khuwayṣṣah and let the Sheikh's own definition carry it
render as 'the time of every man for himself'
render as 'the time of private concern'
flags.note: NEEDS A FIXED RENDERING. al-khuwayṣṣah is the diminutive of khāṣṣah and comes from the report in which the Prophet, asked about a time when enjoining right is not heeded, says 'then take to your own particular concern' (ʿalayka bi-khāṣṣat nafsika). It has no English handle. The Sheikh defines it himself in his first sentence, so the transliteration is not left bare, but the term is not in the glossary and should be added. He does not quote the underlying report here and it has not been supplied.

flags.context: the Sheikh's appeal to a variant canonical reading of Sūrat al-Isrāʾ 17:16
options: keep the variant reading visible in the English as a distinct rendering
render both readings identically
omit the variant
flags.note: This is a point of qirāʾāt: the Sheikh glosses amarnā ('We commanded') as meaning 'We made them commanders', and supports it by citing the variant reading ammarnā, which says so explicitly. The two readings cannot be rendered identically in English without destroying his argument, so they have been given as 'We command' and 'We appointed as commanders'. He names neither reader nor transmission for the variant, and nothing has been supplied.

flags.context: the sentence immediately after the repeated verse
options: They are matters very different from one another
They are matters that are very far apart
mark as corrupt, since it appears to contradict the preceding sentence
flags.note: SOURCE DIFFICULTY. The Sheikh has just argued that the connective fa shows these events follow closely on one another (mutaqāribah), and the very next sentence says they are mutafāwitah jiddan, very disparate — which reads as a flat contradiction. Either a clause has dropped out in transcription, or mutafāwitah is a slip. The Arabic is preserved and the English renders it as it stands, contradiction included, rather than smoothing it. A reviewer should resolve this; it is the one passage in the record whose sense is not recoverable.

flags.arabic: لا يغتر أحد بأن العزلة أفضل في هذا الزمان فهذا غير صحيح
flags.context: the Sheikh's closing counsel
options: let no one be deluded into thinking that withdrawal is better in this time of ours
no one should be misled into supposing seclusion is preferable today
withdrawal from society is not better in our time
flags.note: This closing sentence is the practical point of the whole answer and it reverses the direction a reader might expect from everything before it: having described in detail what the time of withdrawal looks like, the Sheikh rules that this is not that time and that mixing with people is better. Option 3 loses his verb ightarra ('be deluded'), which carries the force of his correction. The final comparison is the wording of a well-known report, which he gives without attribution; nothing has been supplied.
