title_ar: الدرس الثالث من سلسلة دروس دورة الفرائض العلمية
title_en: The third lesson of the series of lessons of the scholarly course on the law of inheritance shares
body_ar:
الكاتب : الشيخ محمد الحسن ولد الددو الدرس الثاني من دروس دورة الفرائض العلمية التي ألقاها ودرسها الشيخ محمد الحسن ولد الددو بمركز تكوين العلماء بنواكشوط

بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

الحمد لله رب العالمين وأصلي وأسلم على من بعث رحمة للعالمين وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين، السلام عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته.

كان الحديث في الدرس الماضي في أواخره عن موانع الإرث، فمن يذكرنا بها؟

بالنسبة لهذه الموانع التي ذكرناها هي موانع في اصطلاح الفرضيين، وإلا فليس ينطبق عليها تعريف المانع لدى الأصوليين، لأن المانع لدى الأصوليين لا بد فيه من تحقق السبب، والزنا النسب فيه وهو سبب الميراث غير موجود، لأن المعدوم شرعا كالمعدوم حسا..
body_en:
Author: Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew. The second lesson of the lessons of the scholarly course on the law of inheritance shares, delivered and taught by Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew at the Centre for the Formation of Scholars in Nouakchott.

In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate.

Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. I pray for blessing and peace upon him who was sent as a mercy to the worlds, and upon his family and his Companions and all who are guided by his guidance and follow his sunnah until the Day of Judgement. Peace be upon you, and the mercy of God and His blessings.

The discussion in the last lesson was, towards its end, about the impediments to inheritance. Who will remind us of them?

As for these impediments that we have mentioned, they are impediments in the terminology of the specialists in the inheritance shares; otherwise the definition of an impediment (māniʿ) among the legal theorists does not apply to them — because for the legal theorists an impediment requires that the cause (sabab) be realised, whereas in the case of fornication the lineage, which is the cause of inheritance, is not present, since what is non-existent in the eyes of the Sharia is like what is non-existent in fact..

flags.arabic: الدرس الثالث … / … الدرس الثاني من دروس دورة الفرائض العلمية
flags.context: the page title says 'the third lesson'; the byline immediately below it says 'the second lesson'
options: keep both as served, flag, and withhold the lesson number from any ordering of the course
treat the title as correct and the byline as the CMS error
treat the byline as correct and the title as the CMS error
flags.note: TITLE/BODY MISMATCH — the same source defect as at id 623, in the same series. Here the body's content does not settle which is right: it refers only to 'the last lesson', which is true of both a second and a third lesson. Note also that id 626 is titled 'the second lesson' and its byline agrees, so if this record's byline were taken as correct there would be two second lessons. The lesson numbers in this series should not be used to order the course until the Sheikh's office confirms them.

flags.context: the Sheikh's justification for why fornication is not strictly an impediment
options: what is non-existent in the eyes of the Sharia is like what is non-existent in fact
what the Sharia treats as non-existent is like what does not exist in reality
what is legally void is as though it did not exist at all
flags.note: A legal maxim (qāʿidah). Ḥissan is 'to the senses', i.e. in observable fact, as against sharʿan, 'in the eyes of the law'. Option 2 imports 'void' (bāṭil), which is a different technical term and would breach the glossary's ruling on bāṭil.

translator_notes: Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.
The date shown by the CMS is a bulk-upload timestamp shared by every item in this range, not the date the Sheikh gave the answer. The real date of composition is unknown. See date_is_cms_bulk_upload.

EXCERPT ONLY. The published text breaks off mid-argument and the full transcript is offered as a .docx download ('taḥmīl al-māddah'). The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends. The download-link label has been removed from body_ar as a navigation element and recorded in source_download_link.

The argument here is a characteristic usuli one and has been preserved as a reasoning chain rather than compressed: the specialists in inheritance call fornication an 'impediment', but on the legal theorists' definition an impediment presupposes that the cause of the ruling is present and only blocked, whereas here the cause — lineage — never arises at all.

'The specialists in the inheritance shares' renders al-farḍiyyūn, the jurists of the farāʾiḍ, as distinct from al-uṣūliyyūn, the legal theorists. The contrast between the two groups' usage is the whole point of the passage and must remain visible.
The lesson opens with a question put to the class ('Who will remind us of them?'). It is part of the spoken transcript and has been kept.

title_ar: الدرس الثاني من دورة الفرائض العلمية
title_en: The second lesson of the scholarly course on the law of inheritance shares
body_ar:
الكاتب : الشيخ محمد الحسن ولد الددو

ها هو الدرس الثاني من سلسلة دروس دورة الفرائض العلمية التي ألقاها و درسها الشيخ محمد الحسن ولد الددو في مركز تكوين العلماء

بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

الحمد لله رب العالمين وأصلي وأسلم على من بعث رحمة للعالمين وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين.

وصلنا بالأمس إلى قول المؤلف رحمه الله:

ونسأل الله لنا الإعانة فيما توخينا من الإبانة

عن مذهب الإمام زيد الفرضي إذ كان ذاك من أهم الغرض

من السنة في كل عمل مهم يقصد به وجه الله تعالى أن يستأنف في الدعاء، كما كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يستأنف حجه وعمرته وأسفاره وجهاده بالدعاء، ولذلك جاء بالدعاء ثالثا بعد حمد الله والصلاة على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وعلى آله وصحبه..
body_en:
Author: Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew.

Here is the second lesson of the series of lessons of the scholarly course on the law of inheritance shares, delivered and taught by Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew at the Centre for the Formation of Scholars.

In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate.

Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. I pray for blessing and peace upon him who was sent as a mercy to the worlds, and upon his family and his Companions and all who are guided by his guidance and follow his sunnah until the Day of Judgement.

Yesterday we reached the author's words, may God have mercy on him:

*And we ask God for help in the clarification we have set ourselves to give of the school of the Imam Zayd, the master of the inheritance shares, since that is among the most important of our purposes.*

It is part of the sunnah, in every important undertaking by which the face of God Most High is sought, that one begin afresh with supplication — as the Prophet, upon whom be God's blessing and peace, would begin his hajj, his lesser pilgrimage, his journeys and his struggle afresh with supplication. That is why he brought in the supplication third, after the praise of God and the prayer upon the Messenger of God, upon whom be God's blessing and peace, and upon his family and his Companions..

flags.arabic: ونسأل الله لنا الإعانة فيما توخينا من الإبانة ** عن مذهب الإمام زيد الفرضي إذ كان ذاك من أهم الغرض
flags.context: two lines of the versified text the Sheikh is commenting on
options: render as prose in italics, as here
render as two verse lines with the hemistich breaks shown
leave untranslated and give only the Arabic
flags.note: The style guide directs that verse be rendered as prose in italics with the Arabic kept in the bilingual pane, which is what has been done. Two points for the reviewer. First, the base text (matn) the Sheikh is teaching from is not named anywhere in the published excerpt; it is a didactic poem on the farāʾiḍ, but which one should be confirmed before the record is catalogued. Second, 'the Imam Zayd, the master of the inheritance shares' is Zayd ibn Thabit, the Companion regarded as the authority on inheritance; 'al-farḍī' is an epithet, not part of his name, and has been rendered as one.

translator_notes: Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.
The date shown by the CMS is a bulk-upload timestamp shared by every item in this range, not the date the Sheikh gave the answer. The real date of composition is unknown. See date_is_cms_bulk_upload.

EXCERPT ONLY. The published text breaks off mid-explanation and the full transcript is offered as a .docx download ('taḥmīl al-māddah'). The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends. The download-link label has been removed from body_ar as a navigation element and recorded in source_download_link.
The title and byline agree on the lesson number in this record. Compare ids 623 and 625, where they do not.

'Begin afresh with supplication' renders yastaʾnif fī al-duʿāʾ. The Sheikh's point is about the structure of an opening formula — praise, then prayer upon the Prophet, then supplication as the third element — not about repeating a supplication.
'His struggle' renders jihādihi. It is listed among the Prophet's undertakings alongside the pilgrimage and travel and is left in that neutral frame, as the Arabic leaves it.

title_ar: فتاوي في التركة
title_en: Fatwas on the estate
body_ar:
حكم أخذ الأجرة على قسم التركة ما الحكم الشرعي في مسألة شائعة في بلادنا وهي أن فقهاء بلدنا لا يقسمون التركة إلا بعد أن يأخذوا نصيبهم من المال قبل أن يقسم، فمثلا يأخذون من الإبل بعيرا ومن البقر جذعة ويقولون بأن هذا حق شرعي لهم علما بأن الورثة قد يكون من بينهم أيتام صغار فهل لهم حق في المال أم لا؟

أن الله سبحانه وتعالى حرم مال المسلم كتحريمه لنفسه، فقد صح عن النبي (ص) أنه قال: «فإن دماءكم وأموالكم وأعراضكم عليكم حرام كحرمة يومكم هذا في بلدكم هذا في شهركم هذا» وقال: «حرمة مال المسلم كحرمة دمه» فلذلك لا يحل أخذ مال امرئ مسلم إلا عن طيبة نفس منه، وهذا من المعلوم من الدين بالضرورة، فلا يحل لأولئك القوم أن يأخذوا من مال اليتامى ولا من مال الذين يقسمون لهم التركات شيئا إلا برضاهم..
body_en:
The ruling on taking a fee for dividing an estate. What is the ruling of the Sharia on a matter that is widespread in our country, namely that the jurists of our country will not divide an estate until they have taken their share of the property before it is divided — so, for example, they take a camel from the camels and a young cow from the cattle, and they say that this is a right the Sharia gives them — bearing in mind that among the heirs there may be young orphans? Have they a right in the property or not?

God, glorified and exalted, has made the property of a Muslim inviolable just as He has made his person inviolable. It is soundly established from the Prophet, upon whom be peace, that he said: "Your blood and your property and your honour are inviolable to one another, like the inviolability of this day of yours, in this land of yours, in this month of yours." And he said: "The inviolability of a Muslim's property is like the inviolability of his blood." For that reason it is not lawful to take the property of a Muslim man except with his willing consent, and this is among the things necessarily known to be part of the religion. So it is not lawful for those people to take anything from the property of the orphans, nor from the property of those for whom they divide estates, except with their consent..

flags.context: the opening of the answer
options: has made the property of a Muslim inviolable just as He has made his person inviolable
has forbidden [taking] the property of a Muslim as He has forbidden [taking] his life
has made a Muslim's wealth sacrosanct as He has made his self sacrosanct
flags.note: Ḥarrama here is used of an inviolability attaching to a thing, the sense carried through the passage by ḥurmah in the hadith, rather than of a prohibition attaching to an act. Option 1 converts it into the five-rulings sense of ḥarām, which would make the sentence say something narrower than the Arabic. Nafs is the person or life, not 'soul' in this idiom.

flags.context: فمثلا يأخذون من الإبل بعيرا ومن البقر جذعة
options: a young cow
a jadhaʿah [a beast in its second or third year]
a yearling
flags.note: Jadhaʿah is an age-grade term from the law of zakat and sacrifice, and its exact age differs by animal and by school — for cattle it is generally in the third year, for sheep in the second. Since the questioner is describing what the local jurists take as their fee, the precise grade matters to the sum involved. Option 1 keeps the Arabic and gives a range rather than asserting one age.

translator_notes: Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.

In the source, the answer begins with the elliptical particle 'anna ('[the answer is] that ...'), the Joomla fatwa template's standing form. The English drops the particle and begins the sentence directly; no content is added or removed by this.
The date shown by the CMS is a bulk-upload timestamp shared by every item in this range, not the date the Sheikh gave the answer. The real date of composition is unknown. See date_is_cms_bulk_upload.

EXCERPT ONLY. The published text breaks off with a double dot and the full material is offered as a .docx download ('taḥmīl al-māddah'). The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends. The download-link label has been removed from body_ar as a navigation element and recorded in source_download_link.

The Sheikh does give a ruling within the published excerpt — that the practice is not lawful without the heirs' consent — so this record is not marked critical_for_display. But the excerpt stops before he addresses the second limb of the question, whether a fee for the work of dividing may lawfully be charged at all, which is a distinct question from taking it unilaterally beforehand. A reviewer should not treat the excerpt as his complete position on remuneration for this service.

'Among the things necessarily known to be part of the religion' renders min al-maʿlūm min al-dīn bi-l-ḍarūrah, a technical expression for a matter so well established that ignorance of it is not excused. Ḍarūrah here does not carry the glossary's sense of 'necessity' as a legal threshold.
The first hadith is from the Farewell Sermon; the Sheikh does not name a collection for either report, and none has been supplied.

title_ar: شرح نخبة الفكر في مصطلح أهل الأثر الشريط الأول
title_en: Commentary on Nukhbat al-Fikr on the terminology of the people of hadith — tape one
body_ar:
الشريط الأول

بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

الحمد لله رب العالمين وأصلي وأسلم على من بعث رحمة للعالمين وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين السلام عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته.

أما بعد فإن طلب العلم من أهم ما يتقرب به إلى الله سبحانه وتعالى، فهو جهاد في سبيل الله وقد أخرج مالك في الموطإ عن أبي بكر بن عبد الرحمن من خرج إلى المسجد لا يخرجه إلا علم يعلمه أو يتعلمه كان كالمجاهد في سبيل الله رجع غانما، وصح عن النبي الحض على تعلم سنته، وقد أمر الله سبحانه وتعالى بتعليمها للناس فقال تعالى في خطابه لأمهات المؤمنين: {واذكرن ما يتلى في بيوتكن من آيات الله والحكمة}..
body_en:
Tape one.

In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate.

Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. I pray for blessing and peace upon him who was sent as a mercy to the worlds, and upon his family and his Companions and all who are guided by his guidance and follow his sunnah until the Day of Judgement. Peace be upon you, and the mercy of God and His blessings.

To proceed: the seeking of knowledge is among the most important means by which one draws near to God, glorified and exalted; it is a struggle in the path of God. Malik recorded in the Muwaṭṭaʾ, from Abu Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman: whoever goes out to the mosque, nothing taking him out but knowledge that he teaches or learns, is like one who struggles in the path of God and has returned with spoils. It is soundly established from the Prophet that he urged the learning of his sunnah, and God, glorified and exalted, has commanded that it be taught to the people, for God Most High said, addressing the Mothers of the Believers: {And remember what is recited in your houses of the signs of God and of the wisdom} (Sūrat al-Aḥzāb 33:34)..

record the spelling as served and flag it
correct silently

The report from the Muwaṭṭaʾ is given without the quotation marks the source uses for other reports, and it is a statement of Abu Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman, a Successor, rather than a saying traced to the Prophet. title_ar: شرح نخبة الفكر في مصطلح أهل الأثر الشريط التاسع -الخاتمة
title_en: Commentary on Nukhbat al-Fikr on the terminology of the people of hadith — tape nine, the conclusion
body_ar: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين، اللهم صل وسلم وبارك على سيدنا محمد عبدك ونبيك ورسولك النبي الأمي وعلى آله وصحبه وسلم تسليما، قال المؤلف رحمه الله: «خاتمة» قد انتهى المؤلف رحمه الله من مصطلح الحديث بالمعنى الأخص، وبدأ في ذكر بعض علوم الحديث المستقلة وهي علوم أخرى يستحق كل واحد منها أن يدرس في دورة مستقلة، وقد ألفت فيها كتب كاملة، وهذه العلوم الأخرى منها علم الرجال والجرح والتعديل، ومنها علم التخريج، ومنها علم العلل، ومنها علم دراسة الأسانيد، وغير ذلك من العلوم المستقلة..
body_en:
In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. O God, bless and grant peace and blessing to our master Muhammad, Your servant and Your prophet and Your messenger, the unlettered Prophet, and to his family and his Companions, and grant them abundant peace.

The author, may God have mercy on him, said: "Conclusion." The author, may God have mercy on him, has finished with the terminology of hadith in its narrowest sense, and has begun to mention some of the independent hadith sciences. These are further sciences, each one of which deserves to be studied in a course of its own, and complete books have been written on them. Among these further sciences are the science of the narrators and their appraisal (al-jarḥ wa-l-taʿdīl); the science of tracing a report to its sources (takhrīj); the science of the hidden defects of reports (ʿilal); the science of the study of chains of transmission; and others besides among the independent sciences..

flags.context: the list of independent hadith sciences
options: the science of the hidden defects of reports (ʿilal)
the science of the defects of hadith
the science of the causes
flags.note: The glossary fixes ʿillah as 'operative cause', which is its sense in legal theory and expressly not 'reason' or 'wisdom'. In the hadith sciences ʿilal is a different word with a different sense entirely: a subtle, hidden flaw in a chain or text that is not apparent on the surface. Option 2 would import the legal-theory sense and make nonsense of the list. The glossary should be extended with this second sense, as it will recur throughout the hadith material in this corpus.

title_ar: شرح نخبة الفكر في مصطلح أهل الأثر الشريط الثامن
title_en: Commentary on Nukhbat al-Fikr on the terminology of the people of hadith — tape eight
body_ar: "وعنعنة المعاصر محمولة على السماع إلا من مدلس\" إذا كان التلميذ لقي شيخه فحدث عنه بعن فهذا يحمل على السماع في حق غير المدلس أما المدلس فإذا قال عن فلا تحمل على السماع لأن هذا من صيغ التدليس وقد سبق التنبيه على ذلك عند ذكر التدليس، \"وعنعنة المعاصر محمولة على السماع إلا من مدلس، وقيل يشترط ثبوت لقائهما\" قيل لا يكفي مجرد المعاصرة بل لا بد من ثبوت اللقي، فالقول الأول هو قول مسلم رحمه الله فكان يرى أن المعاصرة ولو لم يثبت اللقي كافية، فهي إمكان اللقي، مسلم يشترط إمكان اللقي فقط، وأما البخاري فإنه يشترط ثبوت اللقي، ولا يكتفي بمجرد إمكانه، ولذلك قال: \"وقيل يشترط ثبوت لقائهما ولو مرة وهو المختار\" هذا مذهب البخاري واختياره، وأطلقوا المشافهة في الإجازة المتلفظ بها، الإجازة أنواع كثيرة، منها الإجازة العامة، ومنها الإجازة الخاصة، ومنها الإجازة باللفظ ومنها الإجازة بالكتابة ومنها الإجازة المقترنة بالمناولة، ومنها الإجازة بالإذن بالتحديث، ومنها الإجازة بالمشافهة..
body_en:
"And the ʿanʿanah of a contemporary is carried to hearing, except from one who practises concealment (mudallis)." If the student met his teacher and then narrated from him using ʿan ("from"), this is carried to hearing in the case of one who is not a mudallis. As for the mudallis, if he says ʿan, it is not carried to hearing, because this is among the forms of concealment (tadlīs), and attention has already been drawn to that when concealment was mentioned. "And the ʿanʿanah of a contemporary is carried to hearing, except from a mudallis; and it is said that the establishment of their having met is a condition." It is said that mere contemporaneity does not suffice; rather, the meeting must be established. The first view is the view of Muslim, may God have mercy on him: he held that contemporaneity, even where the meeting is not established, is sufficient — that is, the possibility of a meeting. Muslim stipulates only the possibility of a meeting. As for al-Bukhari, he stipulates the establishment of the meeting, and does not content himself with the mere possibility of it. That is why he said: "And it is said that the establishment of their having met, even once, is a condition, and this is the preferred view." This is al-Bukhari's position and his choice.

And they applied "oral communication" without qualification to the licence uttered aloud. The licence (ijāzah) is of many kinds: the general licence; the specific licence; the licence by utterance; the licence in writing; the licence combined with the handing over [of the book]; the licence by permission to narrate; and the licence by oral communication..

'ʿAnʿanah' is a narrator's use of the bare particle ʿan ('from so-and-so') rather than an explicit statement of hearing. It is kept in the Arabic because the whole passage is about that specific form of words; no English equivalent carries it.

'Concealment (tadlīs)' is a narrator's practice of making a chain appear stronger than it is, typically by omitting a weak intermediary; a mudallis is one known for it. 'Concealment' has been preferred to 'deception', which overstates the moral charge the term carries in this literature.

The disagreement between Muslim and al-Bukhari on whether contemporaneity suffices or an actual meeting must be shown is the substance of the passage; both positions are attributed expressly and neither has been collapsed into the other.

'Licence (ijāzah)' is a teacher's authorisation to transmit a text, and 'the handing over' is munāwalah, the physical delivery of the book that may accompany it. The final list breaks off after the seventh kind.
The source runs the passage on the licence directly on from the preceding sentence with a comma. A paragraph break has been inserted in body_en only, where the subject changes; body_ar is as served.

title_ar: شرح نخبة الفكر في مصطلح أهل الأثر الشريط الثانى- تابع
title_en: Commentary on Nukhbat al-Fikr on the terminology of the people of hadith — tape two, continued
body_ar: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد الله رب العالمين وأصلي وأسلم على نبينا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين أما بعد فقد كان الحديث في الحلقة الماضية توقف عند هم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بالأمر، وهم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بالأمر ينقسم إلى قسمين، إلى هم عقبه الترك، أي إلى أن يهم بأمر يقدر عليه فيتركه، أي أن يكون أراد أن يفعل فعلا ثم قوي لديه تركه فتركه كهمه بتحريق بيوت المتخلفين عن الصلاة، وإلى هم حال دونه مانع كصيام اليوم التاسع من شهر المحرم، فإنه قال: [لئن بقيت إلى قابل لأصومن التاسع]، فتوفاه الله ونقله إلى الرفيق الأعلى قبل أن ينفذ عزمه، فالهم إذن إذا كان تركه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من غير مانع كهمه بتحريق بيوت المخالفين عن الصلاة فهذا النوع من الهم لا يقتدى به لأنه لم يفعله..
body_en:
In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. I pray for blessing and peace upon our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family and his Companions and all who are guided by his guidance and follow his sunnah until the Day of Judgement.

To proceed: the discussion in the last session stopped at the Prophet's resolving upon a matter, upon whom be God's blessing and peace. The Prophet's resolving upon a matter, upon whom be God's blessing and peace, divides into two kinds. There is a resolve followed by abandonment — that is, that he resolves upon a matter he is able to do and then leaves it; that is, that he intended to do an act and then leaving it prevailed with him, so he left it, as with his resolving to burn the houses of those who stayed away from the prayer. And there is a resolve which an impediment prevented, as with fasting the ninth day of the month of Muharram, for he said: "If I remain until next year, I shall certainly fast the ninth." Then God took him and removed him to the Highest Companion before he could carry out his resolve. So the resolve, then: where the Prophet, upon whom be God's blessing and peace, left it with no impediment — as with his resolving to burn the houses of those who differed concerning the prayer — this kind of resolve is not to be taken as a precedent to follow, because he did not do it..

flags.context: the second mention of the same example; the first mention reads المتخلفين عن الصلاة
options: those who differed concerning the prayer
those who stayed away from the prayer [reading al-mutakhallifīn, as in the first mention]
those who opposed [the Prophet] over the prayer
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT. The Sheikh gives the same example twice in three lines. The first time the word is al-mutakhallifīn, 'those who stay away'; the second time it is al-mukhālifīn, 'those who differ or oppose'. The two are close in writing and the second is almost certainly a transcription slip for the first, since the hadith concerns non-attendance, and since al-mukhālifīn does not take the preposition ʿan. The style guide forbids silently repairing a source defect, so body_en renders each occurrence as printed and the discrepancy is recorded here. A reviewer working from the audio can settle it in a moment.

title_ar: شرح نخبة الفكر في مصطلح أهل الأثر الشريط الثانى
title_en: Commentary on Nukhbat al-Fikr on the terminology of the people of hadith — tape two
body_ar:
الشريط الثانى

بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين وصلى الله وسلم على نبينا محمد وعلى ءاله وأصحابه ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين أما بعد فسنبدأ إن شاء الله تعالى بهذه المصطلحات الأربعة السنة الحديث الخبر الأثر هذه المصطلحات متقاربة لدى أهل الحديث، فيحتاج الطالب إلى التمييز بينها ومعرفة مقتضياتها ودلالاتها، أولا المصطلح الأول السنة السنة في اللغة الطريقة والصميم من كل شيء، فتطلق على الطريقة سواء كانت خيرا أم شرا فمن إطلاقها على الخير قوله تعالى: {سنة من قد أرسلنا قبلك من رسلنا} أي طريقة من قد أرسلنا قبلك من رسلنا، ولا تكون طريقة الرسل إلا خيرا، ومن إطلاقها على الشر قوله تعالى: {قد خلت من قبلكم سنن فسيروا في الأرض فانظروا كيف كان عاقبة المكذبين} فسنن المكذبين لا تكون إلا شرا، فعلم بهذا أن السنة في اللغة تطلق على الطريقة سواء كانت للخير أو للشر..
body_en:
Tape two.

In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. May God bless our Prophet Muhammad and grant him peace, and his family and his Companions and all who are guided by his guidance and follow his sunnah until the Day of Judgement.

To proceed: we shall begin, God Most High willing, with these four terms — sunnah, ḥadīth, khabar, athar. These terms lie close together in the usage of the people of hadith, and the student needs to distinguish between them and to know what each entails and what each signifies.

First, the first term: sunnah. Sunnah in the language is the way, and the core of a thing. It is applied to a way whether that way is good or evil. An instance of its application to the good is the saying of God Most High: {the way of those of Our messengers whom We sent before you} (Sūrat al-Isrāʾ 17:77) — that is, the way of those of Our messengers whom We sent before you; and the way of the messengers can only be good. An instance of its application to evil is the saying of God Most High: {ways have passed away before you, so travel in the land and see what was the end of those who denied} (Sūrat Āl ʿImrān 3:137) — for the ways of those who denied can only be evil. It is known by this that sunnah in the language is applied to a way, whether it be to good or to evil..

flags.arabic: السنة في اللغة الطريقة والصميم من كل شيء
flags.context: the lexical definition of sunnah
options: the way, and the core of a thing
the way, and the essence of anything
the way, and the best part of anything
flags.note: Al-ṣamīm is the innermost or hardest part of a thing, hence its core. The lexicographers give it for sunnah alongside 'way', and the Sheikh gives it without elaborating. He then illustrates only the first sense with the two verses and does not return to the second within the published excerpt, so the intended force of al-ṣamīm here cannot be settled from this text.

title_ar: شرح نخبة الفكر في مصطلح أهل الأثر -الشريط الرابع
title_en: Commentary on Nukhbat al-Fikr on the terminology of the people of hadith — tape four
body_ar:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين وصلى الله وسلم على سيدنا محمد وعلى آله و أصحابه ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين السلام عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته.

أما بعد فيقول الحافظ رحمه الله: " الخبر إما أن يكون له طرق بلا عدد معين أو مع حصر بما فوق الاثنين أو بهما أو بواحد" بدأ رحمه الله هنا تقسيم الحديث باعتبار عدد الناقلين، وقد سبق أن هذا التقسيم ينقسم به الحديث تقسيمين التقسيم الأول باعتبار عدد الناقلين في كل طبقة، والتقسيم الثاني باعتبار عدد الطبقات، فبدأ بتقسيم الحديث باعتبار عدد الناقلين في كل طبقة فقال إما أن يكون له طرق والمقصود بالطرق الأسانيد وهي جمع طريق والطريق في الأصل السبيل المسلوك والمقصود به في الاصطلاح الناقلون للحديث الذين رووه حتى وصلوه إلى منتهاه، ومنتهاه إن كان مرفوعا هو النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وإن كان موقوفا هو الصحابي وإن كان مقطوعا هو التابعي ومن دونه..
body_en:
In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. May God bless our master Muhammad and grant him peace, and his family and his Companions and all who are guided by his guidance and follow his sunnah until the Day of Judgement. Peace be upon you, and the mercy of God and His blessings.

To proceed: al-Hafiz, may God have mercy on him, says: "The report either has routes without a determinate number, or with a limit above two, or with those two, or with one." Here he began, may God have mercy on him, the division of the hadith by the number of transmitters. It has already been said that the hadith is divided by this into two divisions: the first by the number of transmitters in each layer, and the second by the number of layers. So he began with the division of the hadith by the number of transmitters in each layer, and said "either it has routes". What is meant by routes is the chains of transmission; it is the plural of ṭarīq, and ṭarīq is originally the road that is travelled, and what is meant by it as a technical term is the transmitters of the hadith who narrated it until they brought it to its end-point. Its end-point, if the report is traced to the Prophet (marfūʿ), is the Prophet, upon whom be God's blessing and peace; if it stops at a Companion (mawqūf), it is the Companion; and if it stops at a Successor (maqṭūʿ), it is the Successor and those below him..

flags.context: the third of the three end-points of a chain of transmission
options: a report stopping at a Successor (maqṭūʿ)
a severed report
a report of a Successor
flags.note: Not in the project glossary, which fixes marfūʿ and mawqūf but not maqṭūʿ. The rendering has been built to match those two. It is important that maqṭūʿ ('stopping at a Successor', a classification by end-point) not be confused with munqaṭiʿ ('interrupted', a defect in the chain), which option 1 invites. The glossary should be extended with maqṭūʿ and munqaṭiʿ together.

title_ar: شرح نخبة الفكر في مصطلح أهل الأثر الشريط السابع
title_en: Commentary on Nukhbat al-Fikr on the terminology of the people of hadith — tape seven
body_ar:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين اللهم افتح لنا بحكمتك وانشر علينا من رحمتك وأنزل علينا من بركاتك.

أما بعد فيقول الحافظ رحمه الله: " فإن قل عدده فإما أن ينتهي إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أو إلى إمام ذي صفة علية كشعبة فالأول العلو المطلق والثاني النسبي" هذا التقسيم الذي بدأه الحافظ هنا يسمى تقسيم الحديث باعتبار عدد الناقلين وباعتبار عدد الطبقات، وهو قسم من أقسام الحديث باعتبار عدد الناقلين، باعتبار عدد الناقلين أي عدد الطبقات، قال: فإن قل عدده أي إن قل عدد الإسناد وذلك مثل ثلاثيات البخاري التي يرويها البخاري عن المكي بن إبراهيم عن يزيد بن أبي عبيد عن سلمة بن الأكوع، وأولها في صحيح البخاري قول البخاري رحمه الله حدثنا المكي بن إبراهيم قال حدثنا يزيد بن أبي عبيد عن سلمة بن الأكوع قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: من يقل علي ما لم أقل فليتبوأ مقعده من النار..
body_en:
In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. O God, open for us by Your wisdom, and spread over us of Your mercy, and send down upon us of Your blessings.

To proceed: al-Hafiz, may God have mercy on him, says: "And if its number is few, then it either ends at the Prophet, upon whom be God's blessing and peace, or at an imam possessed of an exalted quality, such as Shuʿbah; the first is absolute elevation and the second relative." This division, which al-Hafiz begins here, is called the division of the hadith by the number of transmitters and by the number of layers; it is one of the divisions of the hadith by the number of transmitters — by the number of transmitters, that is, the number of layers. He said: "and if its number is few", that is, if the number of the chain is few. That is like the three-link chains of al-Bukhari, which al-Bukhari narrates from al-Makki ibn Ibrahim, from Yazid ibn Abi ʿUbayd, from Salamah ibn al-Akwaʿ. The first of them in the Ṣaḥīḥ of al-Bukhari is al-Bukhari's words, may God have mercy on him: "al-Makki ibn Ibrahim narrated to us; he said, Yazid ibn Abi ʿUbayd narrated to us, from Salamah ibn al-Akwaʿ, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, upon whom be God's blessing and peace, say: Whoever says of me what I did not say, let him take his seat in the Fire."..

flags.context: the two kinds of elevation of a chain of transmission
options: absolute elevation and relative elevation
absolute and relative shortness of the chain
absolute and relative proximity
flags.note: ʿUluww is the technical quality of a chain that reaches its end-point through fewer intermediaries than usual, and is prized for that reason. 'Elevation' is the conventional English rendering and has been used. Note that muṭlaq here means 'absolute' as against 'relative', and is not the glossary's uṣūl sense of muṭlaq, 'unqualified' as against muqayyad. That homonym recurs in this corpus and should be added to the glossary's note on muṭlaq.

The download-link label has been removed from body_ar as a navigation element and recorded in source_download_link.
'The three-link chains of al-Bukhari' renders thulāthiyyāt al-Bukhārī — the reports in his Ṣaḥīḥ that reach the Prophet through only three narrators, his shortest chains.

'An imam possessed of an exalted quality' renders imām dhī ṣifah ʿaliyyah: a figure of such standing that reaching him by a short chain is itself a distinction, which is what makes the elevation relative rather than absolute. Shuʿbah is Shuʿbah ibn al-Hajjaj.

title_ar: شرح نخبة الفكر في مصطلح أهل الأثر الشريط السادس تابع
title_en: Commentary on Nukhbat al-Fikr on the terminology of the people of hadith — tape six, continued
body_ar: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين، وصلى الله وسلم على نبينا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه أجمعين، أما بعد فيقول الحافظ رحمه الله: "ثم الطعن إما أن يكون لكذب الراوي أو تهمته بذلك أو فحش غلطه أو غفلته أو فسقه أو وهمه أو مخالفته أو جهالته أو بدعته أو سوء حفظه" فذكر هنا هذه الأقسام من أقسام الطعن على حسب ترتيبه هو، وهو يختلف عن الترتيب الذي عليه جمهور أهل المصطلح، وهو الترتيب الذي سقناه سابقا، فتكون الأقسام به أقل من هذا التقسيم، لأن هذا التقسيم بعضه يشترك في الاسم، فذكره مع كونه مشتركا في الاسم كأقسام مما يزيد العدد من غير كبير فائدة، فلذلك لم ننتهج هذا لكن لا بأس بشرحه، فهنا قال إن الطعن، له أسباب السبب الأول أن يكون لكذب الراوي أي أن يكون الراوي معروفا بالكذب وذلك بإقراره هو..
body_en:
In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. May God bless our Prophet Muhammad and grant him peace, and his family and all his Companions.

To proceed: al-Hafiz, may God have mercy on him, says: "Then the impugning of a narrator is either for the narrator's lying, or for his being suspected of it, or for the grossness of his error, or for his heedlessness, or for his open transgression, or for his misapprehension, or for his contradicting [others], or for his being unknown, or for his innovation, or for his poor retention." He mentioned here these divisions among the divisions of impugning, according to his own arrangement, which differs from the arrangement followed by the majority of the people of the terminology — the arrangement which we set out earlier. The divisions on that arrangement are fewer than on this division, because some parts of this division share a single name; so his mentioning them, while they share a name, as separate divisions, is of the sort that increases the number without great benefit. For that reason we did not follow this, though there is no harm in explaining it. Here, then, he said that impugning has causes. The first cause is the narrator's lying, that is, that the narrator is known for lying, and that by his own admission..

flags.context: the heading of the whole passage
options: the impugning of a narrator
criticism of a narrator
disparagement
flags.note: Ṭaʿn is the technical act of stating a ground on which a narrator's reports are not to be accepted; it is the negative half of al-jarḥ wa-l-taʿdīl, which the glossary fixes as 'the appraisal of narrators'. 'Criticism' is too weak and too general, and 'disparagement' imports a moral charge that some of the ten grounds listed — heedlessness, poor retention, being unknown — do not carry at all. The word should be added to the glossary.

flags.context: the sixth and tenth of the ten grounds of impugning
options: his misapprehension ... his poor retention
his error ... his poor memory
his delusion ... his weak memorisation
flags.note: Two of the ten grounds are easily collapsed into each other or into the third ground, 'the grossness of his error' (fuḥsh ghalaṭihi), in English. Wahm is a narrator's forming a mistaken impression of what he heard; sūʾ al-ḥifẓ is unreliability in retaining it; ghalaṭ is plain error. The Sheikh's whole complaint against Ibn Hajar's arrangement is precisely that some of these grounds share a name, so the English must keep the ten distinguishable or the criticism becomes unintelligible.

title_ar: أجوبة في شرح الحديث 2
title_en: Answers on the explanation of hadith 2
body_ar:
شرح الحديث: «كتب على ابن آدم حظه من الزنا" نرجو منكم توضيحا لمعنى الحديث التالي: «كتب على ابن آدم حظه من الزنا وهو مدرك ذلك لا محالة فالعين تزني وزناها النظر والأذن تزني وزناها السمع والفرج يصدق ذلك أو يكذبه»؟

أن رسول الله (ص) بين أن الزنا من الأمور المنتشرة فهو مثل الشرك، فالشرك كثير الانتشار جدا وهو أخفى في النفوس من دبيب النمل، كما بين النبي (ص)، ولهذا قال الله تعالى: {وما يؤمن أكثرهم بالله إلا وهم مشركون} ولهذا كان النبي (ص) يقول في دعائه: «اللهم إني أعوذ بك أن أشرك بك وأنا أعلم وأستغفرك لما لا أعلم»، مثل ذلك الزنا فهو أيضا أنواع منوعة، وهو منتشر خفي، فكثير من الناس لا يقترفون الجريمة نفسها جريمة الزنا ولكنهم يقتربون منها والله حرم الاقتراب من الزنا ولم يذكر الزنا بنفسه في قوله: {ولا تقربوا الزنا} فلم يقل ولا تزنوا، وإنما قال ولا تقربوا الزنا، فهذا يقتضي تحريم النظر وتحريم الكلام في الريبة وتحريم الاقتراب والدخول على النساء والخلوة والخلطة وغير ذلك فكل ذلك داخل فيما حرمه الله سبحانه وتعالى في قوله ولا تقربوا...
body_en:
Explanation of the hadith: "The son of Adam's portion of fornication is written for him." We ask you for a clarification of the meaning of the following hadith: "The son of Adam's portion of fornication is written for him, and he will attain that inevitably. The eye fornicates, and its fornication is the look; the ear fornicates, and its fornication is listening; and the private part confirms that or gives it the lie"?

The Messenger of God, upon whom be peace, made clear that fornication is among the widespread matters: it is like associating partners with God (shirk). Shirk is very widely spread indeed, and it is more hidden in men's souls than the creeping of ants, as the Prophet, upon whom be peace, made clear. That is why God Most High said: {And most of them do not believe in God without associating partners with Him} (Sūrat Yūsuf 12:106). And that is why the Prophet, upon whom be peace, used to say in his supplication: "O God, I seek refuge in You from associating anything with You knowingly, and I seek Your forgiveness for what I do not know." Fornication is like that: it too is of various kinds, and it is widespread and hidden. Many people do not commit the crime itself, the crime of fornication, but they approach it — and God has forbidden the approaching of fornication, and did not mention fornication itself, in His words: {And do not approach fornication} (Sūrat al-Isrāʾ 17:32). He did not say "do not fornicate"; rather He said "do not approach fornication". This entails the prohibition of the look, the prohibition of speech in which there is cause for suspicion, and the prohibition of drawing near, of entering upon women, of being alone with them, of mingling with them, and of other things besides — all of that falls within what God, glorified and exalted, forbade in His words "and do not approach"...

flags.arabic: «كتب على ابن آدم حظه من الزنا"
flags.context: the heading of the question: the quotation opens with an angle quotation mark and closes with a straight one
options: preserve the mismatched marks in body_ar and normalise in body_en
normalise in both
preserve in both
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT, minor. The heading opens the hadith with « and closes it with a straight double quote, whereas the full quotation immediately below uses « » correctly. Preserved in body_ar; body_en uses consistent English quotation marks. Recorded because inconsistent quotation marking recurs across this corpus and a global clean-up will need to know it is present in headings as well as bodies.

flags.arabic: تحريم الاقتراب والدخول على النساء والخلوة والخلطة
flags.context: the list of what the prohibition of 'approaching' is said to entail
options: the prohibition of drawing near, of entering upon women, of being alone with them, of mingling with them
the prohibition of approach, of visiting women, of seclusion and of free association
the prohibition of approaching and entering upon women, and of seclusion and mixing
flags.note: Khalwah is a man and a woman who may marry each other being alone together, a defined category in fiqh; khulṭah is unstructured mixing. Neither is 'seclusion' in its ordinary English sense, and option 1's 'seclusion' would be read by an English reader as the confinement of women, which is not what the word says. The pronoun 'with them' has been supplied in the English for both terms, since the Arabic nouns are absolute and English requires an object; the supply is marked here rather than made silently.

title_ar: أجوبة في تفسير بعض الآيات
title_en: Answers on the exegesis of certain verses
body_en:
Exegesis of: {O you who believe, be conscious of God and speak a word that is right}.

This question is about the exegesis of God Most High's words: {O you who believe, be conscious of God and speak a word that is right; He will set right your deeds for you and forgive you your sins. And whoever obeys God and His Messenger has attained a mighty attainment} (Sūrat al-Aḥzāb 33:70–71).

God, glorified and exalted, has commanded us to be conscious of Him, and to speak a word that is right — which is the speaking of the truth — and not to speak what is false; and He made clear the good that follows upon that, namely that if we do so He sets our affairs right for us and grants us Paradise. So He said: "He will set right your deeds for you and forgive you your sins." "And whoever obeys God and His Messenger" in what God has commanded and His Messenger has commanded, or what God has forbidden or His Messenger has forbidden, "has attained a mighty attainment", by his obedience to God and His Messenger.

------------------------------------

Exegesis of: {and you will not be asked about the companions of the Blaze}.

[What do you say] about the exegesis of God Most High's words: {and you will not be asked about the companions of the Blaze}?

This verse has two readings. One is {wa-lā tusʾalu ʿan aṣḥāb al-jaḥīm} and the other is {wa-lā tasʾal ʿan aṣḥāb al-jaḥīm} (Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:119). As for the reading wa-lā tasʾal ʿan aṣḥāb al-jaḥīm — that is, let their affair not trouble you, for they are in the utmost of the abiding, perpetual punishment. And as for wa-lā tusʾalu ʿan aṣḥāb al-jaḥīm — that is, that you are not held to account for their disobedience, for every person is answerable for his own sin and no one else is asked about it..

flags.arabic: ما عن تفسير قول الله تعالى
flags.context: the opening of the second question
options: [What do you say] about the exegesis of ...
What is the exegesis of ...
About the exegesis of ...
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT. The Arabic as printed, mā ʿan tafsīr, is not grammatical; a word has dropped out, most probably qawlukum ('what do you say about') or a similar formula, which the first question's phrasing supports. The English marks the supply in square brackets rather than making it silently. body_ar preserves the defect.

flags.context: the two canonical readings of the verse
options: give both readings transliterated, with a distinct English rendering for each
give both readings in Arabic only and one English rendering
give one reading in English and footnote the other
flags.note: The whole answer turns on a difference of vocalisation that cannot be shown in an English translation of the verse: tusʾalu is passive, 'you are not asked', while tasʾal is an imperative, 'do not ask'. The heading and the question quote the verse unvocalised, so the English heading has had to choose one; it uses the passive, which is the majority reading, and the answer then sets out both. A reviewer should decide whether the site's Qur'an display can carry vocalised Arabic for cases like this, which will recur throughout the qirāʾāt material.

flags.context: the gloss on the imperative reading
options: let their affair not trouble you
do not concern yourself with their affair
their affair is not your concern
flags.note: The Arabic is a jussive and the sense is that the Prophet is not to be grieved over their fate. Option 2 turns it into a statement rather than an instruction and would blur the very distinction between the two readings that the answer exists to draw.

title_ar: شرح الجزرية -الجزء الأول
title_en: Commentary on al-Jazariyyah — part one
body_ar: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين وأصلي وأسلم على من بعث رحمة للعالمين وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين، السلام عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته، أما بعد فإن الله تعالى أنزل القرآن على محمد (ص) بلسان عربي مبين، وقد جاء به جبريل عليه السلام إلى رسول الله (ص) منجما في ثلاث وعشرين سنة، ينزل بحسب الوقائع وبحسب ما يسأل عنه أهل الأرض وكان ذلك اتصالا بين أهل السماء وأهل الأرض، وارتباطا بين الخلق والخالق، جل وعلا ببيان ما يريده منهم وتشريع ما يرتضيه لهم، وقد ختم الله الرسائل إلى أهل الأرض برسالة محمد (ص)، وختم الكتب المنزلة إلى أهل الأرض بالقرآن، وجعله مصدقا لما بين يديه من الحق ومهيمنا على كل الكتب وناسخا لها..
body_en:
In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. I pray for blessing and peace upon him who was sent as a mercy to the worlds, and upon his family and his Companions and all who are guided by his guidance and follow his sunnah until the Day of Judgement. Peace be upon you, and the mercy of God and His blessings.

To proceed: God Most High sent down the Qur'an upon Muhammad, upon whom be peace, in a clear Arabic tongue. Gabriel, peace be upon him, brought it to the Messenger of God, upon whom be peace, in instalments over twenty-three years, coming down according to the events and according to what the people of the earth asked about. That was a communication between the people of heaven and the people of the earth, and a bond between the creation and the Creator, mighty and exalted, by the making clear of what He wants from them and the legislating of what He approves for them. God sealed the messages to the people of the earth with the message of Muhammad, upon whom be peace, and sealed the books sent down to the people of the earth with the Qur'an, and made it confirming the truth that was before it, and a guardian over all the books, and abrogating them..

flags.context: the description of the Qur'an's relation to the earlier scriptures
options: a guardian over all the books
a watcher over all the books
having authority over all the books
flags.note: Muhaymin is the word used of the Qur'an at Sūrat al-Māʾidah 5:48, and the Sheikh is echoing that verse without quoting it, so the English should echo a standard rendering of it. The exegetes gloss muhaymin variously as guardian, witness and judge over the earlier scriptures, and the Sheikh does not choose among them. Option 2 picks one of the glosses and states it as the meaning.

title_ar: شرح الجزرية -الجزء الثاني
title_en: Commentary on al-Jazariyyah — part two
body_ar: وبهذا تعلمون أن حفص الدوري مثلا توفي في القرن الثالث والخاقاني توفي في القرن الرابع، ومكي بن أبي طالب توفي في القرن الخامس، وأهل الأندلس عموما اشتهروا بإتقان هذا العلم ولذلك فإن مكيا كان مجددا فيه ثم جاء بعده أبو عمرو الداني وهو إمام علوم القرآن كلها بلا منازع، ثم بعده تلميذه أبو داود سليمان بن النجيح وهو كذلك خليفة الداني في هذا العلم، فأهل الأندلس اشتهروا بعلوم التجويد وبتفسير القرآن كذلك فمنهم ابن عطية وابن جزي والقرطبي وأبو بكر بن العربي وغيرهم من أئمة أهل التجويد كأبي حيان وابن الفرس المالكي مؤلف كتاب أحكام القرآن، فلهم مؤلفات كثيرة جدا في خدمة القرآن..
body_en: And by this you know that Hafs al-Duri, for example, died in the third century; that al-Khaqani died in the fourth century; and that Makki ibn Abi Talib died in the fifth century. The people of al-Andalus in general were renowned for their mastery of this science, and for that reason Makki was a renewer in it. Then after him came Abu ʿAmr al-Dani, who is the imam of all the Qur'anic sciences without dispute; then after him his student Abu Dawud Sulayman ibn al-Najih, who is likewise al-Dani's successor in this science. The people of al-Andalus were renowned for the sciences of recitation, and for the exegesis of the Qur'an as well: among them Ibn ʿAtiyyah, Ibn Juzayy, al-Qurtubi and Abu Bakr ibn al-ʿArabi, and others among the leading authorities of the people of tajwīd, such as Abu Hayyan and Ibn al-Faras al-Maliki, the author of the book Aḥkām al-Qurʾān. They have very many works indeed in the service of the Qur'an..

flags.context: the first name in the chronological list
options: Hafs al-Duri [Abu ʿUmar Hafs ibn ʿUmar al-Duri]
al-Duri
Hafs al-Duri
flags.note: Serious risk of confusion for an English reader. The Duri meant here is Abu ʿUmar Hafs ibn ʿUmar al-Duri, the transmitter of the readings of Abu ʿAmr and of al-Kisa'i, who did die in the third century. Printed as 'Hafs' alone, the name will be taken for Hafs ibn Sulayman, the transmitter of ʿAsim's reading after whom the standard printed muṣḥaf is named, who is a different man of a different century. Option 0 supplies the full name in brackets. This is an expansion the English reader requires and is recorded rather than made silently.

flags.context: al-Dani's student and successor
options: Abu Dawud Sulayman ibn al-Najih [as printed]
Abu Dawud Sulayman ibn Najah
Abu Dawud Sulayman ibn Abi al-Qasim Najah
flags.note: PROBABLE SOURCE DEFECT. The scholar described — Abu ʿAmr al-Dani's foremost student and his successor in the Qur'anic sciences in al-Andalus — is known as Sulayman ibn Najah, not ibn al-Najih. The printed form is most likely a transcription slip from the spoken lecture. Translated as printed under the rule against silently repairing the source; a reviewer should settle it against the audio before the name is indexed.

flags.context: the first words of the published text
options: translate as printed, with no editorial mark
mark the opening with an ellipsis
display with a banner noting the missing opening
flags.note: The record opens on a connective ('And by this you know'), so the lecture's opening is not published. Unlike ids 630 and 634 the first sentence is grammatically complete and intelligible on its own, so no ellipsis has been added and the record is not marked critical_for_display. Noted so that a reviewer laying out the series knows the opening is absent.

title_ar: شرح الجزرية -الشريط التاسع
title_en: Commentary on al-Jazariyyah — tape nine
body_ar:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين وأصلي وأسلم على من بعث رحمة للعالمين وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين يقول المؤلف رحمه الله تعالى: باب معرفة الوقوف عقد هذا الباب لبيان أمر مهم من أمور التجويد وهو حكم الوقف والابتداء، والوقف في اللغة مصدر وقف تستعمل لازمة وتستعمل متعدية، فيقال وقف فلان في الصلاة أي قام، ويقال وقف فلان راحلته أو ناقته إذا حبسها، ومنه قول عنترة

ولقد وقفت بها طويلا ناقتي** أشكو إلى سفع رواكد جثم

وقول امرئ القيس:

وقوفا بها صحبي علي مطيهم** يقولون لا تهلك أسى وتجمل

ونظيره قول طرفة:

وقوفا بها صحبي علي مطيهم** يقولون لا تهلك أسى وتجلد
body_en:
In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. I pray for blessing and peace upon him who was sent as a mercy to the worlds, and upon his family and his Companions and all who are guided by his guidance and follow his sunnah until the Day of Judgement.

The author says, may God Most High have mercy on him: "Chapter on the knowledge of the stopping-places." He set out this chapter to explain an important matter among the matters of recitation, namely the ruling on stopping (waqf) and on beginning (ibtidāʾ). Waqf in the language is the verbal noun of waqafa, which is used intransitively and is used transitively. One says "so-and-so waqafa in the prayer", meaning he stood; and one says "so-and-so waqafa his mount or his she-camel", meaning he brought it to a halt. From this is the saying of ʿAntarah:

*And long did I halt my she-camel there, making my complaint to blackened hearth-stones, motionless and crouching.*

And the saying of Imru' al-Qays:

*My companions halted their mounts over me there, saying: do not perish of grief; bear yourself well.*

And its counterpart, the saying of Tarafah:

*My companions halted their mounts over me there, saying: do not perish of grief; be steadfast.*

flags.context: the line attributed to ʿAntarah, cited to illustrate the transitive use of waqafa
options: translate as printed, with waqaftu ('I halted')
translate as printed and note that the received line reads ḥabastu
restore the received reading ḥabastu
flags.note: PROBABLE MISQUOTATION IN THE SOURCE, and a consequential one. The line as it is received in ʿAntarah's muʿallaqah reads wa-la-qad ḥabastu bihā ṭawīlan nāqatī — 'and long did I hold back my she-camel there'. The source has waqaftu in place of ḥabastu. That substitution matters because the line is being cited for the express purpose of proving that waqafa takes a direct object; if the verb in the line is in fact ḥabasa, the line does not prove the point. This may be the Sheikh quoting from memory, as the style guide warns is common in this tradition, or a transcription slip, or a deliberate paraphrase to make the point. It is translated as printed and must not be repaired; a reviewer with the audio should establish which it is, and the answer affects whether the argument stands as published.

flags.arabic: وقوفا بها صحبي علي مطيهم ** يقولون لا تهلك أسى وتجمل / ... وتجلد
flags.context: two lines given as counterparts, from Imru' al-Qays and from Tarafah
options: render the two closing words distinctly, as 'bear yourself well' and 'be steadfast'
render both as 'be patient'
keep tajammal and tajallad in transliteration
flags.note: The two lines are identical but for the final word, which is the reason the Sheikh pairs them, so the English must keep the two words distinct or the pairing becomes pointless repetition. Tajammul is composure and bearing oneself becomingly; tajallud is endurance and fortitude. The lines are correctly attributed in the source: both muʿallaqāt do carry them.

Per the style guide the three lines of verse are rendered as prose in italics, with the Arabic kept in the bilingual pane; no rhymed English has been attempted. The doubled asterisks in the source are hemistich separators.

'Blackened hearth-stones, motionless and crouching' renders sufʿ rawākid juthṭham — the fire-blackened stones of an abandoned camp, a standing image of the deserted encampment in this poetry. The image has been kept rather than explained away.

The grammatical point being made is that waqafa is both intransitive ('to stand') and transitive ('to halt something'), which is why the Arabic verb has been kept in the two illustrative sentences instead of being replaced by two different English verbs.

title_ar: شرح الجزرية -الشريط الثالث
title_en: Commentary on al-Jazariyyah — tape three
body_ar:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين وأصلي وأسلم على من بعث رحمة للعالمين وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين.

أما بعد فيقول المؤلف رحمه الله: باب مخارج الحروف الباب في اللغة فرجة في ساتر يتوصل بها من داخل إلى خارج وبالعكس حقيقةً في المباني كباب الدار وحكما في المعاني كباب مخارج الحروف، وهو في الاصطلاح اسم لطائفة من الفن تشترك في بعض الأحكام وتتميز عن غيرها، وهو يعقد لما يحتاج لبيانه من العلم، فهذا العلم الذي هو علم الأداء من مسائله التي تحتاج إلى عقد باب مخارج الحروف، والحروف قد سبق تعريفها وهي يبٍحث فيها من أربعة أوجه، الوجه الأول: المخرج (مخرج الحرف)، والوجه الثاني الصفة التي يتصف بها الحرف، والوجه الثالث الشكل أي الضبط الذي يكون عليه سكونا أو حركة، والوجه الرابع العوارض الصوتية عند التركيب كالإدغام والترقيق وغير ذلك من العوارض الصوتية، فمن أتقن هذه الأمور الأربعة كلٌّ على حدة استطاع أداء الحرف على وجهه الصحيح، ومن عرف بعضها دون بعض لا بد أن يدخل عليه الخلل والخطأ من جهة ما جهل منها..
body_en:
In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. I pray for blessing and peace upon him who was sent as a mercy to the worlds, and upon his family and his Companions and all who are guided by his guidance and follow his sunnah until the Day of Judgement.

To proceed: the author says, may God have mercy on him: "Chapter on the points of articulation of the letters." Bāb in the language is an opening in a barrier by which one passes from inside to outside and the reverse — literally so in buildings, as with the door of a house, and by attribution in matters of meaning, as with the "chapter" on the points of articulation of the letters. As a technical term it is a name for a group of topics within a discipline which share certain rulings and are distinguished from others; it is set out for whatever in the science needs explaining. This science, which is the science of performance (ʿilm al-adāʾ), has among its topics those that require a chapter on the points of articulation of the letters to be set out. The letters have already been defined. They are investigated from four aspects. The first aspect: the point of articulation (the makhraj of the letter). The second aspect: the quality by which the letter is characterised. The third aspect: the form, that is, the marking it bears, whether quiescence or a vowel. The fourth aspect: the phonetic accidents that arise on combination, such as assimilation (idghām) and thinning (tarqīq) and other phonetic accidents. Whoever masters these four matters, each one separately, is able to perform the letter in its correct form; and whoever knows some of them and not others will inevitably fall into flaw and error from the side of what he did not know of them..

flags.context: فهذا العلم الذي هو علم الأداء
options: the science of performance (ʿilm al-adāʾ)
the science of recitation
the science of delivery
flags.note: HOMONYM WITH A GLOSSARY ENTRY. The glossary fixes adāʾ as 'performance in its proper time', its sense in the law of worship, where it is opposed to qaḍāʾ, making up a missed act. That sense has nothing to do with this passage: ʿilm al-adāʾ is the science of how the Qur'an is correctly uttered, a synonym in this literature for tajwīd. Applying the glossary entry here would make the sentence unintelligible. The same trap as at id 629 with ʿilal and at id 636 with muṭlaq; the glossary needs a note on each of these three.

EXCERPT ONLY. The published text breaks off and the full material is offered as a .docx download ('taḥmīl al-māddah'). The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends. The download-link label has been removed from body_ar as a navigation element and recorded in source_download_link.
'Points of articulation' renders makhārij, the places in the mouth and throat at which each letter is produced.
'Quiescence or a vowel' renders sukūnan aw ḥarakatan — whether the letter carries no vowel or carries one.

'Phonetic accidents' renders al-ʿawāriḍ al-ṣawtiyyah, changes that come upon a letter only when it is combined with others; idghām is the assimilation of one letter into the next, tarqīq the thinning or lightening of a sound as against its being pronounced heavy.
The source prints يبٍحث with a stray kasratan over the bāʾ, a typographical artefact with no bearing on the sense. It is preserved in body_ar.

The definition of bāb ('chapter', literally 'door') as an opening in a barrier is a piece of lexical play the Sheikh is making deliberately, and has been kept rather than replaced by the bare word 'chapter'.

title_ar: شرح الجزرية -الشريط الثامن
title_en: Commentary on al-Jazariyyah — tape eight
body_ar:
الحمد لله رب العالمين وصلى الله وسلم على نبينا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين، السلام عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته.

أما بعد فإن من الحروف ما هو مختص ببعض الأحكام، فلا بد من العناية به للعناية بتلك الأحكام التي تختص به، وهذه الحروف هي الميم والنون واللام فهذه الحروف الثلاثة تخرج عن قواعد الحروف لبعض الاختصاصات التي تختص بها، فاحتيج لبيان أحكام تختص بها، وقد عقد المؤلف رحمه الله تعالى هذا الباب لبيان أحكام الميم ولبيان حكم النون المشددة فقال:

وأظهر الغنة من نون ومن** ميم إذا ما شددا....

هذه القاعدة تقتضي أن الميم والنون تزداد الغنة معهما في حال الادغام أي في حال التشديد، لأن كل واحد منهما في الأصل حرف أغن، فإذا تكرر ازداد نصيبه من الغنة، فلذلك لا بد من العناية بهما في حال التشديد ..
body_en:
Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. May God bless our Prophet Muhammad and grant him peace, and his family and his Companions and all who are guided by his guidance and follow his sunnah until the Day of Judgement. Peace be upon you, and the mercy of God and His blessings.

To proceed: among the letters are some that are singled out for certain rulings, and these must be attended to in order that those rulings peculiar to them may be attended to. These letters are the mīm, the nūn and the lām. These three letters depart from the rules of the letters, on account of certain particularities that belong to them, so there was a need to set out the rulings peculiar to them. The author, may God Most High have mercy on him, set out this chapter to explain the rulings of the mīm and to explain the ruling of the doubled nūn, and said:

*And make the nasalisation clear, from a nūn and from a mīm, when the two are doubled....*

This rule entails that with the mīm and the nūn the nasalisation is increased in the case of assimilation, that is, in the case of doubling — because each of the two is in origin a nasal letter, so that when it is repeated its share of nasalisation increases. For that reason the two must be attended to in the case of doubling ..

flags.arabic: وهذه الحروف هي الميم والنون واللام ... لبيان أحكام الميم ولبيان حكم النون المشددة
flags.context: the lām is named as one of the three letters with peculiar rulings but is not treated in the published text
options: translate as printed and note that the lām is not reached
treat the mention of the lām as an error
supply nothing and make no note
flags.note: The Sheikh names three letters — mīm, nūn and lām — and then says the author's chapter is set out for the rulings of the mīm and of the doubled nūn. The lām is not returned to before the excerpt ends. This may be because the chapter on the lām follows in the portion behind the download, or because the Sheikh is anticipating. Recorded so that a reviewer does not read the omission as a defect in the translation, and so that the lām is not silently dropped from the English.

'Nasalisation' renders ghunnah, the nasal resonance carried by the letters mīm and nūn, and the central subject of the chapter.
'Doubling' renders tashdīd, the gemination marked by the shaddah, which the Sheikh here treats as the outcome of assimilation (idghām).

The single line of verse from al-Jazariyyah is rendered as prose in italics per the style guide, with the Arabic kept in the bilingual pane. The four dots after it are in the source and mark that the line is quoted only in part.
'In origin a nasal letter' renders ḥarf aghann — a letter that carries nasal resonance by its nature, before any rule of assimilation applies.

title_ar: أهمية اللغة العربية
title_en: The importance of the Arabic language
body_ar:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين وأصلي وأسلم على من بعث رحمة للعالمين، وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين السلام عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته.

أما بعد فإن من لطف الله تعالى ونعمه ورحمته أن جعل للناس لسانا يتفاهمون به، فالناس يحتاج بعضهم لبعض ولا يمكن أن يقوم أحد منهم بحاجته دون بعض، ولا يمكن أن يستقل منهم إنسان بقضاء أموره ولا بأداء مهماته إلا إذا وجد من يساعده على ذلك، ومن هنا احتاجوا إلى التفاهم فيما بينهم والتعارف، فجعل الله لهم وسائل للتعارف ومن أعظمها الأنساب حيث قال تعالى: {يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ إِنَّا خَلَقْنَاكُمْ مِنْ ذَكَرٍ وَأُنْثَى وَجَعَلْنَاكُمْ شُعُوبًا وَقَبَائِلَ لِتَعَارَفُوا إِنَّ أَكْرَمَكُمْ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ أَتْقَاكُمْ} وجعل لهم وسائل للتفاهم وأعظمها اللغات ولهذا ربط الله بين الألوان واللغات وبين خلق السماوات والأرض في قوله تعالى: {وَمِنْ آَيَاتِهِ خَلْقُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَاخْتِلَافُ أَلْسِنَتِكُمْ وَأَلْوَانِكُمْ إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَآَيَاتٍ لِلْعَالِمِينَ} فالبشر لا يمكن أن يتفاهموا إلا عن طريق وسائل الحس، إلا عن طريق الحواس الخمس، لأن وسائل العلم لدى الإنسان ثلاث، هي العقل والروح والحس..
body_en:
In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. I pray for blessing and peace upon him who was sent as a mercy to the worlds, and upon his family and his Companions and all who are guided by his guidance and follow his sunnah until the Day of Judgement. Peace be upon you, and the mercy of God and His blessings.

To proceed: it is among God Most High's kindness and His favours and His mercy that He made for people a tongue by which they understand one another. People have need of one another, and none of them can meet his need without others; none of them can be independent in managing his affairs or in discharging his tasks unless he finds someone to help him in that. From this they had need to understand one another and to know one another. So God made for them means of knowing one another, the greatest of which are lineages, as God Most High said: {O mankind, We have created you from a male and a female, and made you peoples and tribes, that you may know one another. Indeed the most honoured of you with God is the most God-conscious of you} (Sūrat al-Ḥujurāt 49:13). And He made for them means of understanding one another, the greatest of which are languages. For this reason God linked colours and languages with the creation of the heavens and the earth, in His words, Most High: {And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the difference of your tongues and your colours. Indeed in that are signs for those who know} (Sūrat al-Rūm 30:22). Human beings cannot understand one another except by way of the means of sense — except by way of the five senses — because the means of knowledge a person has are three: the intellect, the spirit and the senses..

title_ar: شرح ورقات إمام الحرمين في أصول الفقه الشريط الأول
title_en: Commentary on the Waraqāt of Imam al-Haramayn on legal theory — tape one
body_ar:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم ، الحمد لله رب العالمين وأصلي وأسلم على من بعث رحمة للعالمين وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين.

هذا شرح ورقات إمام الحرمين في أصول الفقه وهو تأليف صغير مختصر للتعريفات المبدئية في أصول الفقه وضعه إمام الشافعية أبو المعالي عبد الملك بن عبد الله بن يوسف بن محمد الجويني نسبة إلى جوينة من نيسابور وقد ولد رحمه سنة 419هـ وتوفي سنة 478هـ ، وكان من مشاهير المتكلمين والفقهاء والأصوليين وقد ألف هذه الورقات لتكون مبدءا لطلاب العلم يعرفون به بعض مصطلحات أصول الفقه ، وأصول الفقه علم من أهم العلوم الشرعية لأنه الذي يمكن أن يتوصل به إلى فهم الكتاب والسنة و أخذ الأحكام منهما ، و ذلك أن الكتاب والسنة يبحث فيهما من جهتين ـ جهة الورود وجهة الدلالة ، أما جهة الورود فهي النقل بمعنى التحقق من ثبوت نسبة القرآن إلى الله والتحقق من ثبوت نسبة الحديث إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وذلك بالرواية والإسناد والجهة الثانية ، جهة الدلالة ومعناها ما يراد بهذا الكلام ، ما يريده الله من عباده بهذا اللفظ ، وما يريده النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من أمته بهذا اللفظ .
body_en:
In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. I pray for blessing and peace upon him who was sent as a mercy to the worlds, and upon his family and his Companions and all who are guided by his guidance and follow his sunnah until the Day of Judgement.

This is the commentary on the Waraqāt of Imam al-Haramayn on legal theory. It is a small, abridged composition of the introductory definitions in legal theory, set down by the imam of the Shafi'is, Abu al-Maʿali ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Yusuf ibn Muhammad al-Juwayni — the name being taken from Juwaynah, of Nishapur. He was born, may God have mercy on him, in the year 419 AH and died in the year 478 AH, and he was among the famous theologians, jurists and legal theorists. He composed these Waraqāt so that they might be a beginning for students of knowledge, by which they would come to know some of the terms of legal theory.

Legal theory is among the most important of the Sharia sciences, because it is that by which one can arrive at an understanding of the Book and the sunnah, and at the taking of rulings from them. That is because the Book and the sunnah are investigated from two sides: the side of their coming down, and the side of their signification. As for the side of their coming down, it is transmission — meaning the ascertaining of the attribution of the Qur'an to God, and the ascertaining of the attribution of the hadith to the Prophet, upon whom be God's blessing and peace; and that is by narration and by the chain of transmission. And the second side, the side of signification, means what is intended by this speech: what God wants from His servants by this wording, and what the Prophet, upon whom be God's blessing and peace, wants from his community by this wording.

'Imam al-Haramayn' — the imam of the two sanctuaries, Mecca and Medina — is al-Juwayni's title and is kept as the name by which the book is known.
'Theologians' renders mutakallimūn, the practitioners of kalām, speculative theology. It should not be read as a general word for religious scholars; the Sheikh is listing three distinct specialisms.

The distinction between the 'side of coming down' (wurūd, i.e. whether a text is authentically transmitted) and the 'side of signification' (dalālah, i.e. what it means) is the organising distinction of the whole discipline, and the English keeps the two labels sharply apart.

title_ar: شرح ورقات إمام الحرمين في أصول الفقه الشريط الثالث
title_en: Commentary on the Waraqāt of Imam al-Haramayn on legal theory — tape three
body_ar: قال "وترد صيغة الأمر والمراد به الإباحة أو التهديد أو التسوية أو التكوين" يقصد أن صيغة الأمر قد ترد لغير المعنى الأصلي لقرينة تدل على ذلك ، فقد ترد للإباحة كقول الله تعالى: (وإذا حللتم فاصطادوا) فاصطادوا هنا لا تدل على الوجوب وإن كانت صيغة أمر ولا تدل أيضا على الندب بل تدل على الإباحة ، وكذلك قد ترد صيغة الأمر للدلالة على التهديد فلا يقصد بها حينئذ الأمر ، كقول الله تعالى: (قل تمتعوا فإن مصيركم إلى النار) فليس هذا أمرا بالتمتع على حقيقته بل المقصود به التهديد ومثله (فمن شاء فليؤمن ومن شاء فليكفر إنا أعتدنا للظالمين نارا) ، فهذا للتهديد ، وكذلك التسوية وهي التسوية بين الفعل والترك وذلك مثل قول الله تعالى: (فاصبروا أو لا تصبروا سواء عليكم) فاصبروا هنا ليس الأمر فيها للوجوب بل هو للتسوية بدلالة ما بعدها ، فالقرينة المقالية اقتضت صرف الأمر عن معناه الأصلي ، أو للتكوين وهو الإيجاد لقول الله تعالى: (كونوا قردة خائسين) فكونوا هنا ليست الأمر فيها للوجوب وإنما هو للتكوين والقرائين أكثر مما ذكر بل هذه أمثلة للقرائن ومثلها في العكس أيضا للنهي فقد يرد النهي على غير ما هو له، قد يرد للكراهة وقد يرد للتهديد ونحو ذلك..
body_en: He said: "And the form of the imperative occurs while what is meant by it is permissibility, or a threat, or equivalence, or bringing into being." He means that the form of the imperative may occur for other than its original meaning, because of an indication pointing to that. It may occur for permissibility (ibāḥah), as in God Most High's words: (And when you have left the state of pilgrim consecration, then hunt) — "then hunt" here does not indicate obligation, even though it is the form of an imperative, and it does not indicate recommendation either; rather it indicates permissibility. Likewise, the form of the imperative may occur to indicate a threat, so that a command is not meant by it in that case, as in God Most High's words: (Say: enjoy yourselves, for your destination is the Fire) — this is not a command to enjoy oneself in the true sense; rather what is meant by it is a threat. And the like of it: (So whoever wishes, let him believe, and whoever wishes, let him disbelieve; We have prepared for the wrongdoers a Fire) — this is for a threat. Likewise equivalence, which is equivalence between doing and leaving undone, as in God Most High's words: (So be patient or be not patient; it is the same for you) — "be patient" here, the command in it is not for obligation, but is for equivalence, by the indication of what follows it; the verbal indication required that the imperative be turned away from its original meaning. Or for bringing into being, which is causing to exist, as in God Most High's words: (Be apes, despised) — "be" here, the command in it is not for obligation, but is for bringing into being. The indications are more than those mentioned; rather these are examples of indications. And the like of them, conversely, for the prohibition also: the prohibition may occur for other than what it is set for — it may occur for dislikedness, and it may occur for a threat, and the like of that..

THE FIVE RULINGS ARE AT ISSUE THROUGHOUT THIS RECORD and the fixed renderings have been applied exactly: ibāḥah as permissibility, wujūb as obligation, nadb as recommendation, karāhah as dislikedness. The Sheikh's whole point is that an imperative form does not by itself establish obligation, so a slip in any of these four would invert the lesson.

'Indication' renders qarīnah, a contextual pointer that turns a form away from its primary meaning; 'the verbal indication' renders al-qarīnah al-maqāliyyah, one arising from the wording itself as against one arising from the situation.

'Equivalence' renders taswiyah, the case where doing and not doing are put on the same footing; 'bringing into being' renders takwīn, God's creative command, which is not addressed to a moral agent at all.

The source uses round brackets for Qur'anic quotation in this record, where other records in the range use brace brackets. body_ar preserves the source's brackets; body_en uses round brackets to match. title_ar: شرح ورقات إمام الحرمين في أصول الفقه -الشريط الرابع
title_en: Commentary on the Waraqāt of Imam al-Haramayn on legal theory — tape four
body_ar:
النسخ:

عقد هذا الباب لبيان النسخ و ذكر أقسامه، و النسخ معناه في اللغة الإزالة، فيقال نسخت الرياح الأثر إذا أزالته و غيرته و يقال نسخت الشمس الظل إذا أزالته، و يطلق أيضا على النقل فيقال نسخ الكتاب إذا نقله، فهذا معناه في اللغة.

و أما معناه في الاصطلاح فهو تغيير الحكم الشرعي بخطاب متراج عنه، و المقصود بالحكم الشرعي ما كان خطابا أيضا، فلا تنسخ البراءة الأصلية و لا ينسخ بها لأن الأحكام كلها إنما نزلت على براءة أصلية سابقة لها، فلو اعتبر ذالك نسخا لكانت الأحكام كلها ناسخة لأمر قد سبق و هو البراءة الأصلية و عدم التكليف و لا ينسخ أيضا إلا بالخطاب فلا نسخ بالقياس و لا بالاجتهاد و لا بالإجماع، و إنما يحصل النسخ بالوحي المنزل.

،قال وأما النسخ فمعناه لغة الإزالة يقال نسخت الشمس الظل إذا أزالته ، وقيل معناه النقل ، من قولهم نسخت ما في هذا الكتاب أي نقلته ..
body_en:
Abrogation:

This chapter is set out to explain abrogation and to mention its divisions. Naskh: its meaning in the language is removal. One says "the winds nasakhat the trace" when they removed it and altered it, and one says "the sun nasakhat the shade" when it removed it. It is also applied to transferring, so one says "he nasakha the book" when he copied it. This is its meaning in the language.

As for its meaning as a technical term, it is the alteration of a ruling of the Sharia by an address subsequent to it. What is meant by the ruling of the Sharia is one that was itself also an address — so the original absence of legal liability (al-barāʾah al-aṣliyyah) is not abrogated, and nothing is abrogated by it, because all the rulings came down upon an original absence of liability that preceded them; and if that were reckoned to be abrogation, all the rulings would be abrogating something that had preceded, namely the original absence of liability and the absence of legal responsibility. Nor is anything abrogated except by an address: so there is no abrogation by analogical reasoning, nor by independent legal reasoning, nor by scholarly consensus; abrogation comes about only by revelation sent down.

, He said: "As for abrogation, its meaning in the language is removal. One says: the sun nasakhat the shade, when it removed it. And it is said that its meaning is transferring, from their saying: I nasakhtu what is in this book, that is, I copied it"..

flags.context: the technical definition of abrogation
options: by an address subsequent to it [reading mutarākhin ʿanhu]
by an address that supersedes it
as printed: mutarāj ʿanhu
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT, and the word carries the definition. Mutarāj is not a word in this construction. The definition of naskh in this literature turns on the abrogating address being LATER than the abrogated ruling — the standard formulation uses tarākhī, 'being subsequent, coming after an interval', and mutarākhin ʿanhu is almost certainly what was said. The point is not decorative: if the abrogating address were simultaneous with the abrogated one there would be a contradiction rather than an abrogation, which is precisely why the interval is in the definition. Translated on the reading mutarākhin, with the printed form preserved in body_ar and the departure recorded here rather than made silently.

options: the original absence of legal liability (al-barāʾah al-aṣliyyah)
