**Question:** We are bound by insurance contracts imposed upon us, insuring housing, health and other things, and we pay substantial sums for them without return over a long period, unless we are exposed to something that obliges those insuring companies to compensate us for it — such as a water leak in the house, or a fire, or an illness, and the like. The question is about the permissibility of making a claim, or of exaggerating the losses, with a view to obtaining a larger compensation in one of these cases; and whether that counts as forbidden deceit — bearing in mind that what we pay is more than what we obtain in the supposed compensation.

And what is the ruling on the money reaped in such cases, if it is in fact unlawful money? And what is a Muslim obliged to do with it? And is it permissible to return it to those companies? We want your view on that; may God reward you well.

**Answer:** A person may resort to a stratagem in order to take what is his. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, permitted al-Hajjaj ibn Ilat al-Sulami, may God be pleased with him, to lie to Quraysh in order to take his property from them, at the time of the campaign of Khaybar. So it is permissible for a person, if he knows that the compensation is equal to the money that was taken from him, or less than it, to resort to a stratagem for that, even by lying; and that is not called deceit. But if he takes more than the money he paid, he does not return it to the company, because its liability is wholly encumbered (mustaghraqat al-dhimmah) and its money is unlawful; yet he does not take ownership of it himself — rather he spends it in avenues of good, as by paying it to Islamic associations working in calling people to Islam and in charitable work, and the like. Of this same kind is exaggerating in the statement of the damages he has suffered: he may exaggerate until he reaches the limit of what was taken from him, so as to recover the money that was taken from him; and whatever exceeds that, it is not lawful for him to take ownership of it, nor to return it to the company if he has taken it — rather he spends it in avenues of good, as we have mentioned.

---

**Question:** Your eminence the Sheikh, I want an urgent legal opinion. I am a Mauritanian student newly arrived in Germany, and I want the decisive word, supported by the evidence, on shaking hands, because I find it extremely awkward, especially with teachers, with doctors, and with fellow students.

**Answer:** The basic ruling is the prohibition of shaking hands with a woman who is not a close relative, absolutely. This is because God, glorified and exalted is He, forbade the strongest form of mixing between persons not related within the prohibited degrees, and the weakest form of mixing between them, and that indicates the prohibition of what lies between the two. He said, exalted is He: {Tell the believing men to lower their gaze and to guard their private parts; that is purer for them. Indeed God is aware of what they do} (30). For the weakest form of mixing between men and women who are not related within the prohibited degrees is the mixing of the sight and the gaze, and God, exalted is He, forbade it by His words, {Tell the believing men to lower their gaze} — the verse. And the strongest form of mixing between them is the mixing of the private parts, and God, exalted is He, forbade it by His words, {and guard their private parts}. So that indicates the prohibition of what lies between the two, by the signification of a fortiori implication (mafhūm al-muwāfaqah); and a fortiori implication is a proof by agreement, even in the view of those who reject analogical reasoning (qiyās).

For this reason it is not lawful for a person to shake hands with a woman who is not lawful for him. A number of reports have come down on this, in the words of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: "I do not shake hands with women; my word to one woman is only as my word to a hundred women." And likewise the hadith of Aisha: "The hand of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, never touched the hand of a woman who was not lawful for him."

So a person must be scrupulous and must restrain himself from that and keep away from it. And if he is compelled to something of it for some reason — as where his female teacher is prejudiced, so that if he does not shake her hand she will fail him or harm him in the examinations — then he confines himself to the point of necessity in that and does not go beyond it. As for fellow students, male and female, and the like, he does not shake hands with them; rather he explains the position and places it within the scope of custom, and says that he is from the people of a country whose custom is to respect women and not to shake hands with them, and that this matter goes back to custom, like dress and the like.

Whoever is not dazzled by any civilisation preserves his customs and what his civilisation and his environment dictate to him. As for those who are dazzled, they follow the one by whom they have been dazzled, and follow the dominant civilisation, and so rid themselves of their customs, their values, their civilisations and their traditions; and perhaps they rid themselves of part of their religion too, in imitation of and in following after those whose civilisation impressed them.

---

**Question:** I am a university student, and I have female lecturers who go uncovered. Is it permissible for me to look at their faces and at the movement of their hands, while their hair is uncovered, and their arms too at times, during the explanation, from the standpoint of instruction — since in instruction there is permitted what is not permitted elsewhere?

**Answer:** If a person feels desire in a case like this, he must lower his gaze. God, exalted is He, said: {Tell the believing men to lower their gaze and guard their private parts}. And if he feels no desire in it, and there is in it no mixing and no effect upon him, and he confines himself to the measure of his need in his studies, then this is like looking at the bondwomen, who used to leave their heads and their extremities uncovered in the Prophet's time; and looking was not forbidden in their case, except for one in whom that stirred desire, or from whom temptation was feared. As for one in whom it stirs no desire and from whom no temptation is feared, the matter in it is broad as regards him. We ask God to enrich you by what He has made lawful, so that you have no need of what He has made unlawful.

---

**Question:** An imam was certain that he had performed four cycles, and the only follower with him — who had joined the prayer late — said "glory be to God" to him, to signal that he had fallen short by a cycle. But the imam persisted in sitting, and gave the closing salutation. And after the follower had made up what he had missed, he told the imam that he had fallen short by a cycle, and the imam replied to him that he had fallen short by a second cycle; so the late-joining follower entered the prayer while seated, and made it up, and performed the prostration before the salutation.

So what is the ruling on the imam and on the follower? And is the prayer to be made up by way of precaution? And if the imam's certainty is shaken after he has prayed, may he act on the follower's word and make up the cycle he has come to doubt?

**Answer:** The prayer is built upon what a person is certain of. If a person is certain that it was complete, he does not abandon that at anyone's word, because of his certainty — unless those behind him are very many, in which case he does go back to their word. But as for the report of a single person, such as a single follower, he does not abandon his certainty for it; and the misgivings that come over him after that belong to whispering suggestion (waswasah), and it is not lawful to follow it, and it is among the steps of Satan. God, exalted is He, said: {O you who believe, do not follow the steps of Satan} (Sūrat al-Nūr 24:21). A person must beware of falling into that.

As for the follower, he believed that the prayer had fallen short by a cycle, and this too may be a certainty with him, and he is excused in that; but his prayer is valid, and so he makes up one cycle. And if he remains upon his certainty that the prayer had also fallen short by a cycle, then he makes up two cycles and prostrates to cut off the doubt.

---

**Question 2:** Someone who is beset, during the prayer, by the whispering suggestion that a drop of urine has come out — and the same suggestion has come to him several times before — and who completed his prayer without paying any attention to it: what is the ruling on him??

**Answer:** A man came to Umar ibn al-Khattab and mentioned that whenever he urinated he felt that a drop was coming out, or that there was some wetness in his garment. He said: when you perform the ablution, sprinkle water on your garment; then if you feel anything, say, it is the water. So a person cuts off the whispering suggestion and does not follow the devices of Satan. And it is established from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the hadith of Abu Hurayrah in the two Ṣaḥīḥ collections, that he said: "Satan blows between the buttocks of one of you during his prayer; so whoever finds that, let him not leave until he hears a sound or finds a smell."

---

**Question 3:** What is the ruling on someone who has money deposited in an Islamic savings account at the Banque Mauritanienne pour le Commerce International (BMCI), and who at times mixes other deposits with it, and the people of the bank tell him that goods are bought with the money, and that the profit is reckoned in favour of the owner of the money at the end of each year, and they consider him a partner in the profit and the loss, as they put it?

So what is the minimum threshold, in ouguiya, in the case of this money — bearing in mind that a withdrawal may occur before the year is complete? And does the depositor have a share of the profit if he does not stipulate it? And is this saving Islamic?

**Answer:** As regards the saving, its first condition is that it be Islamic and trustworthy, together with its Sharia supervisory board, and that it not deal in usurious gain in any respect whatever. If it is so, then there is no harm in a dealing of this kind, because the person in it is a partner in an investment portfolio; and this portfolio must not be mixed with usurious gain. Likewise, it must be that neither the capital nor the profit is guaranteed, but rather that he is a partner in the loss and in the profit. The bank looks to the most profitable transactions for this portfolio and invests in them on a profit-sharing basis, and it is a partner in a profit-sharing partnership (muḍārabah): the depositor stands in the position of the owner of the capital, and the manager of the bank in the position of the working partner, and between them is a qirāḍ partnership, with the profit and the loss according to what the two of them agree upon; and likewise the bank does not guarantee him the capital or the profit.

As for what concerns the minimum threshold (niṣāb) for zakat, in ouguiya, at this time: it is the value of eighty-four grams of gold (84 grams), of whatever kind; and gold at present is high, and the value of 84 grams at present comes to nearly 300,000 ouguiya. This is the threshold. And if this threshold remains throughout the year, then he may pay zakat along with it on the remaining sums that have been added to it, and that suffices — so that paying zakat does not become burdensome for him and the lunar year of possession does not multiply upon him.

---

**Question:** I am a Mauritanian student studying in Algeria. Living near me is a Christian neighbour. I invited him several times to the fast-breaking meal last Ramadan, but some questions have arisen for me from him, namely:

- Is it permissible to drink from the glass he had been drinking from, in the case of making tea, for example?
- Is it permissible to return the greeting of peace to him when he says "peace be upon you"?
- I found a copy of the Qur'an in his room, and he told me that one of the Algerians had made him a gift of it. Was it permissible for the one who gave it to him to do that?
- Is it permissible to congratulate him on the new year of the Christian calendar, given that he always congratulates me on the Islamic festivals?

**Answer:** As for this neighbour, a person must be hoping for his guidance and striving for his rescue from the Fire; otherwise there is no good for him in associating with him. If he is not addicted to drinking wine, it is permissible to drink from a vessel he has drunk from, and that applies to the tea glass and to other vessels. If he begins with the greeting of peace, then the greeting is returned to him. It is not permissible to give him a complete Qur'an as a gift, except together with a translation or a commentary or the like. As for congratulating him on the year of the Christian calendar: if he regards that as a religious festival, then it is not permissible; and if he does not regard it as a religious festival, but rather regards it as a national or an international holiday, then he may be congratulated on it.

---

**Question:** About half an hour before the call to prayer for the Friday prayer, the reciter comes and sits in front of the worshippers and recites whatever God wills him to recite — and mostly the recitation is not from Sūrat al-Kahf. Most of those praying in the mosque are in distraction and discomfort, especially if the reciter's voice is not a good one, to say nothing of the talking and the whispering during the recitation. And if the reciter is one of those with good voices, then he distracts the worshippers, and often the recitation is accompanied by talk and excitement — and this is either from being affected by the recitation, prompted by the voice, or out of love for the reciter, or to encourage him; and in all of it there is distraction of the worshippers, and likewise of the one who sits silent, in intimate converse with his Lord?? Give us a ruling, may God reward you well. And is this established from the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace?

**Answer:** What this reciter does, the people of knowledge have stated explicitly to be an innovation (bidʿah), and that he is to be made to leave the mosque, so that he does not distract people from reciting the Qur'an and from the remembrance of God, majestic is His majesty — unless he is teaching the people, and some learners gather round him in a circle and learn from his recitation, whether they recite along with him or listen attentively to him. In that case it comes under teaching, and not under making people listen to his recitation. Whether his voice is good or harsh, it is not permissible to leave him reciting in this manner, regularly, every Friday, because of the innovating that is in it. No permission for it has come down from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and censure of its like has come down from his Companions. And censure of forming circles on Friday has come down from him, may God bless him and grant him peace, in two reports — but the place of that is where it is not for seeking knowledge and for seizing the opportunity of people's gathering, since they do not ordinarily gather except on Friday.

---

**Question:** What is the ruling on multiplying the call to prayer before the Friday prayer in the mosque?

**Answer:** The multiplying of the call to prayer goes back to public benefit (maṣlaḥah). The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, multiplied it for the dawn prayer for a preponderant benefit, so that the sleeper might wake and perform the ablution, and the one in a state of major ritual impurity might perform the full washing. So Bilal used to give the call while it was still night, and Ibn Umm Maktum used to give the call after the dawn had broken, because he was a blind man who could not see until people said to him, "You are in the morning, you are in the morning."

Then afterwards the Companions, may God bless him and grant him peace, reached consensus (ijmāʿ), in the days of Uthman ibn Affan, may God be pleased with him, upon introducing a first call for the Friday prayer, when people had become occupied away from it by their trades and the like. So they introduced this call, which is the first as regards performance and the later as regards legislation. This, then, is a matter of consensus. And whatever exceeds that: if it is a preponderant benefit, and this benefit has been taken into account in it, then it can be accepted, by analogy with the Companions' introduction of this call, and with what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, adopted of multiplying the call in the case of the dawn prayer.

---

**Question:** What is the ruling on raising the hands during the Friday sermon and outside it?

**Answer:** Raising the hands is one of the causes of a supplication being answered. It is established in the two Ṣaḥīḥ collections that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, mentioned "the man who prolongs his journey, dishevelled and dust-covered, stretching out his hands to the sky: O Lord, O Lord." Likewise there is reported, from the hadith [of Abu Dawud]: "God, exalted is He, is modest and generous; He is ashamed, when a servant stretches out his hands to Him, to send them back empty." And it is established from him, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he stretched out his hands in supplication on many occasions.

But it has not come down from him that he raised his hands in supplication on the pulpit, except in the prayer for rain: for when he sought rain — that is, asked God to send down rain — he would raise his hands and turn their backs towards the sky. This form, narrated from him, may God bless him and grant him peace, is a sunnah in the Friday sermon and in other sermons, such as the sermon of the prayer for rain. As for the imam's raising his hands in supplication on the pulpit on Friday other than in the prayer for rain, that is an innovation (bidʿah).

It is established in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim and in the Sunan collections that Umarah ibn Nuwaybah al-Aslami, may God be pleased with him, when Bishr ibn Marwan raised his hands on the pulpit, rose to him during the sermon to change the wrong, and said: "May God disfigure these two short [hands]! I saw the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the pulpit do no more than this" — and he raised his finger.

This is with respect to the imam. As for the followers, raising the hands remains upon the basic ruling at the time of supplication. Some of the people of knowledge held it to be disliked (makrūh) and said: if it is disliked for the imam, then the follower follows his lead in it, because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "The imam has been appointed only to be followed."

---

**Question:** What is the ruling on girls being schooled outside the homeland without a close male relative (maḥram)?

**Answer:** Girls being schooled in formal schools outside the country takes on whichever of the rulings of the revealed law applies. If the girl does not fear for herself, nor for her religion and her character, and the girl is in a place separate from men at the time of residence — that is, if the girls have accommodation reserved for them — then it is permissible for her.

And if that distance requires a day and a night on the road — that is, if there is a "transit" in it, for example — such that the journey imposes on her twenty-four hours of travelling on the road, then that journey is not lawful for her except with a close male relative, on account of the words of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: "It is not lawful for a woman who believes in God and the Last Day to travel a day and a night except with one who is a close male relative." And if the duration of the journey is less than that, then there is no harm in it, if she is safe as to herself and as to her religion, and does not fear temptation, and does not fear that anyone will assault her.

As for her study, there must also be in it an adherence to the controls of the revealed law: she must not mix with men who are not close relatives, nor shake hands with them, nor uncover anything that God has obliged her to cover. These things are not possible in some countries, and for that reason it is not lawful for her to go to them for study — especially if that country imposes upon her the uncovering of her head, or mixing with men who are not close relatives.

title_ar: الشيخ الددو يترأس حفل اختتام العام الدراسـي 2010-2011 لمركز تكوين العلماء.
title_en: Sheikh al-Dedew Presides over the Ceremony Closing the 2010–2011 Academic Year at the Centre for the Formation of Scholars
body_ar:
خلال حفل اختتام العام الدراسي 2010-2011، الذي أقامه مركز تكوين العلماء بمقره في عرفات مساء أمس الخميس الموافق: 30/06/2011 بعد صلاة المغرب ألقى فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن ولد الددو – رئيس المركز- كلمة رسمية رحب فيها بالضيوف الكرام الذين لبوا الدعوة؛ ومن بينهم سفراء العربية السعودية والكويت وقطر، ومدير شركة شنقيتل، إضافة إلى نائب رئيس المجموعة الحضرية، ووالي انواكشوط المساعد وحاكم عرفات ورجال أعمال ومديري مؤسسات إضافة إلى جمع غفير من العلماء والقضاة والوجهاء والأئمة والدعاة.

وأكد الشيخ محمد الحسن ولد الددو، في مستهل كلمته أن القائمين على المركز أرادوا جمع الحسنيَيْن، مستفيدين من إيجابيات المحظرة التقليدية والمدرسة الحديثة, ومتحاشين سلبياتهما، مشيرا إلى أن جميع طلاب المركز يحفظون القرآن ولديهم برنامج حفظ يومي للحديث الشريف وبقية المتون العلمية الأخرى.

وذكر الشيخ أن المركز مفتوح أمام جميع المسلمين، فلاجنسية له وإن كان يقع على الأرض الموريتانية، شاكرا السلطات الرسمية على إتاحة الفرصة لفتح المركز لكل المسلمين، مؤكدا أن ضيوف المركز وطلابه كانوا دائما محل ترحيب على المستوى الرسمي.

وأشار الشيخ الددو إلى أن مركز تكوين العلماء يرتبط بعلاقات تعاون وتبادل مع مراكز دولية وأخرى محلية، وشهد إقبالا كبيرا خلال السنوات الماضية من طرف العلماء وطلاب العلم، وأكد على أن مهمة المركز الأساسية هي صفته العلمية؛ فلا علاقة له بالسياسة ولا بعلم الاجتماع ولا الفكر الإيديولوجي، فهو مركز علمي يهتم بتخريج كوكبة من أهل العلم مع مسحة ربانية، "لأن العلم سلاح لا يمكن أن يوضع إلا في يد أمينة" –حسب تعبير الشيخ الددو.

وخلال هذا الحفل كانت كلمة المدير العام لمركز تكوين العلماء الدكتور محمد المختار ولد محمد المامي حول أهداف المركز ونظمه التعليمية مشيرا إلى أن "المركز ما هو إلا حلقة من حلقات العطاء في هذا البلد المعطاء، فهو امتداد للمحظرة الشنقيطية العتيقة التي أضاء نورها هذه الربوع وحملت مشعل الهداية في كل أقطار العالم.

وأكد مدير المركز أن القائمين عليه يريدون من خلاله أن يحافظوا على ذلك المجد التليد حتى يرثه الحفيد بعد الحفيد، مستفيدين في ذلك مما وصلت إليه المناهج التربوية الحديثة من وسائل وأدوات، مضيفين إليه ما يرنوه ضروريا من معرفة اللغات ودراسة أساسيات الاقتصاد والقانون والتكوين على الحاسب الآلي، وغير ذلك مما هو ضروري لدارس العلوم الشرعية حتى يكون متوازن الشخصية مكتمل الرؤية قادرا على تبليغ الدين بلسان العصر، متفادين في هذا المركز بعض الوسائل المحظرية التي كانت وليدة بيئتها.

وأضاف أن طلاب المركز يبلغ عددهم حتى الآن 102طالبا؛ منهم 12 طالبا في المرحلة الجامعية، و90 طالبا في المرحلة الإعدادية والثانوية، وستتخرج أول دفعة في المركز السنة القادمة، ويخصص المركز نسبة 10% من المقاعد سنويا للطلاب غير الموريتانيين، ويبلغ عدد الأساتذة 20 أستاذا.

وتحدث مدير المركز عن مشروع الأئمة والدعاة، والذي يضم 25 إماما وداعية؛ من ضمنهم 6 نساء داعيات، بالإضافة إلى 40 امرأة يتم تكوينهنّ طبقا لبرنامج خاص يراعي خصوصيات المرأة وحاجياتها العلمية والدعوية.

وقال مدير المركز إن الدراسة تتم بالتدرج على ثلاث مراحل؛ أولى تعادل الثانوية في العلوم الأصلية ومدتها أربع سنوات وتدرس فيها الكتب والمختصرات، ومرحلة ثانية تعادل الجامعة ومدتها أربع سنوات وتدرس فيها مطولات الكتب، ومرحلة ثالثة تعادل الدراسات العليا بمرحلتيها الماجستير والدكتوراه، وهدفها تعميق الفنون الشرعية واللغوية وتختتم ببحوث معمقة، وخلال المراحل الثلاث يدرس الطالب اثنين وخمسين فنا.

وكان ضمن فقرات هذا الحفل كلمة باسم الأساتذة ألقاها فضيلة الشيخ شيخنا ولد سيد الحاج الذي استعرض في كلمته التربوية البليغة جهود العلماء في هذا البلد، واستحث همم الطلاب على الجد والمثابرة في التحصيل.

كما عبر الطلاب ووكلاء الطلاب – في مداخلاتهم بالحفل - عن سرورهم بما يقدمه المركز من جهود علمية غير مسبوقة في تاريخ البلد، داعين الجميع إلى دعم جهوده من أجل إيصال رسالته النبيلة.

وفي ختام الحفل تم توزيع خمسة دروع على المؤسسات الداعمة للمركز، ووزعت ثلاثون جائزة على الطلاب المتفوقين في الامتحان ومسابقة الشعر والخطابة ..، ومن ضمن هذه الجوائز؛ تذكرة عمرة للديار المقدسة، بالإضافة إلى جوائز نقدية معتبرة.
body_en:
During the ceremony closing the 2010–2011 academic year, held by the Centre for the Formation of Scholars at its premises in Arafat on the evening of yesterday, Thursday 30/06/2011, after the sunset prayer, His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew — president of the Centre — delivered a formal address in which he welcomed the honoured guests who had answered the invitation. Among them were the ambassadors of Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and Qatar, and the director of the Chinguitel company, as well as the deputy head of the Urban Community, the assistant governor of Nouakchott, the prefect of Arafat, businessmen and heads of institutions, besides a large gathering of scholars, judges, notables, imams and preachers.

At the opening of his address Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew affirmed that those running the Centre had wanted to combine the two goods, drawing on the strengths of the traditional maḥẓarah and of the modern school while avoiding the weaknesses of both, noting that all the Centre's students memorise the Qur'an and have a daily programme of memorisation for the noble hadith and for the remaining scholarly primers (mutūn).

The Sheikh stated that the Centre is open to all Muslims and has no nationality, even though it stands on Mauritanian soil, thanking the official authorities for making it possible to open the Centre to all Muslims, and affirming that the Centre's guests and students have always been made welcome at the official level.

Sheikh al-Dedew indicated that the Centre for the Formation of Scholars maintains relations of cooperation and exchange with international centres and with local ones, and that it has seen a large turnout in past years from scholars and students of knowledge. He affirmed that the Centre's essential mission lies in its scholarly character: it has nothing to do with politics, nor with sociology, nor with ideological thought. It is a scholarly centre concerned with graduating a company of people of learning with a godly cast, "because knowledge is a weapon that can only be placed in a trustworthy hand" — in Sheikh al-Dedew's own words.

The ceremony also included an address by the director general of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars, Dr Muhammad al-Mukhtar Ould Muhammad al-Mami, on the Centre's aims and its educational systems, in which he indicated that "the Centre is nothing but one link in the chain of giving in this giving country; it is an extension of the ancient Shinqiti maḥẓarah, whose light illumined these regions and bore the torch of guidance into every quarter of the world.

The Centre's director affirmed that those who run it wish through it to preserve that inherited glory, so that grandson after grandson may inherit it, drawing in this on what modern educational methods have arrived at in the way of means and instruments, and adding to it what they regard as necessary of the knowledge of languages, the study of the fundamentals of economics and law, training in computing, and whatever else is necessary for a student of the Sharia sciences, so that he may be balanced in personality and complete in vision and able to convey the religion in the idiom of the age — while avoiding, in this Centre, certain of the maḥẓarah's practices that were the product of its own environment.

He added that the Centre's students number, to date, 102: of these, 12 are at the university stage and 90 at the intermediate and secondary stage. The first cohort at the Centre will graduate next year. The Centre allocates 10 per cent of its places each year to non-Mauritanian students, and the teaching staff number 20.

The Centre's director spoke about the imams and preachers project, which comprises 25 imams and preachers, among them 6 women preachers, besides 40 women who are being trained under a special programme that takes account of what is particular to women and of their scholarly and daʿwah needs.

The Centre's director said that study proceeds by stages, in three phases: a first, equivalent to secondary level in the original sciences, lasting four years, in which the books and the abridgements (mukhtaṣarāt) are studied; a second, equivalent to university level, lasting four years, in which the extended works are studied; and a third, equivalent to postgraduate study in its two phases of master's and doctorate, whose aim is to deepen the Sharia and linguistic disciplines and which concludes with in-depth research. Across the three phases the student studies fifty-two disciplines.

Among the items of the ceremony was an address on behalf of the teaching staff delivered by Sheikh Shaykhna Ould Sid al-Hajj, who in his eloquent educational address surveyed the efforts of the scholars in this country and stirred the students' resolve to diligence and perseverance in their studies.

The students and the students' representatives, in their interventions at the ceremony, likewise expressed their pleasure at the scholarly efforts the Centre is making, unprecedented in the country's history, and called on everyone to support its efforts so that its noble message may be carried through.

At the close of the ceremony five shields were presented to the institutions supporting the Centre, and thirty prizes were distributed to the students who had excelled in the examination and in the poetry and oratory competition. Among these prizes was a ticket for the lesser pilgrimage (ʿumrah) to the Holy Places, besides substantial cash prizes.

flags.arabic: المحظرة التقليدية / المحظرة الشنقيطية العتيقة / بعض الوسائل المحظرية
flags.context: أرادوا جمع الحسنيَيْن، مستفيدين من إيجابيات المحظرة التقليدية والمدرسة الحديثة
options: maḥẓarah (retained, with a gloss on first occurrence per article)
mahdara (the spelling used in the style guide's own preamble)
traditional Mauritanian seminary
flags.note: The maḥẓarah is the institution this whole record is about, and the corpus needs one fixed rendering for it. The style guide's preamble writes it 'mahdara'; the glossary has no entry. Retained here as maḥẓarah because that is the correct romanisation of محظرة with diacritics, but the discrepancy with the style guide's own spelling should be resolved centrally and applied corpus-wide, not decided record by record. Note the adjective المحظرية in the sixth paragraph, which needs the same base word.

flags.context: أن القائمين على المركز أرادوا جمع الحسنيَيْن
options: to combine the two goods
to have the best of both
to gather the two excellences
flags.note: An idiom, from Sūrat al-Tawbah 9:52 ('one of the two best outcomes'), used here in its ordinary Arabic sense of taking the advantages of both of two things. Rendered literally so the Qur'anic echo is not erased; 'the best of both worlds' would be idiomatic English but would flatten it into a cliché and lose the register.

flags.arabic: مضيفين إليه ما يرنوه ضروريا من معرفة اللغات
flags.context: the director general's account of what the Centre adds to the traditional curriculum
options: read as ما يرونه ('what they regard as')
read as ما يرنون إليه ('what they aspire to')
leave unresolved
flags.note: يرنوه is not a well-formed word here and appears to be a typing error in the CMS. Two readings are possible; the first is adopted because it fits the syntax (ما يرونه ضروريا, 'what they regard as necessary'). Not silently corrected in body_ar. A reviewer with the printed programme could settle it.

flags.arabic: "المركز ما هو إلا حلقة من حلقات العطاء … في كل أقطار العالم.
flags.context: the quotation from the Centre's director general
options: treat the whole two-sentence passage as quoted, as done here
treat only the first clause as quoted
withhold the quotation marks entirely
flags.note: The source opens this quotation and never closes it, so the point at which the director's own words end is not marked. The English follows the source's opening mark and closes at the end of the sentence the source ends with a full stop. This is a CMS punctuation defect of the kind the style guide says to record rather than repair; where a quotation ends is not a trivial matter when the words are being attributed to a named person.

flags.context: list of guests at the ceremony
options: Chinguitel (the Mauritanian telecom operator)
Chinguitell
Shinqitel
flags.note: شنقيتل is the Mauritanian mobile operator that trades in Latin script as Chinguitel. The company's own spelling is used rather than a transliteration of the Arabic.

translator_notes: This is a news report written by the site's news desk, not a text by the Sheikh. What is attributed to him and to the Centre's director arrives at second hand and in summary, and only one sentence is given inside quotation marks as his own words. The site should render it as reportage.

The CMS timestamp is a bulk-upload date and is not evidence of when the report was written. The body supplies its own date for the event — the evening of Thursday 30 June 2011 — which is better evidence than the record's timestamp.

عرفات here is the Arafat moughataa of Nouakchott, where the Centre's premises stand, not the plain near Mecca. The Arabic is bare and is left bare in the English; the identification is recorded here rather than inserted into the text. Compare record 769 in this same span, where عرفات does mean the plain near Mecca.

حاكم عرفات is rendered 'the prefect of Arafat'. In Mauritanian administrative usage the hakem heads a moughataa (department); 'governor' is kept for the wālī of Nouakchott named in the same sentence, so that the two ranks stay distinct in the English.
No ruling words occur in this record, so the five-rulings mapping of style guide section 3 is not engaged anywhere in it.

title_ar: الشيخ الددو ضيف دائم على قناة فور شباب طيلة أيام شهر رمضان في برنامج مفاهيم ج3
title_en: Sheikh al-Dedew a Standing Guest on the 4Shbab Channel throughout Ramadan on the Programme "Concepts", Part 3
body_ar:
تستضيف قناة فور شباب فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن ولد الددو رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء في برنامج مفاهيم ( الجزء الثالث)، بوصفه ضيفا دائما للبرنامج، وذلك طيلة أيام شهر رمضان الكريم ويُحاور الشيخ في هذه الحلقات الدكتور عادل باناعمه.

يبث هذا البرنامج كل يوم من أيام الشهر المبارك في الساعة الخامسة والنصف مساء بتوقيت مكة المكرمة، 1:30 زوالا بالتوقيت العالمي، ويعاد بثه السادسة والنصف مساء بتوقيت مكة المكرمة، 3:30 صباحا بالتوقيت العالمي.

ويهتم برنامج مفاهيم (الجزء الثالث)، بالمصطلحات والمفاهيم المتداولة في الوسط الشبابي بشكل عام، سواء كانت مفاهيم شرعية أو تربوية أو دعوية أو اجتماعية.

حيث يسلط الضوء عليها من خلال تجلية معناها الصحيح وحدود تطبيقاتها المقبولة، والإشارة إلى ما يحصل فيها من خطأ على المستوى المعرفي أو المستوى التطبيقي، وذلك انطلاقا من الموازين الشرعية ومراعاة فقه الفتوى والواقع في المنهج الوسطي المعتدل.

ونشير كذلك إلى أن هناك برامج أخرى تبث في القنوات الأخرى للشيخ خلال الشهر الكريم منها قناة دليل وقناة الرسالة، والتلفزة الوطنية لموريتانيا، وسيعلن عن مواعيدها في وقت لاحق قبل بثها، لذلك ننوه بأهميتها وندعو الجمهور الكريم إلى اغتنام هذه الفرصة الرمضانية الثمينة.

وسيعمل القائمون على الموقع – إنشاء الله- على مواكبة حلقات هذا البرنامج وبثها مباشرة على الموقع ورفعها في القسم الخاص بها في جديد الموقع مع تلخيص لأهم أفكارها وتبسيط معانيها ليحصل النفع وتعم الفائدة.

لمتابعة ما تقدم من حلقات البرنامج اضغط هنا:
body_en:
The 4Shbab channel is hosting His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew, president of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars, on the programme "Concepts" (part three), as a standing guest of the programme, throughout the days of the noble month of Ramadan. In these episodes the Sheikh is in conversation with Dr ʿAdil Banaʿmah.

This programme is broadcast every day of the blessed month at half past five in the evening, Mecca time — 1:30 in the afternoon, universal time — and is repeated at half past six in the evening, Mecca time — 3:30 in the morning, universal time.

The programme "Concepts" (part three) is concerned with the terms and concepts current among young people generally, whether they are concepts of the Sharia, or educational, or daʿwah-related, or social ones.

It throws light on them by bringing out their correct meaning and the limits of their acceptable applications, and by pointing to the error that occurs in them at the level of understanding or at the level of application, proceeding in this from the criteria of the Sharia and from regard for the jurisprudence of issuing legal opinions and for circumstances, within the moderate, middle-way approach.

We note too that there are other programmes with the Sheikh broadcast on other channels during the noble month, among them the Dalil channel, the al-Risalah channel, and Mauritanian national television. Their times will be announced at a later date before they are broadcast, and we accordingly draw attention to their importance and invite the honoured public to take advantage of this precious Ramadan opportunity.

Those running the site will work, God willing, to keep pace with the episodes of this programme, to broadcast them live on the site, and to post them in the section set aside for them among the site's new material, together with a summary of their most important ideas and a simplification of their meanings, so that benefit may be had and may become general.

flags.arabic: الساعة الخامسة والنصف مساء بتوقيت مكة المكرمة، 1:30 زوالا بالتوقيت العالمي، ويعاد بثه السادسة والنصف مساء بتوقيت مكة المكرمة، 3:30 صباحا بالتوقيت العالمي

flags.note: The conversions in the source do not work. Mecca is UTC+3, so 17:30 Mecca is 14:30 UTC, not 13:30; and 18:30 Mecca is 15:30 UTC, not 3:30 in the morning. Both figures are reproduced exactly as the source gives them and neither has been corrected, per style guide section 11. The record is in any case a schedule for Ramadan 1432 and is of no present use except as a record of what was announced.

Fourshbab / Dr Adil Ba Naʿmah
flags.note: فور شباب is the satellite channel that trades in Latin script as 4Shbab, and its own spelling is used rather than a transliteration. The interlocutor's name is a Saudi one; باناعمه is most often written Bana'mah or Ba Na'mah in English and the segmentation is not certain from the Arabic alone. Flagged rather than fixed.

flags.arabic: مراعاة فقه الفتوى والواقع في المنهج الوسطي المعتدل

the fiqh of fatwa and of reality
the practice of issuing opinions with due regard to context

The CMS timestamp is a bulk-upload date and is not evidence of when the announcement was written; the content places it at the start of Ramadan 1432, which began in early August 2011.

title_ar: سماحة الشيخ  الددو  يحاضر في مركز البحوث والدراسات بالبنك الإسلامي للتنمية بجدة .
title_en: His Eminence Sheikh al-Dedew Lectures at the Research and Studies Centre of the Islamic Development Bank in Jeddah
body_ar:
سماحة الشيخ الددو يحاضر في مركز البحوث والدراسات بالبنك الإسلامي للتنمية بجدة .

ألقى سماحة الشيخ محمد الحسن ولد الددو رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء محاضرة بمركز البحوث والدراسات بالبنك الإسلامي للتنمية بجدة اليوم الإثنين (15/ 09 / 1432 ه) الموافق (15/ 09 / 2011م ) تحت عنوان: أصول المعاملات في الشريعة الإسلامية وقد تناول فيها :

• طبيعة الشريعة في بيان الأحكام مقارنا بينها وبين القوانين الوضعية ، مبينا أن الشريعة تذكر الأحكام معللة ومسببة بينما تذكرها القوانين مجردة عن ذلك.

• النصوص القرآنية التي تناولت العقد والجوانب التي تناولتها منه .

• العقود المنهي وأوجه النهي عنها إجمالا.

• شروط العقود إجمالا .

• أوجه السعة والتضييق في العقود .

وقد ختمت المحاضرة بمناقشات من طرف الحضور حول جملة من القضايا أثارتها المحاضرة .

هذا وقد أدار المحاضرة الأستاذ الدكتور والخبير الإقتصادي العياشي فداد وحضرها جمع غفير من الباحثين في مركز الدراسات والبحوث بالبنك والمهتمين بالمعاملات الإسلامية .

كما حظي سماحة الشيخ باستقبال خاص من معالي الأستاذ الدكتور أحمد محمد علي مدير البنك الإسلامي للتنمية وكبار معاونيه في مكتبه قبل المحاضرة .
body_en:
His Eminence Sheikh al-Dedew lectures at the Research and Studies Centre of the Islamic Development Bank in Jeddah.

His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew, president of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars, delivered a lecture at the Research and Studies Centre of the Islamic Development Bank in Jeddah today, Monday (15/09/1432 AH), corresponding to (15/09/2011 CE), under the title: The foundations of transactions (muʿāmalāt) in the Islamic Sharia. In it he took up:

• The nature of the Sharia in setting out rulings, comparing it with man-made law, and showing that the Sharia states rulings with their operative causes (ʿilal) and grounds given, whereas the man-made laws state them stripped of that.

• The Qur'anic texts that deal with the contract, and the aspects of it that they deal with.

• Contracts [that are] prohibited, and the respects in which they are prohibited, in general terms.

• The conditions (shurūṭ) of contracts, in general terms.

• The respects in which contracts are given latitude and the respects in which they are restricted.

The lecture closed with discussions from those present on a number of the questions the lecture had raised.

The lecture was chaired by Professor Dr al-ʿAyyashi Faddad, the economic expert, and was attended by a large gathering of researchers at the Bank's Centre for Studies and Research and of those concerned with Islamic transactions.

His Eminence the Sheikh was also received privately by His Excellency Professor Dr Ahmad Muhammad ʿAli, director of the Islamic Development Bank, and by his senior aides, in his office before the lecture.

flags.context: the date of the lecture
options: reproduce both dates exactly as given and flag the mismatch
correct the Gregorian date to 15/08/2011
give only the hijri date
flags.note: The two dates do not correspond and neither fits the day named. 15 Ramadan 1432 fell on about 15 August 2011, which was a Monday and matches the record's timestamp; 15 September 2011 was a Thursday. The Gregorian figure appears to be a slip for 15/08/2011, in which the month was carried over from the hijri date. Both are reproduced exactly as the source gives them and neither is corrected, per style guide section 11.

flags.arabic: • العقود المنهي وأوجه النهي عنها إجمالا.
flags.context: third of the five headings the lecture covered
options: render with a visible bracketed completion, as done here
read as العقود المنهي عنها and render without marking
leave the lacuna open with an ellipsis
flags.note: المنهي is left dangling in the Arabic: the phrase requires عنها to be complete (العقود المنهي عنها, 'the contracts that are prohibited'). The word is missing in the source. The English supplies the sense in square brackets so that the reader can see something was missing rather than meeting a silently repaired sentence. Style guide section 11 forbids silent repair.

flags.context: the lecture title
options: the foundations of transactions (muʿāmalāt) in the Islamic Sharia
the principles of Islamic commercial law
the fundamentals of dealings in Islamic law
flags.note: أصول here is 'foundations' in the sense of the root principles a body of law rests on, not uṣūl al-fiqh as a discipline, and معاملات is the glossary's 'transactions'. Option 2 would be the natural phrase for a banking audience but would narrow معاملات to commerce, which it is wider than.

translator_notes: A news report on a lecture. It gives the lecture's five headings and no content under any of them, so no ruling is stated anywhere in the record and the five-rulings mapping of style guide section 3 is not engaged. In particular, the third heading announces that prohibited contracts were treated but names none of them and gives no ruling word.
The CMS timestamp is a bulk-upload date and is not evidence of when the report was written.

The first line of the body repeats the record's own title verbatim. It is a CMS duplication, preserved in body_ar and rendered in body_en because the style guide forbids skipping a paragraph; the site should suppress it in display.
The source names the host institution twice in different word orders (مركز البحوث والدراسات and مركز الدراسات والبحوث). Both are rendered as the source has them.

title_ar: سماحة الشيخ يحاضر في جامعة مولاي إسماعيل حول( العلوم الشرعية والمجتمع )
title_en: His Eminence the Sheikh Lectures at Moulay Ismail University on "The Sharia Sciences and Society"
body_ar:
بمناسبة افتتاح العام الدراسي في كلية الآداب بجامعة مولاي إسماعيل بمكناس ألقى فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء محاضرة بالقاعة الكبرى بالكلية تحت عنوان : ( العلوم الشرعية والمجتمع ) وتميز الحضور بتنوع شمل رئيس المجلس العلمي بالمدينة وعميد الكلية ورئيس شعبة الدراسات الإسلامية وعدد كبير من الأساتذة والطلاب.

لمتابعة هذه المحاضرة أضغط هنا: http://dedewnet.com/index.php/adabiyat.html?view=media&id=1564

كما ألقى محاضرة أخرى هامة تحت عنوان: (أولويات الأمة للقيام بالشهادة)

لمتابعة هذه المحاضرة أضغط هنا:http://dedewnet.com/index.php/adabiyat.html?view=media&id=1560
body_en:
On the occasion of the opening of the academic year at the Faculty of Letters of Moulay Ismail University in Meknes, His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew, president of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars, delivered a lecture in the faculty's main hall under the title: (The Sharia sciences and society). The attendance was notable for its variety, taking in the president of the city's scholarly council, the dean of the faculty, the head of the Islamic studies department, and a large number of teaching staff and students.

He also delivered another important lecture under the title: (The community's priorities for carrying out the bearing of witness).

flags.context: the title of the second lecture, given without any content
options: the community's priorities for carrying out the bearing of witness
the community's priorities in discharging its witness over mankind
the ummah's priorities in fulfilling the testimony
flags.note: الشهادة here is the community's bearing witness over mankind (Qur'an 2:143), not testimony in court and not the shahādah of the creed. The English has to choose one of the three senses and the Arabic gives no gloss; option 1 keeps it closest to the words without importing the Qur'anic reference the title only alludes to. Since the record gives the title and nothing else, a reviewer with the recording should confirm the intended sense before it is fixed.

flags.context: list of those attending
options: the president of the city's scholarly council
the head of the local religious council (majlis ʿilmī)
the chairman of the Meknes ulema council
flags.note: The Moroccan majālis ʿilmiyyah are the official regional councils of religious scholars under the Ministry of Habous. 'Scholarly council' is literal and neutral; the other options explain the institution but insert a description the Arabic does not give.

translator_notes: A short announcement written by the site's news desk. It reports that two lectures were given and gives no content from either, so there is nothing in it that could be mistaken for a ruling.
The CMS timestamp is a bulk-upload date and is not evidence of when the announcement was written; nor does the body supply a date for the lectures.

The two 'click here' lines are the site's navigation furniture, and the bare URLs they contain are part of that furniture. They are preserved in body_ar, recorded in source_download_link and embedded_media, and omitted from body_en. Removing them leaves body_en with two paragraphs where body_ar has four; that is deliberate.
The substance of both lectures exists only as audio at the two links recorded. This record is an announcement of them, not a text of either.

title_ar: الشيخ الددو يُحاضر بمدينة ازويرات بدعوة من جمعية المستقبل للدعوة والثقافة والتعليم
title_en: Sheikh al-Dedew Lectures in the City of Zouerate at the Invitation of the Future Association for Daʿwah, Culture and Education
body_ar:
ألقى فضيلة الشيخ العلامة محمد الحسن الددو رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء سلسلة محاضرات في مدينة ازويرات في 17 اكتوبر 2011 بدعوة من جمعية المستقبل للدعوة والثقافة والتعليم.

وقد ألقيت المحاضرة الأولى في مقر محظرة النساء بازويرات في التاسعة صباحا تحت عنوان: " تأملات في سورة الحجرات".

وفي الخامسة مساء ألقى الشيخ – حفظه الله- المحاضرة الثانية في مقر سينما ازويرات وهي بعنوان: "الإسلام مسؤولية وأخلاق"، وتم تنظيمها بالتعاون بين جمعية المستقبل للدعوة والثقافة والتعليم وجمعية بناء زمور.

كما ألقى فضيلته المحاضرة الثالثة والأخيرة بمسجد الرضوان وسط المدينة بعد صلاة المغرب وهي بعنوان " مفاهيم يجب أن تصحح" (مفهوم العبادة، التدين، الاستخلاف في الأرض).

وقد حضر هذا النشاط الدعوي الذي دعت له ونظمته جمعية المستقبل للدعوة والثقافة والتعليم جمهور غفير من شباب مدينة ازويرات إلى جانب الحضور المميز لكل الأعمار رجالا ونساء من جميع شرائح المجتمع.

للمتابعة: اضغط هنا
body_en:
His Eminence the learned Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew, president of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars, delivered a series of lectures in the city of Zouerate on 17 October 2011, at the invitation of the Future Association for Daʿwah, Culture and Education.

The first lecture was given at the premises of the women's maḥẓarah in Zouerate at nine in the morning, under the title "Reflections on Sūrat al-Ḥujurāt".

At five in the evening the Sheikh, may God preserve him, gave the second lecture at the premises of the Zouerate cinema, entitled "Islam is responsibility and character", organised in cooperation between the Future Association for Daʿwah, Culture and Education and the Bina' Zemmour Association.

His Eminence also gave the third and last lecture at the al-Ridwan Mosque in the city centre after the sunset prayer, entitled "Concepts that must be corrected" (the concept of worship; of religiosity; of stewardship on the earth).

This daʿwah activity, called for and organised by the Future Association for Daʿwah, Culture and Education, was attended by a large crowd of the young people of the city of Zouerate, besides a notable attendance of all ages, men and women, from every section of society.

flags.context: the title of the third lecture
options: Concepts that must be corrected
Concepts in need of correction
Concepts it is obligatory to correct
flags.note: يجب here is ordinary Arabic 'must' inside a lecture title, not the technical wājib of the five-rulings table: its subject is a set of concepts, not an act of a legally responsible person, so the table does not apply and option 3 would invent a ruling out of a title. Recorded because يجب is exactly the word the style guide warns about, and because the lecture's content — which is not in this record — may well have contained real rulings.

flags.context: the venue of the first lecture
options: the women's maḥẓarah
the women's mahdara
the women's traditional seminary
flags.note: Same term as in record 756 and it needs the same fixed corpus rendering, decided centrally. Note that this is a women's maḥẓarah, which is worth preserving exactly: the record shows the Sheikh lecturing at a women's teaching institution and to a mixed audience, and a rendering that flattens المحظرة into 'seminary' loses what kind of institution it is.

flags.context: co-organiser of the second lecture
options: the Bina' Zemmour Association
the Zemmour Development Association
the Zemmour Construction Association
flags.note: بناء is 'building' in both the literal and the figurative sense, and the association's own English name is not known from the record. Zemmour is the Mauritanian wilaya of Tiris Zemmour, in which Zouerate lies. The transliterated form is used rather than a guessed translation.

flags.context: the three concepts named in the third lecture's subtitle
options: worship; religiosity; stewardship on the earth
worship; religious practice; vicegerency on earth
worship; piety; succession in the earth
flags.note: الاستخلاف في الأرض is the Qur'anic idea that mankind is set on the earth as God's steward or successor (Qur'an 2:30, 6:165, and elsewhere). English has no settled rendering: 'vicegerency' is the term in the Islamic-studies literature but is opaque outside it; 'stewardship' is clear but carries an environmental colouring the Arabic does not have. The record gives the title only, with no content, so the lecture itself cannot settle the sense.

translator_notes: A short news report giving the titles, times and venues of three lectures and no content from any of them. Nothing in it could be mistaken for a ruling.
The CMS timestamp is a bulk-upload date and is not evidence of when the report was written. The body dates the lectures to 17 October 2011.
ازويرات is the mining city in northern Mauritania written Zouerate (also Zouérat, Zouérate) in Latin script; the commonest form is used.

The closing 'to follow, click here' is the site's navigation furniture; preserved in body_ar, recorded in source_download_link, omitted from body_en. The link is to a single item, while the record describes three lectures; which of the three it carries is not stated.

title_ar: الشيخ الددو رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء يُحاضر في موضوع "الاختلاف.. سنة كونية" بدولة قطر
title_en: Sheikh al-Dedew, President of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars, Lectures in Qatar on "Disagreement — a Pattern Established in Creation"
body_ar:
استضاف معهد الدعوة والعلوم الإسلامية بالدوحة مساء أمس الاثنين 05 دجنبر 2012 فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن ولد الددو رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء لإلقاء دورة علمية في مسجد عمر بن الخطاب بالدوحة بعنوان: "فقه الاختلاف .. سنة كونية".

هذا وصرح الدكتور محمد بن صلاح إبراهيم رئيس معهد الدعوة والعلوم الإسلامية في الافتتاح بأن "هذه الدورة مهمة حيث إنها تتطرق لموضوع مهم نحتاجه جميعا ألا وهو الاختلاف وما يترتب عليه .. خاصة أنه يعرفنا على اختلاف العلماء وكيف كان؟ وطريقتهم في التعامل مع المخالف.

وتتطرق هذه الدورة لعدة محاور تدور حول:

1- الاختلاف وأنواعه.

2- أنواع المخالفين والتعامل معهم.

هذا وقدم الشيخ قبل الدورة ثلاث محاضرات إحداهما عن السحر؛ الوقاية والعلاج، والثانية عن العين حق وما ورد في ذلك من الأحاديث، والثالثة عن : "كيف تعالج نفسك بالرقية الشرعية.

وسينشر الموقع بإذن الله لاحقا محاضرات تلك الدورة مع تلخيصها لتقريبها من الطلاب والمهتمين.

ولمتابعة الحلقة الأولى الرجاء الضغط هنا:
body_en:
The Institute of Daʿwah and Islamic Sciences in Doha hosted His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew, president of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars, on the evening of yesterday, Monday 05 December 2012, to give a course of instruction at the Mosque of ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab in Doha, entitled "The jurisprudence of disagreement — a pattern established in creation (sunnah kawniyyah)".

Dr Muhammad ibn Salah Ibrahim, president of the Institute of Daʿwah and Islamic Sciences, stated at the opening that "this course is important, in that it takes up an important subject that we all have need of — namely disagreement and what follows from it — especially as it acquaints us with the disagreement of the scholars and how it was, and with their way of dealing with one who differs from them.

This course takes up several strands, turning on:

1. Disagreement and its kinds.

2. The kinds of those who differ, and dealing with them.

Before the course the Sheikh gave three lectures: one of them on sorcery — prevention and treatment; the second on "the evil eye is real" and what has come down on that in the prophetic reports; and the third on: "How to treat yourself by means of the ruqyah sanctioned by the Sharia.

The site will publish the lectures of that course later, God willing, together with a summary of them, to bring them within reach of students and of those interested.

flags.context: the date of the course's opening
options: reproduce the year exactly as given and flag it
correct to 2011
drop the year
flags.note: The year in the body cannot be right. The record is timestamped Tuesday 6 December 2011 and says the course opened 'yesterday, Monday'; 5 December 2011 was indeed a Monday, whereas 5 December 2012 was a Wednesday. The body's 2012 is a typing error for 2011. Reproduced exactly as the source gives it and not corrected, per style guide section 11. Note the knock-on risk: a date-sorting pass over the corpus that trusts body text rather than the CMS field would file this record a year late.

flags.context: the course title
options: a pattern established in creation (sunnah kawniyyah)
a law of the universe
a divine norm in creation
flags.note: سنة here is not the sunnah of the Prophet and must not be allowed to read as it: a sunnah kawniyyah is a regularity God has established in the created order, of the kind the Qur'an calls sunnat Allāh. The English needs to make that unmistakable, since 'sunnah' standing alone in an English title would be read the other way. The term is not in the glossary and recurs in the corpus.

flags.context: the course title in the body, against the title of the record
options: render both forms as each stands
reconcile them
flags.note: The record's own headline gives the title as "الاختلاف.. سنة كونية" while the body gives it as "فقه الاختلاف .. سنة كونية". Both are rendered as they stand, in title_en and in body_en respectively. The two are not the same title — the jurisprudence of disagreement is a named discipline, disagreement as such is not — and which the Sheikh used cannot be determined here.

flags.arabic: ثلاث محاضرات إحداهما عن السحر؛ الوقاية والعلاج … والثالثة عن : "كيف تعالج نفسك بالرقية الشرعية.
flags.context: the three lectures given before the course
options: render the titles as given, with no content and no gloss
add an editorial note on the subject matter
flags.note: These are lecture titles only; the record gives no content from any of the three and states no ruling and no instruction. Raised here without setting editorial_review, because there is nothing in this record to review: it neither advises a course of treatment nor makes a claim about one. The flag is entered so that whoever handles the lectures themselves, if they enter the corpus, knows that material presented as self-treatment may need a different editorial judgement from a news announcement of it. Note also that إحداهما is the dual ('one of the two') where three are listed — a slip in the source, not corrected.

flags.arabic: بأن "هذه الدورة مهمة … وطريقتهم في التعامل مع المخالف.
flags.context: the quotation from the Institute's president
options: follow the source: open the quotation and close it where the source's sentence ends
leave the quotation unclosed in the English too
flags.note: The source opens this quotation and never closes it, so where the speaker's own words end is not marked — the same defect as in record 756 in this span. The English follows the opening mark and ends where the source's sentence ends. Recorded rather than repaired.

translator_notes: A news report on the opening of a teaching course. It gives the course's two strands as headings and no content under either, so no ruling appears in the record.

The CMS timestamp is a bulk-upload date and is not evidence of when the report was written. The body's own date is wrong by a year — see the flag — so neither field is reliable on its own; the day and month in the body, read against the timestamp, are the best evidence.

المخالف is rendered 'one who differs' rather than 'the opponent' or 'the dissenter'. In this literature it means a scholar who holds a different view within the bounds of legitimate disagreement, and the adversarial English words would prejudge the second strand's subject.
الرقية الشرعية is rendered 'the ruqyah sanctioned by the Sharia' — recitation over a person for healing, of the kind the Sharia permits, as against the kinds it does not. It is not in the glossary.
العين حق is a prophetic report ('the evil eye is real') used here as a lecture title; no collection and no grading is given in the source and none is supplied.
The closing 'to follow the first session please click here' is the site's navigation furniture; preserved in body_ar, recorded in source_download_link, omitted from body_en.

title_ar: فضيلة الشيخ الددو يلتقي في القاهرة بشيخ الأزهر الشريف
title_en: His Eminence Sheikh al-Dedew Meets the Shaykh of al-Azhar in Cairo
body_ar:
يقوم فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن ولد الددو رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء بزيارة لجمهورية مصر أدى خلالها اليوم الأحد 16 محرم 1433 الموافق: 11/12/2011 زيارة تعاون وأخوة لمقر الأزهر الشريف بالعاصمة المصرية القاهرة، حيث استقبل فضيلته من طرف سماحة الدكتور أحمد الطيب شيخ الأزهر الشريف بمقر مشيخة الأزهر، بحضور فضيلة الدكتور صفوت حجازي الأمين العام لرابطة علماء أهل السنة.

وخلال اللقاء تحدث فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن ولد الددو عن تجربة مركز تكوين العلماء والدور العلمي الذي يضطلع به لتكوين علماء يجمعون بين موسوعية خريجي المحاظر وتخصص المتخرجين وفق المناهج المعاصرة، وتطرق الشيخ باسمه رئيس جامعة عبد الله بن ياسين للحديث عن هذه الجامعة الحديثة، مؤكدا على أنها تعمل من أجل توفير مناخ أكاديمي يغطي عددا من التخصصات الهامة والمتنوعة، وفق منظومة تعليمية متكاملة.

وقد رحب سماحة شيخ الأزهر بهذا النشاط العلمي الهادف إلى إشاعة العلم الشرعي على مذهب أهل السنة والجماعة، والذي ظل يميز بلاد شنقيط الواقعة في أقصى الغرب الإسلامى، وأكد فضيلته على استعداد الأزهر للتعاون العلمي مع مؤسستي مركز تكوين العلماء وجامعة عبد الله بن ياسين بنواكشوط ونظائرهما في موريتانيا وغيرها من دول الغرب الإسلامي الشقيق.
body_en:
His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew, president of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars, is making a visit to the Republic of Egypt, in the course of which he paid today, Sunday 16 Muharram 1433, corresponding to 11/12/2011, a visit of cooperation and brotherhood to the seat of al-Azhar in the Egyptian capital, Cairo, where His Eminence was received by His Eminence Dr Ahmad al-Tayyib, Shaykh of al-Azhar, at the headquarters of the Mashyakhah of al-Azhar, in the presence of His Eminence Dr Safwat Hijazi, secretary general of the League of Scholars of the People of the Sunnah.

During the meeting His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew spoke about the experience of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars and the scholarly role it undertakes in forming scholars who combine the encyclopaedic breadth of the graduates of the maḥāẓir with the specialisation of those who graduate under contemporary curricula. The Sheikh went on, in his name as president of the ʿAbd Allah ibn Yasin University, to speak about that new university, affirming that it works to provide an academic environment covering a number of important and varied specialisms, within an integrated educational system.

His Eminence the Shaykh of al-Azhar welcomed this scholarly activity, aimed at spreading the knowledge of the Sharia according to the school of the People of the Sunnah and the Community, which has continued to distinguish the land of Shinqit, situated in the far west of the Islamic world. His Eminence affirmed al-Azhar's readiness for scholarly cooperation with the two institutions — the Centre for the Formation of Scholars and the ʿAbd Allah ibn Yasin University in Nouakchott — and with their counterparts in Mauritania and in the other countries of the brotherly Islamic west.

flags.arabic: وتطرق الشيخ باسمه رئيس جامعة عبد الله بن ياسين للحديث
flags.context: the Sheikh's second capacity at the meeting
options: render literally ('in his name as president'), as done here
read as بصفته ('in his capacity as') and render accordingly
leave the phrase out
flags.note: باسمه does not construe here; the phrase the sense requires is بصفته, 'in his capacity as'. The literal rendering is kept so that the oddity is visible in the English rather than smoothed away, per style guide section 11. Either reading gives the same substantive fact — that he holds the presidency of the university as well as of the Centre — so nothing material turns on it.

flags.context: what the Centre's graduates are meant to combine
options: the encyclopaedic breadth of the graduates of the maḥāẓir
the breadth of the mahdara graduates
the polymathy of the traditional seminarians
flags.note: المحاظر is the plural of محظرة, the same institution as in records 756 and 768 in this span, and the corpus needs one fixed rendering for both singular and plural, decided centrally. موسوعية is the quality of covering the whole field rather than a specialism, which is exactly the contrast the sentence draws; 'encyclopaedic breadth' keeps the contrast, 'polymathy' shifts it onto the person.

flags.arabic: بحضور فضيلة الدكتور صفوت حجازي الأمين العام لرابطة علماء أهل السنة
flags.context: the third person present at the meeting
options: name him exactly as the source does, with his stated office
name him with an editorial note
omit
flags.note: The record places a named third party at the meeting and gives the office he then held. The name is reproduced exactly as the source gives it and no characterisation is added, which is the correct treatment. Raised so that a reviewer is aware the record names him: what has happened to this figure in Egypt since 2011 is a matter of public record and may bear on how the record reads in English fifteen years on, though nothing in the record itself says anything about him beyond his presence and his title.

flags.context: the closing phrase of the record
options: the countries of the brotherly Islamic west
the sister countries of the Islamic Maghreb
the fraternal states of the Islamic west
flags.note: الغرب الإسلامي is the classical designation for the Maghreb and the lands beyond it, and the record has already used بلاد شنقيط … في أقصى الغرب الإسلامي in the same sentence, so the two should agree in the English. الشقيق is the standard diplomatic epithet between Arab states and is kept rather than dropped, since dropping it would lose the register of the sentence.

translator_notes: A short news report of an official visit. Nothing in it is quoted, no ruling is stated, and the five-rulings mapping of style guide section 3 is not engaged.

The CMS timestamp is a bulk-upload date and is not evidence of when the report was written. Here the two hijri and Gregorian dates in the body agree with each other and with the timestamp — 16 Muharram 1433 was indeed Sunday 11 December 2011 — which is unusual in this span and worth noting.

مذهب أهل السنة والجماعة is rendered 'the school of the People of the Sunnah and the Community'. مذهب here is not one of the four legal schools but the broader Sunni position, and the English should not be allowed to suggest a madhhab in the narrow sense.

مشيخة الأزهر is kept as 'the Mashyakhah of al-Azhar' — the office of the Shaykh of al-Azhar — rather than translated, since 'the Sheikhdom of al-Azhar' would mislead and 'the office of the Shaykh of al-Azhar' is already used in the same sentence for the person.

title_ar: فضيلة الشيخ يقوم بزيارات تعزية لأسر علماء وأعيان في الداخل
title_en: His Eminence the Sheikh Makes Condolence Visits to the Families of Scholars and Notables in the Interior
body_ar:
قدم فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن ولد الددو يومي الأحد والاثنين 23-24 محرم 1433 الموافق 18-19/12/2011 واجب العزاء لعدد من الأسر في الداخل إثر وفاة عدة علماء أجلاء وأعيان محليين نهاية الأسبوع الماضي.

وقد زار فضيلته على وجه الخصوص أسرة أهل الشيخ سيديا في بتلميت لتعزيتها في وفاة المغفور له الخليفة العام لأسرة أهل الشيخ سيديا فضيلة الشيخ عبد الرحمن بن محمد بن سيد المختار بن الشيخ سيديا.

كما زار فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن ولد الددو أيضا أسرة أهل الشيخ القاضي بقرية بوطلحايه، وقدم تعازيه في وفاة المرحوم الخليفة العام لأهل الشيخ القاضي فضيلة الشيخ المصطفى بن الشيخ القاضي.

وأدى فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن ولد الددو زيارة أخرى لأسرة أهل ابات لتعزيتها في وفاة العالم الرباني العلامة محمد ابات ولد محمد ولد أحمد ول ابات شيخ محظرة أم النوار في لعصابه.

وقام فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن ولد الددو بزيارة أيضا لأسرة أهل أحمد زيدان في كامور لتعزيتها في وفاة فضيلة الشيخ محمد يحي ولد باب ولد أحمد زيدان رحمه الله تعالى.

وقد التقى فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن ولد الددو خلال رحلته هذه أعيان بلديتي كامور والغايره، وقدم على هامش تلك اللقاءات بعض التوجيهات والنصائح للتجمعات النسوية في المنطقتين بالتعاون مع الجمعية النسوية.

وقد رافق الشيخ في هذه الرحلة عدد من المشايخ منهم على وجه الخصوص: عبد الرحمن الداخل، وسيدي مولود ولد جاكير، وامادي ولد سيد المختار، ومحمد الحسن ولد امود، وشيخنا ولد سيدي الحاج.
body_en:
On Sunday and Monday, 23–24 Muharram 1433, corresponding to 18–19/12/2011, His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew paid the duty of condolence to a number of families in the interior, following the deaths of several eminent scholars and local notables at the end of last week.

His Eminence visited in particular the family of Ahl al-Shaykh Sidiya in Boutilimit, to offer its members condolences on the death of the late general khalifah of the family of Ahl al-Shaykh Sidiya, His Eminence Sheikh ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad ibn Sid al-Mukhtar ibn al-Shaykh Sidiya.

His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew also visited the family of Ahl al-Shaykh al-Qadi in the village of Boutalhaya, and offered his condolences on the death of the late general khalifah of Ahl al-Shaykh al-Qadi, His Eminence Sheikh al-Mustafa ibn al-Shaykh al-Qadi.

His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew made a further visit to the family of Ahl Abat, to offer its members condolences on the death of the godly scholar, the learned Muhammad Abat Ould Muhammad Ould Ahmad Wal Abat, sheikh of the maḥẓarah of Umm al-Nuwar in Assaba.

His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew also made a visit to the family of Ahl Ahmad Zaydan in Kamour, to offer its members condolences on the death of His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad Yahya Ould Bab Ould Ahmad Zaydan, may God Almighty have mercy on him.

During this journey His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew met the notables of the communes of Kamour and al-Ghayrah, and on the margins of those meetings gave some directions and counsel to the women's gatherings in the two areas, in cooperation with the women's association.

A number of sheikhs accompanied the Sheikh on this journey, among them in particular: ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Dakhil; Sidi Mawlud Ould Jakir; Amadi Ould Sid al-Mukhtar; Muhammad al-Hasan Ould Amud; and Shaykhna Ould Sidi al-Hajj.

flags.arabic: أسرة أهل الشيخ سيديا في بتلميت / أهل الشيخ القاضي بقرية بوطلحايه / أهل ابات … في لعصابه / أهل أحمد زيدان في كامور / بلديتي كامور والغايره
flags.context: the families and places named throughout the record
options: romanise by the commonest Mauritanian Latin-script forms, as done here
transliterate the Arabic strictly with diacritics
give both
flags.note: Mauritanian place and family names have established Latin-script forms that do not follow from the Arabic: بتلميت is Boutilimit, لعصابه is the wilaya of Assaba, كامور is Kamour. Others have no settled form at all — بوطلحايه and الغايره are rendered here as Boutalhaya and al-Ghayrah on the strength of the Arabic alone. The record is almost entirely proper names, so this is the main translation decision in it and a reviewer with local knowledge should go through the list.

flags.arabic: الخليفة العام لأسرة أهل الشيخ سيديا
flags.context: the office held by the two men whose deaths occasioned the visits
options: the general khalifah
the head of the family (khalīfah)
the general successor
flags.note: خليفة عام here is the head of a Mauritanian scholarly house, the successor to its founding sheikh, not a caliph and not an administrative deputy. 'Caliph' would be badly misleading in English; 'general khalifah' keeps the title untranslated but visible as a title; option 2 explains it at the cost of the word. Not in the glossary, and it recurs wherever a Mauritanian scholarly family is reported on.

flags.arabic: محمد ابات ولد محمد ولد أحمد ول ابات
flags.context: the name of the sheikh of the maḥẓarah of Umm al-Nuwar
options: reproduce the sequence exactly as given, including ول
regularise ول to ولد
flags.note: The third link of the name is written ول rather than ولد, which is either a dialect spelling or a typing error in the CMS. It is reproduced exactly as given in body_ar and rendered 'Wal' in the English so that the inconsistency inside a single name remains visible. Style guide section 11 forbids silent repair.

flags.arabic: وقدم … بعض التوجيهات والنصائح للتجمعات النسوية في المنطقتين
flags.context: the meetings with women's gatherings
options: gave some directions and counsel
gave some guidance and advice
issued some instructions and recommendations
flags.note: توجيهات and نصائح are not ruling words and must not be allowed to sound like them. Option 3 in particular would make 'recommendations' out of نصائح, and 'recommended' is the fixed rendering of mandūb in the five-rulings table; a reader would be entitled to think a ruling had been given. Nothing of what was said survives in the record.

translator_notes: A short news report of condolence visits. No ruling is stated anywhere in it and the five-rulings mapping of style guide section 3 is not engaged. واجب in the first sentence is part of the idiom أدى واجب العزاء, 'paid the duty of condolence', and is a social duty in ordinary Arabic, not the technical wājib of the table.
The CMS timestamp is a bulk-upload date and is not evidence of when the report was written. The body dates the visits to 18–19 December 2011, and the hijri and Gregorian dates agree with each other.
المغفور له and المرحوم are the standard Arabic formulae for the recently dead; both are rendered 'the late', which flattens a small difference between them that English has no means of carrying.
شيخنا ولد سيدي الحاج here and شيخنا ولد سيد الحاج in record 756 of this span appear to be the same person, spelled differently in the two records. Neither has been altered.
محظرة أم النوار is the same institution type as in records 756, 768 and 773 in this span, and takes whatever fixed rendering the corpus settles on for محظرة.

title_ar: الشيخ الددو يشرف على افتتاح قسم الاقتصاد الإسلامي بجامعة ابن ياسين
title_en: Sheikh al-Dedew Presides over the Opening of the Islamic Economics Department at Ibn Yasin University
body_ar:
احتضن مقر جامعة عبد الله بن ياسين بنواكشوط مساء اليوم الثلاثاء 25 محرم 1433 الموافق: 20/12/2011 حفلا رسميا لإطلاق قسم الاقتصاد الإسلامي بالجامعة.

وقد أشرف رئيس الجامعة فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن ولد الددو على افتتاح القسم بحضور الطاقم الإداري والعلمي بالجامعة وجمهور من طلبتها ومهتمين بالشأن العلمي، وقد افتتح الحفل من طرف منسق قسم الاقتصاد الإسلامي المستحدث الدكتور محمد ولد سيد أوبك مرحبا بالرئيس وطاقم الجامعة وبالجمهور الحاضر، مذكرا بأهمية إطلاق الجامعة هذا القسم الذي يفتتح لأول مرة في البلاد، ويبدأ باستقبال الطلبة حملة كل من الباكلوريا والليصانص، حيث يقدم لهم تكوينا أكاديميا حرصت الجامعة على أن يكون خاضعا للمقاييس العلمية المعتمدة في هذا المجال.

ثم أحيلت الكلمة إلى رئيس الجامعة فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن ولد الددو الذي نوه بافتتاح الجامعة لقسمها الجديد الذي يكمل مختلف التكوينات التي تجري فيها الدراسة داخل الجامعة، وهنأ الطاقم الإداري على تذليله كل الصعاب في سبيل فتح قسم يعنى بالبحث في مجال حيوي كالاقتصاد الإسلامي، وقدم الشيخ خلال كلمته الرسمية باسم الجامعة شكره للحكومة والسلطات العمومية على تعاونها مع الجامعة، آملا أن يتعزز هذا التعاون حتى تحقق الجامعة طموحاتها في تعليم أكاديمي عصري متكامل، متطلعا لأن تقدم الجامعة من خلال قسم الاقتصاد الإسلامي الاستشارات العلمية التي تحتاجها البنوك الإسلامية العاملة في البلد، مما يساهم في حل بعض الإشكالات المطروحة للعاملين في مجال الصيرفة الإسلامية في مختلف دول العالم.

بدوره تناول الحديث نائب رئيس الجامعة الدكتور محمد سالم ولد الخو مرحبا بالحضور وشاكرا فضيلة الشيخ على الاهتمام الذي يوليه للتحصيل العلمي من خلال افتتاحه لهذا القسم اليوم، كما شكر الدكاترة على التعاون الذي ما فتئوا يقدموه من أجل تحقيق رسالة جامعة ابن ياسين، والجهود العلمية والبحثية التي يقومون بها لتطوير أداء الجامعة والرفع من مستوى خريجيها في مختلف الأقسام والتخصصات.

وفي الأخير فتح الباب للجمهور؛ حيث تداعى إلى المنصة عدد من الدكاترة المدرسين بالجامعة، معبرين عن شكرهم للجامعة على افتتاح هذا القسم، بدورهم أكد المتدخلون من الطلبة على أهمية هذا القسم؛ مسجلين أن الجامعة حازت قصب السبق بافتتاحها هذا القسم المعني بالاقتصاد الإسلامي.

لمتابعة الكلمة الافتتاحية اضغط هنا:
body_en:
The premises of ʿAbd Allah ibn Yasin University in Nouakchott hosted, on the evening of today, Tuesday 25 Muharram 1433, corresponding to 20/12/2011, an official ceremony for the launch of the university's Islamic economics department.

The university's president, His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew, presided over the opening of the department, in the presence of the university's administrative and academic staff and an audience of its students and of those interested in scholarly affairs. The ceremony was opened by the coordinator of the newly created Islamic economics department, Dr Muhammad Ould Sid Oubek, who welcomed the president, the university's staff and the audience present, recalling the importance of the university's launching this department, which is being opened for the first time in the country and which begins by receiving students holding the baccalaureate and the licence, offering them an academic training which the university has been careful to make conform to the scholarly standards adopted in this field.

The floor then passed to the university's president, His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew, who drew attention to the university's opening of its new department, which completes the various courses of training studied within the university, and congratulated the administrative staff on smoothing away every difficulty in the way of opening a department concerned with research in a field as vital as Islamic economics. In his formal address on behalf of the university the Sheikh offered his thanks to the government and the public authorities for their cooperation with the university, expressing the hope that this cooperation would be strengthened so that the university might realise its ambitions for a complete modern academic education, and looking forward to the university's providing, through the Islamic economics department, the scholarly consultancy needed by the Islamic banks operating in the country — thereby contributing to the resolution of some of the problems raised for those working in the field of Islamic banking in the various countries of the world.

In turn the university's vice-president, Dr Muhammad Salim Ould al-Khu, took the floor, welcoming those present and thanking His Eminence the Sheikh for the attention he gives to scholarly attainment through his opening of this department today. He also thanked the doctors for the cooperation they have never ceased to give towards realising the mission of Ibn Yasin University, and for the scholarly and research efforts they make to develop the university's performance and to raise the level of its graduates in its various departments and specialisms.

Finally the floor was opened to the audience, and a number of the doctors teaching at the university came forward to the platform, expressing their thanks to the university for opening this department. In their turn the students who spoke affirmed the importance of this department, recording that the university had taken the lead in opening this department concerned with Islamic economics.

flags.arabic: متطلعا لأن تقدم الجامعة من خلال قسم الاقتصاد الإسلامي الاستشارات العلمية التي تحتاجها البنوك الإسلامية العاملة في البلد
flags.context: the Sheikh's hope for the new department
options: render as a hope for the department, as the Arabic has it
render as an undertaking that the department will advise the banks
flags.note: متطلعا is 'looking forward to', a hope expressed in a speech, not a commitment and certainly not an endorsement of any bank or product.
