body_ar: الشيخ الدّدو لقناة الجزيرة: {لا حرج في استخدام وسائل التقنية الحديثة فيما هو نافع للحاج ومعين له على اداء نسكه دون إسراف } الحمد لله والصلاة والسلام على نبينا محمد وعلى آله واصحابه أجمعين ، أما بعد فإن هذه الوسائل هي من نعم الله سبحانه وتعالى التي أنعم بها على عباده ؛فإذا صرفوها فيما يرضيه وما يقرب اليه كانت عونا على الطاعة ، ولا ينبغي الاسراف فيه وتجاوز الحد ، لكن لا حرج في استعمالها فيما هو نافع ومعين للحاج على اداء نسكه وفي تحديد اوقاته وفي تحديد السير وعلاماته وغير ذلك مما ينظم شؤون الحياة ؛ فهي امور يحتاج الناس اليها ومن نعمة الله ان أنعم بها في هذا الوقت الذي كثر فيه الناس وكثرت فيه وسائل الاتصال وكثرت فيه وسائل النقل واستطاع كثير من الناس الحج ؛ ففي اوقات مضت لم يكن هذا الكم من الناس يستطيع الوصول إلى المناسك والمشاعر ولا أداءها في وقت واحد ، فلذلك احتيج إلى هذه الوسائل في التواصل بين الحجيج ؛ففي السنوات الماضية كنا نشاهد ضياع كثير من الضعفة الذين ليس لهم من يرعاهم ، وبعضهم لا يؤدي نسكه أصلا فلا يقف بعرفة . واليوم بحمد الله اصبح من الممكن الوصول إلى كل انسان في مكانه الذي هو فيه ان استغل هذه الوسائل لذلك بالصوت والصورة. • كيف تستفيد الأمة من اجتماع كهذا ..أكثر من مليوني حاج في موسم مهيب؟الشيخ حفظه الله: الحج هو مؤتمر الأمة السنوي الكبيرُ الذي افترضه الله سبحانه وتعالى وجعله ركنا من أركان الإسلام يجتمع فيه قاصي المسلمين ودانِيهم ، ومشرقيُّهم ومغربيُّهم ، وعربيهم وعجميهم يلبسون زيا موحدا ويلهجون بذكر موحد ، ويسلكون هذه المسالك التي سلكها أنبياء الله من قبل وسلكها أبونا إبراهيم عليه السلام وأحياها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وقال: " خذوا عني مناسككم " فأثر الحج لذلك عظيم من عدة وجوه :- الوجه الأول : أنه يكفر سيئات الحاضرين ويغير حياتهم وسلوكهم فالأمة محتاجة إلى أن يكون فيها عدد من المغفور لهم ترجى دعواتهم وتستجاب ، وهي محتاجة إلى تغيير السلوك فهو بمثابة تغيير الدماء كما إذا أخذ الدم من الإنسان واعيد إليه من جديد بالتغذية - كما أن من فوائد الحج أن فيه اطلاعا على أحوال المسلمين في مشارق الأرض ومغاربها وهذا أمر تشاركون فيه انتم رجال الإعلام وفرسان الأقلام، ولكن ليس من رءا كمن سمع فنحن الآن نلتقي أناسا قدموا من بورما وناسا جاءوا من اليمن وناسا جاءوا من اماكن شتى كلها فيها جراح للمسلمين نابضة ، والمسلمون في مشارق الأرض ومغاربها مطالبون بالشعور بآلام إخوانهم فالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول:" المؤمن للمؤمن كالبنيان يشد بعضه بعضا وشبك بين أصابعه " ويقول صلى الله عليه وسلم:" مثل المؤمنين في توادهم وتراحمهم وتعاطفهم كمثل الجسد إذا اشتكى منه عضو تداعى له سائر الجسد بالحمى والسهر".. فلا يمكن أن يقع ذلك إلا بهذا التعارف في هذا المؤتمر ..وإذا رجعوا بإذن الله سيرجع كل واحد منهم بما رءا وسمع وينقله نقلا مباشرا ويؤدي ذلك إلى زيادة الأخوة بين المسلين وتقوية الترابط بينهم.
body_en:
Sheikh al-Dedew to Al Jazeera: "There is no objection to using modern technological means in what is of benefit to the pilgrim and assists him in performing his rite, without extravagance."

Praise be to God, and prayers and peace upon our Prophet Muhammad and upon his family and his Companions, all of them. To proceed:

These means are among the blessings of God, glorified and exalted, which He has bestowed upon His servants. If they turn them to what pleases Him and what brings them near to Him, they are a help towards obedience. There should be no extravagance in this and no overstepping of the limit; but there is no objection to using them in what is of benefit and assists the pilgrim in performing his rite, in fixing its times, in determining the route and its markers, and in other things by which the affairs of life are ordered. These are matters people need, and it is part of God's favour that He has bestowed them at this time — a time in which people have become many, the means of communication have become many, the means of transport have become many, and many people have become able to perform the hajj. In times past this number of people could not have reached the rites and the sacred sites, nor performed them all at one time; and for that reason these means became needed for communication among the pilgrims. In past years we used to see many of the weak, who have no one to look after them, going astray, and some of them not performing their rite at all, so that they would not stand at Arafat. Today, praise be to God, it has become possible to reach every person in the place where he is, if these means are used for that, by voice and by image.

• How is the community to benefit from a gathering such as this — more than two million pilgrims in an awe-inspiring season?

The Sheikh (may God preserve him): The hajj is the community's great annual conference, which God, glorified and exalted, made obligatory and made a pillar of Islam. In it the far and the near among the Muslims come together, their easterners and their westerners, their Arabs and their non-Arabs. They wear one dress and give voice to one remembrance, and they walk these paths that the prophets of God walked before them, that our father Abraham (peace be upon him) walked, and that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) revived, when he said: "Take from me your rites."

The effect of the hajj is therefore immense, in several respects.

The first respect: that it wipes away the misdeeds of those present and changes their lives and their conduct. The community needs to have within it a number of people who have been forgiven, whose supplications are hoped for and answered; and it needs a change of conduct. It is like a changing of the blood, as when blood is taken from a person and restored to him anew through nourishment.

— Another of the benefits of the hajj is that in it there is an acquaintance with the conditions of the Muslims in the east and the west of the earth. This is something you take part in, you men of the media and knights of the pen; but the one who has seen is not like the one who has heard. We are meeting now people who have come from Burma, people who have come from Yemen, people who have come from various places, in all of which there are throbbing wounds of the Muslims. The Muslims in the east and the west of the earth are required to feel the pains of their brothers, for the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) says: "The believer to the believer is like a building, one part of it supporting another" — and he interlaced his fingers. And he (peace and blessings be upon him) says: "The likeness of the believers in their mutual love, their mutual mercy and their mutual compassion is the likeness of the body: when one limb of it complains, the rest of the body answers it with fever and sleeplessness."

That cannot come about except through this mutual acquaintance at this conference. And when they return, God willing, each one of them will return with what he has seen and heard and will convey it directly, and that will lead to an increase of brotherhood among the Muslims and a strengthening of the bonds between them.

flags.arabic: {لا حرج في استخدام وسائل التقنية الحديثة … دون إسراف }
flags.context: the headline of the piece
options: a pull-quote from the interview, set off by the site in braces
a Qur'anic quotation
flags.note: SOURCE FORMATTING. The source encloses the headline pull-quote in curly braces, which in this corpus are reserved for Qur'anic text (style guide section 4). It is not scripture; it is the Sheikh's own sentence, which recurs almost verbatim in the body. The English puts it in ordinary quotation marks and the Arabic is preserved as the source has it. Whoever cleans the corpus globally should be aware that braces in body_ar are not a reliable marker of scripture.

flags.arabic: فهو بمثابة تغيير الدماء كما إذا أخذ الدم من الإنسان واعيد إليه من جديد بالتغذية
flags.context: the image for the change of conduct the hajj brings about
options: like a changing of the blood, as when blood is taken from a person and restored to him anew through nourishment
like a transfusion, where blood is drawn from a person and replaced after he has been fed
the image is compressed in transcription and its mechanism is unclear
flags.note: The simile is elliptical as transcribed and the third option may be the truth of it. Rendered as literally as English allows, without being turned into a modern transfusion, which the Arabic does not say.

flags.context: كنا نشاهد ضياع كثير من الضعفة الذين ليس لهم من يرعاهم
options: many of the weak going astray, that is, getting lost
many of the weak being lost, that is, perishing
many of the weak being neglected
flags.note: ضياع covers both getting lost and being lost. The following clause — that some did not perform the rite at all and so did not stand at Arafat — points to getting lost rather than dying, which is why the first reading is taken.

flags.context: زيادة الأخوة بين المسلين; ليس من رءا كمن سمع
options: read as المسلمين and رأى
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECTS (house rule 11): a dropped letter in المسلمين and a non-standard spelling of رأى, both twice over. Preserved unchanged in body_ar and translated normally. The record also carries a scattering of missing hamzas (اداء, اوقاته, امور, انتم) which are not individually flagged.

translator_notes: This is an interview with Al Jazeera, not a written fatwa, although the CMS files it under the written-fatwas category. Typed 'transcript'. Two questions and answers are published; whether the interview ran longer cannot be told from the record.
The two prophetic reports quoted at the end are given without narrator, collection or grading, as he gives them. None has been added.
The Sheikh's ruling on the use of technology is 'there is no objection' (لا حرج), qualified by 'without extravagance' — not one of the five rulings, and not rendered as 'permissible (mubāḥ)'.
The references to Burma and Yemen are his own and are translated as given, without gloss or context.

title_ar: الاعتبار بمرور الزمن .. و حرمة العلماء
title_en: Taking Heed from the Passing of Time, and the Inviolability of the Scholars
body_ar: تحدث فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو الشنقيطي ـ حفظه الله تعالى في خطبة الجمعة " 31-10-2014"الموافق "7-1-1436"عن السنة الهجرية الجديدة و فضل شهر الله المحرّم داعيا إلى أخذ العبرة من مرور الزمن و تعاقب الأيام و أذن ذلك يقرب الانسان إلى الدار الآخرة وهو ما يتطلب الاستعداد و المسارعة إلى الخيرات ، كما تحدث فضيلته عن فضل العلماء و مكانتهم بصفتهم ورثة الأنبياء و الموقعين عن الله داعيا في هذا السياق إلى توقير العلماء و توفير الحرمة لهم، واستنكر الشيخ الاعتداء على العلماء مبينا أنه منكر شنيع لا سيما إذا كان في بيوت الله فإن ذلك مما تتضاعف به الحرمة و تعظم به الهيبة.. وقد قال تعالى: " ذلك ومن يعظم حرمات الله فهو خير له عند ربه " .
body_en:
His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew al-Shinqiti (may God the Exalted preserve him) spoke in the Friday sermon of '31-10-2014', corresponding to '7-1-1436', about the new Hijri year and the merit of the month of God, Muharram, calling for a lesson to be drawn from the passing of time and the succession of days, and for the recognition that this brings a person nearer to the abode of the hereafter — which calls for preparation and for hastening towards good works.

His Eminence also spoke of the merit of the scholars and their standing, in that they are the heirs of the prophets and those who sign on God's behalf, calling in this connection for the scholars to be honoured and for their inviolability to be upheld.

The Sheikh condemned assaults upon scholars, explaining that this is a hideous wrong, and the more so if it takes place in the houses of God, for that is among the things by which the inviolability is doubled and the awe made greater. God the Exalted has said: {That — and whoever magnifies the sanctities of God, it is better for him with his Lord} (Sūrat al-Ḥajj 22:30).

flags.context: بصفتهم ورثة الأنبياء و الموقعين عن الله
options: those who sign on God's behalf
those who issue rulings in God's name
God's signatories
flags.note: The phrase is Ibn al-Qayyim's, from the title of Iʿlām al-Muwaqqiʿīn ʿan Rabb al-ʿĀlamīn, and figures the jurist as one who signs a document on behalf of the sovereign. The image must survive: rendering it 'those who issue rulings' loses the whole force of the expression, which is what makes the following call for their inviolability more than a courtesy. Not in the project glossary.

flags.arabic: واستنكر الشيخ الاعتداء على العلماء … لا سيما إذا كان في بيوت الله
flags.context: the second half of the sermon
options: a general condemnation
a response to a particular incident the record does not name
flags.note: The specificity — assault on scholars, in a mosque, in a Friday sermon at the end of October 2014 — reads as a response to a particular event, which the record does not identify. The English keeps it general because the Arabic is general. A reviewer or the Sheikh's office may be able to supply the occasion, which would change how the passage should be displayed.

flags.context: داعيا إلى أخذ العبرة من مرور الزمن و تعاقب الأيام و أذن ذلك يقرب الانسان إلى الدار الآخرة
options: read as وأنّ ذلك يقرب الإنسان
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT (house rule 11): أذن is not construable here and the sentence requires وأنّ. Preserved unchanged in body_ar and translated on the required reading.

translator_notes: A news report of a Friday sermon, not the sermon's text; typed 'news' for that reason.

حرمة is rendered 'inviolability' rather than 'sanctity' where it is used of the scholars, and 'sanctities' in the Qur'anic quotation (حرمات الله), which is the standard English there. The record plays on the two senses.

The source encloses the Qur'anic text in ordinary quotation marks and gives no reference; the English identifies it as Sūrat al-Ḥajj 22:30 and uses the corpus convention. Qur'anic renderings are interpretive and are not a substitute for the Arabic.

title_ar: فضيلة الشيخ يلقي كلمة علماء الأمة في مؤتمر منتدى كوالا لمبور
title_en: The Sheikh Delivers the Address of the Community's Scholars at the Kuala Lumpur Forum Conference
body_ar: ألقى فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن ولد الددو حفظه الله تعالى صباح اليوم الثلاثاء 11 -11-2014 كلمة علماء الأمة في افتتاح المؤتمر السنوي الأول لمنتدى كوالا لمبور حول : " الدولة المدنية رؤية إسلامية " المنظم تحت رئاسة رئيس ماليزيا السابق الدكتور مهاتير محمد وستكون للشيخ مشاركات أخرى ضمن برنامج المؤتمر الذي يستمر مدة ثلاثة أيام . ويشارك في المؤتمر المنعقد في العاصمة الماليزية كوالا لمبور عشرات من العلماء و المفكرين و قادة الرأي في الأمة الإسلامية.
body_en:
His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew (may God the Exalted preserve him) delivered this morning, Tuesday 11-11-2014, the address of the community's scholars at the opening of the first annual conference of the Kuala Lumpur Forum, on 'The Civil State: An Islamic Vision', held under the chairmanship of the former president of Malaysia, Dr Mahathir Mohamad. The Sheikh will make further contributions within the conference programme, which runs for three days.

Taking part in the conference, held in the Malaysian capital Kuala Lumpur, are dozens of scholars, thinkers and opinion leaders of the Muslim community.

flags.arabic: رئيس ماليزيا السابق الدكتور مهاتير محمد
flags.context: the description of the conference's chairman
options: reproduce the source's description
note that Malaysia has a prime minister, not a president
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT (house rule 11). Mahathir Mohamad was Prime Minister of Malaysia; the country's head of state is the Yang di-Pertuan Agong. رئيس is translated as the source has it and flagged rather than silently corrected.

flags.context: the conference title
options: The Civil State: An Islamic Vision
The Civic State: An Islamic Perspective
The Non-Theocratic State: An Islamic Vision
flags.note: الدولة المدنية is a loaded term in contemporary Arabic political debate, contrasted sometimes with a military state and sometimes with a religious one, and the two contrasts pull in opposite directions. 'The Civil State' is the standard English and is kept because it preserves the same ambiguity. The record gives nothing of the Sheikh's address, so his own use of the term is not recoverable here.

translator_notes: A conference notice. Nothing of the Sheikh's address is reported.

title_ar: الشيخ الددو يحاضر عن أمن الأمة و استقرارها بالجزائر
title_en: Sheikh al-Dedew Lectures in Algeria on the Community's Security and Stability
body_ar: حل فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو ـ حفظه الله تعالى مساء أمس الأحد 16 نوفمبر ضيفا على جامعة الأمير عبد القادر الجزائري بولاية قسنطينة شرق الجزائر وذلك للمشاركة في متلقى دولي تنظمه كلية أصول الدين بالجامعة أيام 17 – 18 - 19 نوفمبر الجاري حول " المرجعية الفقهية والعقدية في الجزائر: واقعها وآفاقها " ويتضمن برنامج فضيلة الشيخ في الملتقى محاضرة عن " دور فقهاء المالكية في الحفاظ على أمن الأمة واستقرارها " في صباح اليوم الثاني من الملتقى ( الثلاثاء 18 نوفمبر) إلى جانب محاضرتين لطلبة الدراسات العليا بالكلية الأولى مساء اليوم الأول للملتقى : ( الاثنين 17 نوفمبر) عن "منهج الاستنباط في النوازل المعاصرة" والثانية صباح اليوم الثالث الأربعاء 19 نوفمبر عن " أهمية المقاصد في الاجتهاد الفقهي" .
body_en:
His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew (may God the Exalted preserve him) arrived yesterday evening, Sunday 16 November, as a guest of the Emir Abdelkader University in the wilaya of Constantine in eastern Algeria, to take part in an international forum organised by the university's Faculty of the Fundamentals of Religion on 17, 18 and 19 November of this month, on 'Juristic and Creedal Authority in Algeria: Its Present State and Its Prospects'.

The Sheikh's programme at the forum includes a lecture on 'The Role of the Maliki Jurists in Preserving the Community's Security and Stability', on the morning of the forum's second day (Tuesday 18 November); alongside two lectures for the faculty's postgraduate students — the first on the evening of the forum's first day (Monday 17 November), on 'The Method of Derivation in Contemporary Novel Cases'; and the second on the morning of the third day, Wednesday 19 November, on 'The Importance of the Higher Objectives in Juristic Reasoning'.

flags.context: the title of the first postgraduate lecture: منهج الاستنباط في النوازل المعاصرة
options: contemporary novel cases
newly arising questions of our time
contemporary unprecedented cases (nawāzil)
flags.note: نازلة is a case with no direct precedent in the school's books, requiring fresh derivation; the nawāzil literature is a substantial Maliki and specifically Mauritanian genre. Not in the project glossary and a strong candidate for addition, since it recurs wherever the Sheikh addresses modern questions.

flags.context: منهج الاستنباط في النوازل المعاصرة
options: derivation
extraction of rulings from the sources
deriving a ruling
flags.note: Rendered 'derivation'. Compare record 388 elsewhere in the corpus, which renders istinbāṭ in the same sense. Not in the glossary; worth fixing corpus-wide.

flags.context: للمشاركة في متلقى دولي
options: read as ملتقى, 'forum'
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT (house rule 11): transposed letters; the word appears correctly as ملتقى twice later in the same record. Preserved unchanged in body_ar.

translator_notes: A programme notice. None of the three lectures is reported, only their titles.
المرجعية is rendered 'authority' in the sense of the body of reference a community defers to in law and creed — the subject of the forum being which such authority Algeria holds to.
جامعة الأمير عبد القادر الجزائري is given by the institution's usual English name, Emir Abdelkader University.

title_ar: فضيلة الشيخ يلقي الكلمة الافتتاحية في المؤتمر الدولي للوسطية‎
title_en: The Sheikh Delivers the Opening Address at the International Conference on Moderation
body_ar: ألقى فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو حفظه الله تعالى صباح اليوم 14 فبراير 2015 الكلمة الافتتاحية في المؤتمر الدولي للوسطية المنعقد في العاصمة السنغالية دكار و الذي ينظمه التجمع الإسلامي في السنغال ويستمر لمدة يومين بحضور مشاركين من معظم الدول الإسلامية في إفريقيا وممثلين عن منظمات إسلامية في أوروبا ؛ وقد تناول فضيلة الشيخ في كلمته أسس الوسطية و مظاهر تطبيقها مبينا " أن الدين يسر ولن يشاد أحد الدين إلا غلبه " .. كما تحدث الشيخ عن مجالات الوسطية وأجملها فيما يلي : العقيدة السلوك الفقه الأصالة والمعاصرة السياسة والحكم العلم والعمل العلاقات الدولية الاقتصاد و في ختام كلمته نبه فضيلة الشيخ أن هذه المجالات لم تكتمل فقد بقي منها ثلاثة ضاق عنها الوقت .
body_en:
His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew (may God the Exalted preserve him) delivered this morning, 14 February 2015, the opening address at the International Conference on Moderation, held in the Senegalese capital Dakar, organised by the Islamic Assembly in Senegal. It runs for two days, with participants from most of the Muslim countries of Africa and representatives of Islamic organisations in Europe.

In his address the Sheikh treated the foundations of moderation and the ways it is put into practice, setting out that "the religion is ease, and no one will contend with the religion but it will overcome him".

The Sheikh also spoke of the fields of moderation, summarising them as follows: creed; conduct; jurisprudence; authenticity and contemporaneity; politics and governance; knowledge and action; international relations; the economy.

At the close of his address the Sheikh pointed out that these fields were not complete: three of them remained, for which there had not been time.

flags.context: throughout: المؤتمر الدولي للوسطية, أسس الوسطية, مجالات الوسطية
options: moderation
the middle way
balance
flags.note: وسطية is the abstract noun from the Qur'anic أمة وسطا (Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:143) and carries 'centrality' and 'balance' as much as 'moderation', which in English has acquired a political colouring the Arabic does not have here. 'Moderation' is used as the established rendering. Not in the project glossary; it recurs across the corpus — record 882 in this slice is a whole lecture on it — and should be fixed corpus-wide.

flags.arabic: " أن الدين يسر ولن يشاد أحد الدين إلا غلبه "
flags.context: the text quoted in the address
options: no one will contend with the religion but it will overcome him
no one will overburden himself in religion but it will defeat him
no one will make the religion hard on himself but it will get the better of him
flags.note: A prophetic report; the Sheikh gives no narrator or collection and none has been added. شادّ is to strain against or vie with: the sense is that anyone who forces the religion beyond its ease is worsted by it. The three renderings differ in how much interpretation they carry; the first is the most literal.

flags.arabic: فقد بقي منها ثلاثة ضاق عنها الوقت
flags.context: the closing sentence
options: three of them remained, for which there had not been time
flags.note: The Sheikh himself says his enumeration is incomplete. That admission must be kept: eight fields are listed and he states that three more were not reached. The record does not name them, and they have not been supplied.

translator_notes: A news report. The list of eight fields is run together without punctuation in the Arabic; the English separates them with semicolons and adds nothing.

الأصالة والمعاصرة is a standing pair in modern Arabic thought, roughly rootedness in the tradition set against engagement with the present; rendered literally as 'authenticity and contemporaneity' rather than glossed.

title_ar: حدود العلاقة بين الخطيبين، وما يجوز في ذلك
title_en: The Limits of the Relationship between an Engaged Couple, and What Is Permissible in It
body_ar: · سؤال: حدود العلاقة ما بين الخطيبين، وما يجوز في ذلك؟. الجواب: الخطيب قبل أن يعقد له عقد النكاح لا تحل له الخلوة بمخطوبته ولا التلذذ بها بأي وجه من الوجوه سواء كان ذلك بكلامه أو النظر إليها، بل يجوز له فقط النظر إلى ما يرغب فيها برؤية الوجه والكفين وكذلك الكلام في غير ريبة وأن لا يكون بخلوة بل يكون بحضرة أمها أو أختها أو قريبتها أو أخيها فلا تحل لهما الخلوة ولا يحل لهما الكلام الذي فيه ريبة أو تمتع فذلك ممنوع.
body_en:
Question: The limits of the relationship between an engaged couple, and what is permissible in it?

Answer: Before the marriage contract (ʿaqd al-nikāḥ) has been concluded for him, a man who is engaged may not lawfully be alone in private (khalwah) with the woman to whom he is engaged, nor take pleasure in her in any way whatever, whether by speaking to her or by looking at her. What is permitted to him is only to look at what would incline him towards her, by seeing the face and the hands, and likewise to speak with her where there is nothing suspect in it, and not in private seclusion but in the presence of her mother, her sister, a female relative of hers, or her brother. Private seclusion is not lawful for the two of them, and speech in which there is anything suspect, or any taking of pleasure, is not lawful for them: that is not allowed (mamnūʿ).

flags.context: …ولا يحل لهما الكلام الذي فيه ريبة أو تمتع فذلك ممنوع.
options: not allowed (mamnūʿ)
forbidden (ḥarām)
impermissible
flags.note: ممنوع is not one of the five rulings and the Sheikh does not say ḥarām here. It is rendered 'not allowed' so that the English does not put the word 'forbidden' into his mouth, even though the preceding لا تحل ('is not lawful') is itself strong. A reviewer should decide whether the office wants ممنوع standardised across the corpus.

translator_notes: The answer states the restriction and its single exception (face and hands, speech without seclusion) and stops. Nothing has been added about engagement customs or modern communication, on which this text is silent.
ريبة is rendered 'anything suspect' rather than 'doubt': the sense is conduct that gives rise to suspicion, not intellectual uncertainty.

title_ar: حدود الربح
title_en: The Limits of Profit
body_ar: · سؤال: حدود الربح؟. · الجواب: ينظر فيه إلى المادة، فالله سبحانه وتعالى جعلنا خلفاء في الأرض وجعل أصول المنافع التي يحتاج إليها الناس هي ما ضمن الله لآدم في الجنة عندما قال "إن لك أن لا تجوع فهيا ولا تعرى وأنك لا تظمأ فيها ولا تضحى"، فهذه الأربع هي أصول المنافع، فإذا عمل الإنسان ما يحقق منفعة من هذه المنافع له أن يربح بدون حدود، كالذي يزرع فما قطعته من مزرعتك لك الحق أن تبيعه بما شئت أنت، وكذلك الذي يصنع للناس لباسا أو بناء أو ما يحتاجون إليه فله الحق أن يبيعه بما شاء ومثل ذلك الذي يستورد المصنع فيجلبه ويأتي به فهذا يبيع بما شاء وليس للدولة التسعير في حقه وليس للناس ذلك فقد أخرج الترمذي وغيره من حديث أنس بن مالك رضي الله عنه قال غلا السعر على عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بالمدينة فقلنا يارسول اله سعر لنا فقال "إن الله هو الحي القيوم الخالق الرازق وإنه لأرجو أن ألقى الله غدا وليس أحدا منكم يطالبني بمظلمة في نفس أو مال"، لكن ما جلبته الدولة لها الحق أن تسعره وما صنعته مصانع الدولة لها الحق أن تسعره ومثل ذلك أيضا إذا كان السوق منتظما على سعر معين فجاء من يريد رفع السعر على الناس أو يريد خفضه فللدولة أن تمنع ذلك لما فيه من الفوضى هذا هو المشهور، وقد ذهب ابن رشد الكبير من المالكية إلى أن الرفع ممنوع وأن الخفض مباح، وقد قال محمد عالي ولد عدود رحمة الله عليهما: بحبس ما اشتريته بالبلد *** للربح الاحتكار في البيع احددي وأنت منه مطلقاً في توسعه *** في سعة وامنعه في غير السعه لا فرق في ذلك بين القوت *** وغيره من سائر الوقوت وصانع وزارع من أرضه *** وجالب لقوته وعرضه باعوا أو امسكوا كما قد شاءوا *** وربنا يفعل ما يشاء أما الذي احتيج إلى ذات يده *** باع بسعر وقته في بلده وقل لمن أراد ترخيصاً بع *** كما يبيع الناس أو فارتفع كما رواه مالك عن عمرا *** لذاك قال بعض من تأخرا يمنع ترخيص القليل إن أضر *** بباعة الأسواق رفعاً للضرر وصاحب البيان سام بالغلط *** من لام من سامح في البيع وحط وقال بل مشكور أو مأجور *** وإنما يزجر من يجور.
body_en:
Question: The limits of profit?

Answer: One looks in this to the commodity. God, glorified and exalted, made us successors on the earth, and made the fundamental benefits that people need to be what God guaranteed to Adam in the Garden when He said: {Indeed, it is yours that you shall not go hungry therein, nor go unclothed, and that you shall not thirst therein, nor be exposed to the sun} (Sūrat Ṭā Hā 20:118–119). These four are the fundamental benefits.

So if a person does work that realises one of these benefits, he may profit without limit. Take one who farms: whatever you have cut from your field, you have the right to sell it for whatever you wish. Likewise one who makes clothing for people, or building, or whatever they need — he has the right to sell it for what he wishes. And so too with one who imports the manufactured article and brings it in and fetches it: this man sells for what he wishes, and the state has no right to fix a price (tasʿīr) in his regard, and neither do the people. For al-Tirmidhi and others narrated, from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik (may God be pleased with him), that he said: prices rose in the time of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) in Medina, and we said, "Messenger of God, fix prices for us," and he said: "God is the Living, the Self-Subsisting, the Creator, the Provider; and I hope indeed that I shall meet God tomorrow with none of you claiming against me a wrong done in life or in property."

But what the state has itself brought in, it has the right to set a price for; and what the state's own factories have made, it has the right to set a price for. And likewise, if the market is settled at a certain price and someone comes wanting to raise the price on people, or wanting to lower it, the state may prevent that, because of the disorder in it. This is the well-known position (al-mashhūr). Ibn Rushd the Elder, of the Malikis, held that raising the price is barred and that lowering it is permissible (mubāḥ).

Muhammad Ali Ould Addoud (may God's mercy be upon them both) said:

*Define hoarding (iḥtikār) in trade as the withholding of what you have bought in the town, for the sake of profit. Of that you are entirely free in a time of abundance: allow it in plenty and bar it when there is no plenty. In this there is no difference between staple food and anything else among the provisions. A manufacturer, a farmer working his own land, one who brings in his own food and his own goods — they may sell or hold back as they please, and our Lord does what He wills. But as for the man whose stock is needed, he sells at the price of his own time in his own town. And say to whoever means to undercut: sell as the people sell, or else withdraw — as Malik narrated it from ʿUmar. For that reason some of the later scholars said: the small trader is barred from undercutting if it harms the sellers in the markets, so as to lift the harm. And the author of al-Bayān charged with error anyone who blamed a man for being easy in a sale and coming down in his price, and said: rather he is thanked, or rewarded; it is only the man who acts unjustly who is to be restrained.*

flags.arabic: إن لك أن لا تجوع فهيا ولا تعرى وأنك لا تظمأ فيها ولا تضحى
flags.context: the Qur'anic quotation carrying the argument about the four fundamental benefits
options: read فهيا as فيها ('therein'), a transposition of letters
treat فهيا as an unknown word and leave the lacuna visible
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT (house rule 11): the CMS text has فهيا where Sūrat Ṭā Hā 20:118 has فيها. Preserved unchanged in body_ar; the English translates the Qur'anic text. Also note the source runs 20:118 and 20:119 together as one quotation, which is how the Sheikh cites it.

flags.context: فقلنا يارسول اله سعر لنا
options: read as يا رسول الله
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT (house rule 11): dropped letter in the divine name, an obvious CMS typing error. Preserved in body_ar, translated normally.

flags.arabic: محمد عالي ولد عدود رحمة الله عليهما
flags.context: the attribution of the verse
options: 'upon them both' refers to Muhammad Ali Ould Addoud and Ibn Rushd the Elder, named in the sentence before
'upon them both' refers to Muhammad Ali Ould Addoud and his father or another figure the Sheikh has in mind
the dual is a slip for the singular عليه
flags.note: The dual pronoun has no certain referent in the text as it stands. Muhammad Ali Ould Addoud (d. 2009) was a senior Mauritanian scholar and a relative of the Sheikh, and this is his versified fiqh. Left as a dual in English ('upon them both') rather than resolved. The Sheikh's office can say who is meant.

flags.context: لا فرق في ذلك بين القوت *** وغيره من سائر الوقوت
options: read as الأقوات, 'the provisions' or 'foodstuffs', which the sense and the rhyme both want
an otherwise unattested plural of وقت, 'times'
leave the word unresolved
flags.note: The line contrasts القوت (the staple) with everything else, so a plural of قوت is required; الوقوت is not a standard plural and may be a transmission error in the CMS or in the Sheikh's quotation from memory. Translated on the required sense and flagged rather than emended.

flags.arabic: يمنع ترخيص القليل إن أضر بباعة الأسواق
flags.context: the later scholars' qualification quoted in the verse
options: the small trader is barred from undercutting if it harms the market sellers
undercutting on a small quantity is barred if it harms the market sellers
a small reduction in price is barred if it harms the market sellers
flags.note: القليل can be the man with little stock, the small quantity, or the small reduction, and the three give materially different rules. The first is taken because the preceding lines are about classes of seller, but the Arabic does not settle it.

flags.context: وصاحب البيان سام بالغلط من لام من سامح في البيع وحط
options: Ibn Rushd the Elder, author of al-Bayān wa-l-Taḥṣīl
another author of a work called al-Bayān
flags.note: 'The author of al-Bayān' is almost certainly Ibn Rushd the Elder, whom the Sheikh has just named, and the position quoted in the verse is consistent with the one he attributes to him. The verse does not name him, so the identification is not made in the English text itself. Note that the verse's ruling and the position the Sheikh attributes to Ibn Rushd in his own prose are close but not identical: the prose says lowering is permissible, the verse says the later scholars bar undercutting where it harms other sellers and that the author of al-Bayān rejected blaming the man who lowers his price.

flags.context: أن الرفع ممنوع وأن الخفض مباح
options: barred / permissible (mubāḥ)
forbidden / permissible
prohibited / allowed
flags.note: مباح is rendered by its fixed English, 'permissible'. ممنوع is not one of the five rulings and is rendered 'barred' so that the pair is not read as ḥarām/mubāḥ. This is an attributed position, Ibn Rushd's, not the Sheikh's own.

translator_notes: The structure of the answer must survive: unrestricted profit for the producer, the farmer, the maker and the importer; a right of price-fixing for the state only over what it has itself imported or manufactured, and over a settled market against someone moving the price in either direction; then the well-known position (al-mashhūr), then Ibn Rushd's different position, then the versified statement. The position the Sheikh gives as al-mashhūr is the school's, not necessarily his own, and he does not say in this text which he adopts.

The verse (nazm) is rendered as prose in italics per the style guide, with no attempt at English rhyme. The Arabic is preserved line by line in body_ar, with the source's *** hemistich separators intact.
التسعير is the technical term for the authority fixing a price; rendered 'fixing a price' rather than 'price control', which imports a modern regulatory frame the Arabic does not carry.

خلفاء في الأرض rendered 'successors on the earth' rather than 'vicegerents', which overstates what the word does here — the argument only needs that the earth's goods were committed to human management.
Qur'anic renderings are interpretive and are not a substitute for the Arabic.

title_ar: حكم تشقير النساء لحواجبهن
title_en: The Ruling on Women Lightening Their Eyebrows
body_ar: · سؤال: تشقير النساء لحواجبهن؟ الجواب: بالنسبة لشعر الحواجب حرم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم نتفه وإزالته وسمى ذلك نمصا ولعن فاعلته فبين علة ذلك أنها تغيير خلق الله، فالتشقير هو الصبغ ليس إزالة فتعتبر المادة التي حصل بها التشقير فإن كانت هذه المادة مهلكة للشعر فتضعفه حتى يسقط في المستقبل فهو من النمص المحرم وإن كانت هذه المادة كالحناء لا تزيل الشعر وإنما تبقى عليه مدة فيبقى لونه مثل لون البشرة ثم تزول عنه فيرجع الشعر إلى أصله فلا حرج في ذلك، فالحناء ليست بتغيير خلق الله ولذلك أحلها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لكن حرم الوشم، والفرق بين الوشم والحناء أن الوشم ثابت لا يسقط ولا يتغير والحناء تتغير مع الوقت، فلذلك ما كان ثابتا فهو التغيير لخلق الله وما كان متغيرا فإنه غير تغيير لخلق الله.
body_en:
Question: Women lightening their eyebrows?

Answer: As regards the hair of the eyebrows, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) forbade plucking it and removing it, named that namṣ, and cursed the woman who does it; and he made plain the operative cause (ʿillah) of that, namely that it is an alteration of God's creation.

Now lightening (tashqīr) is dyeing, not removal. So one looks to the substance by which the lightening is brought about. If that substance destroys the hair, weakening it so that it falls out in time, then it belongs to the forbidden (ḥarām) namṣ. And if that substance is like henna — it does not remove the hair, but only stays on it for a period, so that its colour remains like the colour of the skin, and then passes off it and the hair returns to what it was — then there is no objection to that. Henna is not an alteration of God's creation, and for that reason the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) made it lawful, while he forbade tattooing.

The difference between the tattoo and henna is that the tattoo is fixed: it does not come off and does not change, whereas henna changes with time. So what is fixed is the alteration of God's creation, and what changes is not an alteration of God's creation.

flags.context: حرم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم نتفه وإزالته وسمى ذلك نمصا ولعن فاعلته
options: namṣ (plucking the eyebrows)
plucking or thinning of the facial hair
depilation of the eyebrows
flags.note: Left transliterated with a gloss because the whole argument turns on the term's extension: the Sheikh's ruling is that a lightening agent which kills the hair falls under namṣ, which only works if namṣ is read as removal of the hair rather than as plucking specifically. Not in the project glossary.

flags.context: the title and throughout
options: lightening (of the eyebrow hair)
bleaching
tinting
flags.note: The Sheikh glosses it himself as صبغ, dyeing. 'Lightening' is used because the practice is to bring the brow hair towards the skin tone, which is what he describes; 'bleaching' would import a chemical process the Arabic does not name. Not in the glossary.

translator_notes: The Sheikh does not give a single ruling for the practice: he makes it turn on the agent used, forbidden where it destroys the hair and unobjectionable where it behaves like henna. The English keeps that conditional structure and does not collapse it into a verdict.
لا حرج rendered 'there is no objection', not 'it is permissible (mubāḥ)': he does not use a term of the five rulings for the permitted case.

title_ar: فضيلة الشيخ يلقي كلمة ضيوف ملتقى النور الأول للقرآن وأهله بالجزائر
title_en: The Sheikh Delivers the Guests' Address at the First al-Nur Forum for the Qur'an and Its People in Algeria
body_ar: حل فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو حفظه الله تعالى رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء بموريتانيا يوم الأحد ضيفا على وزارة الشؤون الدينية والأوقاف بالجزائر للمشاركة في ملتقى النور الأول للقرآن وأهله الذي تنظمه مديرية الشؤون الدينية والأوقاف لولاية الجزائر أيام 24 و 25 و 26 جمادى الثانية الموافق 14 و 15 و 16 إبريل ويتناول الملتقى موضوع :المناهج والدراسات الحديثة في تحفيظ وتعليم القرآن الكريم . وقد ألقى فضيلة الشيخ ـ اليوم الثلاثاء 14 ابريل 2015م ـ كلمة الضيوف في افتتاح الملتقى كما تم تكريمه في الحفل نفسه من طرف وزير الشؤون الدينية ووالي ولاية الجزائر العاصمة . وستكون للشيخ مشاركات في بقية أيام الملتقى منها كلمة بعنوان : تعليم القرآن الكريم دراسة تأصيلية مساء الثلاثاء هذا بالإضافة إلى محاضرة يوم غد الأربعاء بعنوان : القراءة الجماعية للقرآن الكريم دراسة تأصيلية. من جهة ثانية أعدت الوزارة برنامجا في مساجد العاصمة الجزائر يتمثل في محاضرة كل يوم بعد صلاة المغرب من الاثنين إلى الخميس بدأها مساء أمس بمحاضرة عن طلب العلم في مسجد الجهاد الأكبر وسيختم برنامج المساجد بدرس الجمعة يقدمه الشيخ قبل صلاة الجمعة في مسجد أبي ذر الغفاري.
body_en:
His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew (may God the Exalted preserve him), head of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars in Mauritania, arrived on Sunday as a guest of the Ministry of Religious Affairs and Endowments in Algeria, to take part in the first al-Nur Forum for the Qur'an and Its People, organised by the Directorate of Religious Affairs and Endowments for the wilaya of Algiers on 24, 25 and 26 Jumada al-Thaniyah, corresponding to 14, 15 and 16 April. The forum treats the subject of 'Modern Methods and Studies in the Memorisation and Teaching of the Noble Qur'an'.

His Eminence delivered today, Tuesday 14 April 2015, the guests' address at the opening of the forum, and was honoured at the same ceremony by the Minister of Religious Affairs and by the wali of the wilaya of Algiers.

The Sheikh will make contributions on the remaining days of the forum, among them an address entitled 'The Teaching of the Noble Qur'an: A Study of Its Rooting in the Sources', on Tuesday evening; in addition to a lecture tomorrow, Wednesday, entitled 'Group Recitation of the Noble Qur'an: A Study of Its Rooting in the Sources'.

Separately, the Ministry has prepared a programme in the mosques of the capital, Algiers, consisting of a lecture each day after the sunset prayer from Monday to Thursday, which he began yesterday evening with a lecture on seeking knowledge at the Jihad al-Akbar Mosque. The mosque programme will conclude with the Friday lesson the Sheikh will give before the Friday prayer at the Abu Dharr al-Ghifari Mosque.

flags.context: the subtitle of two of the Sheikh's addresses
options: a study of its rooting in the sources
a foundational study
a study from first principles
flags.note: تأصيل is the operation of tracing a practice back to its basis in the sources, so that the question is not whether group recitation works but whether it has a warrant. 'A foundational study' is shorter but loses that; the fuller rendering is used because in both titles the point of the exercise is precisely the rooting. Not in the project glossary; a candidate for addition.

flags.context: the title of the Wednesday lecture
options: group recitation of the Noble Qur'an
collective recitation in unison
communal recitation
flags.note: The practice is reciting aloud in unison, common in North and West African Qur'an schools and disputed among jurists. The record gives only the title, so the Sheikh's position on it is not recoverable here.

flags.context: the name of the forum
options: the first al-Nur Forum for the Qur'an and Its People
the first Light Forum for the Qur'an and its bearers
flags.note: أهل القرآن, 'the people of the Qur'an', is the traditional designation for those who memorise, recite and teach it, drawn from the report 'the people of the Qur'an are the people of God and His elect'. Kept literal; 'its bearers' would be clearer to an English reader but is not what the name says.

translator_notes: A programme notice. None of the addresses or lectures is reported, only their titles.
ولاية is kept as 'wilaya' and والي as 'wali', the Algerian administrative terms, which have no exact English equivalents.
The Hijri and Gregorian dates given for the forum, 24–26 Jumada al-Thaniyah and 14–16 April 2015, agree.

title_ar: فضيلة الشيخ يفتتح برنامجه العلمي بدولة السودان
title_en: The Sheikh Opens His Teaching Programme in Sudan
body_ar: بدأ فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو ـ حفظه الله تعالى ـ رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء و رئيس جمعية المستقبل للدعوة و الثقافة و التعليم صباح اليوم الثلاثاء 8 شعبان الموافق 26 مايو برنامج أستاذ زائر تستضيفه فيه جامعة إفريقيا العالمية في العاصمة السودانية الخرطوم على مدى خمسة أيام تنتهي يوم السبت 12 شعبان الموافق 30 مايو ويشمل البرنامج تدريس مادة المدخل لدراسة الشريعة الإسلامية لطلاب الشريعة والقانون سنة ثانية جامعية، كما يشمل محاضرات مسائية في المسجد العتيق بنفس الجامعة . وقد تم ترتيب الجدول على النحو التالي: - التدريس يوميا في قاعة إفريقيا للمؤتمرات من الساعة الثامنة صباحا وحتى الساعة 12 زوالا تتخللها استراحة لمدة ربع ساعة - محاضرات مسائية بين المغرب والعشاء في المسجد العتيق ستتعرض لمواضيع مختلفة من بينها: التوسط والاعتدال، والإخلاص في العمل وآثاره، ومرونة التشريع الإسلامي، والمرأة الداعية. - خطبة الجمعة في نفس المسجد العتيق في الجامعة وغيرها من اللقاءات العلمية
body_en:
His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew (may God the Exalted preserve him), head of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars and president of the Future Association for Daʿwah, Culture and Education, began this morning, Tuesday 8 Sha'ban corresponding to 26 May, a visiting professorship for which the International University of Africa in the Sudanese capital Khartoum is hosting him, over five days ending on Saturday 12 Sha'ban corresponding to 30 May.

The programme includes teaching the subject 'Introduction to the Study of Islamic Law' to second-year university students of Sharia and law, and also includes evening lectures in the Old Mosque at the same university. The schedule has been arranged as follows:

— Teaching daily in the Africa Conference Hall from eight in the morning until 12 noon, with a quarter of an hour's break.
— Evening lectures between the sunset and the night prayers in the Old Mosque, which will take up various subjects, among them: the middle way and moderation; sincerity in action and its effects; the flexibility of Islamic legislation; and the woman who calls others to Islam.
— The Friday sermon in the same Old Mosque at the university, and other scholarly meetings.

flags.context: the last of the announced evening-lecture subjects
options: the woman who calls others to Islam
the female daʿwah worker
women in daʿwah
flags.note: داعية is the active noun from daʿwah, which the glossary renders 'calling people to Islam'. English has no single-word equivalent that is not either institutional ('preacher') or awkward. The record gives only the title and nothing of the lecture.

translator_notes: A programme notice. None of the lectures is reported.
مرونة التشريع الإسلامي rendered 'the flexibility of Islamic legislation'; it is a lecture title and the Sheikh's own account of what he means by it is not in the record.

title_ar: الشيخ الددو يترأس الحفل الختامي لمركز تكوين العلماء للعام الدراسي 1436هـ
title_en: Sheikh al-Dedew Chairs the Closing Ceremony of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars for the Academic Year 1436 AH
body_ar: ترأس فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو –حفظه الله تعالى- الحفل الختامي لمركز تكوين العلماء للعامي الدراسي 1436هـ الموافق 2014/ 2015م، والذي نظم يوم الخميس 23/07/2015م، تحت شعار "من جد وجد ". وقد بدأ الشيخ كلمته مرحبا بورثة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حاملي مشعل الهداية والنور إلى الناس { الذي يبلغون رسالات الله ويخشونه ولا يخشون أحدا إلى الله }، مثمنا ما يشتغلون به مؤكدا أن الجميع شركاء في أجر المركز من رجال الأعمال الذين يرعون المركز و العلماء الربانيبن ورجال المجتمع وقادة الرأي فيه الذين هم من أشرعة المركز و الذابين عنه وكذلك الأخوات اللواتي سعين لإرفاد هذا المركز بكل ما يحتاج إليه وكذلك رجال الإعلام الذين يبلغون رسالة المركز وينشرونها بين الناس بكل أمانة. مضيفا أن المركز لم ينشأ ليكون رقما يضاف إلى المؤسسات التعليمية في البلد وإنما أنشئ ليكون مركزا عالميا لتكوين العلماء، ومن أجل ذلك وضع برنامجين أحدهما البرنامج العلمي حيث يتناول 63 تخصصا، سيكون بعدها الطالب خلال 17 سنة بمثابة 63 وستين دكتورا في كل التخصصات الشرعية واللغوية، والثاني البرنامج التربوي الذي يهتم بتربية العلماء وصلتهم بالله. بعد ذلك رحب فضيلة الشيخ بالضيوف الكرام كل بإسمه ووصفه، ثم خاطب طلاب المركز قائلا أنتم ورثة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، موضحا أن طلب العلم مزية كريمة، حيث قال إنهم يريدون أن يكون أدنى الطلاب خيرا من أرفع القائمين على المركز رتبة. ثم شكر الشيخ مشاييخ المركز قائلا: جزاكم الله خيرا، فأنت أنصار هذا الزمان فقد قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الأنصار "إنهم أدو الذي عليكم وبقي الذي لكم". كما شكر فضيلته الإخوة في الإدارة على ما بذلوا من جهود مضنية من أجل إسعاد الآخرين، متمثلا فيهم قول الإمام أحمد بن حنبل "الحمد لله الذي جعل في كل بقية من الناس ورثة للرسل يحملون أمانات الله فيؤدونها بأمانة فما أحسن أثرهم على الناس وما أسوء أثر الناس عليهم" وقال فضيلة الشيخ مخاطبا الذين جاؤوا وحضروا لتتويج المركز وعمله نسأل الله أن يتقبل منكم أجمعين فأنتم مشكورون ومأجورون وخطاهم مكتوبة غير ضائعة إن شاء الله ذاكرا أن من نسيه ولم ينوه بإسمه فهو حاضر في البال ولكن قربه حاضر دون ذكره، فالترحيب موصل بالجميع.
body_en:
His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew (may God the Exalted preserve him) chaired the closing ceremony of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars for the academic year 1436 AH, corresponding to 2014/2015, held on Thursday 23/07/2015 under the motto 'Whoever strives, finds'.

The Sheikh began his address by welcoming the heirs of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), the bearers of the torch of guidance and light to the people — {those who convey the messages of God and fear Him and fear none but God} (Sūrat al-Aḥzāb 33:39) — valuing what they are engaged in, and affirming that all are partners in the Centre's reward: the businessmen who support the Centre; the godly scholars; the men of the society and its opinion leaders, who are among the Centre's sails and its defenders; likewise the sisters who have worked to furnish this Centre with everything it needs; and likewise the media people, who convey the Centre's message and spread it among the people in all trustworthiness.

He added that the Centre was not founded to be one more number added to the country's educational institutions, but was founded to be a world centre for the formation of scholars. To that end it has laid out two programmes. The first is the academic programme, which takes in 63 specialisms, after which the student, over 17 years, will be the equivalent of sixty-three doctors in every one of the Sharia and linguistic specialisms. The second is the formative programme, which attends to the moral formation of scholars and to their connection with God.

His Eminence then welcomed the honoured guests, each by name and description, and then addressed the Centre's students, saying: you are the heirs of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) — explaining that seeking knowledge is a noble distinction, and saying that they want the lowest of the students to be better than the highest in rank of those who run the Centre.

The Sheikh then thanked the Centre's teaching shaykhs, saying: "May God reward you well; you are the Ansar of this age" — for the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said of the Ansar: "They have discharged what was upon them, and what is theirs remains."

His Eminence also thanked the brothers in the administration for the exhausting efforts they have expended in order to bring happiness to others, applying to them the words of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal: "Praise be to God, who has placed in every remnant of the people heirs of the messengers, who carry God's trusts and discharge them faithfully. How good is their effect upon the people, and how evil is the people's effect upon them."

Addressing those who had come and been present to crown the Centre and its work, the Sheikh said: we ask God to accept from you all, for you are thanked and rewarded, and their steps are written down and not lost, God willing — noting that anyone he had overlooked and not named was present in his mind, and that such a person's closeness was present without being mentioned; the welcome reaches everyone.

flags.arabic: { الذي يبلغون رسالات الله ويخشونه ولا يخشون أحدا إلى الله }
flags.context: the Qur'anic text quoted at the opening of the address
options: read as الذين … ولا يخشون أحدا إلا الله (Sūrat al-Aḥzāb 33:39)
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT, SCRIPTURE (house rule 11). Two errors in five words of Qur'anic text: الذي for الذين, and إلى for إلا — the second of which reverses the sense, turning 'they fear none but God' into something ungrammatical that reads towards 'they fear no one towards God'. Preserved unchanged in body_ar; the English translates the Qur'anic text and supplies the reference the source omits. The lacuna is left visible here rather than silently repaired in the Arabic.

flags.arabic: "إنهم أدو الذي عليكم وبقي الذي لكم"
flags.context: the report about the Ansar quoted in thanks to the teachers
options: read as أدَّوا الذي عليهم وبقي الذي لهم
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT (house rule 11). The report speaks about the Ansar in the third person — 'they have discharged what was upon them, and what is theirs remains' — but the source puts the pronouns in the second person, عليكم and لكم, which does not construe with إنهم. Preserved in body_ar; the English uses the third person the sentence requires. The Sheikh gives no narrator or collection.

flags.arabic: سيكون بعدها الطالب خلال 17 سنة بمثابة 63 وستين دكتورا
flags.context: the description of the academic programme
options: read as بمثابة ثلاثة وستين دكتورا, matching the 63 specialisms named in the same sentence
the figure is garbled beyond recovery
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT (house rule 11): the numeral 63 is followed by وستين, 'and sixty', producing '63 and sixty doctors'. The sentence has just named 63 specialisms, so the intended figure is plainly sixty-three. Preserved unchanged in body_ar and translated on the required reading. The claim itself — that a student completes the equivalent of sixty-three doctorates in seventeen years — is the Centre's own and is reproduced without comment.

flags.arabic: "الحمد لله الذي جعل في كل بقية من الناس ورثة للرسل…"
flags.context: the saying attributed to Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal
options: reproduce the source's wording: 'in every remnant of the people'
the familiar form of the saying runs 'in every interval between the messengers, remnants of the people of knowledge'
flags.note: The saying is Ahmad's well-known preface to al-Radd ʿalā al-Zanādiqah, usually transmitted as في كل زمان فترة من الرسل بقايا من أهل العلم. The wording here is a compression, whether the Sheikh's, the reporter's or the CMS's. Translated as the source has it and not replaced with the familiar version.

flags.arabic: البرنامج التربوي الذي يهتم بتربية العلماء
flags.context: the second of the Centre's two programmes
options: the formative programme, attending to the moral formation of scholars
the educational programme, attending to the upbringing of scholars
the character-training programme
flags.note: تربية here is formation of character and religious life, set against the علمي programme of learning; 'educational' would collapse the contrast the sentence is built on. تكوين in the Centre's own name is rendered 'formation' throughout, and تربية is distinguished from it as 'moral formation'.

flags.arabic: العلماء الربانيبن / مشاييخ / بإسمه / ما أسوء / للعامي الدراسي / فأنت أنصار
flags.context: scattered through the record
options: read as الربانيين / مشايخ / باسمه / ما أسوأ / للعام الدراسي / فأنتم أنصار
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECTS (house rule 11), recorded together: a transposed letter, a doubled yāʾ, two hamza errors, a case ending and a singular for a plural. All preserved unchanged in body_ar. This record carries an unusually high density of CMS typing errors, which is itself worth noting when the corpus is cleaned globally.

translator_notes: A news report of an address, mixing indirect report with two short direct quotations. Most of the English is the site's account of what the Sheikh said and must not be cited as his wording.
من جد وجد, the ceremony's motto, is a rhyming proverb ('whoever strives, finds'); the rhyme is not reproducible in English and no attempt has been made.
من أشرعة المركز rendered 'among the Centre's sails' — the image is of what drives the ship forward, and it is kept rather than replaced with an explanation.
The final sentence is grammatically tangled in the Arabic, shifting between second and third person; the English follows the shifts rather than smoothing them.
Qur'anic renderings are interpretive and are not a substitute for the Arabic.

title_ar: كفارة من واقع أهله في رمضان أهي خاصة برمضان أم أنها في قضائه وفي كل فرض؟
title_en: The Expiation for a Man Who Has Intercourse with His Wife in Ramadan: Is It Specific to Ramadan, or Does It Apply to Making It Up and to Every Obligatory Fast?
body_ar: السلام عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته مسألة كفارة من واقع أهله في رمضان أهي خاصة برمضان أم أنها في قضائه وفي كل فرض؟ وما دليل قصرها على شهر رمضان أو تعميمها لكل فرض جزاكم الله خيرا الجواب : هذه الكفارة خاصة برمضان فإن الأصل عدم الكفارة و جاء الحديث الصحيح بوجوبها على من واقع امرأته في نهار رمضان صيانة للشهر الذي عظم الله حرمته و أوجب صيام كل يوم منه أما القضاء و النذر ونحوهما من الواجبات فلم يعين الله لها شهرا و لا يوما
body_en:
Peace be upon you, and the mercy of God and His blessings. The question of the expiation (kaffārah) for a man who has intercourse with his wife in Ramadan: is it specific to Ramadan, or does it apply to making up the fast and to every obligatory fast? And what is the evidence for restricting it to the month of Ramadan, or for extending it to every obligatory fast? May God reward you well.

Answer: This expiation is specific to Ramadan. The baseline presumption is that there is no expiation, and the sound (ṣaḥīḥ) hadith came establishing that it is obligatory (wājib) upon a man who has intercourse with his wife during the daytime in Ramadan — as a safeguarding of the month whose sanctity God has magnified and every day of which He has made it obligatory to fast. As for making up the fast, the vowed fast and the like among the obligatory fasts, God has not designated for them a month or a day.
translator_notes: الأصل عدم الكفارة is rendered 'the baseline presumption is that there is no expiation'. This is the uṣūl move that carries the whole answer: expiation is an exception requiring a text, so it does not extend beyond the case the text names.

The questioner asked for the evidence on both sides. The Sheikh gives only the ground for restricting the expiation to Ramadan and does not set out a case for generalising it; nothing has been supplied for the side he did not argue.

title_ar: هل يجوز جمع صوم السبت وأيام البيض والأيام الثلاثة والخميس و الإثنين بنية واحدة و في وقت واحد إذا أمكن الجمع بينها ؟
title_en: Is It Permissible to Combine the Fast of the Six Days, the White Days, the Three Days, Thursday and Monday under a Single Intention and at a Single Time, Where Combining Them Is Possible?
body_ar: السلام عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته شيخنا الفاضل السلام عليكم ورحمت الله وبركاته أحسن الله إليكم هل يجوز جمع صوم الست وأيام البيض والأيام الثلاثة والخميس و الإثنين بنية واحدة و في وقت واحد إذا أمكن الجمع بينها ؟ وما هو الأصل في جمع أكثر من نية في العمل الواحد هل هو الجواز أم المنع جزاكم الله خيرا وبارك فيكم الجواب : الذي يصوم أيام الليالي البيض و يكمل عليها بقية الستة يحصل له فضلان كالذي يصوم الاثنين و الخميس و لا يحتاج إلى نية مخصوصة غير نية الصوم و هذا الجمع في النية في النوافل أما الواجبات كالقضاء فيحصل لصاحبه فضل الأيام أيضا لكن لا يعد من الست لأنها زائدة على رمضان
body_en:
Peace be upon you, and the mercy of God and His blessings. Our excellent Sheikh, peace be upon you, and the mercy of God and His blessings. May God treat you well. Is it permissible to combine the fast of the six days, the white days, the three days, Thursday and Monday under a single intention and at a single time, where combining them is possible? And what is the baseline rule on combining more than one intention in a single act — is it permissibility or prohibition? May God reward you well and bless you.

Answer: One who fasts the days of the white nights and completes with them the remainder of the six obtains two merits, like one who fasts Monday and Thursday; and he needs no intention specific to that beyond the intention to fast. This combining is a combining in the intention within voluntary acts (nawāfil). As for the obligatory fasts, such as making up a missed fast, the one who performs them obtains the merit of those days as well, but it does not count as part of the six, because the six are additional to Ramadan.

flags.context: the title reads صوم السبت; the question in the body reads صوم الست, and the answer speaks of بقية الستة
options: the six days of Shawwal (reading الست, as the body and the answer have it)
the Saturday fast (reading السبت, as the title has it)
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT (house rule 11): title/body mismatch. The title says 'the fast of Saturday', the body of the question says 'the fast of the six', and the answer twice speaks of 'the remainder of the six', which can only be the six days of Shawwal. The title has almost certainly dropped a letter. The English title has been rendered on the body's reading, since the answer settles it, and the Arabic title is preserved unchanged. Flagged rather than corrected.

flags.arabic: ما هو الأصل في جمع أكثر من نية في العمل الواحد هل هو الجواز أم المنع
flags.context: the second half of the question, on the baseline rule for combining intentions
options: the question is not answered as a general rule
the sentence 'this combining is a combining in the intention within voluntary acts' is the answer to it, confined to the voluntary case
flags.note: The questioner asked a question of legal theory: is combining several intentions in one act permissible or barred as a general matter (tashrīk al-niyyah)? The Sheikh answers the particular cases and marks the distinction between voluntary and obligatory acts, but does not state the general rule the questioner asked for. Nothing has been supplied for it.

translator_notes: أيام الليالي البيض, literally 'the days of the white nights', are the thirteenth, fourteenth and fifteenth of the lunar month; 'the three days' in the question is the same practice. The Sheikh treats them as one item, which is why the answer has fewer elements than the question.
فضلان is rendered 'two merits' and not 'a double reward': the Arabic counts the two recommended fasts whose merit accrues, it does not quantify recompense.

title_ar: ما الفرق بين قول المحدث في رواية بعض الصحابة عن بعض المغيبـات: موقوف له حكم الرفع، وقولهم : بل هذا من أخبار بني إسرائيل ؟
title_en: What Is the Difference between a Hadith Scholar Saying, of a Companion's Report about Matters of the Unseen, 'It Stops at a Companion but Has the Status of a Report Traced to the Prophet', and Their Saying, 'Rather This Is from the Reports of the Children of Israel'?
body_ar: الشيخ المفضال السلام عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته أسأل الله العظيم أن يبارك فيكم ويتقبل منا ومنكم صالح القول والعمل. شيخنا ما الفرق بين قول المحدث في رواية بعض الصحابة عن بعض المغيبـات: موقوف له حكم الرفع، وقولهم : بل هذا من أخبار بني إسرائيل ؟ جزاكم الله كل الخير الجواب : ما حكمه الرفع إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه و سلم إذا صح إسناده إلى الصحابي وجب تصديقه و ما كان من الإسرائيليات فلا يصدق و لا يكذب
body_en:
Most excellent Sheikh, peace be upon you, and the mercy of God and His blessings. I ask God the Magnificent to bless you and to accept from us and from you good word and deed.

Our Sheikh, what is the difference between a hadith scholar saying, of a report by some of the Companions about matters of the unseen, that it is 'a report stopping at a Companion (mawqūf) which has the status of a report traced to the Prophet (marfūʿ)', and their saying, 'rather this is from the reports of the Children of Israel'? May God reward you with all good.

Answer: What has the status of being traced to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), if its chain of transmission to the Companion is sound, must be believed. And what belongs to the Israelite reports (isrāʾīliyyāt) is neither affirmed as true nor denied as false.

flags.context: و ما كان من الإسرائيليات فلا يصدق و لا يكذب
options: the Israelite reports (isrāʾīliyyāt)
material transmitted from the earlier scriptural communities
Judaeo-Christian lore
flags.note: Technical term of Qur'anic exegesis and hadith criticism for narrative material of Jewish or Christian provenance transmitted by early Muslims. Kept transliterated with a plain gloss; not in the project glossary, and a candidate for addition alongside the items listed in section 13.

translator_notes: The distinction is a rule of what the believer owes each class of report, not a grading of authenticity: the first must be believed, the second is neither affirmed nor denied, which is the classical position drawn from the report 'do not believe the People of the Book and do not disbelieve them'. The Sheikh does not cite that report here and it has not been supplied.

المغيبات ('matters of the unseen') is the questioner's term and marks why the distinction matters: a Companion reporting something unknowable by ordinary means is presumed to have it from the Prophet, unless it is the sort of thing that came from the earlier scriptures.

title_ar: فضيلة الشيخ يترأس اجتماع المجلس الإداري للمركز
title_en: The Sheikh Chairs the Meeting of the Centre's Administrative Board
body_ar: ترأس فضيلة الشيخ : محمد الحسن ولد الددو صباح اليوم الأحد 10 صفر 1437هـ الموافق : 22 نوفمبر 2015م اجتماع مجلس إدارة مركز تكوين العلماء في دورته العادية الأولى للعام الدراسي 2015- 2016، بحضور الدكتور محمد المختار ولد محمد المامي المدير العام للمركز وأعضاء المجلس. وسيناقش المجلس ضمن جدول أعماله أبرز بنود الخطة التسييرية، ومتفرقات أخرى، ومن المقرر أن يتخذ المجلس القرارات اللازمة بشأن مختلف النقاط التي شملها جدول أعماله، واعتماد الترتيبات التي من شأنها أن تسهل انسيابية العملية الإدارية والتنفيذية، وتحسين الأداء في مختلف المجالات التي تطالها اهتمامات المركز.
body_en:
His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew chaired this morning, Sunday 10 Safar 1437 AH, corresponding to 22 November 2015, the meeting of the board of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars in its first ordinary session of the academic year 2015–2016, attended by Dr Muhammad al-Mukhtar Ould Muhammad al-Mami, the Centre's director general, and the members of the board.

Among the items on its agenda, the board will discuss the principal points of the management plan and other miscellaneous matters. It is expected that the board will take the necessary decisions on the various points covered by its agenda, and will adopt the arrangements apt to ease the flow of the administrative and executive process and to improve performance in the various fields the Centre's concerns reach into.

flags.arabic: واعتماد الترتيبات التي من شأنها أن تسهل انسيابية العملية الإدارية والتنفيذية، وتحسين الأداء في مختلف المجالات التي تطالها اهتمامات المركز
flags.context: the closing sentence, against record 874 in this slice
options: boilerplate repeated verbatim between the two records
coincidence of wording
flags.note: DUPLICATE TEXT (house rule 11). The second paragraph of this record repeats, word for word, the second paragraph of record 874 of 18 September 2014, which reports a different meeting fourteen months earlier. The site is reusing a template for board-meeting notices. The two records are not duplicates of one another — the dates, session and attendees differ — but neither paragraph reports anything that actually happened. Not deduplicated.

translator_notes: An institutional notice containing nothing by the Sheikh and no religious content.

title_ar: الشيخ الددو يحاضر في منتدى كوالا لمبور للفكر و الحضارة
title_en: Sheikh al-Dedew Lectures at the Kuala Lumpur Forum for Thought and Civilisation
body_ar:
انطلقت صباح اليوم الجمعة 27 نوفمبر 2015 الموافق 15 صفر 1437هـ أنشطة المؤتمر السنوي الثاني من منتدى كوالالمبورللفكر و الحضارة في العاصمة الماليزية تحت عنوان : ( دور الحرية و الديمقراطية في تحقيق الاستقرار و التنمية ) برئاسة رئيس المنتدى حضرة الدكتور : مهاتير محمد رئيس وزراء ماليزيا الأسبق و بحضور كوكبة من العلماء و المفكرين و قادة الرأي في الأمة و يستمر المنتدى لمدة يومين ( 27 ـ 28 نوفمبر 2015م )

وقد ألقى فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو نائب رئيس المنتدى أولى محاضرات هذه النسخة تحت عنوان : ( دور الحريات والديمقراطية في تحقيق الاستقرار والتنمية: دراسة نظرية في الشريعة الإسلامية )

ويحاضر في المنتدى شخصيات علمية وفكرية مرموقة من مختلف أنحاء العالم يقدمون دراسات نظرية ويعرضون تجارب عملية تجيب عن أثر الحرية والديمقراطية في تحقيق الاستقرار والتنمية في المجتمعات البشرية.

كما ستكون لفضيلة الشيخ محاضرات و أنشطة دعوية و فكرية أخرى على هامش المنتدى من بينها محاضرة لطلاب قسم الفقه وأصوله بكلية معارف الوحي والعلوم الإنسانية ـ الجامعة الإسلامية في ماليزيا ( بعنوان : الأنس بالله ) ومحاضرة ينظمها مركز دراسات الشرق الأوسط ..
body_en:
The activities of the second annual conference of the Kuala Lumpur Forum for Thought and Civilisation began this Friday morning, 27 November 2015, corresponding to 15 Safar 1437 AH, in the Malaysian capital, under the title 'The Role of Freedom and Democracy in Achieving Stability and Development'. It is chaired by the forum's president, His Excellency Dr Mahathir Mohamad, former Prime Minister of Malaysia, and attended by a distinguished company of scholars, thinkers and opinion leaders of the community. The forum runs for two days (27–28 November 2015).

His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew, vice-president of the forum, delivered the first of this edition's lectures, entitled 'The Role of Freedoms and Democracy in Achieving Stability and Development: A Theoretical Study in the Islamic Sharia'.

Eminent scholarly and intellectual figures from various parts of the world are lecturing at the forum, presenting theoretical studies and setting out practical experiences that address the effect of freedom and democracy upon the achievement of stability and development in human societies.

The Sheikh will also have further lectures and activities, in calling people to Islam (daʿwah) and in the life of the mind, on the margins of the forum. Among them is a lecture for the students of the Department of Fiqh and Its Principles at the Kulliyyah of Islamic Revealed Knowledge and Human Sciences, International Islamic University Malaysia, entitled 'Intimacy with God (al-uns bi-Llāh)', and a lecture organised by the Centre for Middle Eastern Studies…

flags.context: the title of a lecture at the International Islamic University Malaysia
options: Intimacy with God (al-uns bi-Llāh)
Finding One's Comfort in God
Companionship with God
flags.note: A term of the spiritual literature (tazkiyah) for the settled ease the heart finds in God. 'Intimacy' is the established English rendering but reads oddly in a lecture title; the alternatives are offered. Not in the glossary.

flags.arabic: ومحاضرة ينظمها مركز دراسات الشرق الأوسط ..
flags.context: the final clause of the record
options: end the English where the Arabic ends, with the ellipsis
flags.note: The record breaks off at this point with a bare '..' — the list of the Sheikh's other activities is left unfinished in the source. The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends and completes nothing (addendum section 9).

translator_notes: A programme notice written by the site. None of the lectures is reported, only their titles.
SOURCE DEFECT: 'كوالالمبورللفكر' is run together in the source. Preserved in body_ar.
'كلية معارف الوحي والعلوم الإنسانية ـ الجامعة الإسلامية في ماليزيا' is given by the institution's own English name, the Kulliyyah of Islamic Revealed Knowledge and Human Sciences, IIUM.
The CMS timestamp is a bulk-upload date, not the date of composition.

title_ar: الشيخ الددو يزور الشيخ عائض القرني لعيادته
title_en: Sheikh al-Dedew Visits Sheikh Aidh al-Qarni to Enquire After His Health
body_ar: أدى فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو - حفظه الله- اليوم الأربعاء 5 رجب 1437ھ الموافق 13 إبريل 2016م زيارة للشيخ عائض القرني في بيته بمدينة الرياض عاصمة المملكة العربية السعودية، على إثر حادثة إطلاق النار التي تعرض لها في الفلبين، وقد استقبله الشيخ عائض عند باب منزله، حيث بدأ الشيخ الددو تهنئته على سلامته ودعا له بالصحة والعافية وبلغه تحيات أهل موريتانيا ودعائهم له، قبل أن يرحب الشيخ عائض بضيفه الشيخ الددو ويشكره على الزيارة، مقدما شكره لأهل موريتانيا على تضامنهم ودعمهم مشيدا بما عرفوا به من الاهتمام بالعلم وأهله، هذا وقد ختم الشيخ الددو زيارته برقية للشيخ عائض قرأها عليه.
body_en: His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew (may God preserve him) paid a visit this Wednesday, 5 Rajab 1437 AH, corresponding to 13 April 2016, to Sheikh Aidh al-Qarni at his home in the city of Riyadh, the capital of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, following the shooting incident to which he had been subjected in the Philippines. Sheikh Aidh received him at the door of his house, where Sheikh al-Dedew began by congratulating him on his safety, praying for his health and well-being, and conveying to him the greetings of the people of Mauritania and their prayers for him; after which Sheikh Aidh welcomed his guest Sheikh al-Dedew and thanked him for the visit, offering his thanks to the people of Mauritania for their solidarity and support, and praising the concern for learning and for the learned by which they are known. Sheikh al-Dedew closed his visit with a healing recitation (ruqyah) for Sheikh Aidh, which he recited over him.

flags.context: the closing clause: هذا وقد ختم الشيخ الددو زيارته برقية للشيخ عائض قرأها عليه
options: with a healing recitation (ruqyah) for Sheikh Aidh, which he recited over him
with a message (barqiyyah) to Sheikh Aidh, which he read out to him
with some lines of verse for Sheikh Aidh, which he read to him
flags.note: Unpointed, بـرقية is either 'بِرُقْيَة' — with a ruqyah, a healing recitation — or 'بَرْقِيَّة', a telegram or message. The context (a sick visit after a shooting) and the verb 'قرأها عليه', recited it OVER him rather than TO him, both favour ruqyah; 'قرأ على' is the standard collocation for performing ruqyah. A written message would normally take 'قرأها له'. The choice changes what is reported to have happened, so it should not be fixed without the site's confirmation.

translator_notes: عيادة in the title is the visiting of a sick person, not a clinic; rendered 'to enquire after his health'.
Sheikh Aidh al-Qarni was wounded in a shooting in Zamboanga, the Philippines, in March 2016. The source gives no further detail and none has been added.
The CMS timestamp is a bulk-upload date, not the date of composition.

title_ar: فضيلة الشيخ الددو يشارك في مؤتمر دولي بقطر
title_en: Sheikh al-Dedew Takes Part in an International Conference in Qatar
body_ar: يشارك سماحة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو-حفظه الله- رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء بموريتانيا على مدار ثلاثة أيام ابتداء من يوم الجمعة 08 رجب 1437ھـ الموافق 15 إبريل 2016م بالعاصمة القطرية الدوحة في "المؤتمر العالمي للتعليم الشرعي وسبل ترقيته" المنظم من طرف الاتحاد العالمي لعلماء المسلمين برعاية من حكومة دولة قطر، ويشارك في هذا المؤتمر إلى جانب الشيخ كوكبة من العلماء ورؤساء مؤسسات التعليم الشرعي والباحثين في مجال الشريعة من بلدان مختلفة.
body_en: His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew (may God preserve him), president of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars in Mauritania, is taking part over three days, beginning on Friday 8 Rajab 1437 AH, corresponding to 15 April 2016, in the Qatari capital Doha, in the 'International Conference on Sharia Education and the Means of Advancing It', organised by the International Union of Muslim Scholars under the patronage of the government of the State of Qatar. Taking part in this conference alongside the Sheikh is a distinguished company of scholars, heads of institutions of Sharia education, and researchers in the field of the Sharia from various countries.

flags.context: المؤتمر العالمي للتعليم الشرعي وسبل ترقيته
options: Sharia education
education in the religious sciences
religious legal education
flags.note: 'التعليم الشرعي' is the whole curriculum of the revealed sciences as taught in traditional institutions, wider than fiqh alone. 'Sharia education' is short and is the phrase these institutions use of themselves in English, but it can mislead an English reader into thinking of law schools. Worth fixing once for the corpus.

translator_notes: سماحة is a higher honorific than فضيلة, which the same site uses of the Sheikh elsewhere; English has no matching pair, so both are rendered 'His Eminence' and the difference is noted here rather than invented in the English.
مركز تكوين العلماء is rendered 'the Centre for the Formation of Scholars', the institution's own usage; تكوين here is formation or training, not creation.
The CMS timestamp is a bulk-upload date, not the date of composition.

title_ar: الشيخ الددو يفتتح برنامجه العلمي باسطنبول بدورة في أصول الفقه
title_en: Sheikh al-Dedew Opens His Scholarly Programme in Istanbul with a Course in Legal Theory
body_ar:
افتتح صباح اليوم السبت 16 رجب 1437هـ الموافق 23 ابريل 2016م بالعاصمة التركية اسطنبول فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو حفظه الله تعالى رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء ورئيس جامعة عبد الله بن ياسين برنامجه العلمي بدورة في أًصول الفقه " شرح كتاب " مفتاح الوصول إلى بناء الفروع على الأصول لمؤلفه محمد بن أحمد الحسني التلمساني ، و قد تحدث فضيلته عن أهمية أصول الفقه و مكانته في التشريع الاسلامي باعتباره يشمل على أغلب مصادر التشريع من الاجماع و القياس و ينظم طرق الاستنباط ، متحدثا عن أبرز رجالات هذا الفن و الكتب المؤلفة فيه وذلك قبل شرحه لمتن الكتاب و التعليق عليه ..

وتستمر الدورة لمدة ثلاثة أيام، يكون للشيخ خلالها أنشطة أخرى خارج الدورة من بنيها محاضرة بعنوان: "الشمائل المحمدية"، مساء السبت في مقر وقف دار السلام باسطنبول.
body_en:
This Saturday morning, 16 Rajab 1437 AH, corresponding to 23 April 2016, in the Turkish capital Istanbul, His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew (may God the Exalted preserve him), president of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars and president of Abdullah ibn Yasin University, opened his scholarly programme with a course in legal theory (uṣūl al-fiqh): a commentary on the book Miftāḥ al-Wuṣūl ilā Bināʾ al-Furūʿ ʿalā al-Uṣūl ('The Key to Building the Subsidiary Rulings upon the Principles') by its author Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Hasani al-Tilimsani. His Eminence spoke about the importance of legal theory and its standing in Islamic legislation, in that it takes in most of the sources of law — scholarly consensus (ijmāʿ) and analogical reasoning (qiyās) — and regulates the methods of deriving rulings; and he spoke about the foremost men of this discipline and the books written in it, before expounding the text of the book and commenting upon it…

The course runs for three days, during which the Sheikh will have other activities outside it, among them a lecture entitled 'The Noble Qualities of Muhammad (al-Shamāʾil al-Muḥammadiyyah)', on Saturday evening at the premises of the Dar al-Salam endowment (waqf) in Istanbul.

flags.context: و ينظم طرق الاستنباط
options: deriving rulings
derivation
the extraction of rulings from the sources
flags.note: istinbāṭ is not in the project glossary and recurs across the corpus; record 881 renders it 'derivation'. One fixed rendering should be chosen corpus-wide. Flagged again here so the two records are resolved together.

flags.arabic: يشمل على أغلب مصادر التشريع من الاجماع و القياس
flags.context: the Sheikh's account of what legal theory covers
options: it takes in most of the sources of law — scholarly consensus and analogical reasoning
it comprises most of the sources of law, such as consensus and analogy
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT, recorded not fixed: 'يشمل على' is a solecism for 'يشتمل على'. Substantively, listing only ijmāʿ and qiyās as 'most of the sources' is the reporter's compression, not a considered statement of the sources of law; the English does not tidy it into a fuller list the Sheikh did not give.

translator_notes: A news report written by the site; the Sheikh's remarks are reported indirectly and the English keeps that indirection.
SOURCE DEFECTS preserved in body_ar: 'أًصول' carries a stray tanwīn mark; the opening quotation mark before 'شرح كتاب' is unclosed; 'بنيها' stands for 'بينها'.

Miftāḥ al-Wuṣūl is the well-known Maliki uṣūl work of al-Sharif al-Tilimsani (d. 771/1370). The source gives the author as محمد بن أحمد الحسني التلمساني and the English reproduces that without correcting or expanding it.
The first paragraph breaks off with '..' in the source; the English ends where the Arabic ends.
The CMS timestamp is a bulk-upload date, not the date of composition.

title_ar: فضيلة الشيخ يفتتح ملتقى الفقه الإسلامي بمركز تكوين العلماء
title_en: The Sheikh Opens the Forum on Islamic Fiqh at the Centre for the Formation of Scholars
body_ar:
